# Requirements — the complete set, by module

**GENERATED — do not hand-edit.** Written by `scripts/requirements-doc.ts`
(`npm run docs:reqs`). Edit the source and re-run it.

One document, so there is one place to read what this system is required to
do. It is ASSEMBLED rather than written: every requirement below is
maintained somewhere else, and a hand-kept fifth copy would be the one that
goes stale while reading as authoritative.

| | Where it is maintained | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **URS** | `src/lib/validation.ts` | **User requirements** — what the business needs, in its own words |
| **FRS** | `src/lib/validation.ts` | **System requirements** — how this system does it. Each names the URS it implements |
| **CR** | [`docs/CALL_REQUEST_REQUIREMENTS.md`](CALL_REQUEST_REQUIREMENTS.md) | The CALL REQUEST module, in full |
| **SR** | [`docs/ISO13485_SERVICING.md`](ISO13485_SERVICING.md) | The SERVICING PROCESS against ISO 13485 §7.5.4 — a DRAFT, not approved |
| **CW** | [`docs/COVER_REQUIREMENTS.md`](COVER_REQUIREMENTS.md) | WARRANTY, CONTRACT, OWNERSHIP TRANSFER and the assembled machine record — a DRAFT |
| **OQ / PQ** | `src/lib/validation.ts` | The tests that prove each one |

## How to read it

**A user requirement is a need; a system requirement is a mechanism.** Under
each URS below sit the FRS entries that implement it, and under those the
tests that prove them. Read downwards and you have the whole argument for one
requirement: what was asked for, how it was built, and what shows it works.

**Derived by default, declared by exception — and each entry says which.**
A requirement is filed under a module when its own text names that module —
its route, or every distinctive word of its label — so the grouping is
evidence rather than opinion and it moves when the text does. Where the words
name no screen, the requirement may DECLARE the modules it governs, and those
are marked *declared* below.

That exception exists because derivation alone left **34 of 56 screens** with
no requirement section, the **Field Call Register** among them: URS-003 says
"register a customer call" and never says "field", so the one requirement that
plainly governs the register was filed under "not tied to one screen". The two
are UNIONED rather than one replacing the other, so a requirement that later
gains the words keeps being filed by them.

A requirement naming several modules appears under each: "a manager sees their
team’s calls" really is a requirement of every call register.

**A requirement that names no screen is not forced into one.** Those are
gathered at the end. Most are system-wide — access control, audit, retention —
and belong to no single screen.

### URS-093 — The dashboard states what it counts, and never judges service against targets nobody set

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The dashboard shall show, for the calls the reader may see, the number of field and of installation calls, of requests awaiting a call number, of calls registered this month, of calls breached and due against the service-level targets, of calls answered yes to a public health threat or a serious incident, of customers served and of engineers active, with the charts and recent calls behind them, and shall state whose calls it covers (all, a team, or the reader’s own). A breach shall be judged only against the targets the organisation has configured: where those cannot be read the dashboard shall say so rather than judge against built-in defaults. A figure that could not be read shall be shown as not available, never as nought.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-116** — The Dashboard | Medium | OQ-104 |

**FRS-116.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-116.1 The Field Calls and Installation Calls cards shall count the calls of those types the reader may see, and preventive-maintenance calls shall not be counted in any figure on the page. FRS-116.2 The Pending Registrations card shall count requests awaiting a UCN, and shall show — when that count cannot be read. FRS-116.3 Calls This Month shall count by registration date, falling back to complaint date. FRS-116.4 A call shall be due when it is within a quarter of its target and at least 6 hours from it, and breached when past it. FRS-116.5 The Needs attention table shall list breached calls first and then due calls, at most 20, naming the rule closest to breach, and say how many more there are. FRS-116.6 The SLA rules shall be read from sla_rules; where they cannot be read the page shall say that breach cannot be assessed and show no breach or due figures, never figures computed against built-in defaults (D-024). FRS-116.7 Public Health Threats and Serious Incidents shall count the visible calls answered yes, over all time, and say so. FRS-116.8 Parties Served and Engineers Active shall count distinct customers and distinct allotted engineers over the visible calls. FRS-116.9 The charts shall show calls over the last 6 months, the item status mix, the top products and the top 6 engineers, dates read day-first. FRS-116.10 Recent Calls shall list the latest 8 by registration date. FRS-116.11 Clicking an SLA row or a recent call shall open that call in its own register (Field, Installation or PM). FRS-116.12 The header shall show the scope in force (All calls, Team view with its size, or My calls), and the page shall say when not connected, when a read failed, while loading and, on an empty chart, No data yet.

### URS-087 — The review register shows every call’s stage with exact counts, and can be taken away in its own format

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall present every field call with the stage its review has reached, as a register, as worklists of the calls awaiting each stage and as a review desk; it shall filter by call date, review status, call status, product, engineer, potential effect and free text, opening on the current year. The count of calls at each stage shall be exact over the whole filtered set, or shall say that it is still being counted or could not be counted; a count taken over rows still loading shall carry a “+”. A worklist shall load in full, up to a stated ceiling, so that a reviewer working down it reaches the end. The register shall be exportable, by authorised roles only, as the DCCR in its own columns and order, covering the whole filtered set. A reader without the authority to review shall see the register read-only and be told which permission is missing.

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

My Workload shall gather, on one page, the counts of the work waiting in every register the reader may open — spare requests by stage and those awaiting the reader, RM approvals, pending dispatch with its ageing, hand stock, material returns, stock transfers, the daily complaint review by stage, and installations awaiting Commercial — and shall request nothing from a register the reader may not open. Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

### URS-174 — Only the Indoor delivery challan is approved, and its approval files the visit

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

An Indoor delivery challan shall be created pending approval, naming who authorises it — the issuer's Reporting Manager, Regional Manager or an NSM — and only that person or an administrator shall approve or reject it, with the decision, who made it and when recorded by the system and printed on the challan. A unit shall not be dispatched while its challan is pending. Approving shall file, against each unit's call, the Visit Entry drafted with its Indoor Service Report — the call left Unsolved, pending Return to Field, with the work details and the uploaded report — through the same path and rules as a visit entered on the call, and shall not complete while any of those visits is unfiled. Rejecting shall need a reason, keep the challan and release its units for a new one. The spare-parts challan is not affected.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-234** — The visit drafted with the Indoor report, and filed against the call at the DC's approval | High | OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-234 |
| **FRS-235** — The Indoor DC is approved by its Authorised By; rejection releases the units | High | OQ-223, OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-234, OQ-244 |
| **FRS-237** — The Indoor visit's Visiting Service Engineer is picked from the User Master | Medium | OQ-228, OQ-229 |

**FRS-234.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-234.1 For a job with a UCN the report upload shall be the Visit Entry form itself (CallReportDrawer, Indoor mode) — every field and rule of that form for the call's register — with Call Status Unsolved, Call Pending Reason Return to Field and Update Visit Work Details? Yes fixed and stated, the Visiting Service Engineer picked (FRS-237) — the signed-in Indoor engineer by default — and the Manual Report field replaced by the Indoor Service Report No. and its upload; saving shall store the answers on the job as a draft (`visit_draft`, `visit_date`) and write nothing to the call. FRS-234.2 A job with no UCN shall take the report number and file only and shall file no visit. FRS-234.3 At approval (FRS-235) each job with a UCN whose visit is not filed shall have its draft filed BY THE DATABASE (`approve_indoor_dc()`, 0327) as the Visit Entry's save path files it — the visit row and the drafted spares, in one transaction with the approval, so a refusal leaves the DC pending with nothing filed — as the approver, whatever their role, the engineer and engineer email being the draft's (FRS-237), Call Status / Pending Reason / Update Visit Work Details? forced to the three fixed values, the uploaded report as the visit's Manual Report and the report number as “Manual Report No.” in its data. FRS-234.4 The filed visit shall be recorded on the job (`visit_uid`, `visit_filed_at`) by the approval, or by `record_indoor_visit()`, which only the DC's approver or an administrator may call and only for a job on a DC pending approval; no other signed-in write may change either (0327); the guard shall refuse a visit that is not of the job's own call, that does not read Unsolved / Return to Field / Yes, or before the report is uploaded. FRS-234.5 A visit already filed shall not be filed again on a retry. FRS-234.6 “Return to Field” shall be on the Call Pending Reason master, active (0323). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02: “why should they do the same work twice”, and “ALWAYS set the call to Unsolved, pending reason = Return to Field, Update visit work details = Yes”. Unsolved is not a solved status, so no feedback is asked or written.

**FRS-235.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-235.1 `indoor_dc_authorisers()` shall offer, from the User Master and from nothing else, the signed-in issuer's Reporting Manager and Regional Manager (their own row, matched by login email or gmail) and, as NSM, the Reporting Manager on the Regional Manager's own User Master row; never the issuer, never a blank name, names only (0327). FRS-235.2 `create_indoor_dc()` shall require one of them as AUTHORISED BY, store it as the list spells it, and create the DC Pending approval; the units keep their DC No. as a reservation. FRS-235.3 `approve_indoor_dc()` and `reject_indoor_dc()` shall be allowed only to the person named — their User Master name or profile name matching, ignoring case — or an administrator (`indoor_dc_may_approve()`), only while the DC is pending; approval shall file every unit's drafted visit (FRS-234.3) in the same transaction, refuse the DC's own issuer unless an administrator, and stamp approved_by, approved_by_name and approved_at from the session; a check-only call shall ask who, state and that every unit with a UCN has its visit drafted. FRS-235.4 Rejection shall need a reason, record who and when, keep the DC, and release its units — DC No., DC date and the dispatch stamps cleared — through a release ticket only that function writes, so an approver without indoor.dispatch can release them and nobody else can use the exemption. FRS-235.5 The guard shall refuse a unit on a DC pending approval the move to Dispatched or Closed. FRS-235.6 The Indoor DC list shall show the approval, the Authorised By and the decision, list first and count the DCs awaiting the reader, and offer them Approve and Reject with a reason; My Workload shall show “Awaiting my approval” and “Pending approval” to whoever can open the Indoor Service Register, opening the DC list, and “Awaiting my approval” alone to anybody else a pending DC names, opening /indoor-dc-approvals. FRS-235.9 The person a DC names shall read that DC, its lines and its units whatever their role (indoor_dcs_read, indoor_dc_lines_read, indoor_read), and nothing else of Indoor Service; the DC print shall open for them (0327). FRS-235.7 None of these functions shall be callable by the public key. FRS-235.8 A DC issued before 0323 shall read “Issued before approval”. FRS-235.10 A User Master rename shall carry the Authorised By of a DC still Pending approval to the new name, and leave an approved, rejected or issued-before-approval DC naming whom it was printed with (D-144). The approvals page shall tell a reader who cannot open Indoor Service that no DC names them, rather than that none was issued, and count only theirs (D-146). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02: “Only the INDOOR DC needs an approval” — the spare DC is untouched; no key is added and nothing is granted: the approver is named on the DC. The user, 2026-10-03: “it is dynamic based on the user master. So when I say RM / RGM / NSM - it should map as per the user Master”, the NSM being the Regional Manager's own manager, and the person named approving whatever their role holds.

**FRS-237.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-237.1 On the Repair page's service report for a job with a UCN, Visiting Service Engineer shall be a type-search pick (SelectPicker) of every ACTIVE person on the User Master (useActivePeople — Validity not false), defaulting to the signed-in Indoor engineer and, for a saved draft, to the engineer it was saved with; a name already on the draft shall stay listed after that person leaves. FRS-237.2 Choosing a person shall set the draft's engineer email to that person's User Master Email ID (else GMAIL ID), and to the signed-in user's login email where the chosen name is theirs and the row carries none, so the name and the email always name one person. FRS-237.3 The hand stock the visit's spares are consumed from shall follow the chosen engineer, as on a field visit. FRS-237.4 At the DC's approval the visit shall be filed with that engineer and email (reports.engineer / engineer_email, and each consumption line's engineer) while the filer stays the approver's session; the database pins neither to the session — record_indoor_visit() and the guard check the visit's call and its three fixed values, not its engineer — so no migration was needed. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03: the person who repaired the unit is not always the person signed in, and the visit history must name who attended.

### URS-074 — A decision to supply rests on evidence that is retained

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall record, for each customer, whether that customer has been verified. The system shall retain the records on which that verification rests. The system shall show both wherever the decision to supply is taken. A verification with no record behind it is an assertion, and the person relying on it downstream cannot check it.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-174** — KYC values, how two of them are derived, and the verification stamp | Medium | OQ-167 |
| **FRS-090** — What the period suggests, and what the customer register holds | Medium | OQ-78 |
| **FRS-088** — The installations awaiting Commercial | Low | OQ-76 |
| **FRS-086** — KYC records attached to a customer | Medium | OQ-74 |

**FRS-174.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-174.1 The KYC status shall be one of Pending, Verified or Rejected, anything else refused by a CHECK constraint (0201), and a new party with none shall read Pending. FRS-174.2 The database shall fill a blank GSTIN from the tax fields the party carries, found by its shape, and a blank PAN from the GSTIN (characters 3 to 12) or the tax fields, and shall never overwrite a value already entered. FRS-174.3 The drawer shall take a GSTIN of fifteen characters and, on entry, fill a blank PAN from it. FRS-174.4 When the status becomes Verified the database shall stamp the verifier from the session and the time, discarding values the caller sent in that write. FRS-174.5 When the status leaves Verified the database shall clear both. FRS-174.6 Attaching a KYC record whose link is already attached shall keep one record. RATIONALE: .5 because a party that is no longer verified was not verified by anybody, and leaving the name on it says it was. Proved by `supabase/tests/party_kyc_test.sql` (.1, .2, .4, .5) and `npm run check:kyc` (.6).

**FRS-090.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-090.1 The cover registers shall calculate a PM visit count from the recorded period. FRS-090.2 The cover registers shall accept a PM visit count entered by the operator. FRS-090.3 The cover registers shall retain an entered PM visit count when the period or the start date is subsequently changed. FRS-090.4 The warranty register shall re-read the address, the contact details and the tax registrations of the named customer from the customer register when the operator requests it. FRS-090.5 The warranty register shall state each field that request would change, with its present and its proposed value, before changing any. FRS-090.6 The warranty register shall change no field where the customer register holds no such customer. RATIONALE: .1 and .3 together are the requirement — three visits a year is the standard OFFER and what was sold is on the purchase order, so a count that keeps reverting to the offer whenever a start date is corrected is a field somebody re-types until they give up, and one that never follows the period makes every ordinary sale a manual entry. The test for "has it been changed" is whether it still equals what the period suggested BEFORE the edit, which is the same rule a machine uses to pin a field away from its entry. .5 because the installation address on a sale legitimately differs from the registered one: a sale whose address changed silently under an operator who had corrected it by hand is worse than one that is visibly out of date, because the first is wrong and nobody knows. .6 because blanking a sale on the ground that the customer register has never heard of the customer would destroy the only address anybody has.

**FRS-088.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-088.1 My Workload shall list the number of installation requests for which no call has been raised. FRS-088.2 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is verified. FRS-088.3 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is not verified. FRS-088.4 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is absent from the customer register. FRS-088.5 My Workload shall open the request register filtered to the stated subset when the operator selects a count. FRS-088.6 The request register shall display the verification status of the customer named by each request. RATIONALE: FRS-088.4 is separate from FRS-088.3 because the two need opposite actions — a customer who is absent is added, a customer who is present is verified — and a figure that merges them sends somebody to verify a customer who does not exist. The section is offered to every operator who may open the request register rather than to one department, because a count over a list the reader may not open is both useless and a disclosure of its size.

**FRS-086.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-086.1 The customer register shall attach a document to a customer and shall record its name, its location, the operator who attached it and the time. FRS-086.2 The customer register shall display the verification status of each customer in its list. FRS-086.3 The customer register shall display a link to each attached record in that list. FRS-086.4 The system shall treat a customer as verified on the recorded status alone. FRS-086.5 The system shall treat no customer as verified by the presence of an attached record. FRS-086.6 The customer register shall state, for a verified customer with no attached record, that the record is absent. FRS-086.7 The customer register shall retain a removed record in the document store. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 are the two halves of one asymmetry. The status is a DECISION a person made, and withholding it because the paperwork was filed elsewhere would make the system stricter than the people it serves; attaching a file is not a decision, so it can never make a customer verified. .7 because a KYC record somebody relied on is worth keeping wherever it sits.

### URS-066 — A request awaiting registration is visible and is dispositioned

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A request for service that has not yet become a call shall be visible as such, and shall reach one of a stated set of outcomes — registered as a new call, mapped to an existing call, or cancelled with a reason. It shall not be possible for a request to be silently dropped or to remain in no state at all, a request nobody can see being indistinguishable from a request nobody made.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-125** — A disposition is made against a real call and confirmed written | High | OQ-113 |
| **FRS-078** — Pending Registrations is the queue, and every row leaves it by a stated route | Medium | OQ-59 |

**FRS-125.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-125.1 Pending Registrations shall map a request only to a UCN that `callByUcn()` finds; a UCN not found shall be refused with that reason and shall not be offered for confirmation. FRS-125.2 Mapping and cancelling shall count the rows written; where none were written the screen shall say the request was not changed and name the right it needs (`pending.register`). FRS-125.3 Registering a call from a request, on Pending Registrations or on arrival at a call register, shall write the new UCN and status Registered to the request and shall wait for that write; where it fails, the screen shall name the new UCN and state that the request is still pending. FRS-125.4 A cancellation shall require a reason and may carry a note; it shall record the time, and the request shall remain in the register (CR-020). FRS-125.5 A reader without `pending.register` shall see the queue and be told that they cannot action it. FRS-125.6 Every change to a request shall be captured by the database's row audit on `call_requests` (`record_audit`, 0225) with the person and the time. RATIONALE: .1 because the screen today asks “map anyway?” and closes the request against a UCN that exists nowhere; .2 and .3 because `setCallRequestUcn` and `cancelCallRequest` take no row count, and the back-fill after registering is `try { ... } catch { /* best-effort */ }` on one screen and `void` on the other — a request left Pending beside its own call is registered twice (D-031).

**FRS-078.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Pending Registrations lists requests carrying no UC Number. Opening one offers exactly three outcomes — register it as a new call, map it to an existing call (its UCN is recorded against the request), or cancel it with a reason — and the request’s status records which. IT READS `call_requests`, NOT the sheet-era `pending_registrations` table: two corrections were aimed at the wrong table before that surfaced, and the distinction is recorded in the codebase notes as well as here. Clickable Call Type filters at the top count the requests of each type that the search leaves, and filter the list to one type.

### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

FRS-103.2 The review shall show Review 1 (public health threat, death, serious incident, completed or pending, date) read-only. FRS-103.3 The review shall show the age at failure under Warranty Failure, with a WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR warning below 366 days and “not known” where no warranty start is recorded. FRS-103.4 The review shall show, from the reports, the hour meter of the latest visit, the software version, the pending reason, and every visit newest first with its status, engineer and job done. FRS-103.5 The review shall display the signed service report inside the screen. FRS-103.6 The review shall list the spares booked against the call with part number, description and quantity. FRS-103.7 The review shall open a Machine History pop-up for the call’s machine under the reader’s own visibility. FRS-103.8 The review shall show Any Potential Effect worked out from the three answers as they are chosen, and state that a Field Failure Report is to be raised when it reads YES, before anything is saved. FRS-103.9 All NO shall fill the three Review 2 answers and shall not save them. FRS-103.10 A context read that fails shall say that it could not be read rather than show an empty list.

**FRS-104.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-104.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall return a verdict of frequent when rule 1 (FRS-054) or rule 2 holds, and shall say which fired. FRS-104.2 Rule 2 shall hold where the same standard complaint is recorded on at least ffr.rule2_serials DISTINCT serials of the same product (default 2, never fewer than 2) within ffr.rule2_window_days before the call (default 30), counting serials and not calls. FRS-104.3 Rule 2 shall be switchable by ffr.rule2_enabled, and its window and serial count held in app_settings separately from rule 1’s. ### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

It shall never show a record the person could not open on the register itself.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |

| **FRS-218** — Global search | Medium | OQ-212 |

**FRS-218.** *(v0.10.104 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-218.1 The header search shall list matching screens the person may open, and from three characters shall search, after a 300 ms pause in typing, calls (UCN, call number, party, serial, product), pending call requests (REQID, party, serial, product), spare requests (UID, OR number, UCN, party, serial, and the part on any line), spare consumption (UCN, call number, part), parties (name, key, city), machines (product, serial, party), active parts (code, description), active documents (title, number, product, tags, file name), knowledge-base articles (title, product, tags, category) and field failure reports (FFR number, UCN, customer, serial, product), warranty entries (SA number, party, invoice number, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry) and contract entries (MC number, party, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry), up to five of each; a warranty or contract hit shall open its register's Entries tab searched to the entry's own number (v0.10.104). FRS-218.2 Each register shall be read as the signed-in person, so row-level security bounds the results; a register shall be searched only where the person may open its screen, and each hit shall be offered only where they may open the screen it leads to (Field Solutions, open to everyone, excepted). FRS-218.3 Each register shall be shown as its own read returns; a register whose read fails shall be named as not searched rather than read as empty. FRS-218.4 Choosing a hit shall open that record: a call in its register’s read-only view (fetched by UCN when not loaded); a pending request in Pending Registrations; a spare request in its detail (fetched by UID when not loaded); a consumption line in a read-only detail; a party in its editor for a holder of masters.edit.records and in a read-only view otherwise; a machine in Machine History; a part in Part Search; a document by its Drive link; an article in Field Solutions (fetched by id when older than those listed); an FFR in its report. FRS-218.5 ↑ ↓ shall move through the hits and Enter shall open the highlighted one; the search term shall be stripped of the characters that delimit a PostgREST filter. ### URS-053 — A service record identifies the individual device

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every service call shall identify the single machine it concerns by its serial number, from the request onward. A record that names a product but not a unit cannot be traced to the device serviced, and its cover, warranty and contract cannot be established.

| **FRS-119** — Machine History | High | OQ-107 |

| **FRS-061** — The serial is mandatory | High | OQ-47 |

**FRS-119.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-119.1 The product shall be chosen first and the serial list shall follow it; a new product shall clear the serial; a serial the list does not hold may be typed. FRS-119.2 Arriving from a link with a product and a serial, the serial shall be applied only if it is on that product’s list, and then looked up at once; otherwise the screen shall say so. FRS-119.3 Every register’s rows shall be filtered to the same model AND serial, never the serial alone. FRS-119.4 Where it is now shall show the holder, status, city and state, engineer, warranty number, end and state, and contract type, number, end and state, from products and machine_cover. FRS-119.5 Where the Product Database names a different party from the cover and the calls, the screen shall warn that a transfer is missing; where the machine is not on the Product Database it shall say so. FRS-119.6 The timeline shall draw on the Product Database, Call, Visit, Spare, Field Failure, Feedback, Sale/warranty, Contract, Ownership, Additional entry and Workshop registers, each row naming its register, newest first and undated rows last, with chips (and counts) filtering it by register. FRS-119.7 A voided spare shall read VOIDED, a cancelled call CANCELLED, and a migrated FFR or uploaded feedback shall be labelled so. FRS-119.8 A register whose read fails shall be named on the screen as not read, and no count shall be presented as exact while one has failed (D-019). FRS-119.9 Each register shall be read whole for the machine; where a read is capped and the cap is reached, that register’s count shall carry a “+” and the screen shall name it (D-019). FRS-119.10 The CSV export shall be available only to holders of export.data (FRS-018). FRS-119.11 Every lookup shall be written to the audit trail (machine.history). FRS-119.12 UCNs shall be coloured by call state, and the screen shall say when nothing anywhere mentions the machine, when not connected, and when the product list could not be read.

**FRS-124.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-124.1 Correcting a Pending request shall offer the product and serial through the same machine search as the request form (CR-006), and the party shall be read off the machine chosen (CR-005) except on an installation request (CR-017). FRS-124.2 The Standard Complaint shall be chosen from the product's complaint master with no free text (CR-015, FRS-053). FRS-124.3 The call type shall be chosen from the call-type master. FRS-124.4 The submitted-by address (`email`) and the REQID shall not be correctable, the raiser being the database's to record (CR-028). FRS-124.5 The planned date shall be entered through a date control and stored as a date or as NULL. FRS-124.6 A correction the database applied to no row shall be reported as “Nothing was saved”, naming who may make it, never as saved. FRS-124.7 A correction shall change only the columns listed in FRS-087.1. RATIONALE: every field of the correction editor is a plain text box today, so a Standard Complaint no analysis will match, a serial on no register and a party the machine does not name can each be written through it, and `email` is correctable although `cr_read` grants visibility on it — a raiser can hand the request out of their own sight or into somebody else's (D-030). .6 is met today and is kept because RLS refuses an UPDATE with zero rows, not an error.

**FRS-142.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-142.1 PM Bulk Upload shall refuse any user who does not hold pm.bulk_upload (an administrator holds it; 0302 made it a grantable key), and each call it creates shall still pass the PM register’s own insert policy. FRS-142.2 A CSV template may be downloaded. FRS-142.3 Headings shall be matched by alias; a row with none of party, product and serial shall be dropped as blank and counted. FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.6 Item status shall be normalised through `coverCode()` to WGP, OGP, CMC or AMC, an unrecognised value kept as written. FRS-142.7 The due month shall default to this month, earlier months being loadable; every call shall be dated the 1st of it (`reg_date`) and today recorded as `added_on` (FRS-032). FRS-142.8 The first registration time and the gap between calls shall be prefilled from the latest PM call of that month and editable. FRS-142.9 Unrecognised columns shall be kept on the call in `extra`. FRS-142.10 The first eight calls and the count shall be previewed before import. FRS-142.11 A PM call shall be keyed on product, serial and due month, so that loading the same file again updates the calls it names rather than creating them again. FRS-142.12 Calls shall be written in batches with progress, the database assigning UCN and Call Number; a stop shall state how many were created. FRS-142.13 The loaded file may be cleared. RATIONALE: `pmImport.ts` keeps any row with a party OR a product, so a PM call with no serial is created (URS-053), and the writer is insert-only with “no key to re-run against”, so a file loaded twice is every call twice (URS-062) (D-038).

**FRS-061.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The serial number is a required field on the call request and on the Field, Installation, PM and pending-registration call forms. The request refuses an item without one, and names the cause where the machine is absent from Product Database rather than inviting the field to be skipped. The request identifier is composed REQID-Product-Serial, so a missing serial is visible in the key itself.

**FRS-037.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A dedicated screen answers the question from either end. By product: the product list is the distinct set of item names in the PRODUCT REGISTER (view `product_register_names`, security_invoker) with the machine count beside each, and choosing one narrows Serial Number to that product's serials — an equality match on `products.item_name`, served by the btree index of 0052, so a product name is never a prefix of another. By party: the drop-down is searched on the server over the customers named on the Product Register (`products.party_name`) — the customers who hold a machine — and the box beside it takes any part of a name; the party's details are then read from the Party Master, preferring the party whose name matches exactly. Both land on one answer — the party, its recorded details, and every machine held against it. Export is deliberately absent from this screen.

FRS-122.2 The register's count shall carry a “+” whenever more rows may exist than are loaded, whether or not a filter is applied. FRS-122.3 Each status chip (All, Pending, Registered, Mapped, Cancelled) shall show its count over the rows loaded and shall carry a “+” on the same condition as .2. FRS-122.7 The register shall export the rows shown after search and status filter, through the export gate (FRS-138), warning when rows are still unloaded. FRS-122.9 The register and the request's detail shall show the Installation Report and KYC documents as links that open the stored file in a new tab ("📎 Open", numbered where a field holds several); a value that is not a link shall be shown as written. RATIONALE: .3 because “Waiting on KYC” opens this register filtered to Pending, and a chip reading 312 over a partial load is read as the number pending; the “+” is already on the title for exactly that reason and is missing from the chips (D-040).

**FRS-159.** *(v0.10.150 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-159.1 Hand Stock shall show one line per engineer and part with Opening, From history, Stock out, Consumed, Transfer in, Transfer out, Returned, Stock level and Last movement, read from `handstock_balance` (security_invoker). FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. FRS-159.12 A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's name on spare requests, dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, MRNs and transfers, so the balance is one balance under the new name (0259–0262). FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-160.** *(v0.10.116 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-160.1 Hand Stock Report shall be an administrator's screen by default and grantable to any role (`admin: true`). FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. RATIONALE: .2 because a .csv can carry no second sheet, so a searched file is otherwise indistinguishable from the whole register — the silent partial file URS-077 exists to prevent (D-047).

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. # Quality & Analytics

## Daily Complaint Review Register (R/SER/35) `/daily-review`

Opened by `mod:/daily-review`.

### URS-080 — Review 2 is answered No automatically only while an authorised person has switched Auto Review on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall carry an AUTO REVIEW switch for Review 2. Only a person holding the permission review.auto — by role, Admin, NSM and Technical Support, or given it individually by an administrator — shall be able to turn it on or off, and the register shall show whether it is on, who set it and when. While it is on, each morning every field call logged before that day which failed outside its first year and whose Review 2 is still blank shall be answered NO on all three Review 2 questions. Each such answer shall record, as the Review 2 reviewer, the name of the person who switched Auto Review on, and shall also keep a marker that it was answered by the auto review, so that Review 3 can tell an automatic NO from one a reviewer gave and change it where it is wrong. A call that failed inside its first year, or whose age at failure is not known, shall never be answered automatically, and no Review 2 a person has begun or completed shall be altered. A standing rule that answers a quality question is itself a judgement, so it belongs to the person who authorised it rather than to the system; and a failure in the first year is exactly the case the warranty question exists for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-268** — A PM call whose consumption is a Spare joins the DCCR review | High | OQ-266 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-268.** *(v0.10.133 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-268.1 A consumption line of quantity above 0 on a PM call whose part (the code before "|") is categorised Spare in the Part Master shall open the call's DCCR review with Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration set to SPARE; an existing review shall not be changed. FRS-268.2 The Daily Complaint Review Register and its counts shall list every Field call and every PM call that has a DCCR review, each reader seeing only the calls the call policies give them. FRS-268.3 The 2026 PM calls already carrying a Spare shall be added once (0397); a part the Part Master does not yet categorise Spare adds nothing, and the addition shall be re-runnable once the mapping is complete. FRS-268.4 DCCR rows whose UC Number is an Excel date serial (five digits) or "-" and that match no call shall be removed (0398). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-06: "if a Consumption indicates a Spare then it should be added to DCCR Review ... use the Current Data and Lets review it again and add old calls once the mapping is complete".

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-099.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-099.1 The review drawer shall list the Field Failure Reports already raised on the call, as Already reported, above the Raise FFR action. FRS-099.2 Raise FFR (on the review) and ＋ Raise FFR (on the register) shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage, and the database (ffr_write) shall refuse an insert from anybody else. FRS-099.3 Raise FFR on the review shall open the Field Failure Register form filled from the review and the call. FRS-099.4 The form so filled shall warn where the call is not yet solved. FRS-099.5 ＋ Raise FFR on the register shall open a blank form. FRS-099.6 A report raised by hand shall be numbered, stamped and validated exactly as FRS-109 states for every report. FRS-099.7 A report raised by hand shall also start with CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status blank, the table defaults included.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

### URS-083 — Answering many calls at once, or saving as one chooses, never answers a question nobody looked at

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A reviewer authorised to complete the review shall be able to answer Review 2 = NO for many calls in one confirmed action. Calls that failed inside their first year, calls whose age at failure is unknown and calls whose Review 2 is already answered shall never be included, and the database shall refuse them whatever the screen sends; the action shall be recorded with who took it and how many calls it answered. A reviewer shall also be able to have answers saved as they are chosen (auto save), as a personal choice with an organisation default, provided that every saved answer is attributed to the person whose session saved it and that no keystroke commits a value on its own. Both are conveniences on a quality record, so each must leave the record exactly as a careful reviewer answering one call at a time would have left it.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-101** — Review 2 = NO for many calls at once | High | OQ-89 |
| **FRS-102** — Auto save on the review | High | OQ-90 |

FRS-101.2 The screen shall make eligible only calls whose Review 2 is unanswered and whose age at failure is known and 366 days or more. FRS-101.3 The screen shall ask for confirmation in a dialogue stating how many calls will be answered before writing any. FRS-102.2 While Auto save is on, each answer shall be written after a short delay without the reviewer pressing Save. FRS-102.3 An auto-saved write shall not send a completed-by name; the database shall record as reviewer the person whose session wrote the completing answer (FRS-069). FRS-102.4 Each save shall be acknowledged (saved N ago), and a save that fails shall be shown as failed. FRS-102.5 Auto save shall be available only to holders of review.edit. FRS-102.6 The organisation default shall be changeable only by a holder of config.manage, and each change shall be recorded in the audit trail. FRS-102.7 No picking control on an auto-saving review shall commit a value on a keystroke (FRS-052).

### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. ### URS-085 — A failure is counted against the product that failed, without rewriting the call

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

In Review 3 the reviewer shall code the failure — complaint grouping, root cause key word, and whether the remedy was a spare, a consumable, a correction or a calibration — choosing from lists kept per product, and shall be able to record that what failed was an accessory or another product line rather than the machine the call names. Every analysis of failures shall then count the failure against the product the review records, while the call itself stays as it was registered. The review shall carry the service department’s observation and the action taken, the action reading FFR Generation until the report number is recorded. A failure counted against the wrong product line misstates the failure rate of two products at once, and rewriting the call to fix it would falsify what the customer reported.

### URS-158 — A fault repeating across the fleet is caught by the review

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The rule shall be switchable, and its window and threshold maintainable by an administrator without a code change; answers already recorded shall be left as they were. A batch, a component or a design fault reaches the review as a first failure on each machine it touches, so a rule about one machine can never see it.

FRS-205.2 frequent_failure(ucn) shall count distinct serials, so repeated calls on one serial do not fire the fleet rule. FRS-205.3 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a call a frequent failure where either rule fires, and shall name which rule fired. Thirty days and a month differ in February, which is why it is days. Proved by supabase/tests/frequent_failure_rule2_test.sql.

### URS-058 — A judgement on a quality record names the person who made it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where the system records a judgement about a product failure, it shall record WHO made that judgement. Where a person answers, the identity shall be taken from the authenticated session at the moment the judgement is completed and not from a value supplied by the caller. Where the answer is given by a standing rule that an authorised person has switched on, the judgement shall be attributed to the person who switched the rule on, and the record shall also state that the rule gave it. Where a judgement made before this system is loaded from a historical file, the reviewer and the date the file records shall be kept, and the person loading it shall not be recorded as its maker. The identity shall not be displaced by later editing of the same record, and where the judgement is carried onto a further record the person shall be carried with it. No record shall attribute a judgement to a screen, a process or the system itself.

| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |
| **FRS-069** — The reviewer is stamped by the database at completion | High | OQ-52 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).
