FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

**FRS-069.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A BEFORE trigger on `call_reviews` (0173) records `review2_by_uid` / `review3_by_uid` from auth.uid() at the moment a review stage becomes COMPLETE, and fills the display name from User Master where the client sent none — so the automatic-save and bulk-review paths, which send no name, record a person instead of nothing. A name the client did send is kept: it is what the reviewer saw on screen. A later edit does NOT re-stamp: the person who answered the review is the reviewer, not whoever last corrected a spelling. TWO PATHS ARE NOT A PERSON AT THE KEYBOARD AND ARE NOT STAMPED FROM THE SESSION: an answer given by the Review 2 auto review records the person who switched Auto Review on, with the auto-review marker (FRS-097.5), and never the session that ran or opened anything; a review loaded from a historical file keeps the reviewer names and dates the file carries, is marked imported, and has no identity of the person loading it stamped on it (FRS-100.4). The trigger evaluates the completion test from the source columns rather than reading `review2_done`, because PostgreSQL computes a GENERATED column AFTER the BEFORE triggers have run — the first version read it, stamped nothing on every path, and was caught only by exercising it against a database. The duplicated expression is compared word-for-word with its original by an automated check. raise_ffr() carries the name onto the Field Failure Report, preferring Review 3's reviewer, and no longer writes the string "Daily Call Review" — a screen is not a person, and a report that cannot name one is left blank, blank being a question somebody asks.

FRS-105.5 Product Failure Analysis and every other analysis read from field_call_review shall count a failure under the product the review records where one is recorded (live_product_name), and under the call’s product otherwise. FRS-105.6 Change product? shall be available only to holders of review.edit and shall be written and attributed like any other review answer. FRS-105.7 Service Dept Observation shall be free text. FRS-105.8 Action Taken shall read FFR Generation while Any Potential Effect is YES and no report number is recorded, and a report number once recorded shall be kept.

Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

**FRS-042.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Four database views (0101) compute the analysis: `spare_usage` joins each consumed part to its call for the cover and to the engineer’s User Master row for the region; `spare_usage_rollup` groups it by cover, region and product; `failure_rate_by_product` divides calls in the last 365 days by the machines of that product in the Product Register, giving calls per 100 machines; `failure_modes_by_product` groups calls by standard complaint. All four are security_invoker, so the figures a person reads are computed from exactly the records they may read. The install-base denominator is NOT scoped — it is a property of the fleet — so a user without full call visibility sees their own share of a whole-fleet denominator, and the screen states this rather than leaving it to be inferred. A product with no machines on record shows no rate at all instead of a rate divided by a guess.

## Field Failure Register `/failure-report`

### URS-080 — Review 2 is answered No automatically only while an authorised person has switched Auto Review on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall carry an AUTO REVIEW switch for Review 2. Only a person holding the permission review.auto — by role, Admin, NSM and Technical Support, or given it individually by an administrator — shall be able to turn it on or off, and the register shall show whether it is on, who set it and when. While it is on, each morning every field call logged before that day which failed outside its first year and whose Review 2 is still blank shall be answered NO on all three Review 2 questions. Each such answer shall record, as the Review 2 reviewer, the name of the person who switched Auto Review on, and shall also keep a marker that it was answered by the auto review, so that Review 3 can tell an automatic NO from one a reviewer gave and change it where it is wrong. A call that failed inside its first year, or whose age at failure is not known, shall never be answered automatically, and no Review 2 a person has begun or completed shall be altered. A standing rule that answers a quality question is itself a judgement, so it belongs to the person who authorised it rather than to the system; and a failure in the first year is exactly the case the warranty question exists for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-268** — A PM call whose consumption is a Spare joins the DCCR review | High | OQ-266 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-268.** *(v0.10.133 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-268.1 A consumption line of quantity above 0 on a PM call whose part (the code before "|") is categorised Spare in the Part Master shall open the call's DCCR review with Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration set to SPARE; an existing review shall not be changed. FRS-268.2 The Daily Complaint Review Register and its counts shall list every Field call and every PM call that has a DCCR review, each reader seeing only the calls the call policies give them. FRS-268.3 The 2026 PM calls already carrying a Spare shall be added once (0397); a part the Part Master does not yet categorise Spare adds nothing, and the addition shall be re-runnable once the mapping is complete. FRS-268.4 DCCR rows whose UC Number is an Excel date serial (five digits) or "-" and that match no call shall be removed (0398). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-06: "if a Consumption indicates a Spare then it should be added to DCCR Review ... use the Current Data and Lets review it again and add old calls once the mapping is complete".

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |

FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

### URS-088 — A Field Failure Report is raised, numbered, completed and reviewed weekly under control, and is never deleted

FRS-232.9 (2026-10-04) A Field Return shall be received as a Troubleshooting job, the activity fixed and not chosen; a Troubleshooting job shall not be dispatched or closed before its quality check, as a Repair (0370). The Identification tag of the unit and of each accessory shall be chosen as Yes, Identified or Not Identified, a value typed before being kept; an accessory received shall record its item, quantity and tag, without a serial. FRS-232.10 The cleaning work instruction's revision shall be a number of two digits, 01 when none is given. FRS-232.11 (2026-10-04, 0372) A job with a call shall carry, at the top of its Repair page, a Call Status (the visit form's three) and a Call Pending Reason by the visit form's rules — required while Unsolved, Report Pending for a pending report, none for a completed one — and they shall be the visit's values, the visit filing with them; an Unsolved job with no reason shall not have its Indoor DC approved. The job's status shall be derived from them once cleaned: Solved → Ready (a Repair, Rework or Troubleshooting first needing its QC Pass, until then QC); Unsolved with spares not available → Awaiting spares; otherwise Under repair; never once Dispatched, Closed or Condemned. A DEMO / new device shall keep its Status chosen by hand. FRS-232.12 Create Indoor DC shall not ask for the MIRN No. / Customer Ref No., its date, or the mode of despatch; the printed Indoor DC shall carry no SERVICE CENTER line and three signature boxes: ISSUED BY, AUTHORISED BY and RECEIVED BY (WITH DATE). FRS-232.13 While the Create Indoor DC form is open beside a job, the job's DC page shall show a read-only summary of the unit — customer, product and serial, call and its Call Status, job status, report number, and accessories still to go back — and no fields to fill. FRS-232.14 (0374) The intake shall offer three ways in — Field Return, Demo and New Device — each fixing the job's kind and activity: Customer property / Troubleshooting, DEMO unit / Demo, New device / Troubleshooting. A New device shall be its own kind, consigned like a DEMO unit to the party it is going to, and shall have its own sheet (New Devices) on the R/SER/07 register.

### URS-058 — A judgement on a quality record names the person who made it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where the system records a judgement about a product failure, it shall record WHO made that judgement. Where a person answers, the identity shall be taken from the authenticated session at the moment the judgement is completed and not from a value supplied by the caller. Where the answer is given by a standing rule that an authorised person has switched on, the judgement shall be attributed to the person who switched the rule on, and the record shall also state that the rule gave it. Where a judgement made before this system is loaded from a historical file, the reviewer and the date the file records shall be kept, and the person loading it shall not be recorded as its maker. The identity shall not be displaced by later editing of the same record, and where the judgement is carried onto a further record the person shall be carried with it. No record shall attribute a judgement to a screen, a process or the system itself.

| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |
| **FRS-069** — The reviewer is stamped by the database at completion | High | OQ-52 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

**FRS-069.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A BEFORE trigger on `call_reviews` (0173) records `review2_by_uid` / `review3_by_uid` from auth.uid() at the moment a review stage becomes COMPLETE, and fills the display name from User Master where the client sent none — so the automatic-save and bulk-review paths, which send no name, record a person instead of nothing. A name the client did send is kept: it is what the reviewer saw on screen. A later edit does NOT re-stamp: the person who answered the review is the reviewer, not whoever last corrected a spelling. TWO PATHS ARE NOT A PERSON AT THE KEYBOARD AND ARE NOT STAMPED FROM THE SESSION: an answer given by the Review 2 auto review records the person who switched Auto Review on, with the auto-review marker (FRS-097.5), and never the session that ran or opened anything; a review loaded from a historical file keeps the reviewer names and dates the file carries, is marked imported, and has no identity of the person loading it stamped on it (FRS-100.4). The trigger evaluates the completion test from the source columns rather than reading `review2_done`, because PostgreSQL computes a GENERATED column AFTER the BEFORE triggers have run — the first version read it, stamped nothing on every path, and was caught only by exercising it against a database. The duplicated expression is compared word-for-word with its original by an automated check. raise_ffr() carries the name onto the Field Failure Report, preferring Review 3's reviewer, and no longer writes the string "Daily Call Review" — a screen is not a person, and a report that cannot name one is left blank, blank being a question somebody asks.

### URS-059 — Every change to a field failure report is recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each amendment to a field failure report shall be recorded with what changed — the previous and the new value of each field — together with who changed it and when. The record of amendments shall be produced by the system itself rather than by the application requesting it, shall not be alterable or removable through the application, and shall begin at the creation of the report.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-070** — The report’s amendments are recorded by the database | High | OQ-53 |

**FRS-070.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `ffr_history` (0174) receives one row per UPDATE of a field failure report, written by an AFTER trigger, holding `{column: {from, to}}` for only the columns that actually differ, with the person from auth.uid() and their User Master name. An update that changes nothing writes nothing, and `updated_at` is never an entry on its own — a log whose every line says the timestamp moved buries the one that says the CAPA was closed. It is written IN THE DATABASE rather than by the application because the application’s own audit trail is client-written (FRS-021) and therefore records only what a screen chose to report, seeing nothing of an amendment made directly through the API. The table has no insert, update or delete policy, so it cannot be forged, edited or tidied through the application, and 0166’s deletion guard is armed on it; reading it requires `ffr.manage` or administrator. Reports raised before it existed are given their creation entry, so every report’s history begins somewhere.

## KPI & Failure Analysis `/kpi`

Opened by `mod:/kpi`.

### URS-085 — A failure is counted against the product that failed, without rewriting the call

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

In Review 3 the reviewer shall code the failure — complaint grouping, root cause key word, and whether the remedy was a spare, a consumable, a correction or a calibration — choosing from lists kept per product, and shall be able to record that what failed was an accessory or another product line rather than the machine the call names. Every analysis of failures shall then count the failure against the product the review records, while the call itself stays as it was registered. The review shall carry the service department’s observation and the action taken, the action reading FFR Generation until the report number is recorded. A failure counted against the wrong product line misstates the failure rate of two products at once, and rewriting the call to fix it would falsify what the customer reported.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-105** — Review 3 coding, and the product the failure is counted against | High | OQ-93 |

FRS-105.2 A value already recorded that is no longer on the list shall be kept and shown, not cleared. FRS-105.3 Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration shall be chosen from a pick list. FRS-105.4 Change product? shall record, on the review, the product line that actually failed, and shall not alter the product or serial of the call. FRS-105.5 Product Failure Analysis and every other analysis read from field_call_review shall count a failure under the product the review records where one is recorded (live_product_name), and under the call’s product otherwise. FRS-105.6 Change product? shall be available only to holders of review.edit and shall be written and attributed like any other review answer. FRS-105.7 Service Dept Observation shall be free text. FRS-105.8 Action Taken shall read FFR Generation while Any Potential Effect is YES and no report number is recorded, and a report number once recorded shall be kept.

### URS-045 — Controlled vocabulary is chosen, not typed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a field must match a controlled list — a Standard Complaint above all — the value shall be CHOSEN from that list and shall not be typed freehand, and no keystroke shall commit a value on its own. Counting, filtering, repeat-failure detection and every downstream report match on the stored value, so a hand-entered variant is a record that no analysis will ever find. Where a list is empty the field shall say so rather than accept arbitrary text.

### URS-098 — Quality objectives and their monthly figures are held under control

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall hold each year’s quality objectives with their process, parameter, target, frequency and responsible person, and one figure per month, a month not measured being recorded as not measured and never as nought. A figure the system can compute shall be computed from the service record up to a cut-off date set for that month, with evidence behind it stating its numerator, denominator and assumptions. Typing a figure, re-calculating, changing a cut-off, and adding or altering an objective shall each be restricted to the persons authorised to maintain the objectives, and shall each be recorded with who did it, when and what the value was before. The cut-off dates shall be lockable by an administrator. An objective that carries a recorded figure shall not be deleted. The objectives are reviewed by management on these figures, so a figure nobody can trace to a person or to the record is not evidence of anything.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-121** — Quality objectives: figures, cut-offs, definitions and evidence | High | OQ-264, OQ-109 |
| **FRS-251** — A figure typed over a calculated objective month is a manual override, and Re-calculate asks before touching it | High | OQ-246 |
| **FRS-254** — SLA / Objective Configuration, and the failure-within-months rule | High | OQ-250 |

**FRS-121.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-121.1 The table shall list the current year’s objectives with number, process, parameter, target, frequency, the twelve months and the total, colour a cell good or bad against a <x% or >x% target, mark a computed row ƒ, and explain that a quarterly objective is cumulative in March, June, September and December and not applicable in other months. FRS-121.2 A month shall be typed only by a holder of config.manage (qo_write); a blank shall be stored as not measured (NULL), a % sign shall be accepted, and anything that is not a number refused. FRS-121.3 Re-calculate shall ask for confirmation, write only the computed rows up to the current month, replace a figure typed over a computed one, and report what it wrote. FRS-121.4 Each month shall have its own cut-off date, set in the Re-calculate dialogue and saved as it is set; while the cut-offs are locked only a holder of objective.lock may change one (set_objective_cutoff), and only a holder of objective.lock may lock or unlock them (set_objective_cutoff_lock). FRS-121.5 A holder of config.manage shall be able to add an objective and edit its definition — parameter, process, targets, frequency, responsible, computed-by formula, cut-off days or a fixed cut-off date (never both), and parameters as validated JSON. FRS-121.6 Every typed figure, re-calculation, cut-off change, lock change, addition and edit shall be recorded by the database with the person, the time, and the previous and new value (D-021). FRS-121.7 The database shall refuse to delete an objective that carries any recorded figure (D-021). FRS-121.8 The evidence for a computed month shall download as a workbook of the calls or reports counted, the installed base with the filter used, and a calculation sheet (numerator ÷ denominator, calls solved after the cut-off, stored against computed with whether they agree, assumptions and hard stops), gated by export.data (FRS-112) and per objective by objective_evidence(); a refusal shall read as withheld, a quarterly off-month as not applicable, and a month with nothing behind it as such. FRS-121.9 The explanation shall describe how the computed columns are worked out, and shall not state that every figure is typed. FRS-121.10 The screen shall show the scope in force, say when not connected, and say when no objectives exist for the year and which bundle provides them. FRS-121.11 Each objective shall carry a Status — Active, Not Working or Do Not Use, chosen on its definition; an objective that is not Active shall be hidden from the table and the monthly / quarterly lists unless Show hidden is on, and shall otherwise be edited and re-calculated as before (0392). FRS-121.12 A Failure Rate (DCCR) tab shall show, for each objective worked out by dccr_failure_cohort, one row per month of commissioning with its Parc (machines of the product whose Warranty Start falls in that month) and the number of failures before 3, 6, 12, 24, 36 and 60 months with their rates; a failure shall be a Field call whose DCCR Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration contains SPARE or whose Any Potential Effect is YES, cancelled calls and calls with no serial excluded, counted per call; a month younger than the window shall be blank and a month with no Parc shall have no rate. The objective's figure for a month shall be the average of the 3-month rates of the 12 commissioning months ending in it, blanks left out, as at that month's end and never later than today; the tab and the evidence download shall give the table, the failing calls and the months averaged (0393). FRS-121.13 Re-calculate shall compute only objectives whose Status is Active; a Not Working or Do Not Use objective shall keep its figures (0396). RATIONALE: .7 because an objective reviewed by management is a quality record (0049’s rule): one no longer pursued is retired, not deleted with its twelve figures.

**FRS-251.** *(v0.10.80 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-251.1 Typing a figure into a month of a computed objective shall mark that month as a manual override, recording who, when and the calculated figure it replaced; the mark shall be written by the database and shall not be settable or removable through the API. FRS-251.2 The month shall show a ✎ mark, with who, when and the calculated figure on hover. FRS-251.3 Every Re-calculate that finds a manual override shall list them and ask whether to keep them (the default) or discard them. FRS-251.4 Keeping shall leave every overridden month exactly as typed, on every run; discarding shall write the calculated figure over them and remove the marks. FRS-251.5 A Re-calculate made without the choice shall keep them. FRS-251.6 An objective that is not computed is unaffected: none of its figures is an override. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-04: "I Override it manually, then it should never change.. Or prompt the user if Manually Overrides should be considered or discarded during every re-run".

**FRS-254.** *(v0.10.89 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-254.1 SLA / Objective Configuration shall be opened by mod:/sla-objective-config, listed under Administration, and given by default to the Admin role with config.manage and objective.manage, and to Technical Support with the page alone, its cards read-only until those actions are ticked (0358); every other role shall be granted it on Roles & Permissions. FRS-254.2 It shall present the SLA targets (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.2) and the Product Failure rule: the months after installation within which a field call is a failure (default 3) and the rolling period (default 12), each a whole number from 1 to 120, editable by a holder of objective.manage, and the database shall refuse the change from anyone else. FRS-254.3 objective_value() for failure_rate_12m shall return, for the period end E, the machines of the product (and serial pattern) with a serial and a warranty start in (E − rolling months, E] that have a non-cancelled field call on the same serial (trimmed, case-blind) and product pattern registered from the warranty start to the warranty start plus the window months and not after E, over all such machines; NULL when there are none. FRS-254.4 objective_evidence() shall return one failure row per failed machine (its first call in the window, with the installation date, the days after it and the number of calls in the window), the installed machines, and a filter row stating the rule, so the workbook counts to the figure. FRS-254.5 A missing setting shall fall back to 3 and 12; a change shall be stamped with who and when from the session and recorded in the audit trail with the old and new value; no figure shall change until Re-calculate. FRS-254.7 Re-calculating every computed objective of a year shall complete within the database statement time limit on a register of 20,000 machines and 40,000 calls: the failure rate shall be computed as one join of the window’s machines to the window’s calls, planned with its values on every run (0359; measured 0.7 s for six objectives over ten months, against about 47 s for 0357, which timed out on the live project). FRS-254.6 It shall also present the frequent-failure rules Review 2 applies (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.4), unchanged in behaviour and permission. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-04, and the four answers given that day: warranty start is installation; the rate is over machines installed; it replaces the earlier rule (every field call in 12 months over the whole install base); the SLA targets move to the new page. "By Default Grant Permission to Admin - All Actions, Rest let the Admin Decide through the App"; later the same day, "Grant the page to Technical Support as well, Move Frequent Failure -- the rule Review 2 applies also to this Page".

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

By default only the Admin role shall be given that page. The user, 2026-10-04: "For Product Failures, The Concept is - Failure Within 3 Months, But a Rolling Average for 12 Months".

### URS-099 — The register of requests says how much of it is on the screen

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall keep a register of every call registration request, whatever became of it, newest first, and shall let a user search it, narrow it by status and open any request to read everything recorded on it together with its supporting documents. Every count the register shows, including the count beside each status, shall say when more requests exist than have been loaded, because a filtered count over a partial load reads as a total and is acted on as one.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-122** — The Request Registration register | Medium | OQ-251, OQ-110 |

**FRS-122.** *(v0.10.98 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-122.1 Request Registration shall list every row of `call_requests` the reader's `cr_read` policy admits, newest submitted first with the row id as tiebreaker, read in pages of 1,000 and offered 2,000 at a time with Load more. FRS-122.2 The register's count shall carry a “+” whenever more rows may exist than are loaded, whether or not a filter is applied. FRS-122.3 Each status chip (All, Pending, Registered, Mapped, Cancelled) shall show its count over the rows loaded and shall carry a “+” on the same condition as .2. FRS-122.4 The search box shall match REQID, UCN, engineer, party, city, product, serial and complaint over the rows loaded. FRS-122.5 A UCN shall be coloured by its call's state in the fixed code of `src/lib/callstate.tsx`, and shall be rendered plain where the state is unknown. FRS-122.6 Opening a request shall list every field recorded on it except system columns, and its supporting documents. FRS-122.7 The register shall export the rows shown after search and status filter, through the export gate (FRS-138), warning when rows are still unloaded. FRS-122.8 Refresh shall re-read the register, and the time of the last read shall be shown and remembered on the device. FRS-122.9 The register and the request's detail shall show the Installation Report and KYC documents as links that open the stored file in a new tab ("📎 Open", numbered where a field holds several); a value that is not a link shall be shown as written. FRS-122.10 A holder of `pending.register` shall have an Unmap action on a Mapped request's details that, after a confirmation naming the UCN, clears the UCN and the actioned by / at, and returns the request to Pending and so to the Pending Registrations list; it shall not change the call it was mapped to, shall leave a request that is no longer Mapped untouched, and shall report a write that changed no row instead of reading it as done. RATIONALE: .3 because “Waiting on KYC” opens this register filtered to Pending, and a chip reading 312 over a partial load is read as the number pending; the “+” is already on the title for exactly that reason and is missing from the chips (D-040).

### URS-125 — The documents that travel with a stock out are complete and can be produced again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

For every stock out the system shall produce a Delivery Challan and a Declaration on the company's controlled layout, listing exactly what that stock out carried, and shall produce them again on request for any stock out the reader may see, however old it is. The challan shall carry the stock-out and reference numbers and dates, the recipient, the courier, each part and quantity with the total, and the company's statutory identifiers, on sheets each complete in itself; a signature shall appear on it only as URS-057 allows. The Declaration shall state the recipient's address, the parcel's approximate value and its purpose, and each part once with its total quantity, and shall name what is still missing before it is printed. Correcting the engineer's address from the Declaration may update the User Master only for somebody authorised to dispatch, and only the address. A challan that can no longer be found is a shipment whose paperwork cannot be reproduced.

### URS-126 — A spare line can be found, and its history read, from the register

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A user shall be able to find a spare line by its stage, by its engineer and by any of its identifying numbers; to see which lines await their own action; and to open a line and read the whole order it belongs to and its history — who raised it and on what day, who decided each stage, when, with what answer and note, what was sent on which challan, and who acknowledged it. The register of what Stores has issued shall show how long each issue took from its last approval, and shall reprint that issue's documents.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-145 — A controlled document's revision is never overwritten

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A QMS document entered in the system shall carry its document number, revision and effective date, and the file it refers to shall be a stored copy rather than a link that can change underneath the recorded revision. Once saved, a QMS document's number, revision, effective date and file shall not be edited in place: a new revision shall be a new entry, and the one it supersedes shall be retired, so that what was in force on any date stays readable. A document number and revision shall identify one entry only. A service manual may be edited, and shall say which product it covers or that it covers every product.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-189** — A QMS revision is a new entry, and the one it replaces is retired | High | OQ-182 |

**FRS-189.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-189.1 A QMS document shall be refused without a title, a document number, a revision, an effective date and a file or link. FRS-189.2 A document number and revision shall identify one QMS entry, by the unique `doc_key` (0265). FRS-189.3 The QMS shelf shall store an uploaded file in the document store and mark it 📄, and shall mark a pasted link 🔗 with a warning that it can change under the recorded revision. FRS-189.4 Once saved, a QMS entry's number, revision, effective date and file shall not be changed, by the screen or by the database; its title, tags and notes may be. FRS-189.5 A new revision shall be added as a new entry, and the screen shall offer to retire the entry it supersedes. FRS-189.6 Retire and Restore shall be confirmed, and a retired entry shall stay on the shelf, hidden unless “Show retired” is ticked. FRS-189.7 A document number and revision read from a file name shall be suggested only into empty fields, and the suggestion shall be stated. FRS-189.8 A service manual shall name its product, suggested from the product register with typing allowed and a blank meaning every product, and may be edited. FRS-189.9 The Updated column shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. RATIONALE: .4 because an in-place edit replaces the record of what WAS in force with what IS, which is the destruction URS-030 forbids. Today the ✏️ drawer overwrites all four, only the number is required, and the guidance to publish a new entry is advice nothing enforces (D-061); .9 is open (D-064).

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-218.** *(v0.10.104 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-218.1 The header search shall list matching screens the person may open, and from three characters shall search, after a 300 ms pause in typing, calls (UCN, call number, party, serial, product), pending call requests (REQID, party, serial, product), spare requests (UID, OR number, UCN, party, serial, and the part on any line), spare consumption (UCN, call number, part), parties (name, key, city), machines (product, serial, party), active parts (code, description), active documents (title, number, product, tags, file name), knowledge-base articles (title, product, tags, category) and field failure reports (FFR number, UCN, customer, serial, product), warranty entries (SA number, party, invoice number, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry) and contract entries (MC number, party, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry), up to five of each; a warranty or contract hit shall open its register's Entries tab searched to the entry's own number (v0.10.104). FRS-218.2 Each register shall be read as the signed-in person, so row-level security bounds the results; a register shall be searched only where the person may open its screen, and each hit shall be offered only where they may open the screen it leads to (Field Solutions, open to everyone, excepted). FRS-218.3 Each register shall be shown as its own read returns; a register whose read fails shall be named as not searched rather than read as empty. FRS-218.4 Choosing a hit shall open that record: a call in its register’s read-only view (fetched by UCN when not loaded); a pending request in Pending Registrations; a spare request in its detail (fetched by UID when not loaded); a consumption line in a read-only detail; a party in its editor for a holder of masters.edit.records and in a read-only view otherwise; a machine in Machine History; a part in Part Search; a document by its Drive link; an article in Field Solutions (fetched by id when older than those listed); an FFR in its report. FRS-218.5 ↑ ↓ shall move through the hits and Enter shall open the highlighted one; the search term shall be stripped of the characters that delimit a PostgREST filter. FRS-218.6 Where a register holds more matches than the five shown, its group shall say so rather than read as complete (D-117).

### URS-057 — A person’s signature is applied by that person alone

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A user shall be able to record their own handwritten signature and have it reproduced on the documents that name them as signatory. The recorded signature shall be readable and writable only by the person it belongs to — by no manager, and by no administrator — and shall be reproduced on a document only where the signature block names the person producing it; in every other case the block shall be produced blank for signature by hand. Removal of a signature belonging to a person who has left shall be an authorised act which does not disclose the signature.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-154** — The Delivery Challan | High | OQ-146 |
| **FRS-066** — A signature is held for its owner only | High | OQ-51 |
| **FRS-067** — A document signs only the block that names the printer | High | OQ-51 |
| **FRS-068** — Administration of a signature discloses nothing | Medium | OQ-51 |

**FRS-154.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-154.1 The Delivery Challan shall be opened by stock-out number from Stock Out, from Pending Dispatch and after booking; the page sits outside the module guard and shows a stock out only where the reader's row-level access admits it. FRS-154.2 The Delivery Challan shall find any stock out the reader may see, however many have been booked since it. FRS-154.3 The Delivery Challan shall print the quantity sent on THIS stock out for each line (`spare_dispatch_lines`), ordered by spare ID. FRS-154.4 Each sheet shall carry the company mark (`COMPANY_LOGO`), the company's name, address, telephone and e-mail, and the title DELIVERY CHALLAN. FRS-154.5 Each sheet shall carry the recipient engineer, the courier, the Stock Out No., the Stock Out Date, the Ref No. and the Ref Date. FRS-154.6 The grid shall carry Sr.No, Order No., Item Code, Description and Qty; the last sheet shall carry the total and every other sheet "Continued on sheet N". FRS-154.7 The challan shall be cut into A4 sheets of 20 rows, each with its own letterhead and signature block and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-154.8 The challan shall carry the dispatch remarks and the company's GSTIN, CIN and PAN. FRS-154.9 The company signature block shall carry the printer's saved signature only where the printer booked the stock out, and the customer block shall always be blank (FRS-067). FRS-154.10 The page shall offer Print, Declaration and Back to dispatch, and state the number of sheets. FRS-154.11 The page shall state, in place of the challan, that the database is not connected, that the stock out was not found or cannot be viewed, or the read error verbatim. RATIONALE: .1 is deliberate — the engineer receiving the parcel and Commercial chasing it are legitimate readers who hold neither dispatch module — and is for RA/QA to confirm. .2 is the requirement the page does not meet: it searches the 500 most recent stock outs, so an older one reads as "not found" (D-045).

**FRS-066.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A user records a signature on My Profile, drawn with a finger, stylus or mouse or uploaded as a picture of one on paper; it is stored as a transparent PNG cropped to the ink (0172_user_signatures.sql). It is held in its own table rather than on the profile, because Row-Level Security grants by ROW: a policy permitting a person to save a signature on their profile row would permit them to rewrite the role and permissions on it. The read and update policies test `user_id = auth.uid()` and NOTHING ELSE — no is_admin(), no users.manage — so no second party can obtain the image, and none can set one. The owning user id is stamped from the session by trigger, so a row naming another user is stored under the inserter.

**FRS-067.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* signatureBelongsTo() compares the name printed in the block with the identity of the signed-in user, on an EXACT match of name or e-mail ignoring case and surrounding space; a looser comparison would put one person’s signature on another’s document where names share a part. The Word copy of the Field Failure Report reproduces the CONTROLLED FORM itself — R-SER-03 Rev 02’s header band, two-column grid at the template’s own 6435/4500 split, every label with its exact wording and internal spacing, its A4 page setup and its footer carrying `TMPL No: R/SER/03 Rev: MAR 2020` — and a printable HTML page renders the SAME form from the same definition (src/lib/ffrform.ts), so a second transcription cannot drift from the first. The Delivery Challan reproduces the saved signature in the company block only when the person printing booked the stock out, and never in the customer’s block, which exists to be signed on receipt; the Field Failure Report (R-SER-03) embeds it only when the person generating the document is the raiser named on it. Where a signature is absent or unreadable the document is produced with an empty block, never with a broken image or a failure to produce it.

**FRS-068.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* user_signature_status() reports, per user, WHETHER a signature has been saved and when — never the image. remove_user_signature() deletes one belonging to another person and is refused to a non-administrator and for the caller’s own row (which the Profile page removes). Both are SECURITY DEFINER functions, not views: a definer view over Row-Level-Security-protected tables reads as its owner and defeats the policies beneath it, which this system shipped three times, and the automated check that now refuses such a view is not weakened to admit these. A plain DELETE policy admitting an administrator was written first and does not work: PostgreSQL applies the SELECT policy to a DELETE that must locate its row, so an administrator unable to read the row reported a successful statement affecting nothing.

### URS-030 — Controlled QMS documents

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Quality-system documents (SOPs, work instructions, forms) shall be held with their document number, revision and effective date, be readable by every user, and be maintainable only by the role responsible for the quality system. A superseded document shall be withdrawn from use without being destroyed.
