| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-189** — A QMS revision is a new entry, and the one it replaces is retired | High | OQ-182 |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-036** — QMS document control | High | OQ-21 |

**FRS-189.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-189.1 A QMS document shall be refused without a title, a document number, a revision, an effective date and a file or link. FRS-189.2 A document number and revision shall identify one QMS entry, by the unique `doc_key` (0265). FRS-189.3 The QMS shelf shall store an uploaded file in the document store and mark it 📄, and shall mark a pasted link 🔗 with a warning that it can change under the recorded revision. FRS-189.4 Once saved, a QMS entry's number, revision, effective date and file shall not be changed, by the screen or by the database; its title, tags and notes may be. FRS-189.5 A new revision shall be added as a new entry, and the screen shall offer to retire the entry it supersedes. FRS-189.6 Retire and Restore shall be confirmed, and a retired entry shall stay on the shelf, hidden unless “Show retired” is ticked. FRS-189.7 A document number and revision read from a file name shall be suggested only into empty fields, and the suggestion shall be stated. FRS-189.8 A service manual shall name its product, suggested from the product register with typing allowed and a blank meaning every product, and may be edited. FRS-189.9 The Updated column shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. RATIONALE: .4 because an in-place edit replaces the record of what WAS in force with what IS, which is the destruction URS-030 forbids. Today the ✏️ drawer overwrites all four, only the number is required, and the guidance to publish a new entry is advice nothing enforces (D-061); .9 is open (D-064).

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-036.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* QMS documents are held in the same catalogue under kind = qms with document number, revision and effective date, readable by every signed-in user and maintainable only under `qms.manage` — a right distinct from the one governing service manuals, and enforced in the database so a holder of either cannot move a document onto the other shelf. A document number and revision identify one QMS entry (0265). Withdrawal is by RETIRING the row (active = false): it stops being offered while the record of what was in force is retained; a saved revision's number, revision, effective date and file are not edited in place (FRS-189; OPEN until D-061 is fixed). The uploader is taken from the session where the caller supplies none and is not editable after insert.

### URS-079 — Roles, responsibilities and training are recorded per person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each person shall have a record of the Roles & Responsibilities document in force for them, with the period it applies to; a new one shall end the previous one without deleting it. When a controlled QMS document is issued, the people who must be trained on it shall be chosen and the training assigned to each. Training shall be recorded as sessions with the attendees, the trainer, the method, any assessment result and the attendance evidence, or as the person's own acknowledgement of having read the document; a failed assessment shall keep the training open. A person's profile shall list every past training they received, and shall be visible to the person, their managers and those responsible for users and training only.

| **FRS-216** — My Profile: the account, the R&R period, and what I can do | Medium | OQ-214, OQ-209 |
| **FRS-093** — Profile, R&R periods and training, bounded by one visibility rule | High | OQ-81 |

**FRS-172.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-172.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a User Master row that has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities period, a training assignment or a training attendance, and the refusal shall say to mark the person inactive instead. FRS-172.2 No deletion of a User Master row shall remove a `user_profile` or `user_rr` row by cascade. FRS-172.3 The User Master shall offer 🗑 Delete only on a row with no such history — a duplicate or a mistaken entry — and only after a confirmation. FRS-172.4 Every deletion shall be written to the audit trail with the name removed. RATIONALE: 0264 declares `user_profile` and `user_rr` ON DELETE CASCADE and the two training tables not, so today a person with training cannot be deleted while a person with only an R&R history is deleted together with it — the one record URS-079 says must be ended without being deleted, and FRS-093 says is not deletable (D-059).

**FRS-190.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-190.1 An open assignment shall be cancelled only by a holder of training.manage, with a reason, the database refusing anybody else (`tg_update`); a cancelled assignment shall read Cancelled and keep its reason. FRS-190.2 An assignment not completed and past its due date shall read Overdue (`training_status`, 0264). FRS-190.3 Assigning a document or topic to an audience shall skip anybody already assigned it and report how many were created. FRS-190.4 Re-saving a session shall record, for each attendance, assessment result, score or remark it changes, the previous value, who changed it and when, in a history no user can edit or delete. FRS-190.5 Changing a Roles & Responsibilities period's From or To shall be recorded the same way. FRS-190.6 The Sessions list shall be readable by every signed-in user (`ts_read`); a person's attendance and assessment only through `may_see_person()`. FRS-190.7 The assignments shall be searchable and counted by status with exact counts; where nothing is visible the screen shall say “No training assigned that you may see”, and a load failure shall name the bundle to run. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 because a Pass that was a Fail, or a period that moved, cannot be told from one recorded correctly once the edit leaves no trace; today both are overwritten in place and neither table is audited by `record_audit` (D-062).

**FRS-216.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-216.1 My Profile shall show the account: name, e-mail, designation, Permission (the role) and region. FRS-216.2 My Profile shall state, where the person’s profile did not load, that it did not and what they may do until it exists (FRS-210.5). FRS-216.3 A holder of users.manage or training.manage shall be able to change the period of a recorded R&R document, From remaining required and To not before it, the database stamping who last changed the row and when (sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on). FRS-216.4 My Profile shall show the role in effect, whether its permissions are stored or the built-in fallback, any personal extra permissions, and the actions and pages they grant, and shall say when an administrator is previewing another person. FRS-216.5 My Profile shall present its sections as tabs, one per section — Account, Details & R&R, Training, My Team (only where somebody reports to the person), What I can do, Signature, Password and Appearance — remembering the tab last opened on that device and opening Account when the remembered tab is not offered. **FRS-093.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* 0264: `user_profile` (employee code, joining date), `user_rr` (a trigger closes the previous open period the day before the new From), `training_sessions` + `training_attendance` (bulk, Pass/Fail, score, attachments) and `training_assignments` (one per person per document). `training_status` derives Completed = attended without a Fail OR acknowledged with no Fail recorded; Overdue = open past its due date; Cancelled = cancelled by training.manage with its reason kept. Every per-person row is read through `may_see_person()`: the person, their reporting tree, users.manage, training.manage; the Sessions list is readable by every signed-in user. The trainee acknowledges only their own assignment through `acknowledge_training()`. No row SHALL be deleted, by the application or by a cascade from the User Master (FRS-172; OPEN until D-059 is fixed), and an amendment to attendance, assessment or an R&R period SHALL keep the value it replaced, the author and the time (FRS-190; record_audit keeps both images since 0314, D-062). ### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. ### URS-146 — A training record, once made, is amended with a trace and ended only for a reason

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A training assignment shall be cancellable only by those responsible for training, with the reason kept, and a cancelled assignment shall read as neither open nor completed. An assignment past its due date and not completed shall read Overdue. A correction to a recorded attendance, assessment result, score, or Roles & Responsibilities period shall keep the value it replaced, who changed it and when: a training record is evidence of competence, and an edit that leaves no trace makes it evidence of nothing. The list of training sessions may be read by every signed-in user; who attended and how they were assessed shall be read only as URS-079 states.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-190** — Cancelling, Overdue, and amending a training record | High | OQ-183 |

**FRS-190.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-190.1 An open assignment shall be cancelled only by a holder of training.manage, with a reason, the database refusing anybody else (`tg_update`); a cancelled assignment shall read Cancelled and keep its reason. FRS-190.2 An assignment not completed and past its due date shall read Overdue (`training_status`, 0264). FRS-190.3 Assigning a document or topic to an audience shall skip anybody already assigned it and report how many were created. FRS-190.4 Re-saving a session shall record, for each attendance, assessment result, score or remark it changes, the previous value, who changed it and when, in a history no user can edit or delete. FRS-190.5 Changing a Roles & Responsibilities period's From or To shall be recorded the same way. FRS-190.6 The Sessions list shall be readable by every signed-in user (`ts_read`); a person's attendance and assessment only through `may_see_person()`. FRS-190.7 The assignments shall be searchable and counted by status with exact counts; where nothing is visible the screen shall say “No training assigned that you may see”, and a load failure shall name the bundle to run. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 because a Pass that was a Fail, or a period that moved, cannot be told from one recorded correctly once the edit leaves no trace; today both are overwritten in place and neither table is audited by `record_audit` (D-062).

### URS-079 — Roles, responsibilities and training are recorded per person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each person shall have a record of the Roles & Responsibilities document in force for them, with the period it applies to; a new one shall end the previous one without deleting it. When a controlled QMS document is issued, the people who must be trained on it shall be chosen and the training assigned to each. Training shall be recorded as sessions with the attendees, the trainer, the method, any assessment result and the attendance evidence, or as the person's own acknowledgement of having read the document; a failed assessment shall keep the training open. A person's profile shall list every past training they received, and shall be visible to the person, their managers and those responsible for users and training only.

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

It shall flag where the Product Database names a different customer from the cover and the calls, say when the machine is not on the Product Database, and mark cancelled calls, voided spares and migrated records as such. ### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

### URS-139 — A controlled value that is in use is withdrawn, never erased

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each value list shall be maintainable by those granted that list, a duplicate being refused and each entry attributable to the person who added it. A value that any record carries shall not be deleted; it shall be deactivated, so it stops being offered and the records carrying it still read correctly, and the refusal shall be the database's and not only the screen's. The Standard Complaint list shall be scoped by product, a complaint mapped to no product applying to every product, so a call is offered the complaints that belong to its machine. A value may be renamed by those granted the list; the records already carrying the old wording keep it. An overview shall show every master with its size and whether it loaded.

FRS-180.2 A value already in the list shall be refused with “already in this list”. FRS-180.3 An entry's Added On shall be the day it was added, and its author shall be recorded by the database from the session (`sys_created_by`, 0244); the Added By shown is a label. FRS-180.5 🗑 Delete shall be offered only to a holder of `master.<list>.delete`. FRS-180.6 The database shall refuse the deletion of a value that any record carries, and shall say to deactivate it instead. FRS-180.7 Without the right to edit a list, the screen shall name the permission needed. FRS-180.8 ↻ Refresh on a list shall clear that list's dropdown cache, so forms offer the change without a reload; ↻ Refresh all shall clear every one. FRS-180.9 Where the registry of lists (`master_lists`) is absent, the built-in lists shall be used and the screen shall say which bundle to run. FRS-180.10 All Masters shall list the four registers with a row count each, and every value list with its entry count, whether it Loaded, is Empty or failed, and where it is used; a list may be opened in place or on its own page, and an unknown list address shall return to the overview. RATIONALE: .6 in the database because every count and filter downstream matches the stored value, and a deleted value leaves records carrying a word no list holds. Today a hard DELETE is offered with no such check and nothing in the database refuses it (D-056). FRS-180.11 An entry shall be added through an Add entry form opened by a button, naming each field and marking the required ones, and refusing an empty value; on the DCCR Complaint Grouping and Root Cause Key Word lists the Product shall be required and picked from the Product Master, or COMM for every product.

**FRS-181.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-181.1 Each Standard Complaint shall carry the products it applies to in `extra.products`, and a complaint mapped to none shall apply to every product. FRS-181.2 The mapping shall be edited singly, or for ticked complaints set, added to or removed in bulk, ten at a time with every failure named, by holders of `master.complaint.edit` only. FRS-181.3 Changing the mapping shall keep every other value in `extra`. FRS-181.4 The editor shall offer every product in the register and every product already mapped, so a mapping cannot vanish from its own editor. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Product Database shall present the install base read-only — machines are loaded, or follow from the cover registers and ownership transfer — and shall let a person who may register calls start a field call, and a person who may create installation calls start an installation call, from a machine, with the machine's customer, model, serial and cover already filled. The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. A retired product line shall not be offered on a new sale, and the reason shall be stated where it is missing; it shall remain available to contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback. A product the catalogue does not hold may still be typed on a sale, the catalogue being kept by hand.

### URS-141 — The assembled machine record says how current it is, and who may read it is a decision on record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Product Database 2.0 shall state when it was last assembled and, where a source register has changed since, that it is being updated and within what time. It shall be re-assembled automatically after any source register changes, within a stated interval, and on demand only by those authorised to maintain the registers. Who may read it shall be stated as a decision: it assembles warranty and contract detail, and where its readership is wider than that of the registers it reads, that shall be recorded and approved by the system owner rather than inherited from a technical fix. An empty result shall say, for each source register, how many rows it holds and how many lack a serial or a model, and whether the reader is seeing only their own share.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_database_2_materialised_test.sql` (.3, .5).

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

### URS-163 — Only a known person gets in, and every way in is the production one

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall admit a person only through the organisation’s identity provider and shall record every successful and every refused sign-in. A person whose profile cannot be read shall not be admitted. A signed-in person who has neither a profile nor a User Master entry shall hold no authority beyond seeing that their identity is unresolved. Super administrators shall be designated in one list that the application and the database agree on. A password shall meet a stated strength, changing one shall require the current one, and a forgotten one shall have one stated remedy. A change to a person’s permissions shall reach a session already open within a stated time. An unknown login admitted with an engineer’s authority is an unknown login able to write quality records.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-210** — Sign-in, identity and passwords | High | OQ-203 |
| **FRS-216** — My Profile: the account, the R&R period, and what I can do | Medium | OQ-214, OQ-209 |

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-216.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-216.1 My Profile shall show the account: name, e-mail, designation, Permission (the role) and region. FRS-216.2 My Profile shall state, where the person’s profile did not load, that it did not and what they may do until it exists (FRS-210.5). FRS-216.3 A holder of users.manage or training.manage shall be able to change the period of a recorded R&R document, From remaining required and To not before it, the database stamping who last changed the row and when (sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on). FRS-216.4 My Profile shall show the role in effect, whether its permissions are stored or the built-in fallback, any personal extra permissions, and the actions and pages they grant, and shall say when an administrator is previewing another person. FRS-216.5 My Profile shall present its sections as tabs, one per section — Account, Details & R&R, Training, My Team (only where somebody reports to the person), What I can do, Signature, Password and Appearance — remembering the tab last opened on that device and opening Account when the remembered tab is not offered. FRS-216.6 My Team shall list the people reporting to the person in two groups by their User Master status (Active): Active / Current and Ex Employees, each with its count, the tab counting the current ones, and an ex employee’s profile, R&R and training remaining viewable. RATIONALE: .4 because a person told they cannot do something needs to see whether the role or the fallback is the reason, and the wrong answer there sends an administrator to tick the wrong box.

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

### URS-177 — Equipment sold through a dealer is monitored, and its installation call is raised when the dealer sells it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Sold Through shall record the dealer a machine was sold through, chosen only from parties identified as dealers, on the Warranty Sale Entry, on the Ownership Transfer and in the Product Database. A sale may be made to a dealer, but no installation call shall be raised for a dealer. When the dealer sells the machine to a customer an ownership transfer shall be recorded, and the installation call shall be raised from that transfer, for the customer, with the call number OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL so that it is told apart, dated the transfer date. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-03 (“Sold through -- it is to monitor the equipments sold through Dealer … we can not have an installation call for a dealer … then generate an installation call from the ownership transfer entry … OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL NO”).

FRS-243.6 The Ownership Transfer register shall show Sold Through and offer, to a holder of install.create, “+ Installation call” on a transfer: one call for the transfer's To party, numbered OT-<product>-<serial>, dated the transfer date, built by the same builder as a sale's installation call with the Party Master's city, state and engineer and the Product Database's cover; a machine that already has its OT- call is not given a second. Installation calls made before the system, back to 2018, shall be loadable into the same record in one file, and shall decide their machine's warranty exactly as a call reported in the system does. The engineer shall see, while reporting an installation, the machine's warranty as it stands and as it will stand after the report.

### URS-181 — The month's PM visits are worked out from the Warranty and Contract Registers, each Generated or Missed

*v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall list, for a chosen month, the machines whose warranty or contract has a PM visit due in that month, worked out from the cover's start date, period and PM visits: visit k falls on the start date plus k times (months x 30 / PM visits) days. Each shall be shown as Generated when a PM call for that visit (reading k / N) exists for the machine and is not cancelled, and as a Missed PM otherwise, and the list shall be filterable by Missed PM / Generated, by Products / Accessories, and by product. A PM call shall be created only for a Missed PM whose machine's installation call is solved, or which has no installation call, and whose party is a customer, and each of those two conditions shall also be a filter. The coordinator shall be able to create those calls, dated the 1st of the month, registered after the month's latest PM call and allotted to the Product Database's engineer. The monthly PM upload shall remain. The user, 2026-10-08: "Can we do PM generation from Contract and warranty register?"; the first visit of a cover starting 10 January with 3 visits in 12 months is due on its 120th day; "it should check the largest registeration date and time for the month, then add 10 secs"; Added On "should capture the actual Date of that call generation"; a visit is generated "when the visit is created - like 1/12, 2/12 like that and it is not in Cancelled state"; "Give me an option to segregate Product and Accessory"; "Give me pending list separately.. like a filter at the top, generated, pending (Or name it Missed PM)"; "Add the product as a filter at the top"; "Add 2 more logics - But add these as rules + Filters: 1. The installation call associated with it should be in solved state 2. Party the device is associated to should be a customer"; "Allow machines with no installation call".

FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. ### URS-060 — A record is keyed on what identifies it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The key of a quality or servicing record shall be the whole of what identifies it. Where a record concerns a DEVICE, the device is its model together with its serial number, serial numbers being repeated across models. Where one document concerns SEVERAL devices, each device shall hold its own record under that document’s number. A key narrower than the identity does not fail loudly — it silently replaces one record with another — so the sufficiency of such a key shall be established by MEASUREMENT against the data to be loaded, before that data is loaded.

| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-072** — A device record is keyed on the model and the serial | High | OQ-54 |

FRS-119.4 Where it is now shall show the holder, status, city and state, engineer, warranty number, end and state, and contract type, number, end and state, from products and machine_cover. FRS-119.7 A voided spare shall read VOIDED, a cancelled call CANCELLED, and a migrated FFR or uploaded feedback shall be labelled so. **FRS-178.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-178.1 A change to a part's code or description shall be made only through `rename_part()` (0196), which shall refuse a caller without masters.edit.rename_part (0289); the work behind it, `rename_part_records()` (0309), shall not be callable by any signed-in user or the public key. FRS-178.2 The drawer shall state, before renaming, how many records in which tables will move. FRS-178.3 `rename_part()` shall rewrite the part's identity in the catalogue and in all ten tables that carry it — stock adjustments (0266) included since 0309 — in one transaction. FRS-178.4 It shall refuse a rename onto a part that already exists, never merging two parts. FRS-178.7 The spare-request-line guard and the material-return guard shall let through the one change a rename makes — the part, moved exactly as the rename’s ticket names it, nothing else changed — so a rename does not need an administrator (0310); every other change of part on a line, and every other edit of a return, shall still be refused. FRS-178.8 Stock transfers shall move last of the ten, so the transfer stock check sees the part’s full balance under the new name. FRS-178.5 The consumption guard shall admit that rename by a ticket only the function can write, and shall refuse every other change of part on a consumption line. FRS-178.6 Every engineer's hand stock shall be the same after a rename as before, under the new identity. **FRS-188.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-188.1 The Record a transfer form shall require the model and the serial. FRS-188.2 The destination party shall be chosen from the Party Master. FRS-188.3 A blank previous party shall be completed from the machine's current owner only where exactly one machine carries that model and serial, left empty otherwise, and left empty where it would equal the destination (0182, 0183). FRS-188.4 Recording a transfer shall set the owner in the Product Database of that model and serial only, and not where a later-dated transfer of the same machine exists. FRS-188.7 A save the database refuses shall say why in words. RATIONALE: 298 serials in the recovered-entries export belong to more than one product. Today the transfer form asks for the serial alone, 0072/0183 fill the model and previous owner from the first `products` row with that serial, the owner of EVERY machine sharing the serial is moved, and `recorded_by` keeps a caller-supplied value (D-060); the entry form asks for the serial alone and upserts on `serial_number`, a target 0185 removed, so every save is refused (D-054).

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-072.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Three registers were keyed on less than their identity, and each was corrected against MEASURED data rather than argument. The field failure register was keyed on the report number alone (0181): eight numbers in the 2016–2019 registers each cover several machines — one covers four — so 20 rows collapsed to 8 and TWELVE machines were lost on a load reporting success. Recovered warranty entries were keyed on the serial alone (0185): of 2,263 rows, 298 serials belong to more than one product — one serial is both an ANAVENT and an ORION, another is four machines — so 640 rows collapsed to 298 and THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO machines were lost. Ownership transfers carried no key at all (0184). Each key is now the pair, held as a GENERATED STORED column with a plain unique index. The rule was already stated in the codebase (src/lib/machine.ts) together with the incident that produced it — a request for one model’s serial 201 was offered an open call for another model’s serial 201, one action from being mapped onto it — and these three registers contradicted it.

By product: the product list is the distinct set of item names in the PRODUCT REGISTER (view `product_register_names`, security_invoker) with the machine count beside each, and choosing one narrows Serial Number to that product's serials — an equality match on `products.item_name`, served by the btree index of 0052, so a product name is never a prefix of another. By party: the drop-down is searched on the server over the customers named on the Product Register (`products.party_name`) — the customers who hold a machine — and the box beside it takes any part of a name; the party's details are then read from the Party Master, preferring the party whose name matches exactly. ### URS-040 — A bulk load shall not silently alter what it does not carry

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Loading a file shall change only the fields that file supplies. A field the file does not carry shall take the value the system defines for it, and shall not be written as empty or null; a load that cannot honour this shall fail rather than write. Where a register is declared to be loaded from a file that is the WHOLE of each record (the Product Database), a cell the file carries under its heading and leaves empty shall empty that field, so a correction made at source can remove a value as well as add one; a stamped or a required column shall never be emptied this way.

FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. **FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

**FRS-267.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-267.1 Bulk Uploads shall offer "DCCR Register — historical, with its calls", loaded into a staging register keyed on the UC Number, open to a holder of bulk.upload. FRS-267.2 Each row shall file its call — a P M VISIT row as a PM call, any other as a Field call — dated by the file's CALL DATE, with the customer as the party, the place, product, serial, cover, complaint, engineer, warranty number and Review 1 answers; the month-only warranty start shall be kept as text. FRS-267.3 Each row shall file its review marked imported, keeping the file's reviewers and dates and raising no Field Failure Report. FRS-267.4 Each row shall file one visit carrying the CURRENT CALL STATUS (else CALL STATUS), pending reason, engineer and Call Solved Date & Time, entered at the solved date, else the file's Updated Date, else the call date; no visit shall be filed for Unattended or for a Canceled call, which shall be filed cancelled. FRS-267.5 A call already in the register shall not be changed, and only a review it lacks shall be added. FRS-267.6 Loading shall notify nobody. FRS-267.7 Re-loading shall correct the calls the load filed and add no second call or visit; a correction shall need the same edit rights as on screen. FRS-267.8 The outcome for each UC Number shall be recorded on its staging row. RATIONALE: measured on the live project 2026-10-06, 6,051 DCCR rows of 2025 had been loaded while no Field call before 2026 existed, so the DCCR View could show none of them.

**FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-046.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The API writes a batch of rows as ONE insert whose column list is the union of the rows’ keys; a row lacking one of those keys is written as NULL, not as the column default. The loader therefore groups rows by their column set and sends each group separately, so a column no row in the group carries genuinely defaults. Filling absent values in was rejected as a fix: it would defeat a default that carries meaning. A load that violates a NOT NULL constraint fails the batch and writes nothing of it.

## Warranty Register `/warranties`

Opened by `mod:/warranties`.

### URS-080 — Review 2 is answered No automatically only while an authorised person has switched Auto Review on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall carry an AUTO REVIEW switch for Review 2. Only a person holding the permission review.auto — by role, Admin, NSM and Technical Support, or given it individually by an administrator — shall be able to turn it on or off, and the register shall show whether it is on, who set it and when. While it is on, each morning every field call logged before that day which failed outside its first year and whose Review 2 is still blank shall be answered NO on all three Review 2 questions. Each such answer shall record, as the Review 2 reviewer, the name of the person who switched Auto Review on, and shall also keep a marker that it was answered by the auto review, so that Review 3 can tell an automatic NO from one a reviewer gave and change it where it is wrong. A call that failed inside its first year, or whose age at failure is not known, shall never be answered automatically, and no Review 2 a person has begun or completed shall be altered. A standing rule that answers a quality question is itself a judgement, so it belongs to the person who authorised it rather than to the system; and a failure in the first year is exactly the case the warranty question exists for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-268** — A PM call whose consumption is a Spare joins the DCCR review | High | OQ-266 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-268.** *(v0.10.133 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-268.1 A consumption line of quantity above 0 on a PM call whose part (the code before "|") is categorised Spare in the Part Master shall open the call's DCCR review with Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration set to SPARE; an existing review shall not be changed. FRS-268.2 The Daily Complaint Review Register and its counts shall list every Field call and every PM call that has a DCCR review, each reader seeing only the calls the call policies give them. FRS-268.3 The 2026 PM calls already carrying a Spare shall be added once (0397); a part the Part Master does not yet categorise Spare adds nothing, and the addition shall be re-runnable once the mapping is complete. FRS-268.4 DCCR rows whose UC Number is an Excel date serial (five digits) or "-" and that match no call shall be removed (0398). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-06: "if a Consumption indicates a Spare then it should be added to DCCR Review ... use the Current Data and Lets review it again and add old calls once the mapping is complete".

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The Product Database shall present the install base read-only — machines are loaded, or follow from the cover registers and ownership transfer — and shall let a person who may register calls start a field call, and a person who may create installation calls start an installation call, from a machine, with the machine's customer, model, serial and cover already filled. The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. A retired product line shall not be offered on a new sale, and the reason shall be stated where it is missing; it shall remain available to contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback. A product the catalogue does not hold may still be typed on a sale, the catalogue being kept by hand.
