| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |
| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |
| **FRS-244** — The sale, the contract and the transfer fill the Product Database by product + serial | High | OQ-236 |
| **FRS-245** — The installing engineer's Warranty Start Date? answer decides the Product Database warranty start | High | OQ-237 |
| **FRS-246** — The installation warranty record, its bulk upload, and the Visit Entry preview | High | OQ-238 |

**FRS-182.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-182.1 The Product Database shall have no path that writes a machine. FRS-182.2 It shall filter by party, product, serial and status, the status being the derived cover status rather than a stored one. FRS-182.3 A search that times out shall say how to narrow it and keep the database's message. FRS-182.4 “+ Field” shall be offered on a machine only to holders of calls.create, and “+ Install” only to holders of install.create; each shall open its call form filled with the machine's customer, product, serial and cover. FRS-182.5 The database shall refuse an installation call from anybody without install.create, whatever screen it was started from (FRS-008). FRS-182.6 The Product Master shall list every product line — code, name, type, category, short form, still sold, added on, added by — with All / Active / Inactive counts that are exact, shall be searchable, and shall have no path that writes a line other than its Imported column (FRS-227). FRS-182.7 It shall state that an Inactive line takes no new Sale Entry and still takes contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback, and where it is empty shall point to Bulk Uploads and name the permission needed. FRS-182.8 The Sale Entry's product picker shall offer only Active lines, pair code and name where the catalogue gives one answer, count the retired lines it does not offer and say why, and accept a product the catalogue does not hold. FRS-182.9 No signed-in user shall delete a machine through the API: adding and editing stay with masters.edit.records, and a machine is removed only from the SQL editor (D-139). RATIONALE: .8 is guidance and not a control, and is stated as such: a trigger refusing a retired line would also refuse the historical sales import, in which 30 of 53 lines are retired and the sales really happened, and a catalogue kept by hand may lack a real line. `product_line_sellable()` (0193) holds the same rule in SQL. .4 is open for “+ Install”, offered today to calls.create (D-063).

**FRS-227.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-227.1 A product line shall carry Imported (Yes / No), blank until set. FRS-227.2 The Product Master screen shall show it as a column and let a holder of masters.edit.records set it; a save the database refuses or matches nothing shall be reported. FRS-227.3 The Product Master bulk upload shall read an “Imported” column as Yes / No; a blank cell or an absent column shall leave the stored value alone. RATIONALE: no default either way — Yes would demand a test of in-house equipment, No would let an imported unit out untested (0319).

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

**FRS-242.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-242.1 Parties, parts and product lines shall be written under masters.parties.*, masters.parts.* and masters.product_master.* (add / edit / delete), each its own INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policy (0325), with no FOR ALL write policy. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. FRS-242.3 A value list shall carry master.<list>.add beside .edit and .delete; adding shall be admitted by the add key, the list's edit key or masters.edit.records. FRS-242.4 Each of the four registers shall show an Actions column — ✎ Edit and 🗑 Delete, and on the Part Master and the lists Deactivate — each button only to the holder of its key; Add entry only to the holder of the add key. FRS-242.5 The Product Master's Edit shall change every field but the Product Code; a list's Edit shall rename the value and change its columns, saying before it is saved that records already carrying the old wording keep it. FRS-242.6 master_delete_guard() (security definer, not callable through the API) shall refuse deleting a party named on any machine, call, call request, pending registration, sale, contract, ownership transfer, additional entry, feedback, spare request, consumption history or Indoor job; a part named on any spare request, dispatch, consumption, issue history, opening stock, adjustment, transfer or material return line; and a product line whose code any machine, sale line or contract line carries — counting as the owner, and naming the count. FRS-242.7 A delete or edit that matches no row shall be reported as not done, never as done. FRS-242.8 A party’s name, a part’s code or description and a product line’s code shall not be changed except through Rename part or by an importer, so a row cannot be renamed and then deleted (0335, D-136). FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). RATIONALE: .2 so nobody gains or loses on the day it ships; .6 counts as the owner because under the caller's row-level security a count sees only what the caller may read and would pass a party a thousand other calls name. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

**FRS-244.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-244.1 Every write to a sale line or entry, a contract line or entry, an ownership transfer or an additional entry shall re-sync the Product Database row of that machine — product and serial together, never the serial alone — through sync_product_machine() (0330). FRS-244.2 From the machine's latest sale line (by warranty end; the line's value, else its entry's): Warranty No., start, end, PM visits, Invoice No., Invoice Date, Warranty Years, Warranty Months and Accessories Included. FRS-244.3 From its latest contract line (by contract end; line, else entry): Contract No., start, end, type and status, and its PM visits, which overwrite the sale's (the user's choice) and survive the sale being saved again. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). FRS-244.6 A contract or warranty number a machine carries that a register line holds for ANOTHER model sharing its serial shall be cleared with its dates and type; one no register holds is left. FRS-244.7 Status: a current contract is its type, a current warranty WGP, a machine the registers know with neither OGP. FRS-244.8 A one-time re-sync shall apply this to every machine, the old values of each changed row kept in products_resync_backup. RATIONALE: .1 because a serial is shared by different models — the ORION-G 2410 / CPX CARE MC5521 case — and a contract on one is not cover on the other. Proved by `supabase/tests/registers_fill_product_database_test.sql`.

**FRS-245.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-245.1 Where the customer feedback of a machine's latest installation call answers Warranty Start Date? with "Installation Call Solved Date" and the call is Solved, that product + serial's Product Database warranty start shall be the day the call was solved, in India time (0331). FRS-245.2 Its warranty end shall then be that start plus the sale's warranty period — months, else years × 12 — by cover_period_end(), the application's own arithmetic; with no period known the end is left as the sale has it. FRS-245.3 "Invoice Date", any other answer, or an installation not yet solved shall leave the documented start of the PO / Warranty Sale Entry. FRS-245.4 The machine shall be re-synced whenever an installation's feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, and the answer shall survive the sale being saved again. FRS-245.5 Only the product + serial the installation names shall change. FRS-245.6 A one-time apply shall set this for every machine whose installation already answered "Installation Call Solved Date", the old start, end and status kept in products_install_start_backup. RATIONALE: the two answers are the feedback's own, measured on the live register (328 and 78 installations, 2026-10-03); 28 reports carrying a typed date were left as they are, the user's decision. Proved by `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

**FRS-246.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-246.1 public.installation_warranty_starts shall hold one row per installation call, keyed on the UCN (ucn_key, unique), with call_number, product_name, serial, party_name, reg_date, warranty_choice, call_solved_at, solved_date (the India-time day of call_solved_at where not given), engineer, visit_at, remarks, source (RITHI, Feedback or Upload) and the columns the file carries that it does not name in extra (0332). FRS-246.2 warranty_start, warranty_end and period_months shall be written by the system from the Product Database after the choice is applied; a value sent through the API shall be discarded. FRS-246.3 machine_install_warranty_start() shall read the machine's latest row here (by solved date), so a loaded 2018 row decides its machine's warranty as a reported call does (FRS-245). FRS-246.4 Saving a row shall re-sync its product + serial, and the old machine where the product or serial changed. FRS-246.5 A RITHI installation shall fill its own row when its feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, once the engineer has answered Warranty Start Date?. FRS-246.6 Loading or correcting a row shall need Bulk Uploads (bulk.upload); reading needs a sign-in. FRS-246.9 The record shall be filled once from every installation feedback already on file. Proved by `supabase/tests/installation_warranty_starts_test.sql` and `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

### URS-141 — The assembled machine record says how current it is, and who may read it is a decision on record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Product Database 2.0 shall state when it was last assembled and, where a source register has changed since, that it is being updated and within what time. It shall be re-assembled automatically after any source register changes, within a stated interval, and on demand only by those authorised to maintain the registers. Who may read it shall be stated as a decision: it assembles warranty and contract detail, and where its readership is wider than that of the registers it reads, that shall be recorded and approved by the system owner rather than inherited from a technical fix. An empty result shall say, for each source register, how many rows it holds and how many lack a serial or a model, and whether the reader is seeing only their own share.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_database_2_materialised_test.sql` (.3, .5).

### URS-142 — A cover entry is raised, filled and priced by one rule wherever it is entered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The cover registers shall state for every entry whether it is Active, About to expire or Inactive, by one rule shared with the database, an entry with no readable end date being Not covered and never Active. A new entry shall be offered the next number in its series, which may be changed and shall be refused if already used. The customer shall be chosen from the Party Master, a customer the master does not hold being allowed; choosing a customer on a sale shall fill the address, contact and tax fields from the master, blanks included. A contract line's tax and total shall be derived from its rate by the one GST rule. A renewal shall be re-priced: no price shall be carried from the predecessor, a price entered shall be checked before anything is written, and a revision of the old price by a percentage shall be offered. The installation call for one machine may be raised from that machine, and its call number written back onto that machine only. Starting a call from a cover register shall be offered only to those who may register one.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-184** — Entry state, numbering, the customer and the price on a cover entry | Medium | OQ-177 |
| **FRS-185** — A renewal is priced by what is entered, never by what was paid | Medium | OQ-178 |
| **FRS-186** — The installation call for one machine, raised from the machine | Medium | OQ-179 |
| **FRS-231** — A warranty machine still waiting for its installation call is marked and can be filtered | Low | OQ-225 |
| **FRS-244** — The sale, the contract and the transfer fill the Product Database by product + serial | High | OQ-236 |

**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-184.4 A Sale Entry shall default its warranty start to today and stamp its entry date when created. FRS-184.5 The party picker shall search the Party Master in the database and shall accept a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.6 Choosing a different party on a sale shall fill its eleven address, contact and tax fields from the Party Master, blanks included, and shall fill nothing for a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). Proved by `supabase/tests/cover_expiry_test.sql` (.1) and `npm run check:cover-party` (.6).

**FRS-185.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-185.1 The Renew panel shall show each carried machine's old rate beside an empty rate box. FRS-185.2 It shall offer to revise every ticked machine's old rate by a stated percentage, and to clear every entered rate. FRS-185.3 It shall preview the total with GST. FRS-185.4 A blank rate shall mean “price it later” and be saved as no rate, tax or total. FRS-185.5 Every entered rate shall be checked before anything is written, and a rate that is not a number, or is negative, shall refuse the whole renewal. FRS-185.6 A machine's tax and total shall be derived from its entered rate by the rule of FRS-184.7. FRS-185.7 No rate shall be copied from the predecessor's machines. FRS-185.8 The success message shall say which machines were priced and which were left blank. FRS-185.9 The Renew panel's dates shall read dd-MMM-yyyy and store a date (FRS-089). RATIONALE: .5 before anything because a contract that exists carrying some of its prices is much harder to walk back than one refused. .7 because a price carried forward silently is a price nobody agreed that looks exactly like one they did. .8 and .9 are open (D-064).

**FRS-186.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-186.1 The Register tab (formerly By machine) of the Warranty Register shall offer + Installation call on a saved machine with a model and a serial and no call number, to holders of install.create or cover.edit. FRS-186.2 The confirmation shall list the fixed answers the call will carry (FRS-085.2 to .8) and name the INST Call placeholder it will replace. FRS-186.3 The call number shall be written back through `link_install_call()` (0258), which shall refuse a caller without install.create, cover.edit or administrator. FRS-186.4 It shall refuse to replace a call number already recorded on the machine; a placeholder shall be replaced. FRS-186.5 It shall refuse a call that is not an installation call for that machine's product and serial. FRS-186.6 Calling it with that call number already in place shall change nothing. FRS-186.7 It shall write no other field of the warranty line. FRS-186.8 The row and this device's copy shall show the call number without a reload. RATIONALE: a function rather than a second UPDATE policy, because row-level security cannot grant one column and a policy letting an install.create holder write the link would let them rewrite the whole warranty line. Proved by `supabase/tests/link_install_call_test.sql`.

**FRS-231.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-231.1 The Register tab of the Warranty Register shall mark each machine line Pending when it carries a product and a serial and its INST Call holds no call number, show the call number where one is mapped, and carry the same value to Excel and CSV. FRS-231.2 It shall offer a filter for those machines with their count, applied by the database across the whole register, combining with the search and the cover-state filters. FRS-231.3 The Entries tab shall show, per sale, how many of its machines are pending, counted by the database, and shall offer the same filter there, narrowing to the sales with at least one, with their count; a sale whose count has not been read shall show a dash, not 0. ### URS-143 — A record of cover is corrected, never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A Sale Entry, a Contract Entry, a machine under either, an ownership transfer and an additional entry are the evidence of what a machine was covered by, and whose it was, on a given day. The system shall not allow any of them to be deleted, through the application or the data interface. A machine recorded against the wrong entry shall be corrected, and an entry raised in error shall be closed as such with the record kept. The cover shown on a call, the terms a repeat failure is judged under and whether work is chargeable are all read from these records, so deleting one rewrites what the system will say about work already done.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-187** — No cover record is deleted | High | OQ-180 |

**FRS-187.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-187.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a row of `sale_entries`, `sale_items`, `contract_entries`, `contract_items`, `ownership_transfers` and `product_additional_entries` by every application role, both by having no delete path and by the retention guard of 0049 (`no_hard_delete`). FRS-187.2 The cover registers shall offer neither Delete entry nor Remove machine. FRS-187.3 A machine recorded under the wrong entry shall be corrected by editing it, and the correction shall be recorded with its before and after values by a trigger that cannot be bypassed (`record_audit`). FRS-187.4 An entry raised in error shall be marked as such and kept. RATIONALE: today both buttons exist — `deleteHeader()` removes an entry with all its machines and `deleteItem()` one machine — the write policies are FOR ALL, none of the six tables is in the 0049 guard, and none is audited by `record_audit` (D-055). The cover shown on a call and the terms a repeat failure is judged under are read from these rows.

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

### URS-181 — The month's PM visits are worked out from the Warranty and Contract Registers, each Generated or Missed

*v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall list, for a chosen month, the machines whose warranty or contract has a PM visit due in that month, worked out from the cover's start date, period and PM visits: visit k falls on the start date plus k times (months x 30 / PM visits) days. Each shall be shown as Generated when a PM call for that visit (reading k / N) exists for the machine and is not cancelled, and as a Missed PM otherwise, and the list shall be filterable by Missed PM / Generated, by Products / Accessories, and by product. A PM call shall be created only for a Missed PM whose machine's installation call is solved, or which has no installation call, and whose party is a customer, and each of those two conditions shall also be a filter. The coordinator shall be able to create those calls, dated the 1st of the month, registered after the month's latest PM call and allotted to the Product Database's engineer. The monthly PM upload shall remain. The user, 2026-10-08: "Can we do PM generation from Contract and warranty register?"; the first visit of a cover starting 10 January with 3 visits in 12 months is due on its 120th day; "it should check the largest registeration date and time for the month, then add 10 secs"; Added On "should capture the actual Date of that call generation"; a visit is generated "when the visit is created - like 1/12, 2/12 like that and it is not in Cancelled state"; "Give me an option to segregate Product and Accessory"; "Give me pending list separately.. like a filter at the top, generated, pending (Or name it Missed PM)"; "Add the product as a filter at the top"; "Add 2 more logics - But add these as rules + Filters: 1. The installation call associated with it should be in solved state 2. Party the device is associated to should be a customer"; "Allow machines with no installation call".

| --- | --- | --- |

**FRS-269.** *(v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-269.1 PM Due shall be listed under Administration beside PM Bulk Upload, opened by mod:/pm-due, and its list read only by a holder of pm.generate, through pm_visits_due() (0404), which refuses anybody else and is not executable by the public key. FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.4 Every machine (product + serial, case and spaces ignored) with a visit falling in the month shall be listed, with the last such visit; it shall be Generated when a PM call for that machine, not cancelled, registered from the cover's start month to its end, has a Reported Problem reading k / N with the same visit number and the same number of visits, in whatever month it was registered, and a Missed PM otherwise; the answer shall include calls the reader cannot see, and each row shall show the generating call and the machine's last PM call. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. FRS-269.6 The party, city, state and engineer shall be the machine's Product Database row (its Service Engineer), the register's party where it has none; a Missed PM with no engineer shall be counted and created unallocated. FRS-269.7 The list shall be filtered at the top by status (Missed PM, the default; Generated; All), by type (All; Products; Accessories, an accessory being a product whose Product Master category is ACCESSORY), by installation (Installation solved or none, the default; Solved; No installation call; Installation not solved; Any), by party (Customer, the default; Not a customer; Any) and by one product, each button counting what it would show with the other filters applied. FRS-269.8 A row may be created only when it is a Missed PM, its machine's installation call (Installation register, product + serial; a Solved call taken over a cancelled or later one) reads Solved or it has no installation call (0404), and its party (the Product Database's, else the register's) has Type CUSTOMER on the Party Master; an installation call that exists and is not Solved, or a party not in the master or with no Type, fails; each row shall show its installation call and state and its party's Type. Only such a row shall be tickable; every one shown starts ticked. Create shall need pm.create, the PM register's insert right, and shall write the ticked rows through the calls view with the PM upload's shaping (shapePmRows): call type P M VISIT, Registration Date, Complaint Date and Breakdown Date the 1st of the month, Added On today, Standard Complaint SCHEDULED PM VISIT, Reported Problem SCHEDULED PM VISIT k / N, the SA number as Warranty Number or the MC number as Contract Number, the cover dates, and Item Status WGP or the contract's type normalised. FRS-269.9 The first call shall be registered 10 seconds after the largest registration date-and-time among ALL PM calls of the month (pm_due_latest_reg_at), read when Create is pressed, and each next 10 seconds later; a month with none starts at 00:30 on the 1st, 5 seconds apart, as on PM Bulk Upload. FRS-269.10 After creating, the list shall be read again, so a created visit reads Generated. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-08; the texts are what all 8,720 PM calls of 2026 carry (_pm_generation_inputs.sql). 0401's count of PM calls since the cover started was replaced (D-157).

### URS-076 — A date is a date, whoever is reading it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall present every date in one written form. The system shall store every date as a date rather than as the text of one. A form that renders a date in the reader’s own locale presents one record two ways to two people in one office, and a form that stores what was typed puts text in a date column — which nothing detects until the value is sorted, filtered or subtracted.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-089** — A date field reads dd-MMM-yyyy and stores a date | Medium | OQ-77 |

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-089.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-089.1 The cover registers shall display every date value in the form dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-089.2 The cover registers shall present a date input control when a date field receives focus. FRS-089.3 The cover registers shall store the value produced by that control. FRS-089.4 The cover registers shall derive no date value from text entered by the operator. RATIONALE: a native date control renders in the BROWSER’S locale and no attribute changes it — two machines in one office showed `2026-09-12` and `09/11/2026` for one field. The obvious alternative is the dangerous one: a text box holding `20-Apr-2026` saved as typed puts a formatted string in a date column, and nothing detects it until the value is sorted, filtered or subtracted. FRS-089.4 is therefore a prohibition rather than a convenience, and `check:ui` refuses a parser appearing in that component at all.

### URS-072 — The terms of a parent record reach every record under it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall apply the terms recorded on a parent record to every record under it that states no term of its own. The system shall allow a record under a parent to state a term of its own. The system shall provide a means of returning every record under a parent to the parent’s terms. The system shall state what such a return will discard before it discards it. A bulk load that copies a parent’s values onto every child leaves every child stating terms of its own, so the parent moves nothing and nobody can see why.

Include Force Update Child Records ... Enforce Update as a 1 time activity"), with blanks copied as the button copies them and every sale's machines reset, both at the owner's explicit choice. HIGH because it rewrites quality-relevant records in bulk; the backups (.3) are the control, and they make every changed value recoverable. Proved by supabase/tests/warranty_party_refresh_once_test.sql (0318); measured at 5,000 sales and 20,000 machine lines in 24 s.

The test for "has it been changed" is whether it still equals what the period suggested BEFORE the edit, which is the same rule a machine uses to pin a field away from its entry. .5 because the installation address on a sale legitimately differs from the registered one: a sale whose address changed silently under an operator who had corrected it by hand is worse than one that is visibly out of date, because the first is wrong and nobody knows. .6 because blanking a sale on the ground that the customer register has never heard of the customer would destroy the only address anybody has.

FRS-084.4 The cover registers shall state separately the number of values that repeat the entry. FRS-084.5 The cover registers shall name each field it is about to clear and the number of machines carrying it. FRS-084.6 The cover registers shall offer this action only while at least one value is pinned. FRS-084.7 The cover registers shall clear every machine under one entry in one statement. RATIONALE: .2 because the model, the serial and the machine’s own supplied-with answers are the MACHINE’S facts and clearing them would delete its identity. .3 and .4 are separate because the two are not the same act: clearing a value that repeats the entry changes nothing anybody can see, and clearing one that differs destroys a decision made about one machine, with no undo. .7 because a forty-machine sale would otherwise be forty round trips, any of which can fail half way and leave the entry half-inherited — the state this action exists to resolve.

### URS-068 — One identified record per machine, assembled from every register that names it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every machine the organisation has sold, contracted or recovered shall appear exactly once in a register of machines, identified by its MODEL together with its SERIAL — never by the serial alone, which repeats across models. That record shall be assembled from the warranty sale register, the contract register, the additional entries, the ownership transfer register and the installation call, and shall state for each of the party, the warranty and the contract WHICH register decided it, so the record can be checked against its evidence. Where the registers disagree, the most recently dated evidence shall decide.

| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |
| **FRS-080** — Product Database 2.0 assembles one row per machine from five registers | High | OQ-64 |

FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_database_2_materialised_test.sql` (.3, .5).

**FRS-080.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `product_database_v2` (0218) lists every machine named by `warranty_sale_details`, `contract_details` or `product_additional_entries`, keyed by `machine_key(product, serial)` — the SQL twin of `machineKey()` in `src/lib/machine.ts`, squashed so ORION-G and ORION G are one model, and MODEL-plus-SERIAL so the eleven machines numbered 219 stay eleven rows. Ownership Transfer and the installation call are joined in. The party is the most recently DATED claim among the ownership transfer, the additional entry, the contract and the sale, ties breaking towards the transfer. `party_from`, `warranty_from`, `contract_from` and `item_status_reason` name the deciding register on every row. It does not replace `public.products` or `machine_cover`, both of which are left exactly as they are.

### URS-070 — A warranty starts when the machine was installed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The warranty period of a machine shall start from the date recorded on its installation — the Warranty Start Date captured when the installation call is reported, or failing that the date that call was solved — and shall fall back to the selling register only where no installation was recorded. The end of the period shall be derived from that start and the recorded period, by the same arithmetic the rest of the application uses.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-245** — The installing engineer's Warranty Start Date? answer decides the Product Database warranty start | High | OQ-237 |
| **FRS-246** — The installation warranty record, its bulk upload, and the Visit Entry preview | High | OQ-238 |
| **FRS-082** — Warranty start comes from the installation, and the end is computed like the app | High | OQ-66 |

**FRS-245.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-245.1 Where the customer feedback of a machine's latest installation call answers Warranty Start Date? with "Installation Call Solved Date" and the call is Solved, that product + serial's Product Database warranty start shall be the day the call was solved, in India time (0331). FRS-245.2 Its warranty end shall then be that start plus the sale's warranty period — months, else years × 12 — by cover_period_end(), the application's own arithmetic; with no period known the end is left as the sale has it. FRS-245.3 "Invoice Date", any other answer, or an installation not yet solved shall leave the documented start of the PO / Warranty Sale Entry. FRS-245.4 The machine shall be re-synced whenever an installation's feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, and the answer shall survive the sale being saved again. FRS-245.5 Only the product + serial the installation names shall change. FRS-245.6 A one-time apply shall set this for every machine whose installation already answered "Installation Call Solved Date", the old start, end and status kept in products_install_start_backup. RATIONALE: the two answers are the feedback's own, measured on the live register (328 and 78 installations, 2026-10-03); 28 reports carrying a typed date were left as they are, the user's decision. Proved by `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

**FRS-246.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-246.1 public.installation_warranty_starts shall hold one row per installation call, keyed on the UCN (ucn_key, unique), with call_number, product_name, serial, party_name, reg_date, warranty_choice, call_solved_at, solved_date (the India-time day of call_solved_at where not given), engineer, visit_at, remarks, source (RITHI, Feedback or Upload) and the columns the file carries that it does not name in extra (0332). FRS-246.2 warranty_start, warranty_end and period_months shall be written by the system from the Product Database after the choice is applied; a value sent through the API shall be discarded. FRS-246.3 machine_install_warranty_start() shall read the machine's latest row here (by solved date), so a loaded 2018 row decides its machine's warranty as a reported call does (FRS-245). FRS-246.4 Saving a row shall re-sync its product + serial, and the old machine where the product or serial changed. FRS-246.5 A RITHI installation shall fill its own row when its feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, once the engineer has answered Warranty Start Date?. FRS-246.6 Loading or correcting a row shall need Bulk Uploads (bulk.upload); reading needs a sign-in. FRS-246.7 Bulk Uploads shall offer the register "Installation Warranty Start (old installation calls)", matched on the UCN so a re-loaded file corrects rather than adds, requiring UCN, product and serial. FRS-246.8 On an installation's Visit Entry, below Warranty Start Date?, the system shall show the Product Database warranty of that product + serial as it stands and — when Installation Call Solved Date is chosen on a visit that solves the call — the start and end it will have, computed by the database (machine_warranty_preview). FRS-246.9 The record shall be filled once from every installation feedback already on file. Proved by `supabase/tests/installation_warranty_starts_test.sql` and `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

**FRS-082.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Warranty start is the `Warranty Start Date?` answer on the installation call’s feedback, read through `imported_ts()` so a cell holding "n/a" yields nothing rather than failing the whole view; failing that the installation call’s solved date; failing that the additional entry; failing that the warranty sale. Where a start and a period are both known the end is `cover_period_end(start, months)`, which reproduces `addPeriod()` in `src/lib/dates.ts` INCLUDING its JavaScript month overflow — 31 January plus one month is 2 March, where Postgres’s own interval arithmetic clamps to 27 February. 26 of 458 start/period combinations differ between the two.

## Contract Register `/contracts`

Opened by `mod:/contracts`.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Product Database shall present the install base read-only — machines are loaded, or follow from the cover registers and ownership transfer — and shall let a person who may register calls start a field call, and a person who may create installation calls start an installation call, from a machine, with the machine's customer, model, serial and cover already filled. The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. A retired product line shall not be offered on a new sale, and the reason shall be stated where it is missing; it shall remain available to contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback. A product the catalogue does not hold may still be typed on a sale, the catalogue being kept by hand.

FRS-182.7 It shall state that an Inactive line takes no new Sale Entry and still takes contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback, and where it is empty shall point to Bulk Uploads and name the permission needed. ### URS-141 — The assembled machine record says how current it is, and who may read it is a decision on record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Product Database 2.0 shall state when it was last assembled and, where a source register has changed since, that it is being updated and within what time. It shall be re-assembled automatically after any source register changes, within a stated interval, and on demand only by those authorised to maintain the registers. Who may read it shall be stated as a decision: it assembles warranty and contract detail, and where its readership is wider than that of the registers it reads, that shall be recorded and approved by the system owner rather than inherited from a technical fix. An empty result shall say, for each source register, how many rows it holds and how many lack a serial or a model, and whether the reader is seeing only their own share.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). ### URS-142 — A cover entry is raised, filled and priced by one rule wherever it is entered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The cover registers shall state for every entry whether it is Active, About to expire or Inactive, by one rule shared with the database, an entry with no readable end date being Not covered and never Active. A new entry shall be offered the next number in its series, which may be changed and shall be refused if already used. The customer shall be chosen from the Party Master, a customer the master does not hold being allowed; choosing a customer on a sale shall fill the address, contact and tax fields from the master, blanks included. A contract line's tax and total shall be derived from its rate by the one GST rule. A renewal shall be re-priced: no price shall be carried from the predecessor, a price entered shall be checked before anything is written, and a revision of the old price by a percentage shall be offered. The installation call for one machine may be raised from that machine, and its call number written back onto that machine only. Starting a call from a cover register shall be offered only to those who may register one.

FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-244.2 From the machine's latest sale line (by warranty end; the line's value, else its entry's): Warranty No., start, end, PM visits, Invoice No., Invoice Date, Warranty Years, Warranty Months and Accessories Included. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). FRS-244.6 A contract or warranty number a machine carries that a register line holds for ANOTHER model sharing its serial shall be cleared with its dates and type; one no register holds is left. FRS-244.7 Status: a current contract is its type, a current warranty WGP, a machine the registers know with neither OGP. FRS-244.8 A one-time re-sync shall apply this to every machine, the old values of each changed row kept in products_resync_backup. RATIONALE: .1 because a serial is shared by different models — the ORION-G 2410 / CPX CARE MC5521 case — and a contract on one is not cover on the other. Proved by `supabase/tests/registers_fill_product_database_test.sql`.

### URS-143 — A record of cover is corrected, never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A Sale Entry, a Contract Entry, a machine under either, an ownership transfer and an additional entry are the evidence of what a machine was covered by, and whose it was, on a given day. The system shall not allow any of them to be deleted, through the application or the data interface. A machine recorded against the wrong entry shall be corrected, and an entry raised in error shall be closed as such with the record kept. The cover shown on a call, the terms a repeat failure is judged under and whether work is chargeable are all read from these records, so deleting one rewrites what the system will say about work already done.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-187** — No cover record is deleted | High | OQ-180 |

**FRS-187.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-187.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a row of `sale_entries`, `sale_items`, `contract_entries`, `contract_items`, `ownership_transfers` and `product_additional_entries` by every application role, both by having no delete path and by the retention guard of 0049 (`no_hard_delete`). FRS-187.2 The cover registers shall offer neither Delete entry nor Remove machine. FRS-187.3 A machine recorded under the wrong entry shall be corrected by editing it, and the correction shall be recorded with its before and after values by a trigger that cannot be bypassed (`record_audit`). FRS-187.4 An entry raised in error shall be marked as such and kept. RATIONALE: today both buttons exist — `deleteHeader()` removes an entry with all its machines and `deleteItem()` one machine — the write policies are FOR ALL, none of the six tables is in the 0049 guard, and none is audited by `record_audit` (D-055). The cover shown on a call and the terms a repeat failure is judged under are read from these rows.

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

### URS-181 — The month's PM visits are worked out from the Warranty and Contract Registers, each Generated or Missed

*v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall list, for a chosen month, the machines whose warranty or contract has a PM visit due in that month, worked out from the cover's start date, period and PM visits: visit k falls on the start date plus k times (months x 30 / PM visits) days. Each shall be shown as Generated when a PM call for that visit (reading k / N) exists for the machine and is not cancelled, and as a Missed PM otherwise, and the list shall be filterable by Missed PM / Generated, by Products / Accessories, and by product. A PM call shall be created only for a Missed PM whose machine's installation call is solved, or which has no installation call, and whose party is a customer, and each of those two conditions shall also be a filter. The coordinator shall be able to create those calls, dated the 1st of the month, registered after the month's latest PM call and allotted to the Product Database's engineer. The monthly PM upload shall remain. The user, 2026-10-08: "Can we do PM generation from Contract and warranty register?"; the first visit of a cover starting 10 January with 3 visits in 12 months is due on its 120th day; "it should check the largest registeration date and time for the month, then add 10 secs"; Added On "should capture the actual Date of that call generation"; a visit is generated "when the visit is created - like 1/12, 2/12 like that and it is not in Cancelled state"; "Give me an option to segregate Product and Accessory"; "Give me pending list separately.. like a filter at the top, generated, pending (Or name it Missed PM)"; "Add the product as a filter at the top"; "Add 2 more logics - But add these as rules + Filters: 1. The installation call associated with it should be in solved state 2. Party the device is associated to should be a customer"; "Allow machines with no installation call".

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-269** — PM Due | High | OQ-267 |

**FRS-269.** *(v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-269.1 PM Due shall be listed under Administration beside PM Bulk Upload, opened by mod:/pm-due, and its list read only by a holder of pm.generate, through pm_visits_due() (0404), which refuses anybody else and is not executable by the public key. FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.4 Every machine (product + serial, case and spaces ignored) with a visit falling in the month shall be listed, with the last such visit; it shall be Generated when a PM call for that machine, not cancelled, registered from the cover's start month to its end, has a Reported Problem reading k / N with the same visit number and the same number of visits, in whatever month it was registered, and a Missed PM otherwise; the answer shall include calls the reader cannot see, and each row shall show the generating call and the machine's last PM call. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. FRS-269.6 The party, city, state and engineer shall be the machine's Product Database row (its Service Engineer), the register's party where it has none; a Missed PM with no engineer shall be counted and created unallocated. FRS-269.7 The list shall be filtered at the top by status (Missed PM, the default; Generated; All), by type (All; Products; Accessories, an accessory being a product whose Product Master category is ACCESSORY), by installation (Installation solved or none, the default; Solved; No installation call; Installation not solved; Any), by party (Customer, the default; Not a customer; Any) and by one product, each button counting what it would show with the other filters applied. FRS-269.8 A row may be created only when it is a Missed PM, its machine's installation call (Installation register, product + serial; a Solved call taken over a cancelled or later one) reads Solved or it has no installation call (0404), and its party (the Product Database's, else the register's) has Type CUSTOMER on the Party Master; an installation call that exists and is not Solved, or a party not in the master or with no Type, fails; each row shall show its installation call and state and its party's Type. Only such a row shall be tickable; every one shown starts ticked. Create shall need pm.create, the PM register's insert right, and shall write the ticked rows through the calls view with the PM upload's shaping (shapePmRows): call type P M VISIT, Registration Date, Complaint Date and Breakdown Date the 1st of the month, Added On today, Standard Complaint SCHEDULED PM VISIT, Reported Problem SCHEDULED PM VISIT k / N, the SA number as Warranty Number or the MC number as Contract Number, the cover dates, and Item Status WGP or the contract's type normalised. FRS-269.9 The first call shall be registered 10 seconds after the largest registration date-and-time among ALL PM calls of the month (pm_due_latest_reg_at), read when Create is pressed, and each next 10 seconds later; a month with none starts at 00:30 on the 1st, 5 seconds apart, as on PM Bulk Upload. FRS-269.10 After creating, the list shall be read again, so a created visit reads Generated. ### URS-076 — A date is a date, whoever is reading it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall present every date in one written form. The system shall store every date as a date rather than as the text of one. A form that renders a date in the reader’s own locale presents one record two ways to two people in one office, and a form that stores what was typed puts text in a date column — which nothing detects until the value is sorted, filtered or subtracted.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-089** — A date field reads dd-MMM-yyyy and stores a date | Medium | OQ-77 |

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-089.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-089.1 The cover registers shall display every date value in the form dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-089.2 The cover registers shall present a date input control when a date field receives focus. FRS-089.3 The cover registers shall store the value produced by that control. FRS-089.4 The cover registers shall derive no date value from text entered by the operator. RATIONALE: a native date control renders in the BROWSER’S locale and no attribute changes it — two machines in one office showed `2026-09-12` and `09/11/2026` for one field. The obvious alternative is the dangerous one: a text box holding `20-Apr-2026` saved as typed puts a formatted string in a date column, and nothing detects it until the value is sorted, filtered or subtracted. FRS-089.4 is therefore a prohibition rather than a convenience, and `check:ui` refuses a parser appearing in that component at all.

### URS-072 — The terms of a parent record reach every record under it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall apply the terms recorded on a parent record to every record under it that states no term of its own. The system shall allow a record under a parent to state a term of its own. The system shall provide a means of returning every record under a parent to the parent’s terms. The system shall state what such a return will discard before it discards it. A bulk load that copies a parent’s values onto every child leaves every child stating terms of its own, so the parent moves nothing and nobody can see why.

FRS-224.5 The list and its data shall require mod:/install-calls-unmapped, granted to the administrator role and to Technical Support (which carries every page the administrator holds) and assignable on Roles & Permissions; the public key shall not reach it. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-02: "look for all installation calls using this - Product, Serial No, Party Name or WI-<Product>-<SerialNo>. And map it. If it does not have an installation call give it as a separate list in reports - view only for Admins", and "Map only installation call". Exactly one or nothing, as 0234: a guessed mapping is a false record of which call installed a machine. Proved by supabase/tests/install_call_mapping_once_test.sql (0319).

FRS-090.2 The cover registers shall accept a PM visit count entered by the operator. FRS-090.3 The cover registers shall retain an entered PM visit count when the period or the start date is subsequently changed. FRS-090.4 The warranty register shall re-read the address, the contact details and the tax registrations of the named customer from the customer register when the operator requests it. FRS-090.5 The warranty register shall state each field that request would change, with its present and its proposed value, before changing any. FRS-090.6 The warranty register shall change no field where the customer register holds no such customer. RATIONALE: .1 and .3 together are the requirement — three visits a year is the standard OFFER and what was sold is on the purchase order, so a count that keeps reverting to the offer whenever a start date is corrected is a field somebody re-types until they give up, and one that never follows the period makes every ordinary sale a manual entry. The test for "has it been changed" is whether it still equals what the period suggested BEFORE the edit, which is the same rule a machine uses to pin a field away from its entry. .5 because the installation address on a sale legitimately differs from the registered one: a sale whose address changed silently under an operator who had corrected it by hand is worse than one that is visibly out of date, because the first is wrong and nobody knows. .6 because blanking a sale on the ground that the customer register has never heard of the customer would destroy the only address anybody has.

**FRS-084.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-084.1 The cover registers shall clear every inheriting field on every machine under an entry when the operator requests it. FRS-084.2 The cover registers shall alter no field that the register does not declare as inheriting. FRS-084.3 The cover registers shall state the number of values that differ from the entry before clearing them. FRS-084.4 The cover registers shall state separately the number of values that repeat the entry. FRS-084.5 The cover registers shall name each field it is about to clear and the number of machines carrying it. FRS-084.6 The cover registers shall offer this action only while at least one value is pinned. FRS-084.7 The cover registers shall clear every machine under one entry in one statement. RATIONALE: .2 because the model, the serial and the machine’s own supplied-with answers are the MACHINE’S facts and clearing them would delete its identity. .3 and .4 are separate because the two are not the same act: clearing a value that repeats the entry changes nothing anybody can see, and clearing one that differs destroys a decision made about one machine, with no undo. .7 because a forty-machine sale would otherwise be forty round trips, any of which can fail half way and leave the entry half-inherited — the state this action exists to resolve.

### URS-011 — Warranty & contract cover

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Warranty and contract cover per machine shall be maintained and reflected on calls.
