**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-184.4 A Sale Entry shall default its warranty start to today and stamp its entry date when created. FRS-184.5 The party picker shall search the Party Master in the database and shall accept a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.6 Choosing a different party on a sale shall fill its eleven address, contact and tax fields from the Party Master, blanks included, and shall fill nothing for a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). Proved by `supabase/tests/cover_expiry_test.sql` (.1) and `npm run check:cover-party` (.6).

**FRS-016.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Warranty (Sale Entry) and Contract (Contract Entry) registers hold the parent record; machines inherit its values unless individually pinned.

### URS-048 — Cover continues across a contract renewal

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A maintenance contract shall be renewable from its predecessor without the machine list being re-keyed, and the renewal shall carry a recorded link back to the contract it replaces. Cover shall be continuous: the successor begins the day after the predecessor ends, so no machine is momentarily uncovered and none is covered twice. Prices shall NOT be carried forward, a renewal being re-priced.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-185** — A renewal is priced by what is entered, never by what was paid | Medium | OQ-178 |
| **FRS-221** — A warranty becomes a contract without re-keying its customer or machines | Medium | OQ-218, OQ-233 |
| **FRS-056** — Contract renewal carries the machines, not the prices | Medium | OQ-42 |

**FRS-185.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-185.1 The Renew panel shall show each carried machine's old rate beside an empty rate box. FRS-185.2 It shall offer to revise every ticked machine's old rate by a stated percentage, and to clear every entered rate. FRS-185.3 It shall preview the total with GST. FRS-185.4 A blank rate shall mean “price it later” and be saved as no rate, tax or total. FRS-185.5 Every entered rate shall be checked before anything is written, and a rate that is not a number, or is negative, shall refuse the whole renewal. FRS-185.6 A machine's tax and total shall be derived from its entered rate by the rule of FRS-184.7. FRS-185.7 No rate shall be copied from the predecessor's machines. FRS-185.8 The success message shall say which machines were priced and which were left blank. FRS-185.9 The Renew panel's dates shall read dd-MMM-yyyy and store a date (FRS-089). RATIONALE: .5 before anything because a contract that exists carrying some of its prices is much harder to walk back than one refused. .7 because a price carried forward silently is a price nobody agreed that looks exactly like one they did. .8 and .9 are open (D-064).

**FRS-221.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-221.1 The Warranty Register shall offer, on a saved sale entry and to a holder of contract.edit.entries, a conversion that creates a contract entry. FRS-221.2 The conversion shall carry the sale's Party Name to the contract, and each machine's Product Code, Product Name and Serial Number to a contract line, recording on that line the SA Number and the machine's warranty end. FRS-221.3 It shall propose the Contract Start Date as the day after the sale's warranty end, editable, and shall offer the next MC Number in the series without reserving it. FRS-221.4 It shall ask for Contract Type, Contract Period (Months), PM Visits (Total), Payment Schedule, Bill Generate At and an optional rate per machine, suggesting PM Visits from the months until the operator types over it, and shall work out the End Date and years by the contract form's own rule. FRS-221.5 It shall refuse, before anything is written, an MC Number that exists, a blank required field of the contract form, no ticked machine, and a rate that is not a non-negative number. FRS-221.6 It shall state when machines from the sale are already on a contract. FRS-221.7 It shall never offer a machine that is now with a different customer — the customer machine_current_party() names from the latest dated sale or ownership transfer — and shall list each such machine apart with the statement "Product serial number was transferred to a different customer" and the customer who has it; it shall ask again when the contract is created, refuse a ticked machine that has since left the buyer, and refuse to create the contract while the question is unanswered. RATIONALE: requested by the system owner on 2026-10-02 ("Give a Provision to convert the Warranty into a Contract - Can you map it to the Respective fields + Add the Products to the List"). FRS-221.7 is the owner's rule of 2026-10-03 ("if the product is not with that user never given that product in the list of the Contract.. and add a statement - Product serial number was transferred to a different customer"). The contract type is asked for, never guessed (CW-008), and no rate is carried, a sale having no service price.

**FRS-056.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A contract raises its successor from the register: the machines (each removable before saving), contract type, party, period, PM visit count and billing schedule are carried; `prev_mc_number` on the header and `last_contract_number` / `last_contract_end` on each item record the link back. The successor starts the day AFTER the predecessor ends and a period ends the day BEFORE its anniversary, so `machine_cover` has one unambiguous answer per day. The MC number is entered, never generated, and is refused if it already exists. NO PRICE IS CARRIED from the predecessor: each machine's rate is what is entered in the Renew panel (optionally the old rate revised by a stated percentage), a blank meaning no rate, and tax and total are derived from it by the contract form's own rule; every rate is checked before anything is written (FRS-185).

### URS-068 — One identified record per machine, assembled from every register that names it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every machine the organisation has sold, contracted or recovered shall appear exactly once in a register of machines, identified by its MODEL together with its SERIAL — never by the serial alone, which repeats across models. That record shall be assembled from the warranty sale register, the contract register, the additional entries, the ownership transfer register and the installation call, and shall state for each of the party, the warranty and the contract WHICH register decided it, so the record can be checked against its evidence. Where the registers disagree, the most recently dated evidence shall decide.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |
| **FRS-080** — Product Database 2.0 assembles one row per machine from five registers | High | OQ-64 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_database_2_materialised_test.sql` (.3, .5).

**FRS-080.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `product_database_v2` (0218) lists every machine named by `warranty_sale_details`, `contract_details` or `product_additional_entries`, keyed by `machine_key(product, serial)` — the SQL twin of `machineKey()` in `src/lib/machine.ts`, squashed so ORION-G and ORION G are one model, and MODEL-plus-SERIAL so the eleven machines numbered 219 stay eleven rows. Ownership Transfer and the installation call are joined in. The party is the most recently DATED claim among the ownership transfer, the additional entry, the contract and the sale, ties breaking towards the transfer. `party_from`, `warranty_from`, `contract_from` and `item_status_reason` name the deciding register on every row. It does not replace `public.products` or `machine_cover`, both of which are left exactly as they are.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. ### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Product Database shall present the install base read-only — machines are loaded, or follow from the cover registers and ownership transfer — and shall let a person who may register calls start a field call, and a person who may create installation calls start an installation call, from a machine, with the machine's customer, model, serial and cover already filled. The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. A retired product line shall not be offered on a new sale, and the reason shall be stated where it is missing; it shall remain available to contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback. A product the catalogue does not hold may still be typed on a sale, the catalogue being kept by hand.

### URS-143 — A record of cover is corrected, never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A Sale Entry, a Contract Entry, a machine under either, an ownership transfer and an additional entry are the evidence of what a machine was covered by, and whose it was, on a given day. The system shall not allow any of them to be deleted, through the application or the data interface. A machine recorded against the wrong entry shall be corrected, and an entry raised in error shall be closed as such with the record kept. The cover shown on a call, the terms a repeat failure is judged under and whether work is chargeable are all read from these records, so deleting one rewrites what the system will say about work already done.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-187** — No cover record is deleted | High | OQ-180 |

**FRS-187.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-187.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a row of `sale_entries`, `sale_items`, `contract_entries`, `contract_items`, `ownership_transfers` and `product_additional_entries` by every application role, both by having no delete path and by the retention guard of 0049 (`no_hard_delete`). FRS-187.2 The cover registers shall offer neither Delete entry nor Remove machine. FRS-187.3 A machine recorded under the wrong entry shall be corrected by editing it, and the correction shall be recorded with its before and after values by a trigger that cannot be bypassed (`record_audit`). FRS-187.4 An entry raised in error shall be marked as such and kept. RATIONALE: today both buttons exist — `deleteHeader()` removes an entry with all its machines and `deleteItem()` one machine — the write policies are FOR ALL, none of the six tables is in the 0049 guard, and none is audited by `record_audit` (D-055). The cover shown on a call and the terms a repeat failure is judged under are read from these rows.

An ownership transfer and an additional entry shall identify the machine by its model together with its serial, and the form shall ask for both. Recording a transfer shall move the recorded owner of that machine only, never of another model that shares the serial; the previous owner shall be completed only where the machine is identified without doubt, and left empty otherwise. The person recording a transfer shall be taken from the signed-in session. The customer a machine goes to shall be chosen from the Party Master. Saving an additional entry for a machine that already has one shall correct it.

### URS-177 — Equipment sold through a dealer is monitored, and its installation call is raised when the dealer sells it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Sold Through shall record the dealer a machine was sold through, chosen only from parties identified as dealers, on the Warranty Sale Entry, on the Ownership Transfer and in the Product Database. A sale may be made to a dealer, but no installation call shall be raised for a dealer. When the dealer sells the machine to a customer an ownership transfer shall be recorded, and the installation call shall be raised from that transfer, for the customer, with the call number OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL so that it is told apart, dated the transfer date. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-03 (“Sold through -- it is to monitor the equipments sold through Dealer … we can not have an installation call for a dealer … then generate an installation call from the ownership transfer entry … OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL NO”).

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-243** — Sold Through is the dealer; a dealer gets no installation call; the transfer raises the customer's OT- call | High | OQ-235, OQ-247 |

**FRS-243.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-243.1 A dealer shall be a Party Master entry whose Type is DEALER (`party_is_dealer()`, 0328). FRS-243.2 Sold Through on the Warranty Sale Entry and on each machine line shall be chosen only from dealers (no free text). FRS-243.3 An ownership transfer shall record as Sold Through its From party when that party is a dealer, and nothing otherwise, stamped by the database with any value sent discarded. FRS-243.4 The Product Database's Sold Through shall be the dealer on the machine's latest transfer that names one, else the sale line's, else the sale entry's, and re-saving the sale shall not change it. FRS-243.5 The Warranty Register shall offer no installation call for a sale whose Type is DEALER — on the entry or on a Register line — shall say instead that the call is raised from the Ownership Transfer, and shall not count a dealer's machines as waiting for a call; the database shall refuse any signed-in insert of an installation call, or change of its party, to a dealer, however raised. FRS-243.6 The Ownership Transfer register shall show Sold Through and offer, to a holder of install.create, “+ Installation call” on a transfer: one call for the transfer's To party, numbered OT-<product>-<serial>, dated the transfer date, built by the same builder as a sale's installation call with the Party Master's city, state and engineer and the Product Database's cover; a machine that already has its OT- call is not given a second. FRS-243.7 Once, the Sold Through 0318 cleared from machine lines shall be restored from its backup where the line still follows its entry and the entry's value is blank or different (0328). FRS-243.8 A re-load of an installation call that already exists under the same party shall not be refused as a new call for a dealer; a new call, or a re-load that moves a call onto a dealer, shall still be refused (0351, D-148). The Sold Through picker shall read a party as a dealer the way the database does, ignoring outer spaces (D-152). RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-03, and their choices: Sold Through on a transfer is the From party when a dealer; the transfer's call is dated the transfer date; the dealer rule is kept by the database as well as the screen; the 249 cleared values are restored.

### URS-011 — Warranty & contract cover

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Warranty and contract cover per machine shall be maintained and reflected on calls.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-184** — Entry state, numbering, the customer and the price on a cover entry | Medium | OQ-177 |
| **FRS-016** — Cover registers | Medium | OQ-27 |

**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-184.4 A Sale Entry shall default its warranty start to today and stamp its entry date when created. FRS-184.5 The party picker shall search the Party Master in the database and shall accept a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.6 Choosing a different party on a sale shall fill its eleven address, contact and tax fields from the Party Master, blanks included, and shall fill nothing for a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). Proved by `supabase/tests/cover_expiry_test.sql` (.1) and `npm run check:cover-party` (.6).

**FRS-016.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Warranty (Sale Entry) and Contract (Contract Entry) registers hold the parent record; machines inherit its values unless individually pinned.

### URS-068 — One identified record per machine, assembled from every register that names it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every machine the organisation has sold, contracted or recovered shall appear exactly once in a register of machines, identified by its MODEL together with its SERIAL — never by the serial alone, which repeats across models. That record shall be assembled from the warranty sale register, the contract register, the additional entries, the ownership transfer register and the installation call, and shall state for each of the party, the warranty and the contract WHICH register decided it, so the record can be checked against its evidence. Where the registers disagree, the most recently dated evidence shall decide.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-183** — Product Database 2.0 is rebuilt on a schedule, and read by the audience of its screen | High | OQ-242, OQ-176 |
| **FRS-080** — Product Database 2.0 assembles one row per machine from five registers | High | OQ-64 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). RATIONALE: .5 is stated because it is an exposure decision taken inside a fix (0221 says so itself) and CW-020 still reads Met against the old rule (R-85). Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_database_2_materialised_test.sql` (.3, .5).

**FRS-080.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `product_database_v2` (0218) lists every machine named by `warranty_sale_details`, `contract_details` or `product_additional_entries`, keyed by `machine_key(product, serial)` — the SQL twin of `machineKey()` in `src/lib/machine.ts`, squashed so ORION-G and ORION G are one model, and MODEL-plus-SERIAL so the eleven machines numbered 219 stay eleven rows. Ownership Transfer and the installation call are joined in. The party is the most recently DATED claim among the ownership transfer, the additional entry, the contract and the sale, ties breaking towards the transfer. `party_from`, `warranty_from`, `contract_from` and `item_status_reason` name the deciding register on every row. It does not replace `public.products` or `machine_cover`, both of which are left exactly as they are.

### URS-147 — Guidance is written by the team, and published knowing who can read it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Any signed-in user shall be able to add a field-solution article; only its author or an administrator shall edit or remove it, and removal shall be confirmed. An article shall name the product lines it concerns from the lines still sold, together with any it already names. An article filed as How-To shall appear in the How to Use guide. The documents describing how the system works shall be treated as readable by anybody who has their address, because they are published with the application: they shall hold no customer, patient or personal data, and limiting the screen that presents them shall not be relied on to limit the documents themselves.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-191** — Articles, How-To routing, and the published design documents | Medium | OQ-184 |

**FRS-191.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-191.1 Any signed-in user shall be able to add a Field Solutions article (`kb_insert`, 0042). FRS-191.2 Only its author or an administrator shall edit or delete it (`kb_update`, `kb_delete`), deletion after a confirmation saying it cannot be undone. FRS-191.3 An article shall require a title, and its products shall be chosen from Active Product Master lines together with any it already names. FRS-191.4 An article filed as How-To shall be listed on How to Use, and saving it shall say so and offer to open it. FRS-191.5 How to Use shall show “Open <screen>” only for screens the reader may open, and shall show its written tasks when the database cannot be reached. FRS-191.6 Only an administrator shall add, replace, caption or remove a How to Use screenshot (`help_screenshots`, 0043). FRS-191.7 How RITHI Functions shall present the documents in `public/docs/`, which are served without sign-in; those documents shall hold no customer, patient or personal data, and the four-role limit (0209) governs the menu entry only. FRS-191.8 How RITHI Functions shall remember the chosen document on the device, pass the application's theme to it, accept its height only from its own frame, and report a document that cannot be found rather than show a blank frame. FRS-191.10 How RITHI Functions shall open on All modules: every screen in the menu, in menu order and group, with what it is for, what is done there, what it refuses, the records it keeps, whether the reader's role opens it, and the flows it is part of, each opening that flow; check:ui shall fail when a menu screen has no entry or an entry names no menu screen. FRS-191.9 Field Solutions shall search title, category, product, tags, body and author, and open the article a call's Supporting Documents linked to. RATIONALE: .7 states a boundary rather than a control, because a static file on the site is readable by anybody holding its address and no module key can change that.

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

## Service Manuals `/service-manuals`

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-145 — A controlled document's revision is never overwritten

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A QMS document entered in the system shall carry its document number, revision and effective date, and the file it refers to shall be a stored copy rather than a link that can change underneath the recorded revision. Once saved, a QMS document's number, revision, effective date and file shall not be edited in place: a new revision shall be a new entry, and the one it supersedes shall be retired, so that what was in force on any date stays readable. A document number and revision shall identify one entry only. A service manual may be edited, and shall say which product it covers or that it covers every product.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-189** — A QMS revision is a new entry, and the one it replaces is retired | High | OQ-182 |

**FRS-189.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-189.1 A QMS document shall be refused without a title, a document number, a revision, an effective date and a file or link. FRS-189.2 A document number and revision shall identify one QMS entry, by the unique `doc_key` (0265). FRS-189.3 The QMS shelf shall store an uploaded file in the document store and mark it 📄, and shall mark a pasted link 🔗 with a warning that it can change under the recorded revision. FRS-189.4 Once saved, a QMS entry's number, revision, effective date and file shall not be changed, by the screen or by the database; its title, tags and notes may be. FRS-189.5 A new revision shall be added as a new entry, and the screen shall offer to retire the entry it supersedes. FRS-189.6 Retire and Restore shall be confirmed, and a retired entry shall stay on the shelf, hidden unless “Show retired” is ticked. FRS-189.7 A document number and revision read from a file name shall be suggested only into empty fields, and the suggestion shall be stated. FRS-189.8 A service manual shall name its product, suggested from the product register with typing allowed and a blank meaning every product, and may be edited. FRS-189.9 The Updated column shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. RATIONALE: .4 because an in-place edit replaces the record of what WAS in force with what IS, which is the destruction URS-030 forbids. Today the ✏️ drawer overwrites all four, only the number is required, and the guidance to publish a new entry is advice nothing enforces (D-061); .9 is open (D-064).

**FRS-191.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-191.1 Any signed-in user shall be able to add a Field Solutions article (`kb_insert`, 0042). FRS-191.2 Only its author or an administrator shall edit or delete it (`kb_update`, `kb_delete`), deletion after a confirmation saying it cannot be undone. FRS-191.3 An article shall require a title, and its products shall be chosen from Active Product Master lines together with any it already names. FRS-191.5 How to Use shall show “Open <screen>” only for screens the reader may open, and shall show its written tasks when the database cannot be reached. FRS-191.6 Only an administrator shall add, replace, caption or remove a How to Use screenshot (`help_screenshots`, 0043). FRS-191.7 How RITHI Functions shall present the documents in `public/docs/`, which are served without sign-in; those documents shall hold no customer, patient or personal data, and the four-role limit (0209) governs the menu entry only. FRS-191.8 How RITHI Functions shall remember the chosen document on the device, pass the application's theme to it, accept its height only from its own frame, and report a document that cannot be found rather than show a blank frame. FRS-191.10 How RITHI Functions shall open on All modules: every screen in the menu, in menu order and group, with what it is for, what is done there, what it refuses, the records it keeps, whether the reader's role opens it, and the flows it is part of, each opening that flow; check:ui shall fail when a menu screen has no entry or an entry names no menu screen. FRS-191.9 Field Solutions shall search title, category, product, tags, body and author, and open the article a call's Supporting Documents linked to. RATIONALE: .7 states a boundary rather than a control, because a static file on the site is readable by anybody holding its address and no module key can change that.

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

### URS-029 — Service manuals available at the point of work

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The service documentation for a product shall be held centrally and presented to the engineer on the call for that product, so the machine is worked on against its own manual rather than one found by memory or by hunting a shared folder.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-252** — Technical / Service Notes grouped per product, dated, with the latest note tagged | Medium | OQ-248 |
| **FRS-253** — Technical / Service Notes: every field on the Edit form, and Beta Edit saving many notes at once | Medium | OQ-249 |
| **FRS-035** — Service manual library & call lookup | Medium | OQ-215, OQ-21 |

**FRS-252.** *(v0.10.86 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-252.1 The Technical / Service Notes shelf shall list one row per note per product it covers, ALWAYS grouped by product -- a grouping the reader cannot turn off or change, whatever they chose on that screen before (v0.10.86; DataTable `lockGroup`) -- and a note naming no product under "Every product". FRS-252.2 A note shall carry a Dated, entered by hand on the add / edit form or by the Dated column of the bulk upload (`documents.dated`, 0354). FRS-252.3 The shelf shall order notes by Dated, newest first, an undated note after every dated one. FRS-252.4 The database shall mark, per product, the live note with the newest Dated as the latest (`documents.latest_for`), comparing products case-insensitively; a note with no Dated, or retired, shall never be marked, and two notes on the same newest date shall both be marked. FRS-252.5 The mark shall be recalculated by the database after any insert or delete of a document and after any change to its kind, products, Dated or live state, so adding a newer note for a product moves the mark. FRS-252.6 The shelf shall show the mark as a Latest tag before the typed tags, without writing it into them, and the search shall find "latest". FRS-252.7 A holder of `docs.manage` shall have a Refresh Latest tags button that recalculates every mark (`refresh_service_note_latest()`) and says how many notes changed; the database shall refuse it to anybody else and to the public key. RATIONALE: .4 is per product because a note covering two products can be the newest for one and not the other; .5 makes the button a correction, never a step somebody must remember.

**FRS-253.** *(v0.10.84 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-253.1 The Technical / Service Notes Edit form shall show every field a note carries: Title, Dated, Products, Document No, Revision, Issue / Effective date, Tags, Notes, the file or link, the file name, and each text column the upload kept (`documents.extra`) under its own heading, each editable; values in `extra` that are not text shall be kept unchanged. FRS-253.2 A holder of `docs.manage` shall have a Beta Edit button that turns the shelf into a grid of the notes, one row per note, newest Dated first, offering Title, Dated, Products, Document No, Revision, Issue / Effective date, Tags, Notes, Link and File name. FRS-253.3 The grid shall mark each changed cell and row, count the changed notes, write nothing until Save all, and ask before discarding changes on Cancel. FRS-253.4 Save all shall write every changed note in one database call (`save_service_notes`, 0356) that saves all of them or none, under the caller's own rights (`documents_update`); a note the caller may not edit, a non-note id or a blank title or link shall stop the whole batch with the note named, and the screen shall say nothing was saved. FRS-253.5 A changed Dated or Products shall move the Latest tags (FRS-252.5). RATIONALE: .4 is SECURITY INVOKER and counts each row, because a refused UPDATE matches nothing and raises no error (finding 48) -- without the count a refused batch would read as saved.

**FRS-035.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Service manuals are catalogued in `documents` against the product they cover and stored in Google Drive. Opening a call lists its Supporting Documents — the manuals matching the call’s product, plus manuals held with no product (general to every machine) — alongside Knowledge Base articles whose title, product or tags match the call’s product or standard complaint. ACTIVE Technical / Service Notes (kind = service_note) are listed by the same rule and marked as notes; a retired note is never offered. A note may name SEVERAL products, kept comma-separated and chosen on a multi-select, and reaches a call on any one of them (`docProducts()` in docmatch.ts). Technical / Service Notes may be loaded in bulk (Bulk Uploads → Technical / Service Notes), matched on the Drive link (`documents.url_key`, service notes only, 0272), so loading the list again corrects those notes rather than adding them twice. A note loaded from a Drive listing keeps that listing’s Created, Last Modified and Last Modified By in their own columns (0299), which the notes shelf shows as Added, Updated and Added By; the entry’s own `created_at`, `updated_at` and author are kept beside them and shown in the record details. Every signed-in user may read the library; `docs.manage` maintains it.

# Service Calls

## Call Review `/call-review`

Opened by `mod:/call-review`.

### URS-080 — Review 2 is answered No automatically only while an authorised person has switched Auto Review on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall carry an AUTO REVIEW switch for Review 2. Only a person holding the permission review.auto — by role, Admin, NSM and Technical Support, or given it individually by an administrator — shall be able to turn it on or off, and the register shall show whether it is on, who set it and when. While it is on, each morning every field call logged before that day which failed outside its first year and whose Review 2 is still blank shall be answered NO on all three Review 2 questions. Each such answer shall record, as the Review 2 reviewer, the name of the person who switched Auto Review on, and shall also keep a marker that it was answered by the auto review, so that Review 3 can tell an automatic NO from one a reviewer gave and change it where it is wrong. A call that failed inside its first year, or whose age at failure is not known, shall never be answered automatically, and no Review 2 a person has begun or completed shall be altered. A standing rule that answers a quality question is itself a judgement, so it belongs to the person who authorised it rather than to the system; and a failure in the first year is exactly the case the warranty question exists for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-268** — A PM call whose consumption is a Spare joins the DCCR review | High | OQ-266 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-268.** *(v0.10.133 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-268.1 A consumption line of quantity above 0 on a PM call whose part (the code before "|") is categorised Spare in the Part Master shall open the call's DCCR review with Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration set to SPARE; an existing review shall not be changed. FRS-268.2 The Daily Complaint Review Register and its counts shall list every Field call and every PM call that has a DCCR review, each reader seeing only the calls the call policies give them. FRS-268.3 The 2026 PM calls already carrying a Spare shall be added once (0397); a part the Part Master does not yet categorise Spare adds nothing, and the addition shall be re-runnable once the mapping is complete. FRS-268.4 DCCR rows whose UC Number is an Excel date serial (five digits) or "-" and that match no call shall be removed (0398). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-06: "if a Consumption indicates a Spare then it should be added to DCCR Review ... use the Current Data and Lets review it again and add old calls once the mapping is complete".

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-099.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-099.1 The review drawer shall list the Field Failure Reports already raised on the call, as Already reported, above the Raise FFR action. FRS-099.2 Raise FFR (on the review) and ＋ Raise FFR (on the register) shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage, and the database (ffr_write) shall refuse an insert from anybody else. FRS-099.3 Raise FFR on the review shall open the Field Failure Register form filled from the review and the call. FRS-099.4 The form so filled shall warn where the call is not yet solved. FRS-099.5 ＋ Raise FFR on the register shall open a blank form. FRS-099.6 A report raised by hand shall be numbered, stamped and validated exactly as FRS-109 states for every report. FRS-099.7 A report raised by hand shall also start with CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status blank, the table defaults included.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

### URS-083 — Answering many calls at once, or saving as one chooses, never answers a question nobody looked at

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A reviewer authorised to complete the review shall be able to answer Review 2 = NO for many calls in one confirmed action. Calls that failed inside their first year, calls whose age at failure is unknown and calls whose Review 2 is already answered shall never be included, and the database shall refuse them whatever the screen sends; the action shall be recorded with who took it and how many calls it answered. A reviewer shall also be able to have answers saved as they are chosen (auto save), as a personal choice with an organisation default, provided that every saved answer is attributed to the person whose session saved it and that no keystroke commits a value on its own. Both are conveniences on a quality record, so each must leave the record exactly as a careful reviewer answering one call at a time would have left it.

| **FRS-102** — Auto save on the review | High | OQ-90 |

FRS-101.3 The screen shall ask for confirmation in a dialogue stating how many calls will be answered before writing any. FRS-101.4 bulk_set_review2() (0119) shall refuse a caller without review.edit and an empty selection. FRS-101.6 The reviewer recorded on each answer shall be the person whose session made the bulk action (FRS-069). ### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

### URS-085 — A failure is counted against the product that failed, without rewriting the call

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

In Review 3 the reviewer shall code the failure — complaint grouping, root cause key word, and whether the remedy was a spare, a consumable, a correction or a calibration — choosing from lists kept per product, and shall be able to record that what failed was an accessory or another product line rather than the machine the call names. Every analysis of failures shall then count the failure against the product the review records, while the call itself stays as it was registered. The review shall carry the service department’s observation and the action taken, the action reading FFR Generation until the report number is recorded. A failure counted against the wrong product line misstates the failure rate of two products at once, and rewriting the call to fix it would falsify what the customer reported.

FRS-105.2 A value already recorded that is no longer on the list shall be kept and shown, not cleared. FRS-105.3 Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration shall be chosen from a pick list. FRS-105.4 Change product? shall record, on the review, the product line that actually failed, and shall not alter the product or serial of the call.
