**FRS-205.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-205.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a fleet failure where the same Standard Complaint appears on at least the stated number of distinct serials of the same product within the stated number of days, the call under review counted. FRS-205.2 frequent_failure(ucn) shall count distinct serials, so repeated calls on one serial do not fire the fleet rule. FRS-205.3 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a call a frequent failure where either rule fires, and shall name which rule fired. FRS-205.4 The fleet rule’s on/off, window (days, at least 1, default 30) and distinct serials (at least 2, default 2) shall be held in app_settings and editable in Admin Config. FRS-205.5 The window of the fleet rule shall be held in DAYS and separately from rule 1’s window in months, so a change to one cannot move the other. FRS-205.6 An answer already recorded in call_reviews.frequent_failure shall not be re-based when a rule changes. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-15: "Rule 2, Same Complaint across same product, but multiple serial nos in the last 30 days." Thirty days and a month differ in February, which is why it is days. Proved by supabase/tests/frequent_failure_rule2_test.sql.

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

### URS-075 — A request may be corrected until it has been answered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow a request for service to be corrected while it is awaiting a decision. The system shall prevent alteration of what a request asked for once a call has been raised from it. A request corrected after the call exists leaves two records of one event disagreeing about the customer, the machine or the fault, and the call is the record every count, report and review reads.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-124** — A correction holds the controls the request was raised under | High | OQ-112 |
| **FRS-087** — Correcting a call request, and the freeze that ends it | Medium | OQ-75 |

**FRS-124.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-124.1 Correcting a Pending request shall offer the product and serial through the same machine search as the request form (CR-006), and the party shall be read off the machine chosen (CR-005) except on an installation request (CR-017). FRS-124.2 The Standard Complaint shall be chosen from the product's complaint master with no free text (CR-015, FRS-053). FRS-124.3 The call type shall be chosen from the call-type master. FRS-124.4 The submitted-by address (`email`) and the REQID shall not be correctable, the raiser being the database's to record (CR-028). FRS-124.5 The planned date shall be entered through a date control and stored as a date or as NULL. FRS-124.6 A correction the database applied to no row shall be reported as “Nothing was saved”, naming who may make it, never as saved. FRS-124.7 A correction shall change only the columns listed in FRS-087.1. RATIONALE: every field of the correction editor is a plain text box today, so a Standard Complaint no analysis will match, a serial on no register and a party the machine does not name can each be written through it, and `email` is correctable although `cr_read` grants visibility on it — a raiser can hand the request out of their own sight or into somebody else's (D-030). .6 is met today and is kept because RLS refuses an UPDATE with zero rows, not an error.

**FRS-087.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-087.1 The request register shall allow an operator holding call-creation rights, registration rights or authorship of the request to alter the customer, the machine, the fault, the engineer and the plan recorded on it. FRS-087.2 The request register shall refuse every such alteration to a request whose status is other than Pending. FRS-087.3 The database shall refuse every such alteration to a request whose status is other than Pending. FRS-087.4 The database shall name, in its refusal, each field it refused. FRS-087.5 The database shall permit alteration of the unique call number, the status, the actioning operator, the actioning time, the cancellation reason and the cancellation time in every status. FRS-087.6 The request register shall exclude the unique call number and the status from the fields an operator may alter. RATIONALE: FRS-087.3 repeats .2 in the DATABASE and is not redundant — `cr_update` lets the person who raised a request write their own row, so a control that lives only in the form is one a direct API call walks past. FRS-087.5 is what makes this a trigger rather than a policy: registering a request writes four of those columns and cancelling writes three, so a rule over the whole row would refuse the very actions that answer a request.

### URS-065 — A recovered quality record is reviewed before it is written

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where records of work already done are recovered from a superseded system, each shall be resolved to the record it belongs to AND SHOWN TO AN OPERATOR BEFORE ANY OF IT IS WRITTEN, and only rows that resolved cleanly shall be written. A visit attached to the wrong call, or carrying another machine’s photograph, is a worse outcome than a visit still missing: the first is a false record of what was done to a device, the second is a gap that is visible as a gap. Rows that did not resolve shall be reported with the reason and left unwritten rather than written with a guess.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-140** — Solved Without a Report, and the two lists' chips and wording | Medium | OQ-131, OQ-132 |
| **FRS-145** — Bulk Report Mapping: who may use it, and what it keeps | Medium | OQ-128 |
| **FRS-077** — Bulk Report Mapping reads, resolves and only then writes | High | OQ-58 |

**FRS-140.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-140.1 Solved Without a Report shall list, from a `security_invoker` view, every call reading Solved whose record has no visit, no visit date, no service report, or a visit entry date equal to its import stamp, naming every gap on the row and omitting unsolved calls and complete ones. FRS-140.2 Gap chips (and on Feedback Without a Report, finding chips) shall show exact counts, a record counting under each of its gaps, and a click shall narrow the list. FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. FRS-140.5 A load failure shall name the missing migration or grant, or show the error verbatim. FRS-140.6 Each list shall export to Excel, with an About sheet explaining each gap and the scope, or to CSV, through FRS-138. FRS-140.7 Refresh shall re-read the list. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-145.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-145.1 Bulk Report Mapping shall be open only to an administrator or a holder of `calls.report`, with the database connected, and shall say so to anyone else. FRS-145.2 The preview may be narrowed to the rows with a problem. FRS-145.3 A column of the file the screen does not recognise shall be kept on the visit written, under its own heading. FRS-145.4 A row with no attachment resolved shall be skipped at write, not written without its report, whether or not step 2 was run.

**FRS-077.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* The screen runs in three stated steps and in this order: READ the sheet and work out which call each row belongs to; RESOLVE the superseded system’s file references into links; WRITE only the rows that came through both cleanly. Nothing is written until the operator has SEEN what each row resolved to, and rows that did not resolve are listed with the reason and are not written. The register it writes into is the visit history, whose records are never deleted, so a wrong write cannot be taken back — which is why the review is a step rather than a confirmation dialogue. Bulk Report Mapping shall count a visit as attached only when the update changed it, and stop, naming the visit, when row-level security matched nothing (D-091).

FRS-120.9 reopen_call() shall refuse an empty reason (D-025). FRS-120.10 Visits and spares shall be matched on call number or UCN, report links shall open in a new tab, and a solved call with no visit shall be stated as the finding. FRS-120.11 Marking, Reco and Re-open shall each be written to the audit trail; a reader without callreview.mark shall be told so; errors and successes shall be shown; Refresh shall re-read the list. **FRS-063.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A register (call_report_reviews, one row per call) records that a closed call’s report has been reviewed, with the reviewer taken from the authenticated session and a caller-supplied identity discarded. Writing requires the callreview.mark permission and visibility of the call; reading follows the call’s own visibility. The register lists solved calls only — a report-pending call has no report to review — filtered in the database.

**FRS-064.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* From the review the reviewer may book a Reconciliation consumption line against the call, off the ATTENDING engineer's hand stock and capped at what that engineer holds by the same database trigger as any other consumption; or re-open the call, which the review refuses without a reason. The reason is required on screen and is NOT yet recorded on the call: reopen_call() discards it (D-035); FRS-133.4 states the requirement. After re-opening the call leaves the review list. Consumption shown for a call is matched on the call number OR the unique call number, so a call predating the call-number series still shows its parts.

### URS-058 — A judgement on a quality record names the person who made it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where the system records a judgement about a product failure, it shall record WHO made that judgement. Where a person answers, the identity shall be taken from the authenticated session at the moment the judgement is completed and not from a value supplied by the caller. Where the answer is given by a standing rule that an authorised person has switched on, the judgement shall be attributed to the person who switched the rule on, and the record shall also state that the rule gave it. Where a judgement made before this system is loaded from a historical file, the reviewer and the date the file records shall be kept, and the person loading it shall not be recorded as its maker. The identity shall not be displaced by later editing of the same record, and where the judgement is carried onto a further record the person shall be carried with it. No record shall attribute a judgement to a screen, a process or the system itself.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |
| **FRS-069** — The reviewer is stamped by the database at completion | High | OQ-52 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

**FRS-069.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A BEFORE trigger on `call_reviews` (0173) records `review2_by_uid` / `review3_by_uid` from auth.uid() at the moment a review stage becomes COMPLETE, and fills the display name from User Master where the client sent none — so the automatic-save and bulk-review paths, which send no name, record a person instead of nothing. A name the client did send is kept: it is what the reviewer saw on screen. A later edit does NOT re-stamp: the person who answered the review is the reviewer, not whoever last corrected a spelling. TWO PATHS ARE NOT A PERSON AT THE KEYBOARD AND ARE NOT STAMPED FROM THE SESSION: an answer given by the Review 2 auto review records the person who switched Auto Review on, with the auto-review marker (FRS-097.5), and never the session that ran or opened anything; a review loaded from a historical file keeps the reviewer names and dates the file carries, is marked imported, and has no identity of the person loading it stamped on it (FRS-100.4). The trigger evaluates the completion test from the source columns rather than reading `review2_done`, because PostgreSQL computes a GENERATED column AFTER the BEFORE triggers have run — the first version read it, stamped nothing on every path, and was caught only by exercising it against a database. The duplicated expression is compared word-for-word with its original by an automated check. raise_ffr() carries the name onto the Field Failure Report, preferring Review 3's reviewer, and no longer writes the string "Daily Call Review" — a screen is not a person, and a report that cannot name one is left blank, blank being a question somebody asks.

FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

**FRS-031.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* An authorised role may re-open a closed call and close it again without inventing a visit; the transition is recorded. Re-opening, closing, closing again, cancelling and restoring shall each be refused on a call the caller cannot see under the call read rule (0341, D-128).

### URS-046 — Repeat failure determined to the documented rule

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The review shall determine whether a call is a repeat failure by the rule the servicing procedure states — counting the call under review, within the stated window, on the same equipment or the same part in the same machine — and shall present the rule alongside the verdict so a judgement recorded under one rule is not mistaken for one recorded under another. Window and threshold shall be maintainable by an administrator without a code change. Where the machine cannot be identified the review shall say so rather than report no repeat failure.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-104** — Repeat failure across the fleet (rule 2) | High | OQ-92 |
| **FRS-205** — Frequent failure rule 2: the same complaint across the fleet | High | OQ-198 |
| **FRS-206** — Admin Config: the settings that decide quality answers | High | OQ-199 |
| **FRS-054** — Repeat-failure verdict computed in the database | High | OQ-40 |

**FRS-104.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-104.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall return a verdict of frequent when rule 1 (FRS-054) or rule 2 holds, and shall say which fired. FRS-104.2 Rule 2 shall hold where the same standard complaint is recorded on at least ffr.rule2_serials DISTINCT serials of the same product (default 2, never fewer than 2) within ffr.rule2_window_days before the call (default 30), counting serials and not calls. FRS-104.3 Rule 2 shall be switchable by ffr.rule2_enabled, and its window and serial count held in app_settings separately from rule 1’s. FRS-104.4 The review shall show, for each rule, the count, the threshold and the earlier UCNs with date, days before, engineer and what they matched on. FRS-104.5 Answers already recorded shall not be re-based when a rule or its settings change. RATIONALE: URS-046 names the procedure’s rule, which is rule 1; rule 2 (0198, the user’s of 2026-09-15) sees the batch, component or design fault that rule 1 cannot, because every one of those calls is a first failure on its own machine.

**FRS-205.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-205.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a fleet failure where the same Standard Complaint appears on at least the stated number of distinct serials of the same product within the stated number of days, the call under review counted. FRS-205.2 frequent_failure(ucn) shall count distinct serials, so repeated calls on one serial do not fire the fleet rule. FRS-205.3 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a call a frequent failure where either rule fires, and shall name which rule fired. FRS-205.4 The fleet rule’s on/off, window (days, at least 1, default 30) and distinct serials (at least 2, default 2) shall be held in app_settings and editable in Admin Config. FRS-205.5 The window of the fleet rule shall be held in DAYS and separately from rule 1’s window in months, so a change to one cannot move the other. FRS-205.6 An answer already recorded in call_reviews.frequent_failure shall not be re-based when a rule changes. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-15: "Rule 2, Same Complaint across same product, but multiple serial nos in the last 30 days." Thirty days and a month differ in February, which is why it is days. Proved by supabase/tests/frequent_failure_rule2_test.sql.

**FRS-206.** *(v0.10.89 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-206.1 Admin Config shall present the legacy importer, the Hotline desk and Audit Mode on one page, opened by mod:/admin-config. FRS-206.2 The SLA targets, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.87 (FRS-254), shall accept hours of at least 1 and on/off per rule, save only the rules changed, and display the defaults, naming 0044, where the table is missing or empty. FRS-206.3 The Hotline desk shall be chosen from the Hotline profiles, saved on choice, fall back to the single hotline profile when cleared, and display who new calls resolve to now; where no desk exists the card shall say so, and a failure to load shall name call_requests.sql. FRS-206.4 The frequent-failure rules, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.89 (FRS-254.6), shall be saved by an administrator or a holder of config.manage, the card stating on saving that the rule applies from now on and that recorded answers are unchanged. FRS-206.5 The database shall refuse a change to sla_rules or app_settings from anyone other than an administrator or a holder of config.manage. FRS-206.6 The system shall record each change to an SLA target, the Hotline desk or a frequent-failure rule with the setting, its previous and new value, who changed it and when (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because none of the three cards writes an audit entry and neither table is under record_audit, so a Review 2 verdict that differs from last month’s cannot be traced to the rule change that caused it.

**FRS-054.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `frequent_failure(ucn)` returns the verdict and the calls behind it: earlier calls on the same product and serial within the window, matched on the same complaint OR the same part fitted, counted INCLUDING the call under review against the threshold. Window, threshold and whether the same-equipment path also requires a matching complaint are held in `app_settings` and editable in Admin Config; the defaults are the procedure’s (one month, two, on). The window is measured from the CALL’s date, not today, so reopening an old review cannot change its answer. A blank serial returns `known: false` — reported as “cannot tell” rather than “no repeat failure”. SECURITY DEFINER by design: an answer narrowed to the reader’s own call scope would read LOWER than the truth. Answers already recorded are not re-based; the screen shows the rule in force with the verdict.

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. **FRS-092.** *(v0.10.106 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-092.1 Each device shall record what it holds of the offline registers in `device_cache_status`, one row per person per device, upserted on (user_id, device_id). FRS-092.2 The person on that row shall be stamped by the database from the session, any value sent by the device being discarded. FRS-092.3 A device shall write only its own row, and a person shall read only their own rows unless they hold `mod:/device-cache`. FRS-092.4 `device_cache_report()` shall refuse a caller without `mod:/device-cache`, shall not be callable without signing in, and shall return every profile including those with no device reported. FRS-092.5 A device shall report after each download completes or fails and when its user signs out, and shall not re-send an unchanged report within six hours. FRS-092.6 The report shall carry, beside the machines and customers, how many Standard Complaints (0253) and how many Part Master parts (0380) the device holds and when each was stored; the device shall keep the parts list, with each part's products and each product's accessories, for six hours and serve the spare pickers from it with no signal; the Spare Requests page and its new-request form shall show how many parts this device holds and when they were cached, with Download now to fetch a fresh copy at once, a failed download keeping the copy already held. RATIONALE: .2 because a report somebody else could file is a report nobody can rely on; .4 because the engineer most worth finding is the one with no copy anywhere, and a list of reports cannot show an absence. Proved by `supabase/tests/device_cache_status_test.sql`.

### URS-075 — A request may be corrected until it has been answered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall allow a request for service to be corrected while it is awaiting a decision. The system shall prevent alteration of what a request asked for once a call has been raised from it. A request corrected after the call exists leaves two records of one event disagreeing about the customer, the machine or the fault, and the call is the record every count, report and review reads.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-124** — A correction holds the controls the request was raised under | High | OQ-112 |
| **FRS-087** — Correcting a call request, and the freeze that ends it | Medium | OQ-75 |

**FRS-124.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-124.1 Correcting a Pending request shall offer the product and serial through the same machine search as the request form (CR-006), and the party shall be read off the machine chosen (CR-005) except on an installation request (CR-017). FRS-124.2 The Standard Complaint shall be chosen from the product's complaint master with no free text (CR-015, FRS-053). FRS-124.3 The call type shall be chosen from the call-type master. FRS-124.4 The submitted-by address (`email`) and the REQID shall not be correctable, the raiser being the database's to record (CR-028). FRS-124.5 The planned date shall be entered through a date control and stored as a date or as NULL. FRS-124.6 A correction the database applied to no row shall be reported as “Nothing was saved”, naming who may make it, never as saved. FRS-124.7 A correction shall change only the columns listed in FRS-087.1. RATIONALE: every field of the correction editor is a plain text box today, so a Standard Complaint no analysis will match, a serial on no register and a party the machine does not name can each be written through it, and `email` is correctable although `cr_read` grants visibility on it — a raiser can hand the request out of their own sight or into somebody else's (D-030). .6 is met today and is kept because RLS refuses an UPDATE with zero rows, not an error.

**FRS-087.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-087.1 The request register shall allow an operator holding call-creation rights, registration rights or authorship of the request to alter the customer, the machine, the fault, the engineer and the plan recorded on it. FRS-087.2 The request register shall refuse every such alteration to a request whose status is other than Pending. FRS-087.3 The database shall refuse every such alteration to a request whose status is other than Pending. FRS-087.4 The database shall name, in its refusal, each field it refused. FRS-087.5 The database shall permit alteration of the unique call number, the status, the actioning operator, the actioning time, the cancellation reason and the cancellation time in every status. FRS-087.6 The request register shall exclude the unique call number and the status from the fields an operator may alter. RATIONALE: FRS-087.3 repeats .2 in the DATABASE and is not redundant — `cr_update` lets the person who raised a request write their own row, so a control that lives only in the form is one a direct API call walks past. FRS-087.5 is what makes this a trigger rather than a policy: registering a request writes four of those columns and cancelling writes three, so a rule over the whole row would refuse the very actions that answer a request.

### URS-066 — A request awaiting registration is visible and is dispositioned

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A request for service that has not yet become a call shall be visible as such, and shall reach one of a stated set of outcomes — registered as a new call, mapped to an existing call, or cancelled with a reason. It shall not be possible for a request to be silently dropped or to remain in no state at all, a request nobody can see being indistinguishable from a request nobody made.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-125** — A disposition is made against a real call and confirmed written | High | OQ-113 |
| **FRS-078** — Pending Registrations is the queue, and every row leaves it by a stated route | Medium | OQ-59 |

**FRS-125.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-125.1 Pending Registrations shall map a request only to a UCN that `callByUcn()` finds; a UCN not found shall be refused with that reason and shall not be offered for confirmation. FRS-125.2 Mapping and cancelling shall count the rows written; where none were written the screen shall say the request was not changed and name the right it needs (`pending.register`). FRS-125.3 Registering a call from a request, on Pending Registrations or on arrival at a call register, shall write the new UCN and status Registered to the request and shall wait for that write; where it fails, the screen shall name the new UCN and state that the request is still pending. FRS-125.4 A cancellation shall require a reason and may carry a note; it shall record the time, and the request shall remain in the register (CR-020). FRS-125.5 A reader without `pending.register` shall see the queue and be told that they cannot action it. FRS-125.6 Every change to a request shall be captured by the database's row audit on `call_requests` (`record_audit`, 0225) with the person and the time. RATIONALE: .1 because the screen today asks “map anyway?” and closes the request against a UCN that exists nowhere; .2 and .3 because `setCallRequestUcn` and `cancelCallRequest` take no row count, and the back-fill after registering is `try { ... } catch { /* best-effort */ }` on one screen and `void` on the other — a request left Pending beside its own call is registered twice (D-031).

**FRS-078.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Pending Registrations lists requests carrying no UC Number. Opening one offers exactly three outcomes — register it as a new call, map it to an existing call (its UCN is recorded against the request), or cancel it with a reason — and the request’s status records which. IT READS `call_requests`, NOT the sheet-era `pending_registrations` table: two corrections were aimed at the wrong table before that surfaced, and the distinction is recorded in the codebase notes as well as here. Clickable Call Type filters at the top count the requests of each type that the search leaves, and filter the list to one type.

FRS-146.2 The request form shall offer two request types, Call Based and HandStock. FRS-146.3 The request form shall require a HandStock reason for a HandStock request and shall refuse the submission with "Enter the reason for the HandStock request." where it is empty. FRS-146.4 The request form shall find the call of a Call Based request by its UCN, call number, party or serial once three characters are typed, and shall offer at most 25 calls. FRS-146.5 The request form shall copy the party, product, serial, complaint and item status (cover) of the chosen call onto the request and shall not offer them for editing. FRS-146.9 The request form shall accept a quantity per part as a whole number of at least one, and shall treat a blank or lower value as one. FRS-146.10 The request form shall accept at most 20 spare rows on one request. FRS-146.11 The request form shall accept optional additional remarks. FRS-146.12 The request form shall refuse a submission with no spare ("Add at least one spare."), with no engineer, or of a Call Based request with no UCN ("A Call-Based request needs a call (UC Number)."). FRS-146.13 The database shall assign the OR number (OR-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month) and the OR request date on insert; the form shall show "OR No assigned on submit" and shall not accept either. **FRS-040.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Where a manager may act for their team, the engineer is a field on the form rather than an assumption: the Spare Request, Call Registration Request and Reporting forms offer the manager and every engineer reporting to them, defaulting to the manager. ### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

RATIONALE: .6 because none of the three cards writes an audit entry and neither table is under record_audit, so a Review 2 verdict that differs from last month’s cannot be traced to the rule change that caused it.

**FRS-051.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each call carries `created_by` — the Hotline DESK it is filed to, defaulting to the hotline-role profile or to an administrator’s configured choice (app_settings.calls.default_registrant_email) — and `actual_created_by`, the authenticated individual who registered it. A BEFORE INSERT trigger (0114, named so it fires last) sets the second from auth.uid() and DISCARDS any value the caller supplied; it accepts a supplied desk only when that user is a hotline desk, and otherwise substitutes the default. Where there is no authenticated session (a migration, a restore, an administrative load) both are kept as supplied and a missing one is filled from the other, so restored provenance is not erased. The two columns DIFFERING is the finding the control exists to produce, and the register lists and groups by the individual. Where neither can be determined — records bulk-loaded from the superseded system — both are empty and the record says so rather than implying attribution; `_registered_by_check.sql` reports where that line falls. Row-level security admits a reader on either column, so the individual who registered a call retains access to it.

### URS-080 — Review 2 is answered No automatically only while an authorised person has switched Auto Review on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Daily Complaint Review Register shall carry an AUTO REVIEW switch for Review 2. Only a person holding the permission review.auto — by role, Admin, NSM and Technical Support, or given it individually by an administrator — shall be able to turn it on or off, and the register shall show whether it is on, who set it and when. While it is on, each morning every field call logged before that day which failed outside its first year and whose Review 2 is still blank shall be answered NO on all three Review 2 questions. Each such answer shall record, as the Review 2 reviewer, the name of the person who switched Auto Review on, and shall also keep a marker that it was answered by the auto review, so that Review 3 can tell an automatic NO from one a reviewer gave and change it where it is wrong. A call that failed inside its first year, or whose age at failure is not known, shall never be answered automatically, and no Review 2 a person has begun or completed shall be altered. A standing rule that answers a quality question is itself a judgement, so it belongs to the person who authorised it rather than to the system; and a failure in the first year is exactly the case the warranty question exists for.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-096** — The Auto Review switch, and who may turn it | High | OQ-84 |
| **FRS-097** — What the auto review answers, and whom it names | High | OQ-85 |
| **FRS-268** — A PM call whose consumption is a Spare joins the DCCR review | High | OQ-266 |

**FRS-096.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-096.1 The Daily Complaint Review Register shall show an Auto Review switch stating whether automatic Review 2 answering is on or off, the name of the person who last set it, and the date and time it was set. FRS-096.2 The register shall offer the switch as operable only to a person holding review.auto, and shall show it read-only to every other reader. FRS-096.3 The database shall refuse a change of the switch from any caller not holding review.auto, whatever the screen offers. FRS-096.4 The database shall take who set the switch, and when, from the authenticated session, discarding any name or time the caller sends. FRS-096.5 Every change of the switch shall be retained, with the person, the time and the new state, in a record written only by the function that changes the switch (auto_review_changes) and not alterable through the application. FRS-096.6 review.auto shall be held by role — Admin, NSM and Technical Support (0285, which replaced the two names 0269 granted it to) — and otherwise only as a permission an administrator gives a person individually; no person shall be granted it by name in code or migration, it shall not be implied by review.edit, and for Technical Support it shall be the one write that role holds. FRS-096.7 The switch shall start OFF, and shall refuse to be switched on by a person whose sign-in carries no name on the User Master, since its answers must be able to name that person. RATIONALE: .3 because a rule that answers a quality question on many calls is itself a decision, and a control that lives on the screen alone is one a direct API call walks past. .6 because review.edit is held by every reviewing role, and the authority to have the system answer for everyone is narrower than the authority to answer one call; and because a grant by name reaches whoever the name happens to match on the day it runs, and follows nobody who changes job.

**FRS-097.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-097.1 While the switch is on, the database shall once each morning answer Risk to Patient, Warranty Failure 1 yr and Frequent Failure all NO on every field call registered before that day (India time) on which none of the three Review 2 questions has been answered. FRS-097.2 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure (complaint date, else registration date, less warranty start) is under 366 days. FRS-097.3 It shall exclude a call whose age at failure cannot be computed. FRS-097.4 It shall not alter a Review 2 that is completed or part-answered. FRS-097.5 Each answer shall record as the Review 2 reviewer the name (and the account) of the person who switched Auto Review on, as recorded by FRS-096.4 at the time of the answer, and shall carry, in a field of its own (review2_auto), a marker that the auto review gave it; the marker shall be settable by the auto review alone, a value sent through the API being discarded. FRS-097.6 The Review 2 completion date of each such answer shall be the day it was given. FRS-097.7 While the switch is off, nothing shall be answered automatically, and opening the register shall answer nothing. FRS-097.8 The answering shall not depend on anybody opening the register, and shall never record the person who happened to open it, or the session that ran it, as the reviewer. FRS-097.9 The register, the review drawer and the Review 3 view shall show, on each call answered this way, that the auto review answered Review 2, beside the name recorded. FRS-097.10 Each run shall report how many calls it answered and how many it left for a person, split into first-year and unknown-age. RATIONALE: .5 because URS-058 forbids attributing a judgement to a process — the judgement here is the standing decision of the person who switched the rule on, and the marker is what Review 3 needs in order to know it may overrule it. .4 because a part-answered Review 2 is a person in the middle of answering it. .8 because the present sweep runs from the browser of whoever opens the register and the database stamps that person on answers they never saw (D-028).

**FRS-268.** *(v0.10.133 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-268.1 A consumption line of quantity above 0 on a PM call whose part (the code before "|") is categorised Spare in the Part Master shall open the call's DCCR review with Spare / Consumable / Correction / Calibration set to SPARE; an existing review shall not be changed. FRS-268.2 The Daily Complaint Review Register and its counts shall list every Field call and every PM call that has a DCCR review, each reader seeing only the calls the call policies give them. FRS-268.3 The 2026 PM calls already carrying a Spare shall be added once (0397); a part the Part Master does not yet categorise Spare adds nothing, and the addition shall be re-runnable once the mapping is complete. FRS-268.4 DCCR rows whose UC Number is an Excel date serial (five digits) or "-" and that match no call shall be removed (0398). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-06: "if a Consumption indicates a Spare then it should be added to DCCR Review ... use the Current Data and Lets review it again and add old calls once the mapping is complete".

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

FRS-099.2 Raise FFR (on the review) and ＋ Raise FFR (on the register) shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage, and the database (ffr_write) shall refuse an insert from anybody else. ### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

### URS-087 — The review register shows every call’s stage with exact counts, and can be taken away in its own format

### URS-101 — A request is closed only against a real call, and only once that is recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A request mapped to a call that does not exist is a customer's complaint attached to nothing; a request reported as closed that is still pending gets registered a second time.

**FRS-125.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-125.1 Pending Registrations shall map a request only to a UCN that `callByUcn()` finds; a UCN not found shall be refused with that reason and shall not be offered for confirmation. FRS-125.2 Mapping and cancelling shall count the rows written; where none were written the screen shall say the request was not changed and name the right it needs (`pending.register`). FRS-125.3 Registering a call from a request, on Pending Registrations or on arrival at a call register, shall write the new UCN and status Registered to the request and shall wait for that write; where it fails, the screen shall name the new UCN and state that the request is still pending. FRS-125.4 A cancellation shall require a reason and may carry a note; it shall record the time, and the request shall remain in the register (CR-020). FRS-125.6 Every change to a request shall be captured by the database's row audit on `call_requests` (`record_audit`, 0225) with the person and the time. RATIONALE: .1 because the screen today asks “map anyway?” and closes the request against a UCN that exists nowhere; .2 and .3 because `setCallRequestUcn` and `cancelCallRequest` take no row count, and the back-fill after registering is `try { ... } catch { /* best-effort */ }` on one screen and `void` on the other — a request left Pending beside its own call is registered twice (D-031).

RATIONALE: the three fields carry `defaultValue: ’NO’` today, so a registration saved without the section being read records three answers nobody gave (D-033).

### URS-108 — A call after registration is amended, cancelled and re-opened under stated rules

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend each part of a call shall be usable wherever the call is amended, and a call that is solved or cancelled shall be amended by nobody until it is re-opened or restored. A call shall be cancelled only while nobody has yet closed it, only with a reason, and never deleted; restoring it shall keep the reason. Re-opening a closed call shall record who did it, when and why. Each rule shall be enforced by the database, so that a direct request to the data interface meets the same refusal as the screen.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-132** — Editing a call, by section, and never once it is closed | High | OQ-120 |
| **FRS-133** — Cancelling, restoring, re-opening and closing again | High | OQ-121, OQ-122, OQ-123 |

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). FRS-132.4 Visit entry and spare requests shall not be offered on a Solved, Cancelled or not-yet-synced call. FRS-132.5 A save the database applied to no row shall be reported as not saved (finding 48, `updateCall`). RATIONALE: `canEditRow` tests `can(’calls.edit’)` and `parentAction()` resolves a section key UP to its parent, never down, so a role granted only `calls.edit.contact` — the grant URS-067 exists to make possible — is offered no Edit on any register (D-034). .3 is the user's rule “Closed means closed — for admins too” and supersedes the “non-admins” wording of FRS-007.

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.5 Close again shall withdraw a re-open without adding a visit, returning the call to its last visit's state and giving the re-open count back. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

### URS-142 — A cover entry is raised, filled and priced by one rule wherever it is entered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The cover registers shall state for every entry whether it is Active, About to expire or Inactive, by one rule shared with the database, an entry with no readable end date being Not covered and never Active. A new entry shall be offered the next number in its series, which may be changed and shall be refused if already used. The customer shall be chosen from the Party Master, a customer the master does not hold being allowed; choosing a customer on a sale shall fill the address, contact and tax fields from the master, blanks included. A contract line's tax and total shall be derived from its rate by the one GST rule. A renewal shall be re-priced: no price shall be carried from the predecessor, a price entered shall be checked before anything is written, and a revision of the old price by a percentage shall be offered. The installation call for one machine may be raised from that machine, and its call number written back onto that machine only. Starting a call from a cover register shall be offered only to those who may register one.

**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). FRS-185.4 A blank rate shall mean “price it later” and be saved as no rate, tax or total. FRS-185.5 Every entered rate shall be checked before anything is written, and a rate that is not a number, or is negative, shall refuse the whole renewal. **FRS-244.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-244.1 Every write to a sale line or entry, a contract line or entry, an ownership transfer or an additional entry shall re-sync the Product Database row of that machine — product and serial together, never the serial alone — through sync_product_machine() (0330). FRS-244.3 From its latest contract line (by contract end; line, else entry): Contract No., start, end, type and status, and its PM visits, which overwrite the sale's (the user's choice) and survive the sale being saved again. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). ### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

### URS-173 — Indoor Service runs in stages, from intake to the approved delivery challan

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Indoor Service workflow shall run in stages — Intake, Cleaning, Repair, Service Report, Delivery Challan (pending approval) and Dispatched — shown on each job and on each row of the register, each job showing only the fields of its current and completed stages. Intake shall start from the call the unit came in on (chosen from the open calls of the machine, or by its UCN) and fill the job from that call — the customer and place, the engineer the call is allotted to, the machine, its current cover, the complaint — or receive a DEMO / new device with no call, and shall record the accessories received with their quantities. The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded only after the unit is cleaned, with its report number, the stored file named after that number and the uploader recorded by the system; for a unit with a call the same step shall capture the Visit Entry for that call so the work is not entered twice. A spare shall be requestable from the job through the Spare Request workflow without changing the call.

| **FRS-236** — Request spare from an Indoor job | Low | OQ-227 |
| **FRS-237** — The Indoor visit's Visiting Service Engineer is picked from the User Master | Medium | OQ-228, OQ-229 |
| **FRS-239** — The Indoor job as a window with the DC beside it, the DC in the form's language, and the register in the app's table | Medium | OQ-229 |

No, Problem Reported (the call's Complaint Reported), the call's Standard Complaint (shown read only, kept on the job as `standard_complaint`) and Status (cover) — the machine's cover now from the Product Database through coverCode(), else the call's item status; every filled value shall stay editable. FRS-232.3 A DEMO / new device shall be received with no call, as a DEMO unit, Engineer Name “Indoor Service”. FRS-232.4 The accessories received shall be an add-item list — item, quantity, serial, tag — the quantity stored on `indoor_job_accessories.qty`, default 1, refused at 0 or below by the database. FRS-232.5 Filing shall need indoor.receive and create the job (numbered by the database) and its accessory lines, then open it.
