FRS-237.4 At the DC's approval the visit shall be filed with that engineer and email (reports.engineer / engineer_email, and each consumption line's engineer) while the filer stays the approver's session; the database pins neither to the session — record_indoor_visit() and the guard check the visit's call and its three fixed values, not its engineer — so no migration was needed. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03: the person who repaired the unit is not always the person signed in, and the visit history must name who attended.

**FRS-239.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-239.1 A job shall open as a centred window (up to 1100px wide and 90% of the screen high, scrolling inside), closed by × or Esc — Esc first shutting an open pick list and leaving a drawer or confirmation opened inside it alone — showing the job number, product, serial, consignee and call. FRS-239.2 “Create Indoor DC” on the DC page shall turn the window into two panes, the job left and the DC form right, with a divider the reader drags or moves with the arrow keys between 30% and 75%, remembered per device; × on the DC pane or Esc shall return to one pane; on a phone the panes stack. The DC form shall keep every field and rule of FRS-228 / FRS-235 (To from the Party Master, MIRN / Customer Ref and its date, mode of despatch, purpose per line, Authorised By, the DC date shown, the lines with the accessories' quantities). Ticked units from the Workshop view still open the same form in a drawer. FRS-239.3 The DC form and the Indoor DC list shall use the job form's look: one column, eyebrows, hairlines, read-only values as text, one solid button, and the approval as a chip — Pending approval, Approved, Rejected (Issued before approval for a DC older than 0323) — in theme tokens and the same hue in both themes; DCs awaiting the reader marked by a solid rule and listed first. FRS-239.4 The R/SER/07 view shall be the app's register table (DataTable, storage key indoorRegister.rser07): column widths, order, wrap and the column picker the reader's, the R/SER/07 columns in the paper's order by default after the on-screen Stage column, the Indoor Service Report No cell keeping its link or Upload button, a row opening the job window, and the sheet switch, incoming-date range, Excel and Print above it. FRS-239.5 Every job is read (listIndoorJobs, a page at a time), so the register shows the exact count with no “+” and no Load more. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03: Create DC used to open a drawer BEHIND the job; the job, the DC and the register were asked to look like the rest of the app.

### URS-067 — Authority over a quality record is held section by section

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend a call in progress shall be grantable SEPARATELY for each part of the record whose amendment means a different thing: the complaint as reported, the customer and device it names, the vigilance answers, and the customer’s contact details. Re-allocating a call to another engineer, and cancelling or restoring one, shall each be their own authority. A single “edit” right cannot express the distinction the record requires — correcting a telephone number and re-answering whether a patient was harmed are not the same act — and each shall be attributable to the person who performed it.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-132** — Editing a call, by section, and never once it is closed | High | OQ-120 |
| **FRS-133** — Cancelling, restoring, re-opening and closing again | High | OQ-121, OQ-122, OQ-123 |
| **FRS-079** — The call edit rights are four sections, plus allotment and cancellation | High | OQ-60 |

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). FRS-132.4 Visit entry and spare requests shall not be offered on a Solved, Cancelled or not-yet-synced call. FRS-132.5 A save the database applied to no row shall be reported as not saved (finding 48, `updateCall`). RATIONALE: `canEditRow` tests `can(’calls.edit’)` and `parentAction()` resolves a section key UP to its parent, never down, so a role granted only `calls.edit.contact` — the grant URS-067 exists to make possible — is offered no Edit on any register (D-034). .3 is the user's rule “Closed means closed — for admins too” and supersedes the “non-admins” wording of FRS-007.

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.5 Close again shall withdraw a re-open without adding a visit, returning the call to its last visit's state and giving the re-open count back. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

**FRS-079.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance` and `calls.edit.contact` each gate one part of the record and are granted independently; `calls.allot` gates re-allocation to another engineer and `calls.cancel` gates cancelling and restoring a call. `calls.edit` remains the parent, so a role holding it holds the four sections — `parentAction()` resolves a section key to it — and a role may instead be given one section alone. `cover.edit` is the equivalent authority over the warranty and contract registers, and `admin.view` opens the administration pages READ-ONLY, so somebody may inspect configuration without the right to change users.

### URS-053 — A service record identifies the individual device

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every service call shall identify the single machine it concerns by its serial number, from the request onward. A record that names a product but not a unit cannot be traced to the device serviced, and its cover, warranty and contract cannot be established.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-119** — Machine History | High | OQ-107 |
| **FRS-124** — A correction holds the controls the request was raised under | High | OQ-112 |
| **FRS-142** — The PM batch load | High | OQ-135 |
| **FRS-061** — The serial is mandatory | High | OQ-47 |

**FRS-119.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-119.1 The product shall be chosen first and the serial list shall follow it; a new product shall clear the serial; a serial the list does not hold may be typed. FRS-119.2 Arriving from a link with a product and a serial, the serial shall be applied only if it is on that product’s list, and then looked up at once; otherwise the screen shall say so. FRS-119.3 Every register’s rows shall be filtered to the same model AND serial, never the serial alone. FRS-119.4 Where it is now shall show the holder, status, city and state, engineer, warranty number, end and state, and contract type, number, end and state, from products and machine_cover. FRS-119.5 Where the Product Database names a different party from the cover and the calls, the screen shall warn that a transfer is missing; where the machine is not on the Product Database it shall say so. FRS-119.6 The timeline shall draw on the Product Database, Call, Visit, Spare, Field Failure, Feedback, Sale/warranty, Contract, Ownership, Additional entry and Workshop registers, each row naming its register, newest first and undated rows last, with chips (and counts) filtering it by register. FRS-119.7 A voided spare shall read VOIDED, a cancelled call CANCELLED, and a migrated FFR or uploaded feedback shall be labelled so. FRS-119.8 A register whose read fails shall be named on the screen as not read, and no count shall be presented as exact while one has failed (D-019). FRS-119.9 Each register shall be read whole for the machine; where a read is capped and the cap is reached, that register’s count shall carry a “+” and the screen shall name it (D-019). FRS-119.10 The CSV export shall be available only to holders of export.data (FRS-018). FRS-119.11 Every lookup shall be written to the audit trail (machine.history). FRS-119.12 UCNs shall be coloured by call state, and the screen shall say when nothing anywhere mentions the machine, when not connected, and when the product list could not be read.

**FRS-124.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-124.1 Correcting a Pending request shall offer the product and serial through the same machine search as the request form (CR-006), and the party shall be read off the machine chosen (CR-005) except on an installation request (CR-017). FRS-124.2 The Standard Complaint shall be chosen from the product's complaint master with no free text (CR-015, FRS-053). FRS-124.3 The call type shall be chosen from the call-type master. FRS-124.4 The submitted-by address (`email`) and the REQID shall not be correctable, the raiser being the database's to record (CR-028). FRS-124.5 The planned date shall be entered through a date control and stored as a date or as NULL. FRS-124.6 A correction the database applied to no row shall be reported as “Nothing was saved”, naming who may make it, never as saved. FRS-124.7 A correction shall change only the columns listed in FRS-087.1. RATIONALE: every field of the correction editor is a plain text box today, so a Standard Complaint no analysis will match, a serial on no register and a party the machine does not name can each be written through it, and `email` is correctable although `cr_read` grants visibility on it — a raiser can hand the request out of their own sight or into somebody else's (D-030). .6 is met today and is kept because RLS refuses an UPDATE with zero rows, not an error.

**FRS-142.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-142.1 PM Bulk Upload shall refuse any user who does not hold pm.bulk_upload (an administrator holds it; 0302 made it a grantable key), and each call it creates shall still pass the PM register’s own insert policy. FRS-142.2 A CSV template may be downloaded. FRS-142.3 Headings shall be matched by alias; a row with none of party, product and serial shall be dropped as blank and counted. FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.6 Item status shall be normalised through `coverCode()` to WGP, OGP, CMC or AMC, an unrecognised value kept as written. FRS-142.7 The due month shall default to this month, earlier months being loadable; every call shall be dated the 1st of it (`reg_date`) and today recorded as `added_on` (FRS-032). FRS-142.8 The first registration time and the gap between calls shall be prefilled from the latest PM call of that month and editable. FRS-142.9 Unrecognised columns shall be kept on the call in `extra`. FRS-142.10 The first eight calls and the count shall be previewed before import. FRS-142.11 A PM call shall be keyed on product, serial and due month, so that loading the same file again updates the calls it names rather than creating them again. FRS-142.12 Calls shall be written in batches with progress, the database assigning UCN and Call Number; a stop shall state how many were created. FRS-142.13 The loaded file may be cleared. RATIONALE: `pmImport.ts` keeps any row with a party OR a product, so a PM call with no serial is created (URS-053), and the writer is insert-only with “no key to re-run against”, so a file loaded twice is every call twice (URS-062) (D-038).

**FRS-061.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The serial number is a required field on the call request and on the Field, Installation, PM and pending-registration call forms. The request refuses an item without one, and names the cause where the machine is absent from Product Database rather than inviting the field to be skipped. The request identifier is composed REQID-Product-Serial, so a missing serial is visible in the key itself.

**FRS-110.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-110.1 A report shall be editable from its table row or from Edit / weekly review on the desk, and both shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage; the database (ffr_update) shall refuse anybody else. FRS-110.2 The edit form shall carry the weekly review date, the reviewer and the attachment, so that recording a weekly review clears Due a review. FRS-110.3 The update log (FRS-070) shall be shown with the report. FRS-110.4 The desk shall list reports with search and the chips All, Open and Due a review (open and not reviewed within 7 days), and shall show the report and the call as it stands now, in panes whose widths are remembered. FRS-110.5 The live call shall be shown beside each report, marked — withdrawn where the review no longer answers YES. FRS-110.6 ffr_read shall give a holder of ffr.view the whole register, and anybody else the reports on calls they may see or reports they raised (0165, 0176). FRS-110.7 An empty register shown to a reader without ffr.view shall say that it may be their access rather than an empty register. FRS-110.8 No report shall be deletable (0166). FRS-110.9 Year and product filters (opening on the current year, by FFR date, products limited to the chosen years) shall apply to the register and to Insights alike, and a filter matching nothing shall offer to clear them. FRS-110.10 The table view shall offer search, status buttons All, Open, Closed and Cancelled, and a CSV export available only to holders of export.data, warning when more than 5,000 rows were read.

**FRS-111.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-111.1 ffr_call_context() (0178) shall return the visits and spares of a report’s call to a caller holding ffr.view, an office role or administration, even where the caller cannot see the call itself. FRS-111.2 It shall return nothing for a UCN that carries no Field Failure Report, and nothing to a caller without that authority, so that it is not a general reader of calls. FRS-111.3 It shall leave the call’s own engineer and team with everything they could see before. FRS-111.4 The printable report (/ffr/:ffrNo) shall open only for a reader who may open the Field Failure Register (mod:/failure-report), and shall otherwise say that the reader cannot open it; within that, row-level security shall decide which report is found. FRS-111.5 The printable report shall lay out R-SER-03 Rev 02 from the same form definition as the Word copy (FRS-067), with Print, a Word copy download written to the audit trail, and Back to the register. FRS-111.6 The register's count shall carry a + once it reaches the 5,000 the register reads, and a failed read of the call report reviews shall be reported rather than read as no review (D-135). RATIONALE: .1 deliberately widens visibility (the user, 2026-09-12: a right to read a failure report that does not carry the visits it was raised from is not much of a right), so .2 is what keeps it to that and nothing more. .4 because the print route sits outside the module guard today (D-026).

**FRS-117.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-117.1 A section shall appear only when the reader holds the module key of the register behind it, tested before anything is requested, so that no request is made otherwise. FRS-117.2 Each section shall load on its own and in a fixed order, and a section that fails shall show its own error while the others arrive. FRS-117.3 Loading shall begin only once the reader’s reporting team is known. FRS-117.4 Spare Requests shall show Awaiting me, In approval, Awaiting dispatch, Dispatched, Received and Rejected, computed with the register’s own stage rule, each opening Spare Requests filtered to that stage. FRS-117.5 RM Approval shall show the number waiting, the engineers waiting and the longest wait in days. FRS-117.6 Pending Dispatch shall show spares waiting, those waiting a week or more, units, engineers and orders. FRS-117.7 Hand Stock shall show Short (opening Hand Stock filtered to short lines), units in the field, engineers holding, part codes, stock out, consumed and returned. FRS-117.8 Material Returns shall show MRNs, lines, good quantity and defective quantity; Stock Transfer shall show transfers, lines, units moved and engineers involved. FRS-117.9 Daily Complaint Review shall show exact counts of Review 1, 2 and 3 Pending, Any Potential Effect, Completed and Calls in view, each opening the register filtered to the rows counted — Any Potential Effect to the potential-effect calls (D-022). FRS-117.10 A count taken over a read that stopped at its 4,000-row budget shall carry a “+”. FRS-117.11 A card that is a figure shall open nothing and shall not be styled as a link. FRS-117.12 Each section shall offer Open the register; the page shall offer Refresh, the time of the last read and the number of cards, say Counting N more registers while sections load, say when not connected, and say when no register is open to the reader.

**FRS-131.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-131.1 Each register shall show the 800 most recent calls, Load more adding 800, and its count shall carry a “+” while more exist. FRS-131.2 Of the calls the database returns, an engineer shall be shown their own and a manager their team's; a call with no allottee shall be shown to every reader the database returns it to, so that the desk which must allot it can find it. FRS-131.3 An Open only toggle shall be on by default for engineers. FRS-131.4 A Re-opened chip shall narrow the list to re-opened calls and show their count. FRS-131.5 Engineer chips shall show each engineer's count, with a “+” while more exist, narrow the list on a click and be remembered per user. FRS-131.6 Aging shall show whole days since registration and shall stop, saying on which date, when the call is Solved or Cancelled. FRS-131.7 UCN and Call Status shall be coloured by the latest visit in the fixed code, and the re-open count shown on hover. FRS-131.8 The header shall state the reader's visibility scope, the data source and the time since the last sync. FRS-131.9 The table's Filters panel, column picker, sort, column order and widths shall be remembered per user. FRS-131.10 The grid columns shall be exportable to CSV through the export gate (FRS-138), warning when the load is partial or a search stopped at 1,000. FRS-131.11 Arriving with a UCN to edit shall open that call whether or not it is among the rows loaded, and arriving with a search shall open the register already searched. FRS-131.12 The same actions shall be offered in one order on the row and at the top of an opened call. FRS-131.13 A manager without `calls.allot` shall be told where the right is granted. FRS-131.14 On the sheet path the list shall be reused while under 30 minutes old and re-synced every 30 minutes. RATIONALE: .11 because an edit link to a call older than the 800 loaded opens nothing and says nothing (D-040).

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-170.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-170.1 The 🔐 Access drawer shall let an administrator set a person's role and tick individual permissions, held in `profiles.extra_permissions` and honoured by `has_perm()` on top of the role; the database shall accept the write only from an administrator. FRS-170.2 The Access drawer shall show every individual permission the person holds beside those the role gives. FRS-170.3 ⧉ Clone shall create a new login carrying the source person's role and individual permissions, shall add `data.view_all` only when “can see all records” is ticked, and shall say that ticking it grants sight of every record. FRS-170.4 Every access save, clone and login creation shall be written to the audit trail, a clone naming the person copied. FRS-170.5 Saving a User Master row whose role differs from the person's sign-in shall write the role to the sign-in, or say that it could not and which role the sign-in keeps; a person with no sign-in shall be told they receive it on first sign-in. FRS-170.6 The User Master shall count the people whose sign-in role differs from the directory, show “X (now Y)” against each, and offer to apply the directory's role, writing each person separately, naming each failure and auditing each change. RATIONALE: .2 because an individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, and authority not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews. .6 one person at a time so that one failure does not leave the office unsure which of forty changes happened.

**FRS-203.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-203.1 Roles & Permissions shall allow change to a holder of rbac.manage, display the matrix read-only to a holder of admin.view, and state to anyone else that they lack permission. FRS-203.2 Roles & Permissions shall display the permissions stored for each role and shall not re-seed the matrix over an edit in progress. FRS-203.3 Roles & Permissions shall group pages by menu heading, then page, then action, each level expandable, with controls expanding and collapsing every level. FRS-203.4 Roles & Permissions shall grant the right to open a page (View) and each action on it separately per role, and shall provide a control granting or removing every right on one page for one role. FRS-203.5 Roles & Permissions shall display the administrator role holding every permission, and shall not allow it to be narrowed. FRS-203.6 Roles & Permissions shall, on Save, write only the roles the operator changed, re-assert the administrator’s full set where it has fallen behind, and state "Nothing was changed" when nothing was. FRS-203.7 Roles & Permissions shall refuse to save a role left with no permission (URS-056). FRS-203.8 The system shall record each saved change with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when (D-067). FRS-203.9 Roles & Permissions shall export the matrix as .xlsx — a Matrix sheet (group, page, route, grant, key, Yes / No per role), a Roles sheet (permissions held, stored or NOT CONFIGURED fallback) and a How to read this sheet (who, when, saved or UNSAVED) — recorded as rbac.export and available to rbac.manage and admin.view. FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.11 Each page's row shall list every key its controls test, including a key of another module used on that page, so a control is governed by a tick shown where the control is (findings 63 and 64). FRS-203.12 The Installation Call and PM Call registers, the Contract Register, the Objective page, chart sharing, validation results, shared table layouts, the Product Database 2.0 rebuild, deleting a Tracker item and returning stock in another engineer's name shall each be governed by keys of their own, and each screen shall ask the key the database asks. FRS-203.13 A key may have parent keys; holding a parent shall grant its children in the database and in the application alike, from one list held in both (public.perm_parents, PERM_PARENTS), and the matrix shall show a child held through its parent as held; unticking it shall untick the parent and tick the parent's other children in their own right, so the role loses only that child (the user, 2026-10-02: “All Greyed out Permissions should be editable”). Manage users, Edit masters, Edit sales / warranties, Edit contracts and each register's Edit and Report keys shall be parents of their parts (finding 67). FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). FRS-203.15 A new per-page key shall be granted once to exactly the roles and people holding the key it replaces, and a re-run shall not restore a key an administrator has since removed. RATIONALE: .6 because permsForRole() returns the STORED set whenever it is non-empty, so a save that rewrote every role would replace an administrator’s tuning with whatever the screen held; .8 because rbac.save records only the role keys, and app_roles is not one of the ten tables record_audit covers — today nothing can say what a role could do on a given day.

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-212.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-212.1 An administrator shall be able to choose any profile (searchable, the first 60 shown) and see the application with that person’s permissions until Exit, the choice surviving a reload, with a banner throughout. FRS-212.2 While previewing, the application shall refuse every write — insert, update, delete, a function call that writes, a file upload — stating that a preview is read-only (D-069). FRS-212.3 The system shall record each start and end of a preview with the administrator and the person previewed (D-069). FRS-212.4 A screen that narrows its rows to the previewed person (Hand Stock, Stock Transfer, MRN, Spare Requests) shall do so by that person’s name and address. RATIONALE: .2 — the component’s own comment says "Nothing is written — a read-only preview" and nothing enforces it; a write made during a preview runs under the administrator’s session while the screen shows another person, so the record is attributed to the administrator and believed to be the other person’s.

**FRS-213.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-213.1 The menu shall show an entry exactly when the route guard would open its page for that person. FRS-213.2 The route guard shall state, for a known screen the person may not open, that they lack access and whom to ask, and shall send an unknown address to the Dashboard. FRS-213.3 The address /users shall open the User Master. FRS-213.4 The printable routes (/dc/, /declaration/, /ffr/, /indoor-pdt/, /indoor-register/, /indoor-dc/, /mtn/, /mrn-print/) shall render without the menu, their rows bounded by row-level security; /ffr/ shall require the Field Failure Register's module key, the three indoor routes the Indoor Service Register's, /mtn/ the Stock Transfer screen's and /mrn-print/ the Material Returns screen's. FRS-213.5 A screen that fails to render shall show an error in its own place, the menu and header remaining. FRS-213.6 While a saved session is restored the application shall show Loading rather than the sign-in screen. FRS-213.7 The menu shall be grouped, each group and the whole menu collapsible, the sidebar collapsible to icons and remembered per device, and shown as a drawer on a narrow screen; the Knowledge Base heading shall flash until a page in it has been opened on the device. FRS-213.8 The header search shall list the screens the person may open, and from three characters the records they may open (FRS-218); Enter shall open the highlighted entry, the first by default. FRS-213.9 The header shall show a breadcrumb (group · screen), the person’s name and designation, "Permission · <role>", and a menu offering My Profile, Clear Cache and Update, and Sign out. FRS-213.10 A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be able to switch between team calls and own calls, the choice remembered. FRS-213.11 The counts beside menu entries shall carry "+" where they are taken from a partial read. FRS-213.12 The update banner shall check version.json when the tab gains focus and every 5 minutes, name the new version only where it differs from the running one and otherwise say the running build is older, and Update now shall clear the screen caches, keep the offline registers and reload. FRS-213.13 Clear Cache and Update shall clear the screen and dropdown caches, the browser caches and service workers, and reload, keeping the offline registers. FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. **FRS-003.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each role maps to a permission set (app_roles). Data visibility is scoped by a reporting tree resolved from User Master; enforced in the client and, authoritatively, by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.

**FRS-004.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every read/write is governed by RLS policies keyed on the authenticated user (auth.uid()) and SECURITY DEFINER helper functions; the UI gate is secondary.

**FRS-014.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock, transfers and returns are scoped to the reporting tree at the database, so a user sees only their own and their team’s stock.

**FRS-050.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every view over a table carrying row-level security is created `security_invoker`, so the policies are evaluated for the READER. `create or replace view` does not carry the setting over, and a view running as its owner returns everything with no error and no warning. `npm run check:views` fails on any view over an RLS-protected table that lacks it, and `_status.sql` reports it on a live project; views intentionally readable by every signed-in user are enumerated with their reason.

### URS-003 — Register a service call

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

| **FRS-005** — Call registration & UCN | High | OQ-03 |
| **FRS-006** — Call type segregation | Medium | OQ-04 |

**FRS-182.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-182.1 The Product Database shall have no path that writes a machine. FRS-182.2 It shall filter by party, product, serial and status, the status being the derived cover status rather than a stored one. FRS-182.3 A search that times out shall say how to narrow it and keep the database's message. FRS-182.4 “+ Field” shall be offered on a machine only to holders of calls.create, and “+ Install” only to holders of install.create; each shall open its call form filled with the machine's customer, product, serial and cover. FRS-182.5 The database shall refuse an installation call from anybody without install.create, whatever screen it was started from (FRS-008). FRS-182.6 The Product Master shall list every product line — code, name, type, category, short form, still sold, added on, added by — with All / Active / Inactive counts that are exact, shall be searchable, and shall have no path that writes a line other than its Imported column (FRS-227). FRS-182.7 It shall state that an Inactive line takes no new Sale Entry and still takes contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback, and where it is empty shall point to Bulk Uploads and name the permission needed. FRS-182.8 The Sale Entry's product picker shall offer only Active lines, pair code and name where the catalogue gives one answer, count the retired lines it does not offer and say why, and accept a product the catalogue does not hold. FRS-182.9 No signed-in user shall delete a machine through the API: adding and editing stay with masters.edit.records, and a machine is removed only from the SQL editor (D-139). RATIONALE: .8 is guidance and not a control, and is stated as such: a trigger refusing a retired line would also refuse the historical sales import, in which 30 of 53 lines are retired and the sales really happened, and a catalogue kept by hand may lack a real line. `product_line_sellable()` (0193) holds the same rule in SQL. .4 is open for “+ Install”, offered today to calls.create (D-063).

**FRS-005.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Registering a request or a direct call inserts a call row; a database trigger assigns a unique UCN (date + type letter F/I/P + sequence) and a Call Number (request UniqueID or CLYY##### running series).

**FRS-006.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Field, Installation and PM calls are stored in separate physical tables (field_calls / installation_calls / pm_calls) behind a compatibility view with routing triggers; a CHECK constraint prevents mis-filing.

FRS-120.9 reopen_call() shall refuse an empty reason (D-025). FRS-120.10 Visits and spares shall be matched on call number or UCN, report links shall open in a new tab, and a solved call with no visit shall be stated as the finding. FRS-120.11 Marking, Reco and Re-open shall each be written to the audit trail; a reader without callreview.mark shall be told so; errors and successes shall be shown; Refresh shall re-read the list. FRS-120.12 A call's visits shall be found by its UCN or its call number, and a read that fails shall say so rather than read as no visit (D-131).

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.5 Close again shall withdraw a re-open without adding a visit, returning the call to its last visit's state and giving the re-open count back. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

**FRS-031.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* An authorised role may re-open a closed call and close it again without inventing a visit; the transition is recorded. Re-opening, closing, closing again, cancelling and restoring shall each be refused on a call the caller cannot see under the call read rule (0341, D-128).

### URS-044 — Attributable registration

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A registered call shall record BOTH the Hotline desk it belongs to and the individual who registered it. Only the Hotline engineer is trained on the vigilance questions answered at registration, so a call registered by anyone else shall be identifiable from the record without reconstruction. The individual shall be taken from the authenticated session and shall not be settable by the application or by a client of the API.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |
| **FRS-206** — Admin Config: the settings that decide quality answers | High | OQ-199 |
| **FRS-051** — Two names on a registration | High | OQ-37 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

**FRS-206.** *(v0.10.89 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-206.1 Admin Config shall present the legacy importer, the Hotline desk and Audit Mode on one page, opened by mod:/admin-config. FRS-206.2 The SLA targets, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.87 (FRS-254), shall accept hours of at least 1 and on/off per rule, save only the rules changed, and display the defaults, naming 0044, where the table is missing or empty. FRS-206.3 The Hotline desk shall be chosen from the Hotline profiles, saved on choice, fall back to the single hotline profile when cleared, and display who new calls resolve to now; where no desk exists the card shall say so, and a failure to load shall name call_requests.sql. FRS-206.4 The frequent-failure rules, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.89 (FRS-254.6), shall be saved by an administrator or a holder of config.manage, the card stating on saving that the rule applies from now on and that recorded answers are unchanged. FRS-206.5 The database shall refuse a change to sla_rules or app_settings from anyone other than an administrator or a holder of config.manage. FRS-206.6 The system shall record each change to an SLA target, the Hotline desk or a frequent-failure rule with the setting, its previous and new value, who changed it and when (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because none of the three cards writes an audit entry and neither table is under record_audit, so a Review 2 verdict that differs from last month’s cannot be traced to the rule change that caused it.

**FRS-051.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each call carries `created_by` — the Hotline DESK it is filed to, defaulting to the hotline-role profile or to an administrator’s configured choice (app_settings.calls.default_registrant_email) — and `actual_created_by`, the authenticated individual who registered it. A BEFORE INSERT trigger (0114, named so it fires last) sets the second from auth.uid() and DISCARDS any value the caller supplied; it accepts a supplied desk only when that user is a hotline desk, and otherwise substitutes the default. Where there is no authenticated session (a migration, a restore, an administrative load) both are kept as supplied and a missing one is filled from the other, so restored provenance is not erased. The two columns DIFFERING is the finding the control exists to produce, and the register lists and groups by the individual. Where neither can be determined — records bulk-loaded from the superseded system — both are empty and the record says so rather than implying attribution; `_registered_by_check.sql` reports where that line falls. Row-level security admits a reader on either column, so the individual who registered a call retains access to it.

### URS-108 — A call after registration is amended, cancelled and re-opened under stated rules

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend each part of a call shall be usable wherever the call is amended, and a call that is solved or cancelled shall be amended by nobody until it is re-opened or restored. A call shall be cancelled only while nobody has yet closed it, only with a reason, and never deleted; restoring it shall keep the reason. Re-opening a closed call shall record who did it, when and why. Each rule shall be enforced by the database, so that a direct request to the data interface meets the same refusal as the screen.

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). FRS-132.4 Visit entry and spare requests shall not be offered on a Solved, Cancelled or not-yet-synced call. FRS-132.5 A save the database applied to no row shall be reported as not saved (finding 48, `updateCall`). RATIONALE: `canEditRow` tests `can(’calls.edit’)` and `parentAction()` resolves a section key UP to its parent, never down, so a role granted only `calls.edit.contact` — the grant URS-067 exists to make possible — is offered no Edit on any register (D-034). .3 is the user's rule “Closed means closed — for admins too” and supersedes the “non-admins” wording of FRS-007.

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

FRS-244.3 From its latest contract line (by contract end; line, else entry): Contract No., start, end, type and status, and its PM visits, which overwrite the sale's (the user's choice) and survive the sale being saved again. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). FRS-244.6 A contract or warranty number a machine carries that a register line holds for ANOTHER model sharing its serial shall be cleared with its dates and type; one no register holds is left. FRS-244.7 Status: a current contract is its type, a current warranty WGP, a machine the registers know with neither OGP. ### URS-179 — A product failure is a field call within months of installation, measured over a rolling period

*v0.10.87 · 04-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall compute each product failure rate objective as the share of the machines of that product installed (warranty start) in a rolling period ending at the month’s cut-off that had a field call on their serial within a stated number of months of installation, counting a machine once however many calls it had, and leaving out a cancelled call, a call before installation and a machine with no warranty start. The number of months and the rolling period shall be maintainable by an administrator, or by a role the administrator grants, on an SLA / Objective Configuration page under Admin, without a code change, defaulting to 3 and 12; every change shall be recorded with the old and new value, who and when; and a change shall alter no figure already written until the objectives are re-calculated. By default only the Admin role shall be given that page. The user, 2026-10-04: "For Product Failures, The Concept is - Failure Within 3 Months, But a Rolling Average for 12 Months".

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-254** — SLA / Objective Configuration, and the failure-within-months rule | High | OQ-250 |

FRS-254.2 It shall present the SLA targets (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.2) and the Product Failure rule: the months after installation within which a field call is a failure (default 3) and the rolling period (default 12), each a whole number from 1 to 120, editable by a holder of objective.manage, and the database shall refuse the change from anyone else. FRS-254.3 objective_value() for failure_rate_12m shall return, for the period end E, the machines of the product (and serial pattern) with a serial and a warranty start in (E − rolling months, E] that have a non-cancelled field call on the same serial (trimmed, case-blind) and product pattern registered from the warranty start to the warranty start plus the window months and not after E, over all such machines; NULL when there are none. FRS-254.4 objective_evidence() shall return one failure row per failed machine (its first call in the window, with the installation date, the days after it and the number of calls in the window), the installed machines, and a filter row stating the rule, so the workbook counts to the figure. FRS-254.5 A missing setting shall fall back to 3 and 12; a change shall be stamped with who and when from the session and recorded in the audit trail with the old and new value; no figure shall change until Re-calculate. FRS-254.7 Re-calculating every computed objective of a year shall complete within the database statement time limit on a register of 20,000 machines and 40,000 calls: the failure rate shall be computed as one join of the window’s machines to the window’s calls, planned with its values on every run (0359; measured 0.7 s for six objectives over ten months, against about 47 s for 0357, which timed out on the live project). FRS-254.6 It shall also present the frequent-failure rules Review 2 applies (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.4), unchanged in behaviour and permission. *v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall list, for a chosen month, the machines whose warranty or contract has a PM visit due in that month, worked out from the cover's start date, period and PM visits: visit k falls on the start date plus k times (months x 30 / PM visits) days. Each shall be shown as Generated when a PM call for that visit (reading k / N) exists for the machine and is not cancelled, and as a Missed PM otherwise, and the list shall be filterable by Missed PM / Generated, by Products / Accessories, and by product. The coordinator shall be able to create those calls, dated the 1st of the month, registered after the month's latest PM call and allotted to the Product Database's engineer. The monthly PM upload shall remain. The user, 2026-10-08: "Can we do PM generation from Contract and warranty register?"; the first visit of a cover starting 10 January with 3 visits in 12 months is due on its 120th day; "it should check the largest registeration date and time for the month, then add 10 secs"; Added On "should capture the actual Date of that call generation"; a visit is generated "when the visit is created - like 1/12, 2/12 like that and it is not in Cancelled state"; "Give me an option to segregate Product and Accessory"; "Give me pending list separately.. like a filter at the top, generated, pending (Or name it Missed PM)"; "Add the product as a filter at the top"; "Add 2 more logics - But add these as rules + Filters: 1. The installation call associated with it should be in solved state 2. Party the device is associated to should be a customer"; "Allow machines with no installation call".

FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.4 Every machine (product + serial, case and spaces ignored) with a visit falling in the month shall be listed, with the last such visit; it shall be Generated when a PM call for that machine, not cancelled, registered from the cover's start month to its end, has a Reported Problem reading k / N with the same visit number and the same number of visits, in whatever month it was registered, and a Missed PM otherwise; the answer shall include calls the reader cannot see, and each row shall show the generating call and the machine's last PM call. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. ## Preventive (PM) `/pm-calls`

Opened by `mod:/pm-calls`.

### URS-104 — A call is registered in the database or it is not registered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A call shall exist only once the database has accepted it, and only under the number the database gave it. Where registration is refused or cannot reach the database the person shall be told so, with the reason, and the call shall not be presented under a number of the browser's own making. A provisional number that a later sync replaces is two identities for one complaint, one of which may already have been given to the customer.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-128** — A registration is written or refused | High | OQ-116 |

**FRS-128.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-128.1 Registering a call shall insert it through `addFieldCall()` and show the UCN the database assigned. FRS-128.2 Where the insert is refused or fails, the form shall stay open with the values entered and show the reason; no call shall be recorded in the browser and no UCN shown. FRS-128.3 Where neither the database nor the sheet bridge is connected, registration shall be refused with that reason. FRS-128.4 A call already held in the browser by an earlier version may be synced, receiving the database's UCN, or discarded after a confirmation stating that it cannot be undone; the register shall mark such calls as not yet in the database. FRS-128.5 Each registration attempt shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.create` with its outcome and duration. RATIONALE: `handleCreate` today catches every failure, including a refusal by row-level security, and writes the call to local storage under `makeLocalUcn()` with “Saved locally as …”; `syncPending` later inserts it again and the database gives it a different UCN (D-032).

### URS-105 — The vigilance questions are answered, not defaulted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Whether a call involves a public health threat, a death or a serious incident shall be answered by the person registering it, each answer given actively. The system shall not supply an answer on the person's behalf. A pre-filled “No” records that the question was asked and answered when it may never have been read, and it is exactly the record a vigilance review relies on.

FRS-129.2 Registration shall be refused until each is answered YES or NO, naming the question unanswered. FRS-129.3 The three shall be shown in a section of their own, emphasised. FRS-129.4 An answer changed after registration requires `calls.edit.vigilance` and is captured by the row audit (FRS-079, FRS-021). FRS-129.5 An installation call raised from a Sale Entry keeps FRS-085.5 (No, recorded as the honest answer for a machine not yet switched on). RATIONALE: the three fields carry `defaultValue: ’NO’` today, so a registration saved without the section being read records three answers nobody gave (D-033).

### URS-108 — A call after registration is amended, cancelled and re-opened under stated rules

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend each part of a call shall be usable wherever the call is amended, and a call that is solved or cancelled shall be amended by nobody until it is re-opened or restored. A call shall be cancelled only while nobody has yet closed it, only with a reason, and never deleted; restoring it shall keep the reason. Re-opening a closed call shall record who did it, when and why. Each rule shall be enforced by the database, so that a direct request to the data interface meets the same refusal as the screen.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-132** — Editing a call, by section, and never once it is closed | High | OQ-120 |
| **FRS-133** — Cancelling, restoring, re-opening and closing again | High | OQ-121, OQ-122, OQ-123 |

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). FRS-132.4 Visit entry and spare requests shall not be offered on a Solved, Cancelled or not-yet-synced call. FRS-132.5 A save the database applied to no row shall be reported as not saved (finding 48, `updateCall`). RATIONALE: `canEditRow` tests `can(’calls.edit’)` and `parentAction()` resolves a section key UP to its parent, never down, so a role granted only `calls.edit.contact` — the grant URS-067 exists to make possible — is offered no Edit on any register (D-034). .3 is the user's rule “Closed means closed — for admins too” and supersedes the “non-admins” wording of FRS-007.

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.5 Close again shall withdraw a re-open without adding a visit, returning the call to its last visit's state and giving the re-open count back. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

**FRS-269.** *(v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-269.1 PM Due shall be listed under Administration beside PM Bulk Upload, opened by mod:/pm-due, and its list read only by a holder of pm.generate, through pm_visits_due() (0404), which refuses anybody else and is not executable by the public key. FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.4 Every machine (product + serial, case and spaces ignored) with a visit falling in the month shall be listed, with the last such visit; it shall be Generated when a PM call for that machine, not cancelled, registered from the cover's start month to its end, has a Reported Problem reading k / N with the same visit number and the same number of visits, in whatever month it was registered, and a Missed PM otherwise; the answer shall include calls the reader cannot see, and each row shall show the generating call and the machine's last PM call. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. FRS-269.6 The party, city, state and engineer shall be the machine's Product Database row (its Service Engineer), the register's party where it has none; a Missed PM with no engineer shall be counted and created unallocated. FRS-269.7 The list shall be filtered at the top by status (Missed PM, the default; Generated; All), by type (All; Products; Accessories, an accessory being a product whose Product Master category is ACCESSORY), by installation (Installation solved or none, the default; Solved; No installation call; Installation not solved; Any), by party (Customer, the default; Not a customer; Any) and by one product, each button counting what it would show with the other filters applied. FRS-269.8 A row may be created only when it is a Missed PM, its machine's installation call (Installation register, product + serial; a Solved call taken over a cancelled or later one) reads Solved or it has no installation call (0404), and its party (the Product Database's, else the register's) has Type CUSTOMER on the Party Master; an installation call that exists and is not Solved, or a party not in the master or with no Type, fails; each row shall show its installation call and state and its party's Type. Only such a row shall be tickable; every one shown starts ticked. Create shall need pm.create, the PM register's insert right, and shall write the ticked rows through the calls view with the PM upload's shaping (shapePmRows): call type P M VISIT, Registration Date, Complaint Date and Breakdown Date the 1st of the month, Added On today, Standard Complaint SCHEDULED PM VISIT, Reported Problem SCHEDULED PM VISIT k / N, the SA number as Warranty Number or the MC number as Contract Number, the cover dates, and Item Status WGP or the contract's type normalised. FRS-269.9 The first call shall be registered 10 seconds after the largest registration date-and-time among ALL PM calls of the month (pm_due_latest_reg_at), read when Create is pressed, and each next 10 seconds later; a month with none starts at 00:30 on the 1st, 5 seconds apart, as on PM Bulk Upload. FRS-269.10 After creating, the list shall be read again, so a created visit reads Generated. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-08; the texts are what all 8,720 PM calls of 2026 carry (_pm_generation_inputs.sql). 0401's count of PM calls since the cover started was replaced (D-157).

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.6 Item status shall be normalised through `coverCode()` to WGP, OGP, CMC or AMC, an unrecognised value kept as written. FRS-142.7 The due month shall default to this month, earlier months being loadable; every call shall be dated the 1st of it (`reg_date`) and today recorded as `added_on` (FRS-032). FRS-142.8 The first registration time and the gap between calls shall be prefilled from the latest PM call of that month and editable. FRS-142.9 Unrecognised columns shall be kept on the call in `extra`. FRS-142.10 The first eight calls and the count shall be previewed before import. FRS-142.11 A PM call shall be keyed on product, serial and due month, so that loading the same file again updates the calls it names rather than creating them again. FRS-142.12 Calls shall be written in batches with progress, the database assigning UCN and Call Number; a stop shall state how many were created. FRS-142.13 The loaded file may be cleared. RATIONALE: `pmImport.ts` keeps any row with a party OR a product, so a PM call with no serial is created (URS-053), and the writer is insert-only with “no key to re-run against”, so a file loaded twice is every call twice (URS-062) (D-038).

**FRS-006.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Field, Installation and PM calls are stored in separate physical tables (field_calls / installation_calls / pm_calls) behind a compatibility view with routing triggers; a CHECK constraint prevents mis-filing.

**FRS-009.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A holder of pm.bulk_upload (an administrator unless one is granted it) uploads a CSV; rows are mapped, forced to PM type, previewed, then inserted in batches with UCN/Call Number assigned by the database.
