### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-103** — The evidence beside the review | High | OQ-91 |
| **FRS-104** — Repeat failure across the fleet (rule 2) | High | OQ-92 |

**FRS-103.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-103.1 The review shall show a call card: call number, call date, customer, product and serial, engineer, call status and nature of complaint, the UCN coloured by call state. FRS-103.2 The review shall show Review 1 (public health threat, death, serious incident, completed or pending, date) read-only. FRS-103.3 The review shall show the age at failure under Warranty Failure, with a WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR warning below 366 days and “not known” where no warranty start is recorded. FRS-103.4 The review shall show, from the reports, the hour meter of the latest visit, the software version, the pending reason, and every visit newest first with its status, engineer and job done. FRS-103.5 The review shall display the signed service report inside the screen. FRS-103.6 The review shall list the spares booked against the call with part number, description and quantity. FRS-103.7 The review shall open a Machine History pop-up for the call’s machine under the reader’s own visibility. FRS-103.8 The review shall show Any Potential Effect worked out from the three answers as they are chosen, and state that a Field Failure Report is to be raised when it reads YES, before anything is saved. FRS-103.9 All NO shall fill the three Review 2 answers and shall not save them. FRS-103.10 A context read that fails shall say that it could not be read rather than show an empty list.

**FRS-104.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-104.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall return a verdict of frequent when rule 1 (FRS-054) or rule 2 holds, and shall say which fired. FRS-104.2 Rule 2 shall hold where the same standard complaint is recorded on at least ffr.rule2_serials DISTINCT serials of the same product (default 2, never fewer than 2) within ffr.rule2_window_days before the call (default 30), counting serials and not calls. FRS-104.3 Rule 2 shall be switchable by ffr.rule2_enabled, and its window and serial count held in app_settings separately from rule 1’s. FRS-104.4 The review shall show, for each rule, the count, the threshold and the earlier UCNs with date, days before, engineer and what they matched on. FRS-104.5 Answers already recorded shall not be re-based when a rule or its settings change. RATIONALE: URS-046 names the procedure’s rule, which is rule 1; rule 2 (0198, the user’s of 2026-09-15) sees the batch, component or design fault that rule 1 cannot, because every one of those calls is a first failure on its own machine.

### URS-108 — A call after registration is amended, cancelled and re-opened under stated rules

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend each part of a call shall be usable wherever the call is amended, and a call that is solved or cancelled shall be amended by nobody until it is re-opened or restored. A call shall be cancelled only while nobody has yet closed it, only with a reason, and never deleted; restoring it shall keep the reason. Re-opening a closed call shall record who did it, when and why. Each rule shall be enforced by the database, so that a direct request to the data interface meets the same refusal as the screen.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-132** — Editing a call, by section, and never once it is closed | High | OQ-120 |
| **FRS-133** — Cancelling, restoring, re-opening and closing again | High | OQ-121, OQ-122, OQ-123 |

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). FRS-132.4 Visit entry and spare requests shall not be offered on a Solved, Cancelled or not-yet-synced call. FRS-132.5 A save the database applied to no row shall be reported as not saved (finding 48, `updateCall`). RATIONALE: `canEditRow` tests `can(’calls.edit’)` and `parentAction()` resolves a section key UP to its parent, never down, so a role granted only `calls.edit.contact` — the grant URS-067 exists to make possible — is offered no Edit on any register (D-034). .3 is the user's rule “Closed means closed — for admins too” and supersedes the “non-admins” wording of FRS-007.

**FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. FRS-133.2 A cancellation shall require `calls.cancel` and a reason, shall warn where the call has been visited, and shall retain the call, its UCN, visits and consumption; the call shall read Cancelled and leave the pending list, recording who cancelled it, when and why. FRS-133.3 Restore shall require `calls.cancel`, return the call to the state its visits give, and retain the cancellation reason. FRS-133.4 Re-open shall be offered on a Solved call to holders of the register’s re-open key (`calls.reopen`, `install.reopen`, `pm.reopen`; corrected 2026-10-03), shall require a reason on every screen that offers it, and `reopen_call()` shall record the reason, the person and the time on the call. FRS-133.5 Close again shall withdraw a re-open without adding a visit, returning the call to its last visit's state and giving the re-open count back. FRS-133.6 A call solved again after a re-open shall keep the feedback already recorded; the visit form shall state that the call already carries feedback rather than report the feedback as failed. FRS-133.7 Re-open, close again, cancel and restore shall each be written to `audit_log` with outcome and duration, and the row change captured by `record_audit`. RATIONALE: .1 because the rule lives only in `canCancelRow` and `cancel_call()` tests nothing but the right and the reason (D-036). .4 because the register asks no reason and `reopen_call(p_ucn, p_reason)` accepts one from the Call Review and stores it nowhere, while that screen tells the reviewer “the reason goes on the call” (D-035). .6 because `feedback_ucn_key_uniq` allows one feedback per UCN and the form inserts a second (D-035).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-173 — Indoor Service runs in stages, from intake to the approved delivery challan

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Indoor Service workflow shall run in stages — Intake, Cleaning, Repair, Service Report, Delivery Challan (pending approval) and Dispatched — shown on each job and on each row of the register, each job showing only the fields of its current and completed stages. Intake shall start from the call the unit came in on (chosen from the open calls of the machine, or by its UCN) and fill the job from that call — the customer and place, the engineer the call is allotted to, the machine, its current cover, the complaint — or receive a DEMO / new device with no call, and shall record the accessories received with their quantities. The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded only after the unit is cleaned, with its report number, the stored file named after that number and the uploader recorded by the system; for a unit with a call the same step shall capture the Visit Entry for that call so the work is not entered twice. A spare shall be requestable from the job through the Spare Request workflow without changing the call.

| **FRS-239** — The Indoor job as a window with the DC beside it, the DC in the form's language, and the register in the app's table | Medium | OQ-229 |

No, Problem Reported (the call's Complaint Reported), the call's Standard Complaint (shown read only, kept on the job as `standard_complaint`) and Status (cover) — the machine's cover now from the Product Database through coverCode(), else the call's item status; every filled value shall stay editable. The job's status shall be derived from them once cleaned: Solved → Ready (a Repair, Rework or Troubleshooting first needing its QC Pass, until then QC); Unsolved with spares not available → Awaiting spares; otherwise Under repair; never once Dispatched, Closed or Condemned. FRS-232.14 (0374) The intake shall offer three ways in — Field Return, Demo and New Device — each fixing the job's kind and activity: Customer property / Troubleshooting, DEMO unit / Demo, New device / Troubleshooting. A New device shall be its own kind, consigned like a DEMO unit to the party it is going to, and shall have its own sheet (New Devices) on the R/SER/07 register.

FRS-233.5 The upload shall be offered on the drawer's Repair page — reached also from the register's Indoor Service Report No cell — only once cleaned and only while the unit is on no DC; it is a form on that page, not a second drawer. ### URS-111 — A visit is recorded as it happened

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The record of a visit shall be dated no later than today and no earlier than the complaint, because the latest visit decides whether the call is closed. It shall state why an unsolved call is pending, carry the signed service report where the call is completed, record the customer's feedback on a solved call, and record the parts fitted with the traceability of each. Where only part of a visit could be saved the person shall be told exactly which part, and shall be able to complete it without entering the visit twice.

**FRS-136.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-136.1 The visit date shall be no later than today (IST) and no earlier than the call's complaint date, checked on save by `visitDateProblem()` and refused by the database for every visit entered on the form (`uid WEB-…`, 0115); imported history is exempt. FRS-136.2 The Visit Entry Date shall be stamped by the application at the moment of entry and shall not be editable. FRS-136.3 The Visiting Service Engineer shall be required; a manager or administrator may choose an engineer of their team, whose hand stock is then used, while the visit records the signed-in person as its author (`engineer_email`). FRS-136.4 Call Status shall be one of three values. FRS-136.5 Call Pending Reason shall be required from the pending-reason master when the status is Unsolved, and fixed to Report Pending when the report is pending. FRS-136.6 Update Visit Work Details? shall be answered, and shall be Yes when the status is Solved - Report Completed; No shall omit the service report fields. FRS-136.7 The service report shall require software version and filter changed, take the complaint from the master, and offer the accessory serial from the party's CPX/ASU units. FRS-136.8 On an installation, Warranty Start Date? shall be required and answered by choosing one of the customer feedback's two answers — Installation Call Solved Date or Invoice Date — with no default, and be stored on the feedback (FRS-082, FRS-245). FRS-136.9 The manual report shall be a PDF or photo up to 10 MB uploaded to the call type's Drive folder, never a pasted link, and shall be required when the status is Solved - Report Completed; it may be shown, opened, replaced or removed before save. FRS-136.10 On a solved call the feedback questions shall be those for the call type, rating and yes/no answers required, and the customer sign-off name, number and designation optional. FRS-136.11 The form shall show the previous visits (status, engineer, date) and open the last manual report. FRS-136.12 A missing hand-stock view shall be reported as needing its migration.

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-065 — A recovered quality record is reviewed before it is written

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where records of work already done are recovered from a superseded system, each shall be resolved to the record it belongs to AND SHOWN TO AN OPERATOR BEFORE ANY OF IT IS WRITTEN, and only rows that resolved cleanly shall be written. A visit attached to the wrong call, or carrying another machine’s photograph, is a worse outcome than a visit still missing: the first is a false record of what was done to a device, the second is a gap that is visible as a gap. Rows that did not resolve shall be reported with the reason and left unwritten rather than written with a guess.

FRS-145.2 The preview may be narrowed to the rows with a problem. FRS-145.3 A column of the file the screen does not recognise shall be kept on the visit written, under its own heading. FRS-145.4 A row with no attachment resolved shall be skipped at write, not written without its report, whether or not step 2 was run.

**FRS-077.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* The screen runs in three stated steps and in this order: READ the sheet and work out which call each row belongs to; RESOLVE the superseded system’s file references into links; WRITE only the rows that came through both cleanly. Nothing is written until the operator has SEEN what each row resolved to, and rows that did not resolve are listed with the reason and are not written. The register it writes into is the visit history, whose records are never deleted, so a wrong write cannot be taken back — which is why the review is a step rather than a confirmation dialogue. Bulk Report Mapping shall count a visit as attached only when the update changed it, and stop, naming the visit, when row-level security matched nothing (D-091).

FRS-245.6 A one-time apply shall set this for every machine whose installation already answered "Installation Call Solved Date", the old start, end and status kept in products_install_start_backup. RATIONALE: the two answers are the feedback's own, measured on the live register (328 and 78 installations, 2026-10-03); 28 reports carrying a typed date were left as they are, the user's decision. ### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-071 — Two records of one visit shall not contradict each other

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where the system holds a customer’s feedback about a visit, it shall also hold a completed service report for that visit, and every instance where it does not shall be visible as a list naming which record is absent. Feedback is collected after a visit has taken place, so its existence is evidence that the work occurred; the completed report is the record of what was done. The two disagreeing means a device was serviced and the servicing was never written up — a gap that is invisible from either record read on its own, because neither record is wrong in itself.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-140** — Solved Without a Report, and the two lists' chips and wording | Medium | OQ-131, OQ-132 |
| **FRS-083** — Feedback Without a Report | Medium | OQ-72 |

**FRS-140.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-140.1 Solved Without a Report shall list, from a `security_invoker` view, every call reading Solved whose record has no visit, no visit date, no service report, or a visit entry date equal to its import stamp, naming every gap on the row and omitting unsolved calls and complete ones. FRS-140.2 Gap chips (and on Feedback Without a Report, finding chips) shall show exact counts, a record counting under each of its gaps, and a click shall narrow the list. FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. FRS-140.5 A load failure shall name the missing migration or grant, or show the error verbatim. FRS-140.6 Each list shall export to Excel, with an About sheet explaining each gap and the scope, or to CSV, through FRS-138. FRS-140.7 Refresh shall re-read the list. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-083.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `feedback_without_report` (0229) lists every customer feedback with no visit reading “Solved - Report Completed” behind it, and names WHICH of four things is absent, because each needs a different fix: the feedback records no UCN; no call carries that UCN; the call has no visit at all; or the call has visits and none of them is the completed one. The last is the commonest, and the row carries `latest_visit_status` beside it so that “Solved - Report Pending” — the system stating a known absence — is distinguishable from “Unsolved”, which is a different problem. THE STATUS IS MATCHED ON ITS LETTERS AND DIGITS, not as a string: `is_report_completed()` reduces to lower-case alphanumerics, so a trailing space, a lower-case spelling and an en-dash all read as completed, and `isCompletedVisit()` in src/lib/reportMapping.ts is the client copy of the same rule. That is not defensive coding — the export this was written for carried “Solved - Report Completed ” with a trailing space in all 378 rows, and a string comparison would have reported every one of those calls as missing its report. ANY visit reading completed is enough rather than the latest one: a call written up and then re-visited still has its report. A false entry here sends somebody to re-file a report that exists, which is wasted work and teaches them the list may mean nothing — the same argument as a `_status.sql` row that answers NO for nothing — so both rules are tested with the spellings that actually arrive. The view is `security_invoker`, so the ordinary call and feedback policies decide the rows; the SCREEN is restricted to administrators by `mod:/feedback-without-report`, at the user’s direction (2026-09-22).

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

### URS-118 — A spare request says what is asked for, for which call or which stock, and is numbered by the system

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall let an engineer, or a manager for an engineer in their team, request spare parts either against a call or to replenish the engineer's own hand stock (a HandStock request), and a HandStock request shall state why it is needed. A request against a call shall carry the customer, product, serial, complaint and cover that the call records, copied from the call rather than typed again, and a request raised from within a call shall not be movable to a different call. Each part shall be chosen from the Part Master and never typed, offered first from the parts that fit the call's product with the whole master available on request, and asked for in a whole quantity of at least one. The request number and its date shall be assigned by the system. Re-keying what a call already records is where the request and the call stop describing the same machine, and a part typed freehand is a part no stock figure will ever find.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-146** — Raising a spare request | High | OQ-242, OQ-138 |
| **FRS-247** — A spare request on a call with no visit files the visit it implies | High | OQ-239 |

**FRS-146.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-146.1 The Spare Requests screen shall offer the New Spare Request action only to a holder of `spare.request`. FRS-146.2 The request form shall offer two request types, Call Based and HandStock. FRS-146.3 The request form shall require a HandStock reason for a HandStock request and shall refuse the submission with "Enter the reason for the HandStock request." where it is empty. FRS-146.4 The request form shall find the call of a Call Based request by its UCN, call number, party or serial once three characters are typed, and shall offer at most 25 calls. FRS-146.5 The request form shall copy the party, product, serial, complaint and item status (cover) of the chosen call onto the request and shall not offer them for editing. FRS-146.6 The request form shall fix the call, and offer no "Change call", when it is opened from a call. FRS-146.7 The request form shall offer as parts only Part Master entries, chosen from a pick list that takes no free text, and shall state why the list is disabled while the master is empty or still loading. FRS-146.8 The request form shall offer, for a Call Based request, the parts mapped to the call's product, its accessories and the common parts, with a "Show all parts" option offering the whole Part Master; it shall offer the whole Part Master to a HandStock request. FRS-146.9 The request form shall accept a quantity per part as a whole number of at least one, and shall treat a blank or lower value as one. FRS-146.10 The request form shall accept at most 20 spare rows on one request. FRS-146.11 The request form shall accept optional additional remarks. FRS-146.12 The request form shall refuse a submission with no spare ("Add at least one spare."), with no engineer, or of a Call Based request with no UCN ("A Call-Based request needs a call (UC Number)."). FRS-146.13 The database shall assign the OR number (OR-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month) and the OR request date on insert; the form shall show "OR No assigned on submit" and shall not accept either. FRS-146.14 The request form shall generate the request reference WA-yyyymmdd-xxxx when it opens; the reference is the request's primary key, so a colliding reference is refused by the database and never merged into another request. FRS-146.15 The request form shall disable Submit, and say why, while the database is not connected. FRS-146.16 On success the screen shall name the OR number and the reference, reload the register and write an audit entry `spare.request`. FRS-146.17 Once the RM has decided a line, its part and quantity shall not be changed by anybody, the requester included, except by a part rename; Item Status shall be taken from the call when the request is raised and change afterwards only to the call’s own value, and the request type shall not change (0340, D-121, D-122). RATIONALE: .5 because the request is read downstream (cover-based routing under FRS-147.8, the unused-spare report) through the call's own identity, and a re-typed serial is where the two stop agreeing. .14 records that the reference is made in the browser: that is acceptable only because the database key refuses a duplicate rather than overwriting.

**FRS-247.** *(v0.10.67 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-247.1 When a Call Based spare request and its lines have saved, the Spare Request form shall ask the database to file a visit for the request's call (`file_visit_for_spare_request`, 0333). FRS-247.2 The database shall file that visit only where the call has no visit at all, and shall file nothing for a HandStock request or a UCN that is not a call. FRS-247.3 The visit shall read Call Status Unsolved, the requesting engineer, the request's date (India) as the visit date, the Call Pending Reason master entry meaning spare not available (matched on its letters, so SPARE / SPARES and NOT AVAILABLE / UNAVAILABLE all qualify; SPARES NOT AVAILABLE where the master holds none), Update Visit Work Details? = No, and the OR number as Spare Request; the call shall then read Unsolved. FRS-247.4 A second request on the same call, or a retry, shall file nothing more. FRS-247.5 Only the person who raised the request, holding spare.request, may call it; the public key may not. FRS-247.6 Where the visit cannot be filed, the screen shall say the request was submitted but its visit entry was not added, naming the error. RATIONALE: .1 calls it after the lines rather than from a trigger on the request, because a request whose lines fail stays behind (D-044) and must not turn its call Unsolved, and because the bulk import of request history must not file visits for past requests.

### URS-119 — A spare moves to the next approver only on an answer that means yes

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each spare line shall pass an approval stage only when that stage's recorded answer means yes — Approved, Auto-Approved, or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing — and any other answer, however it is worded, shall hold the line with that approver. Which of the Commercial and NSM stages a line needs shall be settled once, when the Reporting Manager approves it: a line under AMC or OGP needs both, a HandStock request needs NSM, and any other line needs neither. A stage that is not needed shall be recorded as Auto-Approved and shall name no approver. A line that has been rejected, dropped, dispatched or received shall read as such wherever its stage is shown. Before the rule was whole-word, "Not Approved" read as approved and parts reached Stores that nobody had cleared.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-147** — The stage of a spare line is read from its answers, whole-word | High | OQ-217, OQ-139 |

**FRS-147.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-147.1 The system shall compute the stage of a spare line in this order: Rejected where any of the RM, Commercial or NSM answers is a rejection; Received where the line has a receipt time; Dropped where Stores dropped it; Dispatched where Stores dispatched it in full; otherwise the first of RM Approval, Commercial and NSM whose answer does not mean yes; otherwise Stores. FRS-147.2 An answer shall mean yes only when, ignoring case and surrounding space, it is exactly Approved, Auto-Approved (with or without the hyphen) or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing. FRS-147.3 Any other answer — "Not Approved", "Approval Pending", "Not cleared for stores processing", a word from an imported sheet — shall hold the line at that stage. FRS-147.4 The database (`spare_line_stage`, 0256 and 0270) shall compute the stored stage by the same rule as the screen (`APPROVED_RE` in src/lib/spareflow.ts), and `check:ui` shall hold the two patterns together. FRS-147.5 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the Commercial answer unless the line is AMC or OGP (`spare_needs_commercial`). FRS-147.6 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the NSM answer unless the line is AMC or OGP or belongs to a HandStock request (`spare_needs_nsm`, 0210). FRS-147.7 An Auto-Approved answer shall be written with no approver name and no approval time. FRS-147.8 The RM approval dialog shall state, before the approval is written, which later stages the line will skip and which it will stop at. FRS-147.9 The Spare Upload shall keep an unrecognised approval word exactly as written (`approvalWord`), so that it holds the line rather than being guessed into Approved or Rejected. RATIONALE: .2 is whole-word because finding 20 was a substring test that read every way of saying no as yes. .7 because inventing an approver on a quality record is worse than an outcome with no name against it. The rule is settled at RM approval and then READ from the record, which is why `spare_line_stage` keeps its six arguments.

### URS-120 — A spare ended without being supplied says why

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall refuse to reject a spare line, or to drop it (close it unsent), without a stated reason, on every path by which either can be done — one line, one order, a selection, and the Stores queue — and shall record the stage at which it ended, the reason and who ended it. Dropping shall be an authority of its own and shall be possible only until the line is dispatched. A register of requests closed with no reason cannot be reviewed afterwards, and a reason demanded on one path and not on another is demanded of nobody.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-148** — A rejection, a drop and a change of engineer each need a reason, on every path | High | OQ-242, OQ-140 |

**FRS-148.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-148.1 The Spare Requests screen shall require a reason before it rejects one spare line, the lines of one order, or a selection. FRS-148.2 The database shall refuse a rejection whose reason is empty on every write path — `decide_spare_lines()` (0118) and a direct update of the line alike. FRS-148.3 The system shall record the stage at which a line was rejected (`rejected_stage`) and the reason (`reject_reason`). FRS-148.4 The system shall allow a line to be dropped only by a holder of `spare.drop`, at RM Approval, Commercial, NSM or Stores, and shall refuse a drop of a line already dispatched or received. FRS-148.5 The Spare Requests and Pending Dispatch screens shall refuse a drop with an empty reason. FRS-148.6 The database shall refuse a drop whose reason is empty on every write path. FRS-148.7 A dropped line shall record the reason in `dispatch_remarks`, generate no challan, and add nothing to the engineer's hand stock. FRS-148.8 `reassign_spare_request()` shall refuse a change of engineer with no reason, and the screen shall not submit one. FRS-148.9 A change of engineer shall go through Change engineer on every path, before dispatch as well as after; a plain update of the engineer is refused (0340, D-122). RATIONALE: .2 and .6 exist because the rule already lives in `decide_spare_lines()` for the bulk path and nowhere else, so the single-line and Pending Dispatch paths pass an empty reason (D-043). .8 is URS-035's "retained with ... the reason": a reason the function defaults to an empty string is not retained, it is absent.

### URS-121 — Many spares may be decided in one action, each at its own stage

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

An approver shall be able to approve, reject or drop many spare lines in one action. Each line shall be decided at the stage it is at and shall advance by one stage at most; a line the approver may not decide shall be left undecided and counted with the reason, and shall neither be passed silently nor fail the rest. A Reporting Manager shall decide each spare on its own, never a whole order at once. The Reporting Manager's queue shall list every line awaiting that approval, shall mark the lines the reader may not approve — their own, or outside their team — and shall not let them be selected. A decision on many lines shall be confirmed, with its count, before it is written. Bulk is exactly where a line is approved past a review it never had without anybody noticing.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |

**FRS-149.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-149.1 The Spare Requests screen shall show selection boxes only to a holder of an approval permission, and a Drop action only to a holder of `spare.drop`. ### URS-122 — The grounds of a Commercial or NSM clearance are recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

At the Commercial stage the system shall record whether the spare is cleared for Stores or still in process, and why: the cover or purchase order it is cleared under, the contract or service-agreement number where it is cleared under a contract or warranty, and the answer to each purchase-order step where it is a direct purchase; where it is still in process, the reason it is pending. At the NSM stage it shall record whether the spare is cleared or put on hold, and the reasons. An answer that does not clear the spare shall keep it with that approver. Every answer shall be kept with the person and the time, and shown wherever the spare's history is read. A charging decision with no grounds recorded cannot be checked against the contract it claims to rest on.

### URS-131 — A spare or stock record is saved whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A spare request, a material return and a stock hand-over, each written as a header and its lines, shall be saved whole or not at all: where any part of one cannot be written, nothing of it shall remain, and the person shall be told that nothing was saved. A header with no lines, or a return with some of its lines, is a record that says less than happened — and for a return, stock has already been taken off an engineer for parts the record does not list.

| --- | --- | --- |

**FRS-164.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-164.1 A spare request and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.2 A material return and all its lines shall be written by one database call that writes all or none. FRS-164.3 A stock transfer and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.4 Where such a call fails, the screen shall say that nothing was saved. FRS-164.5 A stock out is already written this way by `dispatch_spare_lines()` (FRS-153.9). RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-021 — Partial issue of spares

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Stores shall be able to issue fewer units of a spare than were requested when only part of the quantity is available, and the outstanding balance shall remain visible as still due.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-153** — The Stores queue and booking out | High | OQ-145 |
| **FRS-026** — Partial dispatch | Medium | OQ-18 |

**FRS-153.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-153.1 Pending Dispatch shall list every line that has cleared its approvals and still has a quantity owed, read through `spare_pending_dispatch` (security_invoker), up to 2,000 lines, with "+" on the count at that limit. FRS-153.2 Where the 2,000-line limit is reached, Pending Dispatch shall name the engineer at whom the read stopped and state that engineers after that one, A to Z, are missing. FRS-153.3 Pending Dispatch shall group the queue into one card per engineer, longest-waiting engineer first, each stating its spares, units, orders and days waiting (14 or more red, 7 or more amber). FRS-153.4 Pending Dispatch shall search by engineer, order, spare ID, part, UCN, call and party, and shall pre-fill the search from `?engineer=`. FRS-153.5 Pending Dispatch shall let Stores tick single lines or a whole engineer, a tick on a second engineer replacing the selection. FRS-153.6 Pending Dispatch shall refuse to book out a selection spanning more than one engineer, stating "A stock out goes to one engineer", and `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall refuse the same. FRS-153.7 Pending Dispatch shall accept a quantity per line between one and the quantity still owed, and shall mark a line already partly sent "N of M sent". FRS-153.8 The dispatch dialog shall take a DC date defaulting to today, a courier and dispatch remarks, and shall list what goes. FRS-153.9 `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall create the stock out, assign its stock-out and DC numbers in the series of the DC date, and stamp every line, in one statement that writes all or nothing. FRS-153.10 Pending Dispatch shall disable Dispatch without `spare.dispatch`. FRS-153.11 The engineer's hand stock shall count the parts from the booking time of the stock out (`handstock_movements`), not from the DC date and not from the acknowledgement. FRS-153.12 On success Pending Dispatch shall name the stock out, write an audit entry `spare.dispatch` and open the Delivery Challan. FRS-153.13 Pending Dispatch shall let each engineer's card be expanded and collapsed, offer Expand all and Collapse all, and open every card by itself the first time a queue holds three engineers or fewer. FRS-153.14 The Queue tab shall carry its count and a Stock outs tab shall list what has been issued (FRS-157.14). RATIONALE: .11 is why a DC date may be set: it is the date on the paper, and the stock movement is dated by the database clock, so a back-dated challan cannot move a balance into a closed period.

**FRS-026.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* A stock out records a quantity per requested line in spare_dispatch_lines; spare_request_lines.dispatched_qty accumulates it. The Stores queue shows the outstanding remainder and the line stays queued until fully issued. Issuing more than the remainder is rejected by dispatch_spare_lines().

### URS-022 — Acknowledged receipt

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The engineer shall confirm each delivery of a spare as it is received, and a spare shall be recorded as received only when the whole quantity has been confirmed. Only the engineer who raised the request shall confirm it. The confirmation records the parts' arrival; they count in the engineer's hand stock from the moment they were dispatched.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-152** — Only the engineer who raised a spare acknowledges it, and only after it is sent | Medium | OQ-144 |
| **FRS-027** — Per-shipment receipt | Medium | OQ-18 |

**FRS-152.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-152.1 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of receipt by anybody other than the engineer named on the request (`is_spare_requester`, 0217). FRS-152.2 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of a line that has not been dispatched. FRS-152.3 The database shall require `spare.receive` for an acknowledgement. FRS-152.4 The Spare Requests screen shall offer Mark received per line and for every line of one order at that stage, with optional receipt remarks. FRS-152.5 An acknowledgement shall confirm every delivery on the line not yet confirmed, and the line shall read Received only when the confirmed quantity reaches the quantity requested (FRS-027). FRS-152.6 "Needs my action" shall offer an acknowledgement only on the reader's own requests. FRS-152.7 The acknowledgement shall not change the engineer's hand stock, which counts the parts from dispatch (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: .1 is enforced in the database because `sr_update` lets the requester write their own request, so a rule held only by the screen is one a direct call walks past; .7 restates the counting rule so that nobody reads the receipt as the moment the stock arrives.

**FRS-027.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* receive_spare_shipments() stamps each delivery with who confirmed it and when, accumulating spare_request_lines.received_qty. The line is marked Received (received_at) only when the acknowledged quantity reaches the requested quantity, so a part-delivered line remains at the Stores stage.

### URS-035 — Correcting who a spare order is for

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

An administrator shall be able to correct the engineer a spare order was raised against while it is still awaiting issue, and shall be prevented from doing so once any part of it has been issued. A change shall be refused without a reason, and every change shall be retained with both names, the person who made it, the time and the reason.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-148** — A rejection, a drop and a change of engineer each need a reason, on every path | High | OQ-242, OQ-140 |
| **FRS-041** — Reassigning a spare order, with a log | High | OQ-23 |

**FRS-148.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-148.1 The Spare Requests screen shall require a reason before it rejects one spare line, the lines of one order, or a selection. FRS-148.2 The database shall refuse a rejection whose reason is empty on every write path — `decide_spare_lines()` (0118) and a direct update of the line alike. FRS-148.3 The system shall record the stage at which a line was rejected (`rejected_stage`) and the reason (`reject_reason`). FRS-148.4 The system shall allow a line to be dropped only by a holder of `spare.drop`, at RM Approval, Commercial, NSM or Stores, and shall refuse a drop of a line already dispatched or received. FRS-148.5 The Spare Requests and Pending Dispatch screens shall refuse a drop with an empty reason. FRS-148.6 The database shall refuse a drop whose reason is empty on every write path. FRS-148.7 A dropped line shall record the reason in `dispatch_remarks`, generate no challan, and add nothing to the engineer's hand stock. FRS-148.8 `reassign_spare_request()` shall refuse a change of engineer with no reason, and the screen shall not submit one. FRS-148.9 A change of engineer shall go through Change engineer on every path, before dispatch as well as after; a plain update of the engineer is refused (0340, D-122). RATIONALE: .2 and .6 exist because the rule already lives in `decide_spare_lines()` for the bulk path and nowhere else, so the single-line and Pending Dispatch paths pass an empty reason (D-043). .8 is URS-035's "retained with ... the reason": a reason the function defaults to an empty string is not retained, it is absent.

**FRS-041.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `reassign_spare_request()` changes the engineer on a spare request and writes `spare_request_engineer_log` in the same statement, so a change cannot exist without its record or a record without its change. It refuses a caller without spare.reassign (0304; an administrator's alone before), and refuses ANY caller once the order has been issued — tested three ways: the order says dispatched, any of its lines does, or a stock-out line points at one of its lines. A BEFORE UPDATE trigger on the table enforces the dispatch rule again for every path that does not go through the function, including PostgREST and the bulk upload. The reason: hand stock is DERIVED from the request, so after issue the engineer’s name is not a label on a record but the identity of whose parts they are. The log is readable by administrators, approvers, Stores, and both engineers named on the row.

Opened by `mod:/spare-rm-approval`.

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

My Workload shall gather, on one page, the counts of the work waiting in every register the reader may open — spare requests by stage and those awaiting the reader, RM approvals, pending dispatch with its ageing, hand stock, material returns, stock transfers, the daily complaint review by stage, and installations awaiting Commercial — and shall request nothing from a register the reader may not open. Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-117** — My Workload | Medium | OQ-105 |

**FRS-117.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-117.1 A section shall appear only when the reader holds the module key of the register behind it, tested before anything is requested, so that no request is made otherwise. FRS-117.2 Each section shall load on its own and in a fixed order, and a section that fails shall show its own error while the others arrive. FRS-117.3 Loading shall begin only once the reader’s reporting team is known. FRS-117.4 Spare Requests shall show Awaiting me, In approval, Awaiting dispatch, Dispatched, Received and Rejected, computed with the register’s own stage rule, each opening Spare Requests filtered to that stage. FRS-117.5 RM Approval shall show the number waiting, the engineers waiting and the longest wait in days. FRS-117.6 Pending Dispatch shall show spares waiting, those waiting a week or more, units, engineers and orders. FRS-117.7 Hand Stock shall show Short (opening Hand Stock filtered to short lines), units in the field, engineers holding, part codes, stock out, consumed and returned. FRS-117.8 Material Returns shall show MRNs, lines, good quantity and defective quantity; Stock Transfer shall show transfers, lines, units moved and engineers involved. FRS-117.9 Daily Complaint Review shall show exact counts of Review 1, 2 and 3 Pending, Any Potential Effect, Completed and Calls in view, each opening the register filtered to the rows counted — Any Potential Effect to the potential-effect calls (D-022). FRS-117.10 A count taken over a read that stopped at its 4,000-row budget shall carry a “+”. FRS-117.11 A card that is a figure shall open nothing and shall not be styled as a link. FRS-117.12 Each section shall offer Open the register; the page shall offer Refresh, the time of the last read and the number of cards, say Counting N more registers while sections load, say when not connected, and say when no register is open to the reader.

### URS-119 — A spare moves to the next approver only on an answer that means yes

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each spare line shall pass an approval stage only when that stage's recorded answer means yes — Approved, Auto-Approved, or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing — and any other answer, however it is worded, shall hold the line with that approver. Which of the Commercial and NSM stages a line needs shall be settled once, when the Reporting Manager approves it: a line under AMC or OGP needs both, a HandStock request needs NSM, and any other line needs neither. A stage that is not needed shall be recorded as Auto-Approved and shall name no approver. A line that has been rejected, dropped, dispatched or received shall read as such wherever its stage is shown. Before the rule was whole-word, "Not Approved" read as approved and parts reached Stores that nobody had cleared.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-147** — The stage of a spare line is read from its answers, whole-word | High | OQ-217, OQ-139 |

**FRS-147.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-147.1 The system shall compute the stage of a spare line in this order: Rejected where any of the RM, Commercial or NSM answers is a rejection; Received where the line has a receipt time; Dropped where Stores dropped it; Dispatched where Stores dispatched it in full; otherwise the first of RM Approval, Commercial and NSM whose answer does not mean yes; otherwise Stores. FRS-147.2 An answer shall mean yes only when, ignoring case and surrounding space, it is exactly Approved, Auto-Approved (with or without the hyphen) or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing. FRS-147.3 Any other answer — "Not Approved", "Approval Pending", "Not cleared for stores processing", a word from an imported sheet — shall hold the line at that stage. FRS-147.4 The database (`spare_line_stage`, 0256 and 0270) shall compute the stored stage by the same rule as the screen (`APPROVED_RE` in src/lib/spareflow.ts), and `check:ui` shall hold the two patterns together. FRS-147.5 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the Commercial answer unless the line is AMC or OGP (`spare_needs_commercial`). FRS-147.6 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the NSM answer unless the line is AMC or OGP or belongs to a HandStock request (`spare_needs_nsm`, 0210). FRS-147.7 An Auto-Approved answer shall be written with no approver name and no approval time. FRS-147.8 The RM approval dialog shall state, before the approval is written, which later stages the line will skip and which it will stop at. FRS-147.9 The Spare Upload shall keep an unrecognised approval word exactly as written (`approvalWord`), so that it holds the line rather than being guessed into Approved or Rejected. RATIONALE: .2 is whole-word because finding 20 was a substring test that read every way of saying no as yes. .7 because inventing an approver on a quality record is worse than an outcome with no name against it. The rule is settled at RM approval and then READ from the record, which is why `spare_line_stage` keeps its six arguments.

### URS-121 — Many spares may be decided in one action, each at its own stage

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

An approver shall be able to approve, reject or drop many spare lines in one action. Each line shall be decided at the stage it is at and shall advance by one stage at most; a line the approver may not decide shall be left undecided and counted with the reason, and shall neither be passed silently nor fail the rest. A Reporting Manager shall decide each spare on its own, never a whole order at once. The Reporting Manager's queue shall list every line awaiting that approval, shall mark the lines the reader may not approve — their own, or outside their team — and shall not let them be selected. A decision on many lines shall be confirmed, with its count, before it is written. Bulk is exactly where a line is approved past a review it never had without anybody noticing.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-149** — Deciding many spare lines at once | High | OQ-217, OQ-141 |

**FRS-149.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-149.1 The Spare Requests screen shall show selection boxes only to a holder of an approval permission, and a Drop action only to a holder of `spare.drop`. FRS-149.2 A selection shall be decided through `decide_spare_lines()` (0116/0118), which shall decide each line at the stage it is at and advance it by one stage at most. FRS-149.3 `decide_spare_lines()` shall skip, and count with a reason, each line the caller may not decide — at a stage whose permission they lack, their own request or outside their team at RM (`spare_rm_may_approve`, 0033), or already past the approval stages — and shall not fail the batch for it. FRS-149.4 The screen shall report the outcome as "N approved — M skipped (reason)". FRS-149.5 The screen shall confirm a decision on many lines, naming the decision and the count, before writing it. FRS-149.6 The "all N" action shall decide every line of one order at one stage, and shall be offered at Commercial, NSM and receipt, never at RM Approval (`canBulkApprove`). FRS-149.7 The RM Approval screen shall read every line awaiting RM approval through `spare_pending_rm`, in pages, up to 2,000 lines, and shall mark the count with "+" when that limit is reached. FRS-149.8 The RM Approval screen shall list the lines the reader may not approve, marked "Not yours" with the rule on hover, and shall not let them be selected. FRS-149.9 The RM Approval screen shall offer "Select all N of mine". FRS-149.10 Each batch shall write an audit entry naming the decision and the numbers selected, decided and skipped. RATIONALE: .3 because a batch that fails whole on one ineligible line teaches people to select less, and one that approves it quietly is the failure R-04 exists for.

### URS-123 — A decision on a spare or a consumption line names the person who made it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every approval, rejection, drop, dispatch and acknowledgement of receipt of a spare, and every consumption line booked or adjusted by the office, shall name the person who made it, taken from the authenticated session at the moment it is written and not from a value supplied by the screen or by a client of the interface. A stage decided by rule rather than by a person shall name nobody. A name the caller supplies is a name anybody can supply — the Delivery Challan once carried the wrong person's for exactly that reason (0211).

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-151** — The person against a spare or consumption decision is stamped from the session | High | OQ-243, OQ-143 |

**FRS-151.** *(v0.10.78 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-151.1 The database shall stamp `spare_dispatches.dispatched_by` from the authenticated session and discard a caller-supplied value (0211). FRS-151.2 The database shall stamp the RM, Commercial and NSM approver names (`rm_by`, `commercial_by`, `nsm_by`) and times from the session whenever it records a person's approval or rejection, and shall discard a caller-supplied name, on the single-line, per-order and bulk paths. FRS-151.3 The database shall stamp the name recorded against a drop from the session. FRS-151.4 The database shall stamp `received_by` from the session in `receive_spare_shipments()` and on any other receipt path. FRS-151.7 Where there is no authenticated session (a migration or an administrative load) the supplied value shall be kept, as FRS-051 keeps it for a call. FRS-151.8 Once a stock out is issued, a signed-in update shall keep its `dispatched_by` and discard a new value, so the Delivery Challan and the Declaration cannot be re-signed afterwards and a re-load of the Stock Out Register cannot replace it (0345, D-126); FRS-151.7 still applies. FRS-157.8 The drawer shall show the rejected stage and reason, the call identity, the HandStock reason, the remarks and every spare on the order with its DC and date. FRS-157.9 The trail shall list Raised, RM, Commercial, NSM, Stores (with DC and courier) and Received, each with who, when and note, and the Commercial and NSM form answers. RATIONALE: .7 because an import stamps the load day into `created_at`, and a trail saying Raised on the upload day is wrong in the one place that must not be.

### URS-128 — A material return records what came back, from whom, and in what condition

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall record each return of spares from an engineer to Stores against the paper slip it came with, stating each part, how many came back good and how many defective, and the call or customer it came from where known. An engineer shall return only their own stock; a return on another engineer's behalf shall be recorded only by somebody holding an administrator, approval or dispatch authority. No return shall exceed what the engineer holds. The system shall give each return its own unique reference, keep the slip number as written, and record the return in the audit trail. A return, once recorded, shall not be edited; a mistake is corrected by a further entry.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-161** — Recording a material return | High | OQ-153 |
| **FRS-230** — The Material Return Note R/SER/STR/002, printed from what the return holds | Medium | OQ-224 |

FRS-161.2 The form shall fix the engineer to the signed-in person, and shall let a holder of `users.manage`, `spare.dispatch` or `spare.approve_rm` choose another engineer from the User Master. FRS-161.3 The database shall accept a return for another engineer only from an administrator or a holder of an approval or dispatch authority (`mr_insert`, `can_approve_spares`), and otherwise only a return of the caller's own stock. FRS-161.4 The form shall require the MRN No from the paper slip and keep it as written; the database shall assign the unique reference MRN-YYMM-NNNN. FRS-161.5 The form shall take an MRN date defaulting to today (see FRS-163). FRS-161.6 The form shall offer only parts the engineer holds, and shall not offer a part already on another line. FRS-161.7 The form shall take a good and a defective quantity per line, capped together at what the engineer holds less the other lines, and shall say why a typed value was reduced. FRS-161.8 The database shall refuse a return exceeding the engineer's holding (0039). FRS-161.9 The form shall refuse a submission with no engineer, no MRN No, no spare, a line of zero, or a line or part total above what is held, each with its own message; and shall say, with the hand-stock formula, when the engineer holds nothing. FRS-161.10 The form shall take remarks. FRS-161.11 The database shall refuse an edit of a return (0039). FRS-161.12 On success the screen shall name the reference and write an audit entry `stock.return`.
