### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. ### URS-173 — Indoor Service runs in stages, from intake to the approved delivery challan

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Indoor Service workflow shall run in stages — Intake, Cleaning, Repair, Service Report, Delivery Challan (pending approval) and Dispatched — shown on each job and on each row of the register, each job showing only the fields of its current and completed stages. Intake shall start from the call the unit came in on (chosen from the open calls of the machine, or by its UCN) and fill the job from that call — the customer and place, the engineer the call is allotted to, the machine, its current cover, the complaint — or receive a DEMO / new device with no call, and shall record the accessories received with their quantities. The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded only after the unit is cleaned, with its report number, the stored file named after that number and the uploader recorded by the system; for a unit with a call the same step shall capture the Visit Entry for that call so the work is not entered twice. A spare shall be requestable from the job through the Spare Request workflow without changing the call.

| **FRS-239** — The Indoor job as a window with the DC beside it, the DC in the form's language, and the register in the app's table | Medium | OQ-229 |

### URS-174 — Only the Indoor delivery challan is approved, and its approval files the visit

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

An Indoor delivery challan shall be created pending approval, naming who authorises it — the issuer's Reporting Manager, Regional Manager or an NSM — and only that person or an administrator shall approve or reject it, with the decision, who made it and when recorded by the system and printed on the challan. A unit shall not be dispatched while its challan is pending. Approving shall file, against each unit's call, the Visit Entry drafted with its Indoor Service Report — the call left Unsolved, pending Return to Field, with the work details and the uploaded report — through the same path and rules as a visit entered on the call, and shall not complete while any of those visits is unfiled. Rejecting shall need a reason, keep the challan and release its units for a new one. The spare-parts challan is not affected.

### URS-120 — A spare ended without being supplied says why

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall refuse to reject a spare line, or to drop it (close it unsent), without a stated reason, on every path by which either can be done — one line, one order, a selection, and the Stores queue — and shall record the stage at which it ended, the reason and who ended it. Dropping shall be an authority of its own and shall be possible only until the line is dispatched. A register of requests closed with no reason cannot be reviewed afterwards, and a reason demanded on one path and not on another is demanded of nobody.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-148** — A rejection, a drop and a change of engineer each need a reason, on every path | High | OQ-242, OQ-140 |

FRS-148.2 The database shall refuse a rejection whose reason is empty on every write path — `decide_spare_lines()` (0118) and a direct update of the line alike. FRS-148.3 The system shall record the stage at which a line was rejected (`rejected_stage`) and the reason (`reject_reason`). FRS-148.4 The system shall allow a line to be dropped only by a holder of `spare.drop`, at RM Approval, Commercial, NSM or Stores, and shall refuse a drop of a line already dispatched or received. FRS-148.5 The Spare Requests and Pending Dispatch screens shall refuse a drop with an empty reason. FRS-148.6 The database shall refuse a drop whose reason is empty on every write path. FRS-148.7 A dropped line shall record the reason in `dispatch_remarks`, generate no challan, and add nothing to the engineer's hand stock. FRS-148.8 `reassign_spare_request()` shall refuse a change of engineer with no reason, and the screen shall not submit one. FRS-148.9 A change of engineer shall go through Change engineer on every path, before dispatch as well as after; a plain update of the engineer is refused (0340, D-122). RATIONALE: .2 and .6 exist because the rule already lives in `decide_spare_lines()` for the bulk path and nowhere else, so the single-line and Pending Dispatch paths pass an empty reason (D-043). .8 is URS-035's "retained with ... the reason": a reason the function defaults to an empty string is not retained, it is absent.

### URS-124 — Stores books spares out to one engineer at a time, whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A booking out shall go to one engineer; shall record the quantity sent of each line, which may be less than was asked; shall record the challan date, the courier and remarks; and shall be written whole or not at all, with the stock-out and challan numbers assigned by the system. The parts shall count in the engineer's hand stock from the moment they are booked out: the engineer's acknowledgement confirms their arrival and does not decide it. ### URS-130 — A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. In particular a movement dated inside a stock period that has already been closed shall be refused, because the closing figure was fixed without it. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-163** — A back-dated movement is counted, or refused | High | OQ-155 |

**FRS-163.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. ### URS-173 — Indoor Service runs in stages, from intake to the approved delivery challan

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Indoor Service workflow shall run in stages — Intake, Cleaning, Repair, Service Report, Delivery Challan (pending approval) and Dispatched — shown on each job and on each row of the register, each job showing only the fields of its current and completed stages. Intake shall start from the call the unit came in on (chosen from the open calls of the machine, or by its UCN) and fill the job from that call — the customer and place, the engineer the call is allotted to, the machine, its current cover, the complaint — or receive a DEMO / new device with no call, and shall record the accessories received with their quantities. The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded only after the unit is cleaned, with its report number, the stored file named after that number and the uploader recorded by the system; for a unit with a call the same step shall capture the Visit Entry for that call so the work is not entered twice. A spare shall be requestable from the job through the Spare Request workflow without changing the call.

### URS-174 — Only the Indoor delivery challan is approved, and its approval files the visit

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

An Indoor delivery challan shall be created pending approval, naming who authorises it — the issuer's Reporting Manager, Regional Manager or an NSM — and only that person or an administrator shall approve or reject it, with the decision, who made it and when recorded by the system and printed on the challan. A unit shall not be dispatched while its challan is pending. Approving shall file, against each unit's call, the Visit Entry drafted with its Indoor Service Report — the call left Unsolved, pending Return to Field, with the work details and the uploaded report — through the same path and rules as a visit entered on the call, and shall not complete while any of those visits is unfiled. Rejecting shall need a reason, keep the challan and release its units for a new one. The spare-parts challan is not affected.

RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02: “Only the INDOOR DC needs an approval” — the spare DC is untouched; no key is added and nothing is granted: the approver is named on the DC. The user, 2026-10-03: “it is dynamic based on the user master. So when I say RM / RGM / NSM - it should map as per the user Master”, the NSM being the Regional Manager's own manager, and the person named approving whatever their role holds.

**FRS-237.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-237.1 On the Repair page's service report for a job with a UCN, Visiting Service Engineer shall be a type-search pick (SelectPicker) of every ACTIVE person on the User Master (useActivePeople — Validity not false), defaulting to the signed-in Indoor engineer and, for a saved draft, to the engineer it was saved with; a name already on the draft shall stay listed after that person leaves. FRS-237.2 Choosing a person shall set the draft's engineer email to that person's User Master Email ID (else GMAIL ID), and to the signed-in user's login email where the chosen name is theirs and the row carries none, so the name and the email always name one person. FRS-237.3 The hand stock the visit's spares are consumed from shall follow the chosen engineer, as on a field visit. FRS-237.4 At the DC's approval the visit shall be filed with that engineer and email (reports.engineer / engineer_email, and each consumption line's engineer) while the filer stays the approver's session; the database pins neither to the session — record_indoor_visit() and the guard check the visit's call and its three fixed values, not its engineer — so no migration was needed. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03: the person who repaired the unit is not always the person signed in, and the visit history must name who attended.

**FRS-151.** *(v0.10.78 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-151.1 The database shall stamp `spare_dispatches.dispatched_by` from the authenticated session and discard a caller-supplied value (0211). FRS-151.2 The database shall stamp the RM, Commercial and NSM approver names (`rm_by`, `commercial_by`, `nsm_by`) and times from the session whenever it records a person's approval or rejection, and shall discard a caller-supplied name, on the single-line, per-order and bulk paths. FRS-151.3 The database shall stamp the name recorded against a drop from the session. FRS-151.4 The database shall stamp `received_by` from the session in `receive_spare_shipments()` and on any other receipt path. FRS-151.5 The database shall stamp `recorded_by` on a reconciliation consumption line and `adjusted_by` on an adjusted line from the session, discarding a caller-supplied value. FRS-151.6 An Auto-Approved stage shall carry no name (FRS-147.7). FRS-151.7 Where there is no authenticated session (a migration or an administrative load) the supplied value shall be kept, as FRS-051 keeps it for a call. FRS-151.8 Once a stock out is issued, a signed-in update shall keep its `dispatched_by` and discard a new value, so the Delivery Challan and the Declaration cannot be re-signed afterwards and a re-load of the Stock Out Register cannot replace it (0345, D-126); FRS-151.7 still applies. RATIONALE: `sys_created_by` / `sys_updated_by` (0244) already record the login on every row; the columns above are the ones a reader is SHOWN, on the approval trail and on the Consumption Report, and today they carry whatever the client sent (D-041, D-042).

**FRS-152.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-152.1 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of receipt by anybody other than the engineer named on the request (`is_spare_requester`, 0217). FRS-152.2 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of a line that has not been dispatched. FRS-152.3 The database shall require `spare.receive` for an acknowledgement. FRS-152.4 The Spare Requests screen shall offer Mark received per line and for every line of one order at that stage, with optional receipt remarks. FRS-152.5 An acknowledgement shall confirm every delivery on the line not yet confirmed, and the line shall read Received only when the confirmed quantity reaches the quantity requested (FRS-027). FRS-152.6 "Needs my action" shall offer an acknowledgement only on the reader's own requests. FRS-152.7 The acknowledgement shall not change the engineer's hand stock, which counts the parts from dispatch (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: .1 is enforced in the database because `sr_update` lets the requester write their own request, so a rule held only by the screen is one a direct call walks past; .7 restates the counting rule so that nobody reads the receipt as the moment the stock arrives.

**FRS-153.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-153.1 Pending Dispatch shall list every line that has cleared its approvals and still has a quantity owed, read through `spare_pending_dispatch` (security_invoker), up to 2,000 lines, with "+" on the count at that limit. FRS-153.2 Where the 2,000-line limit is reached, Pending Dispatch shall name the engineer at whom the read stopped and state that engineers after that one, A to Z, are missing. FRS-153.3 Pending Dispatch shall group the queue into one card per engineer, longest-waiting engineer first, each stating its spares, units, orders and days waiting (14 or more red, 7 or more amber). FRS-153.4 Pending Dispatch shall search by engineer, order, spare ID, part, UCN, call and party, and shall pre-fill the search from `?engineer=`. FRS-153.5 Pending Dispatch shall let Stores tick single lines or a whole engineer, a tick on a second engineer replacing the selection. FRS-153.6 Pending Dispatch shall refuse to book out a selection spanning more than one engineer, stating "A stock out goes to one engineer", and `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall refuse the same. FRS-153.7 Pending Dispatch shall accept a quantity per line between one and the quantity still owed, and shall mark a line already partly sent "N of M sent". FRS-153.8 The dispatch dialog shall take a DC date defaulting to today, a courier and dispatch remarks, and shall list what goes. FRS-153.9 `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall create the stock out, assign its stock-out and DC numbers in the series of the DC date, and stamp every line, in one statement that writes all or nothing. FRS-153.10 Pending Dispatch shall disable Dispatch without `spare.dispatch`. FRS-153.11 The engineer's hand stock shall count the parts from the booking time of the stock out (`handstock_movements`), not from the DC date and not from the acknowledgement. FRS-153.12 On success Pending Dispatch shall name the stock out, write an audit entry `spare.dispatch` and open the Delivery Challan. FRS-153.13 Pending Dispatch shall let each engineer's card be expanded and collapsed, offer Expand all and Collapse all, and open every card by itself the first time a queue holds three engineers or fewer. FRS-153.14 The Queue tab shall carry its count and a Stock outs tab shall list what has been issued (FRS-157.14). RATIONALE: .11 is why a DC date may be set: it is the date on the paper, and the stock movement is dated by the database clock, so a back-dated challan cannot move a balance into a closed period.

**FRS-012.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Stores dispatch generates a DC and stock-out; the engineer acknowledges receipt. A line may be dropped (closed unsent, no DC) by a holder of spare.drop at RM Approval, Commercial, NSM or Stores, with a reason (FRS-148).

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

My Workload shall gather, on one page, the counts of the work waiting in every register the reader may open — spare requests by stage and those awaiting the reader, RM approvals, pending dispatch with its ageing, hand stock, material returns, stock transfers, the daily complaint review by stage, and installations awaiting Commercial — and shall request nothing from a register the reader may not open. Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

### URS-118 — A spare request says what is asked for, for which call or which stock, and is numbered by the system

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let an engineer, or a manager for an engineer in their team, request spare parts either against a call or to replenish the engineer's own hand stock (a HandStock request), and a HandStock request shall state why it is needed. A request against a call shall carry the customer, product, serial, complaint and cover that the call records, copied from the call rather than typed again, and a request raised from within a call shall not be movable to a different call. Each part shall be chosen from the Part Master and never typed, offered first from the parts that fit the call's product with the whole master available on request, and asked for in a whole quantity of at least one. The request number and its date shall be assigned by the system. Re-keying what a call already records is where the request and the call stop describing the same machine, and a part typed freehand is a part no stock figure will ever find.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-146** — Raising a spare request | High | OQ-242, OQ-138 |
| **FRS-247** — A spare request on a call with no visit files the visit it implies | High | OQ-239 |

**FRS-146.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-146.1 The Spare Requests screen shall offer the New Spare Request action only to a holder of `spare.request`. FRS-146.2 The request form shall offer two request types, Call Based and HandStock. FRS-146.3 The request form shall require a HandStock reason for a HandStock request and shall refuse the submission with "Enter the reason for the HandStock request." where it is empty. FRS-146.4 The request form shall find the call of a Call Based request by its UCN, call number, party or serial once three characters are typed, and shall offer at most 25 calls. FRS-146.5 The request form shall copy the party, product, serial, complaint and item status (cover) of the chosen call onto the request and shall not offer them for editing. FRS-146.6 The request form shall fix the call, and offer no "Change call", when it is opened from a call. FRS-146.7 The request form shall offer as parts only Part Master entries, chosen from a pick list that takes no free text, and shall state why the list is disabled while the master is empty or still loading. FRS-146.8 The request form shall offer, for a Call Based request, the parts mapped to the call's product, its accessories and the common parts, with a "Show all parts" option offering the whole Part Master; it shall offer the whole Part Master to a HandStock request. FRS-146.9 The request form shall accept a quantity per part as a whole number of at least one, and shall treat a blank or lower value as one. FRS-146.10 The request form shall accept at most 20 spare rows on one request. FRS-146.11 The request form shall accept optional additional remarks. FRS-146.12 The request form shall refuse a submission with no spare ("Add at least one spare."), with no engineer, or of a Call Based request with no UCN ("A Call-Based request needs a call (UC Number)."). FRS-146.13 The database shall assign the OR number (OR-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month) and the OR request date on insert; the form shall show "OR No assigned on submit" and shall not accept either. FRS-146.14 The request form shall generate the request reference WA-yyyymmdd-xxxx when it opens; the reference is the request's primary key, so a colliding reference is refused by the database and never merged into another request. FRS-146.15 The request form shall disable Submit, and say why, while the database is not connected. FRS-146.16 On success the screen shall name the OR number and the reference, reload the register and write an audit entry `spare.request`. FRS-146.17 Once the RM has decided a line, its part and quantity shall not be changed by anybody, the requester included, except by a part rename; Item Status shall be taken from the call when the request is raised and change afterwards only to the call’s own value, and the request type shall not change (0340, D-121, D-122). RATIONALE: .5 because the request is read downstream (cover-based routing under FRS-147.8, the unused-spare report) through the call's own identity, and a re-typed serial is where the two stop agreeing. .14 records that the reference is made in the browser: that is acceptable only because the database key refuses a duplicate rather than overwriting.

**FRS-247.** *(v0.10.67 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-247.1 When a Call Based spare request and its lines have saved, the Spare Request form shall ask the database to file a visit for the request's call (`file_visit_for_spare_request`, 0333). FRS-247.2 The database shall file that visit only where the call has no visit at all, and shall file nothing for a HandStock request or a UCN that is not a call. FRS-247.3 The visit shall read Call Status Unsolved, the requesting engineer, the request's date (India) as the visit date, the Call Pending Reason master entry meaning spare not available (matched on its letters, so SPARE / SPARES and NOT AVAILABLE / UNAVAILABLE all qualify; SPARES NOT AVAILABLE where the master holds none), Update Visit Work Details? = No, and the OR number as Spare Request; the call shall then read Unsolved. FRS-247.4 A second request on the same call, or a retry, shall file nothing more. FRS-247.5 Only the person who raised the request, holding spare.request, may call it; the public key may not. FRS-247.6 Where the visit cannot be filed, the screen shall say the request was submitted but its visit entry was not added, naming the error. RATIONALE: .1 calls it after the lines rather than from a trigger on the request, because a request whose lines fail stays behind (D-044) and must not turn its call Unsolved, and because the bulk import of request history must not file visits for past requests.

### URS-119 — A spare moves to the next approver only on an answer that means yes

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each spare line shall pass an approval stage only when that stage's recorded answer means yes — Approved, Auto-Approved, or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing — and any other answer, however it is worded, shall hold the line with that approver. Which of the Commercial and NSM stages a line needs shall be settled once, when the Reporting Manager approves it: a line under AMC or OGP needs both, a HandStock request needs NSM, and any other line needs neither. A stage that is not needed shall be recorded as Auto-Approved and shall name no approver. A line that has been rejected, dropped, dispatched or received shall read as such wherever its stage is shown. Before the rule was whole-word, "Not Approved" read as approved and parts reached Stores that nobody had cleared.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-147** — The stage of a spare line is read from its answers, whole-word | High | OQ-217, OQ-139 |

**FRS-147.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-147.1 The system shall compute the stage of a spare line in this order: Rejected where any of the RM, Commercial or NSM answers is a rejection; Received where the line has a receipt time; Dropped where Stores dropped it; Dispatched where Stores dispatched it in full; otherwise the first of RM Approval, Commercial and NSM whose answer does not mean yes; otherwise Stores. FRS-147.2 An answer shall mean yes only when, ignoring case and surrounding space, it is exactly Approved, Auto-Approved (with or without the hyphen) or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing. FRS-147.3 Any other answer — "Not Approved", "Approval Pending", "Not cleared for stores processing", a word from an imported sheet — shall hold the line at that stage. FRS-147.4 The database (`spare_line_stage`, 0256 and 0270) shall compute the stored stage by the same rule as the screen (`APPROVED_RE` in src/lib/spareflow.ts), and `check:ui` shall hold the two patterns together. FRS-147.5 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the Commercial answer unless the line is AMC or OGP (`spare_needs_commercial`). FRS-147.6 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the NSM answer unless the line is AMC or OGP or belongs to a HandStock request (`spare_needs_nsm`, 0210). FRS-147.7 An Auto-Approved answer shall be written with no approver name and no approval time. FRS-147.8 The RM approval dialog shall state, before the approval is written, which later stages the line will skip and which it will stop at. FRS-147.9 The Spare Upload shall keep an unrecognised approval word exactly as written (`approvalWord`), so that it holds the line rather than being guessed into Approved or Rejected. RATIONALE: .2 is whole-word because finding 20 was a substring test that read every way of saying no as yes. .7 because inventing an approver on a quality record is worse than an outcome with no name against it. The rule is settled at RM approval and then READ from the record, which is why `spare_line_stage` keeps its six arguments.

### URS-125 — The documents that travel with a stock out are complete and can be produced again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

For every stock out the system shall produce a Delivery Challan and a Declaration on the company's controlled layout, listing exactly what that stock out carried, and shall produce them again on request for any stock out the reader may see, however old it is. The challan shall carry the stock-out and reference numbers and dates, the recipient, the courier, each part and quantity with the total, and the company's statutory identifiers, on sheets each complete in itself; a signature shall appear on it only as URS-057 allows. The Declaration shall state the recipient's address, the parcel's approximate value and its purpose, and each part once with its total quantity, and shall name what is still missing before it is printed. Correcting the engineer's address from the Declaration may update the User Master only for somebody authorised to dispatch, and only the address. A challan that can no longer be found is a shipment whose paperwork cannot be reproduced.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-154** — The Delivery Challan | High | OQ-146 |
| **FRS-155** — The Declaration | High | OQ-147 |

**FRS-154.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-154.1 The Delivery Challan shall be opened by stock-out number from Stock Out, from Pending Dispatch and after booking; the page sits outside the module guard and shows a stock out only where the reader's row-level access admits it. FRS-154.2 The Delivery Challan shall find any stock out the reader may see, however many have been booked since it. FRS-154.3 The Delivery Challan shall print the quantity sent on THIS stock out for each line (`spare_dispatch_lines`), ordered by spare ID. FRS-154.4 Each sheet shall carry the company mark (`COMPANY_LOGO`), the company's name, address, telephone and e-mail, and the title DELIVERY CHALLAN. FRS-154.5 Each sheet shall carry the recipient engineer, the courier, the Stock Out No., the Stock Out Date, the Ref No. and the Ref Date. FRS-154.6 The grid shall carry Sr.No, Order No., Item Code, Description and Qty; the last sheet shall carry the total and every other sheet "Continued on sheet N". FRS-154.7 The challan shall be cut into A4 sheets of 20 rows, each with its own letterhead and signature block and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-154.8 The challan shall carry the dispatch remarks and the company's GSTIN, CIN and PAN. FRS-154.9 The company signature block shall carry the printer's saved signature only where the printer booked the stock out, and the customer block shall always be blank (FRS-067). FRS-154.10 The page shall offer Print, Declaration and Back to dispatch, and state the number of sheets. ### URS-130 — A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. In particular a movement dated inside a stock period that has already been closed shall be refused, because the closing figure was fixed without it. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-163** — A back-dated movement is counted, or refused | High | OQ-155 |

**FRS-163.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050).

FRS-164.2 A material return and all its lines shall be written by one database call that writes all or none. FRS-164.3 A stock transfer and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.4 Where such a call fails, the screen shall say that nothing was saved. FRS-164.5 A stock out is already written this way by `dispatch_spare_lines()` (FRS-153.9). RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). ### URS-138 — A spare part keeps its identity, and a machine is offered the parts that fit it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Part Master shall accept a new part only with a code in the agreed form, a description, a category of Spare or Consumable, and either the products it fits or a deliberate statement that it is common to all products, and shall refuse a code that already exists. A part shall never be deleted; it shall be deactivated. A change to a part's code or description shall carry every record that names the part, in one act, after stating what will move, because hand stock is derived from those records and a part renamed in the catalogue alone changes an engineer's balance. The products a part is mapped to, and the accessories mapped to a main product, decide which parts a call offers; they shall be maintainable only by those who maintain masters, in bulk as well as singly, with any failure named, and a mapping that names a product the register does not hold shall be flagged.

| **FRS-219** — A part's HSN code | Medium | OQ-213 |

FRS-177.3 A description shall be required. FRS-177.4 Spare or Consumable shall be required on a new part. FRS-177.5 The product(s) the part fits, or “Common to all products”, shall be required on a new part, Common being stored as no product. FRS-177.6 A purchase cost shall be a number where entered, and a blank shall be stored as not recorded, never as 0. FRS-177.7 A code that already exists shall be refused. FRS-177.8 The form shall show the part as it will be listed, CODE|Description. FRS-177.9 Editing a part shall allow its category, products and cost to change, shall keep a category the Item Master file brought even where it is not one of those offered, and shall allow an older part with those fields blank to be saved. ### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-153 — A migrated stock movement is recorded as history, and loaded once

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where material returns, stock transfers and stock issues are loaded from the superseded system, they shall be recorded as having happened — exempt from the check that an engineer holds what they return or transfer, that check being a control on ENTRY — and shall be marked as imported so that the exemption applies to them and to nothing else. Each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, so that loading a file a second time corrects it rather than moving the stock again. A line whose parent record is absent shall be held back and counted. Hand stock is derived from these movements, so a movement loaded twice is not a duplicate row — it is an engineer holding parts that do not exist.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |

FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

### URS-077 — A stock report is complete, or it is not a report

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall provide a Hand Stock Report of the stock held by each engineer, showing the movements the balance is composed of and not the balance alone. The system shall load every line of that report before permitting it to be exported. A stock figure is RECONCILED AGAINST, so a file cut short is not a shorter answer but a wrong one — parts read as absent and balances as short, with nothing in the file saying that rows were still arriving when it was written. The balance shall be derived from the recorded movements rather than stored, so the report and the register it is taken from cannot disagree.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-160** — The Hand Stock Report says what its file holds | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-152 |
| **FRS-091** — The Hand Stock Report loads whole before it can be exported | Medium | OQ-79 |

**FRS-160.** *(v0.10.116 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-160.1 Hand Stock Report shall be an administrator's screen by default and grantable to any role (`admin: true`). FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. RATIONALE: .2 because a .csv can carry no second sheet, so a searched file is otherwise indistinguishable from the whole register — the silent partial file URS-077 exists to prevent (D-047).

**FRS-091.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The Hand Stock Report reads `handstock_balance` — the same derived view the Hand Stock register reads, so the two cannot disagree — through `handstock_balance_all()` (0384), ONE request returning the whole balance as one array, because the view costs the same for a page as for everything and paging it was one full aggregate per page. The row count carries a “+” until that one result is in. Every download control is disabled while rows are still arriving, and the writer refuses as well as the button. The file is named HandStock_dd-MMM-yyyy_HHmmss with the extension of the format chosen — the month NAMED, as every date in this system is, and the clock stripped of the colons a file name may not carry. The .csv carries dates as text, being all a CSV can carry; the .xlsx carries a number as a number and a date as a serial plus a format; the .xls is SpreadsheetML 2003, chosen over an HTML table so that it too keeps the types. Every workbook carries a second sheet stating its scope, its row count and the time it was taken, a file whose filter is not written down being one somebody later mistakes for the whole register. The export is recorded in the audit trail.

**FRS-152.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-152.1 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of receipt by anybody other than the engineer named on the request (`is_spare_requester`, 0217). FRS-152.2 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of a line that has not been dispatched. FRS-152.3 The database shall require `spare.receive` for an acknowledgement. FRS-152.4 The Spare Requests screen shall offer Mark received per line and for every line of one order at that stage, with optional receipt remarks. FRS-152.5 An acknowledgement shall confirm every delivery on the line not yet confirmed, and the line shall read Received only when the confirmed quantity reaches the quantity requested (FRS-027). FRS-152.6 "Needs my action" shall offer an acknowledgement only on the reader's own requests. FRS-152.7 The acknowledgement shall not change the engineer's hand stock, which counts the parts from dispatch (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: .1 is enforced in the database because `sr_update` lets the requester write their own request, so a rule held only by the screen is one a direct call walks past; .7 restates the counting rule so that nobody reads the receipt as the moment the stock arrives.

**FRS-153.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-153.1 Pending Dispatch shall list every line that has cleared its approvals and still has a quantity owed, read through `spare_pending_dispatch` (security_invoker), up to 2,000 lines, with "+" on the count at that limit. FRS-153.2 Where the 2,000-line limit is reached, Pending Dispatch shall name the engineer at whom the read stopped and state that engineers after that one, A to Z, are missing. FRS-153.3 Pending Dispatch shall group the queue into one card per engineer, longest-waiting engineer first, each stating its spares, units, orders and days waiting (14 or more red, 7 or more amber). FRS-153.4 Pending Dispatch shall search by engineer, order, spare ID, part, UCN, call and party, and shall pre-fill the search from `?engineer=`. FRS-153.5 Pending Dispatch shall let Stores tick single lines or a whole engineer, a tick on a second engineer replacing the selection. FRS-153.6 Pending Dispatch shall refuse to book out a selection spanning more than one engineer, stating "A stock out goes to one engineer", and `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall refuse the same. FRS-153.7 Pending Dispatch shall accept a quantity per line between one and the quantity still owed, and shall mark a line already partly sent "N of M sent". FRS-153.8 The dispatch dialog shall take a DC date defaulting to today, a courier and dispatch remarks, and shall list what goes. FRS-153.9 `dispatch_spare_lines()` shall create the stock out, assign its stock-out and DC numbers in the series of the DC date, and stamp every line, in one statement that writes all or nothing. FRS-153.10 Pending Dispatch shall disable Dispatch without `spare.dispatch`. FRS-153.11 The engineer's hand stock shall count the parts from the booking time of the stock out (`handstock_movements`), not from the DC date and not from the acknowledgement. FRS-153.12 On success Pending Dispatch shall name the stock out, write an audit entry `spare.dispatch` and open the Delivery Challan. FRS-153.13 Pending Dispatch shall let each engineer's card be expanded and collapsed, offer Expand all and Collapse all, and open every card by itself the first time a queue holds three engineers or fewer. FRS-153.14 The Queue tab shall carry its count and a Stock outs tab shall list what has been issued (FRS-157.14). RATIONALE: .11 is why a DC date may be set: it is the date on the paper, and the stock movement is dated by the database clock, so a back-dated challan cannot move a balance into a closed period.

**FRS-012.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Stores dispatch generates a DC and stock-out; the engineer acknowledges receipt. A line may be dropped (closed unsent, no DC) by a holder of spare.drop at RM Approval, Commercial, NSM or Stores, with a reason (FRS-148).

### URS-009 — Stock accuracy

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Hand stock, stock transfers and material returns shall be tracked so an engineer cannot transfer or return more than they hold.

| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |
| **FRS-094** — Hand stock adjustment: signed, reasoned, bounded, permanent | High | OQ-82 |
| **FRS-013** — Stock derivation & guard | Medium | OQ-242, OQ-08 |
| **FRS-014** — Stock visibility scope | Medium | OQ-62 |

**FRS-159.** *(v0.10.150 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-159.1 Hand Stock shall show one line per engineer and part with Opening, From history, Stock out, Consumed, Transfer in, Transfer out, Returned, Stock level and Last movement, read from `handstock_balance` (security_invoker). FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.3 Hand Stock shall offer In hand (the default), Short (below zero), Settled (zero) and All, each with its exact count once the balance is loaded ("+" only while a restored device cache cut at its cap is shown, which also offers a reload). FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. FRS-159.12 A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's name on spare requests, dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, MRNs and transfers, so the balance is one balance under the new name (0259–0262). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 replace URS-024's old claim that a balance cannot go negative: a consumption line cannot exceed the balance when it is written (FRS-030), but a level can stand below zero where migrated history or an issue never recorded says so, and FRS-044 keeps such a figure exactly — so the register shows it as a finding. FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-161.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-161.1 Material Returns shall offer New MRN only to a holder of `stock.return`. FRS-161.2 The form shall fix the engineer to the signed-in person, and shall let a holder of `users.manage`, `spare.dispatch` or `spare.approve_rm` choose another engineer from the User Master. FRS-161.3 The database shall accept a return for another engineer only from an administrator or a holder of an approval or dispatch authority (`mr_insert`, `can_approve_spares`), and otherwise only a return of the caller's own stock. FRS-161.4 The form shall require the MRN No from the paper slip and keep it as written; the database shall assign the unique reference MRN-YYMM-NNNN. FRS-161.5 The form shall take an MRN date defaulting to today (see FRS-163). FRS-161.6 The form shall offer only parts the engineer holds, and shall not offer a part already on another line. FRS-161.7 The form shall take a good and a defective quantity per line, capped together at what the engineer holds less the other lines, and shall say why a typed value was reduced. FRS-161.8 The database shall refuse a return exceeding the engineer's holding (0039). FRS-161.9 The form shall refuse a submission with no engineer, no MRN No, no spare, a line of zero, or a line or part total above what is held, each with its own message; and shall say, with the hand-stock formula, when the engineer holds nothing. FRS-161.10 The form shall take remarks. FRS-161.11 The database shall refuse an edit of a return (0039). FRS-161.12 On success the screen shall name the reference and write an audit entry `stock.return`. FRS-161.13 A row shall open the MRN: its number, date, reference, engineer, total good and defective, and each item with customer, report number and remarks. FRS-161.14 The register shall list returned items newest MRN first, one row per item, and shall search the MRN number, reference, engineer, spare, description, customer, report number and remarks, with an engineer filter. FRS-161.15 A return shall name the returner’s own stock -- their profile or User Master name -- unless they hold stock.return.others; a return marked import by anybody but an importer is an ordinary, checked return (0339, D-119, D-123). RATIONALE: .4 keeps the slip number as written and does not key on it, because the slips are not issued by this system and two engineers' slips can carry one number; the reference is the identity. The defective quantity is recorded (.7) but raises no nonconforming-material record — that is SR-017, a process gap, and is not claimed here.

**FRS-162.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-162.1 Stock Transfer shall offer New Transfer only to a holder of `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.2 The From engineer shall default to the signed-in person, and shall be changeable only by a holder of an authority to act for others. FRS-162.3 The database shall accept a transfer whose From is not the caller only from an administrator or a holder of that authority. FRS-162.4 The From and To engineers shall be chosen from the active engineers of the User Master, and the database shall refuse a To that is not one. FRS-162.5 The form and the database shall refuse a transfer whose From and To are the same person. FRS-162.6 The form shall offer only parts the From engineer holds, re-read when From changes, shall not offer a part twice, and shall take a quantity from one to what is held; the database shall refuse more than is held (0020). FRS-162.7 The form shall take a transfer date defaulting to today (see FRS-163) and remarks. FRS-162.8 Where the From engineer holds nothing, the form shall say so and state that stock comes from what Stores has dispatched to them, less what they have consumed, handed on or returned. FRS-162.9 On success the screen shall name the transfer number and write an audit entry `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.10 The register shall list every transfer line the reader may see (either engineer in their scope), in pages with Load more, with "+" on its count while more remain, searchable by transfer number, engineers, part and remarks. FRS-162.11 A recorded transfer’s From, To and date are not changed afterwards, except by an importer re-loading it or a User Master rename; a transfer marked import by anybody else is an ordinary, checked transfer (0339, D-119, D-120). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 are the database's because the insert policy today asks only for `stock.transfer`, so anybody holding it can move anybody's stock to any name (D-049); .8 because the screen says stock comes from an acknowledged receipt, which is not how it is counted (D-052).

**FRS-199.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-199.1 The MRN Register upload shall stamp source = import on every row, and the return shortfall check shall pass a row carrying that provenance. FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

**FRS-094.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* 0266: `handstock_adjustments` holds engineer, part, a SIGNED quantity, a mandatory reason and an optional reference (the MTN number); it is the tenth arm of `handstock_movements` (Adjustment, IN when positive, OUT when negative), so the balance and every guard reading the movements include it. The database refuses an engineer who is not an ACTIVE User Master name, a part not on the Part Master, and a minus that would take the engineer below zero, and stamps who recorded it. Insert needs `consumption.reconcile`; there is no update or delete policy, so a wrong adjustment is reversed by another. 0267 adds the table to the User Master rename list (0259). Replaces WinMax's eBizWiz Admin account, whose opening rows 0266 removes. Proved by `handstock_adjustments_test`.

**FRS-013.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock = opening balance + stock-out (from the moment of dispatch) − consumption − transfer-out + transfer-in − returned ± office stock adjustments (0266), with the migrated stock outs and consumption as their own arms (FRS-043). A guard prevents a transfer/return exceeding holdings, counting every movement regardless of visibility. Lowering a stock-out line’s quantity or an opening balance, or deleting either, is refused when it would leave the engineer below zero, and both tables are imaged in record_audit; corrections are Hand Stock adjustments (0339, D-124).

**FRS-014.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock, transfers and returns are scoped to the reporting tree at the database, so a user sees only their own and their team’s stock.

### URS-022 — Acknowledged receipt

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The engineer shall confirm each delivery of a spare as it is received, and a spare shall be recorded as received only when the whole quantity has been confirmed. Only the engineer who raised the request shall confirm it. The confirmation records the parts' arrival; they count in the engineer's hand stock from the moment they were dispatched.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-152** — Only the engineer who raised a spare acknowledges it, and only after it is sent | Medium | OQ-144 |
| **FRS-027** — Per-shipment receipt | Medium | OQ-18 |

**FRS-152.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-152.1 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of receipt by anybody other than the engineer named on the request (`is_spare_requester`, 0217). FRS-152.2 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of a line that has not been dispatched. FRS-152.3 The database shall require `spare.receive` for an acknowledgement. FRS-152.4 The Spare Requests screen shall offer Mark received per line and for every line of one order at that stage, with optional receipt remarks. FRS-152.5 An acknowledgement shall confirm every delivery on the line not yet confirmed, and the line shall read Received only when the confirmed quantity reaches the quantity requested (FRS-027). FRS-152.6 "Needs my action" shall offer an acknowledgement only on the reader's own requests. FRS-152.7 The acknowledgement shall not change the engineer's hand stock, which counts the parts from dispatch (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: .1 is enforced in the database because `sr_update` lets the requester write their own request, so a rule held only by the screen is one a direct call walks past; .7 restates the counting rule so that nobody reads the receipt as the moment the stock arrives.

**FRS-027.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* receive_spare_shipments() stamps each delivery with who confirmed it and when, accumulating spare_request_lines.received_qty. The line is marked Received (received_at) only when the acknowledged quantity reaches the requested quantity, so a part-delivered line remains at the Stores stage.

### URS-024 — Stock integrity

*v0.10.141 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A spare fitted shall be recorded as consumed even where it exceeds the quantity the engineer holds at the moment it is recorded; the hand stock then stands below zero and the Spare Coordinator shall be notified at once, naming the engineer, the part, the quantities and the call, so the stock is corrected afterwards (the user, 2026-10-08: "Allow even if it's negative but notify the Spare Coordinator about the negative spare"). Where a balance stands below zero — from such a booking, migrated history, or an issue that was never recorded — it shall be shown as a finding to be investigated, never hidden or reset.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-137** — Saving a visit, its spares and its feedback | High | OQ-127 |
| **FRS-030** — Consumption beyond hand stock is booked and notified | High | OQ-242, OQ-15 |

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

**FRS-030.** *(v0.10.141 · 08-Oct-2026)* A consumption line, reported or reconciled, exceeding the engineer’s hand-stock balance for that part shall be BOOKED, the balance going below zero, and every active profile whose role is Spare Coordinator shall receive an in-app notification naming the engineer, the part, the balance before, the quantity consumed, the balance after and the UCN (0401, `notify_negative_handstock`); an increase on amendment is treated the same on the delta. Until 0401 such a line was refused (0061). The visit form lists the parts on the engineer’s hand stock including those at or below zero, accepts any quantity, and warns before saving which parts will go below zero. Stock transfers and material returns still move only what is held (0339). Rows naming no engineer or part are not checked, having no balance to check against. A line carrying an import reference (source_ref) is exempt from the cap only when written by a holder of bulk.upload or import.panel, or with no signed-in user; anyone else’s reference is discarded before the cap is read, and raising an imported line’s quantity asks the same (0339, D-119).

### URS-037 — Migrated data is distinguishable from the system’s own record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a stock or service figure is derived partly from records MIGRATED from the superseded system and partly from records this system created, a user shall be able to see how much of the figure comes from each, and to read the figure without the migrated part. Neither reading shall be presented as a correction of the other.
