| **FRS-159** — Reading hand stock, and the movements behind it | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-151, OQ-158 |
| **FRS-194** — What each report holds | Medium | OQ-187 |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |
| **FRS-267** — The old DCCR register loads with its calls | High | OQ-265 |
| **FRS-071** — The field failure register is loaded year by year, whatever shape each year is | Medium | OQ-63 |
| **FRS-043** — The balance declares its migrated part | High | OQ-30 |

**FRS-113.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-113.1 Product Failure Analysis shall read field_call_review in pages up to 8,000 rows, and a figure taken over a capped read shall carry a “+”; Refresh and the time of the last read shall be shown. FRS-113.2 It shall open on the current year, dating a review by complaint date or else registration date, and Every year shall warn that migrated history is included. FRS-113.3 Its cards shall be failures reviewed, any potential effect, risk to patient, failed in warranty, frequent failure and product corrected. FRS-113.4 Its built-in analyses shall be which products fail (under the product as reviewed, FRS-105.5), per cover, root cause, complaint grouping, standard complaint, spare category, machines failing more than once (model and serial), software version in version order and age at failure in age order. FRS-113.5 Each analysis shall be a chart with a table beside it (rank, count, share, cumulative) and a Data labels switch. FRS-113.6 Clicking any bar or table row shall narrow every chart, shown as Narrowed to chips with Clear all. FRS-113.7 The trend shall be offered by month, quarter or year, as a line and a table, each period clickable. FRS-113.8 A user shall be able to build a chart from 22 named dimensions and a form (Pareto, share or ordered), name it and keep it; sharing it with everyone or a role shall need charts.share (a part of config.manage since 0286), enforced by the saved_charts policies; the owner shall be stamped by the database; a shared chart shall be drawn from the reader’s own rows; a chart whose dimension no longer exists shall say so. FRS-113.9 Field Failure Insights shall show reports, open, due a review, CAPA in hand, call still open, effect withdrawn, closed, cancelled and migrated. FRS-113.10 Insights shall cross-filter across machine, cover, status, CAPA, root cause, grouping, customer and period, with chips and Clear all. FRS-113.11 Insights shall chart which machines fail, cover, root cause, grouping, customer, report status and CAPA status, the trend by month, quarter or year with change, share and running total, and a Pareto drilled freely through machine, complaint grouping and root cause with the 80% line; its raw sheet shall say of each report whether it was migrated or raised here. FRS-113.12 Both screens shall say when not connected, when a read failed and while reading.

**FRS-141.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-141.1 Customer Feedback shall list feedback 1,000 at a time with Load more, the count carrying a “+” while more exist, one column per question answered (FRS-017). FRS-141.2 Date shall be the feedback's own `entry_at` — the export's Visit Entry Date on a loaded row, the moment of recording on one entered here — and Loaded on shall show `created_at`. FRS-141.3 A filter shall separate Uploaded from Entered here, by `imported_from`, with counts. FRS-141.4 The database shall admit a reader to a feedback row only where the reader may see the call it names, by the call visibility rule, or holds `feedback.view` with `can_view_all_calls()`; the screen shall apply no further filter by engineer name. FRS-141.5 Search shall cover every column and the complaint; the UCN shall be coloured by its call's state. FRS-141.6 The register shall be kept on the device, reused while fresh and re-synced every 30 minutes; Refresh re-reads it. FRS-141.7 Export shall go through FRS-138. FRS-141.8 The feedback read, write and update permissions shall be asked once per query, not once per row (D-132; measured 12,109 ms to 7.9 ms over 30,000 rows). RATIONALE: .4 because `fb_read` (0008) is `has_perm(’feedback.view’) or has_perm(’calls.report’)` and nothing more, so every engineer can read every customer's feedback through the data interface; the only scoping is a browser filter on the engineer's NAME, which also hides rows the reader may see where the name is spelled differently or absent (D-037).

**FRS-159.** *(v0.10.150 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-159.1 Hand Stock shall show one line per engineer and part with Opening, From history, Stock out, Consumed, Transfer in, Transfer out, Returned, Stock level and Last movement, read from `handstock_balance` (security_invoker). FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.3 Hand Stock shall offer In hand (the default), Short (below zero), Settled (zero) and All, each with its exact count once the balance is loaded ("+" only while a restored device cache cut at its cap is shown, which also offers a reload). FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. FRS-159.12 A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's name on spare requests, dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, MRNs and transfers, so the balance is one balance under the new name (0259–0262). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 replace URS-024's old claim that a balance cannot go negative: a consumption line cannot exceed the balance when it is written (FRS-030), but a level can stand below zero where migrated history or an issue never recorded says so, and FRS-044 keeps such a figure exactly — so the register shows it as a finding. FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-043.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock is derived from nine arms, three of which are migrated: the opening pools (`ref_type = Opening balance`) and the pre-2026 stock outs and yearly consumption exports (`ref_type = Historical`). `handstock_balance` carries `hist_stock_out`, `hist_consumed`, `hist_net` and `on_hand_live` (0102), so the register shows what the migration contributes per line and can present the balance without it. The identity `on_hand - hist_net = on_hand_live` holds for every row. The whole line is restated when the migrated part is excluded, not only the total, so the components on screen still reconcile. Both figures are labelled; neither is offered as a correction of the other.

### URS-038 — Closing a stock period

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

An authorised role shall be able to close a stock period, fixing an opening figure per engineer and part that stands for every movement up to that date, so the register need not re-derive settled history. A close shall not change any balance.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-044** — Period close | High | OQ-31 |

**FRS-044.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `close_handstock_period(date)` writes an opening figure per engineer and part equal to the net of every movement up to that date, then moves a cut-off (`handstock_cutoff()`) that every arm of the movement view tests. The sum and the arms divide the SAME instant — the close takes `< cutoff`, the arms `>= cutoff` — so no movement can fall on both sides. Restricted to an administrator or `consumption.reconcile`; refuses a period that has not ended. A closing figure may be negative, because it must equal exactly what it replaces.

### URS-041 — Migrated stock belongs to a person who can hold it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A stock balance shall be opened only against an active member of the user directory; identifiers appearing in a migrated file that are not people (dealers, customers) shall be excluded before loading, and what is excluded shall be reported.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-047** — Opening stock is an engineer’s | Medium | OQ-34 |

**FRS-047.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Both opening-stock registers resolve each row’s name against the ACTIVE user directory before writing, matching on `lower(btrim(name))` — the same normalisation the balance is keyed on. Rows that do not match are withheld and NAMED before anything is written, so the count approved is the count loaded. An empty directory is refused rather than treated as "nothing matches". `_handstock_opening_engineers.sql` applies the same rule to already-loaded data and reports what it removes.

### URS-049 — Custody of equipment held on the organisation’s premises

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Equipment taken into the organisation’s own premises shall be recorded on a register that identifies it, states WHOSE property it is, and holds the condition it arrived in — that condition being the baseline against which any later damage is judged. Where such equipment is lost, damaged or found unfit for use, that shall be recorded and reported to its owner. The register shall distinguish the organisation’s own stock from a customer’s property, because the duty of care applies to one and not the other, and shall not require a service call to exist: equipment may be held for reasons that have no call.

| **FRS-143** — The Indoor Service Register: list, intake and retained records | High | OQ-136 |
| **FRS-144** — The Indoor Service Register: what each kind of job records | Medium | OQ-137 |
| **FRS-057** — The Indoor Service Register, on two axes | High | OQ-43 |

**FRS-143.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-143.1 The register shall list every job the reader may see, newest first, paged, and its count shall carry a “+” while more exist. FRS-143.2 Status, activity and kind chips with counts shall narrow the list and be remembered; dispatched, closed and condemned jobs may be shown or hidden. FRS-143.3 A banner shall count DEMO units out past their expected return. FRS-143.4 Receive shall file a job at once as Customer property / Repair / Received with a database-issued job number, stamped received by and at, and open it; the condition on arrival is recorded on that job. FRS-143.5 Each field shall be saved when the operator leaves it, and a save that fails shall be shown. FRS-143.6 Marking the unit cleaned shall record the work instruction and its revision (default WI/SER/01) and set status Cleaned; the person and the time shall be stamped by the database from the session, any value the browser sends being discarded. FRS-143.7 A harvested part shall be recorded with its code, description, quantity, condition grade and destination, entered on screen. FRS-143.8 Harvested parts, accessories and checks shall not be deletable through the application; an entry made in error shall be marked void with the reason, the person and the time retained. FRS-143.9 Damage shall be recorded with the date it was reported to the owner and by whom. FRS-144.2 The status shall be settable from nine states, the database refusing Ready, Dispatched or Closed as FRS-059 states. FRS-144.3 A quality check of Fail shall return the job to Under repair; the signer and time shall be shown, and a check signed by the person who received the unit shall be flagged, not blocked. FRS-144.4 A rework shall record the nonconformity reference, the instruction and revision, authorised by, re-verified by and the result, the disposition, and whether an adverse effect was assessed with a note. FRS-144.5 A pre-delivery inspection shall record the source reference, checklist and revision, firmware, result (Pass, Pass with observation, Fail), a held reason and the accessories per packing list. FRS-144.6 A demonstration loan shall record where it went, requested by, expected and actual out and back, custodian, outcome, sale reference, condition out and back and consumables. FRS-144.7 A job of activity Other shall be refused by the database without a description. FRS-144.8 WITHDRAWN (2026-10-04, the user: "Remove only the Checks table, keep QC"): the job no longer records checks of parameter, expected, measured, verdict, instrument and calibration due; rows recorded before are kept, unshown. The quality check (FRS-144 QC, 4.5.6) is unchanged. FRS-144.9 Dispatch shall record a reference, warn (not block) while accessories are outstanding, and show who dispatched and when. FRS-144.10 Condemnation shall be as FRS-060 states.

**FRS-057.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Equipment taken into the workshop is recorded in `indoor_jobs`, one row per intake, carrying `received_at` / `received_by`, `condition_on_arrival`, the physical `tag_no` and a `status` through nine states. TWO INDEPENDENT AXES: `kind` states whose property it is (Customer property | DEMO unit) and is what makes the custody duty applicable or not; `activity` states what is being done to it (Repair | Rework | Salvage | Pre-delivery inspection | Demo | Other). Neither is reachable from the other, so equipment does not change ownership because the work on it changed. `ucn` is NULLABLE — a demonstration unit has no call — which is why the register stands alone rather than being a state of a call. Damage is `damage_note` with `reported_to_customer_at` / `_by`. Accessories are rows in `indoor_job_accessories`, each tagged to the parent job, so what came in with the equipment is a list that can be checked off when it goes back.

## Spare Consumption `/spare-consumption`

Opened by `mod:/spare-consumption`.

### URS-091 — Spare consumption is analysed over a chosen period, counting only what was really fitted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Authorised users shall be able to read, for a chosen period defaulting to the current calendar year, how many spares were consumed, of how many parts and on how many calls; how consumption divides between consumables and spares and between types of cover; which parts and which products consumed most; and how consumption ran month by month. A voided line shall count as nothing; a line shall be dated by when it was booked, in Indian time; and the share of consumption whose part is not yet classified shall be stated, and never shown as nought when it is not. Each figure shall be computed only from the consumption the reader may see.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-114** — Spare Insights | Medium | OQ-102 |

**FRS-114.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-114.1 The period shall default to 1 January of the CURRENT year to today, and This year shall set the same (D-023). FRS-114.2 The figures shall be recalculated when the dates change, after a pause, and on Refresh. FRS-114.3 Every figure shall come from one call of spare_insights(), which runs as the invoker so that cons_read decides the rows (0148, 0254). FRS-114.4 A voided line (quantity 0) shall count as nothing. FRS-114.5 A line shall be dated by when it was booked, and the period shall be read as whole days in India time (0254). FRS-114.6 The cards shall show spares consumed (quantity and lines), distinct parts, calls involved and the percentage unclassified, which shall never be rounded to 0 when any line is unclassified. FRS-114.7 Where any consumption is unclassified, a banner shall say how much and point to Part Master. FRS-114.8 The screen shall show consumable against spare as a donut and a table, consumption by the call’s cover, the highest-consuming parts (25 in the table, 12 in the chart), and consumption by product (top 25) saying whether that list is complete. FRS-114.9 A month-by-month chart shall be shown when the period spans more than one month. FRS-114.10 A failure shall be shown with its message and the bundle that provides the function; not connected and empty results shall be said.

### URS-123 — A decision on a spare or a consumption line names the person who made it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every approval, rejection, drop, dispatch and acknowledgement of receipt of a spare, and every consumption line booked or adjusted by the office, shall name the person who made it, taken from the authenticated session at the moment it is written and not from a value supplied by the screen or by a client of the interface. A stage decided by rule rather than by a person shall name nobody. A name the caller supplies is a name anybody can supply — the Delivery Challan once carried the wrong person's for exactly that reason (0211).

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-151** — The person against a spare or consumption decision is stamped from the session | High | OQ-243, OQ-143 |

**FRS-151.** *(v0.10.78 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-151.1 The database shall stamp `spare_dispatches.dispatched_by` from the authenticated session and discard a caller-supplied value (0211). FRS-151.2 The database shall stamp the RM, Commercial and NSM approver names (`rm_by`, `commercial_by`, `nsm_by`) and times from the session whenever it records a person's approval or rejection, and shall discard a caller-supplied name, on the single-line, per-order and bulk paths. FRS-151.3 The database shall stamp the name recorded against a drop from the session. FRS-151.4 The database shall stamp `received_by` from the session in `receive_spare_shipments()` and on any other receipt path. FRS-151.5 The database shall stamp `recorded_by` on a reconciliation consumption line and `adjusted_by` on an adjusted line from the session, discarding a caller-supplied value. FRS-151.6 An Auto-Approved stage shall carry no name (FRS-147.7). FRS-151.7 Where there is no authenticated session (a migration or an administrative load) the supplied value shall be kept, as FRS-051 keeps it for a call. FRS-151.8 Once a stock out is issued, a signed-in update shall keep its `dispatched_by` and discard a new value, so the Delivery Challan and the Declaration cannot be re-signed afterwards and a re-load of the Stock Out Register cannot replace it (0345, D-126); FRS-151.7 still applies. RATIONALE: `sys_created_by` / `sys_updated_by` (0244) already record the login on every row; the columns above are the ones a reader is SHOWN, on the approval trail and on the Consumption Report, and today they carry whatever the client sent (D-041, D-042).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). **FRS-158.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-158.1 The reconciliation form shall fill the call number, the engineer and that engineer's hand stock from the UCN when the UCN is left, and shall say "No call found for X" where there is none. FRS-158.2 The reconciliation form shall let the office change the engineer from the call's, re-reading the named engineer's hand stock, and the database shall take the stock off, and cap the line at, the engineer named on the line. FRS-158.3 The reconciliation form shall take a GRIR / traceability value (batch, goods receipt or serial) per part and the database shall keep it on the line (`grir`). FRS-158.4 The database shall accept a Reconciliation line against a call that has no visit (0243), and `cons_write` shall refuse `source = Reconciliation` to anybody without `consumption.reconcile`. FRS-158.5 The register shall mark a Reconciliation line as such and a reported line as Report. FRS-158.6 The register shall show a voided line's quantity as "Voided" and an adjusted line's as its quantity with "was N", naming who adjusted it. FRS-158.7 The adjust dialog shall accept a quantity from 0 up to the current quantity plus what the engineer holds, shall require a reason, and shall refuse a line with no database id ("Refresh and try again"). FRS-158.8 The form shall reword a permission refusal as "Your role cannot add a reconciliation line (needs consumption.reconcile)" and shall repeat an error inside the open drawer. FRS-158.9 The register shall show dates dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-158.10 The register shall search every column of the loaded rows, and shall build its columns from the data, the first nine in a preferred order and every field selectable. RATIONALE: .2 is the office correcting whose van the part came out of, and is safe only because the cap in .2 is the database's. .4 is not a hole: the reconciliation exists for a part fitted and never reported, which under 0214 alone could not be booked on exactly the calls it was built for.

**FRS-194.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-194.1 The Consumption Report shall list one row per spare booked, with its call and that call’s latest visit, filterable by call date range, product, customer, city, engineer, part (code or name), UCN and call type. FRS-194.2 The Consumption Report file shall state that its two visit dates are the call’s LATEST visit; that where the call has no visit they fall back to the import file’s date and then to when the spare was booked, and are to be read as "no later than"; and that Visit UID is blank on exactly those rows. FRS-194.3 The Call Report shall list one row per CALL, never one per visit, carrying its latest visit by ENTRY and the spares booked on it, voided lines excluded. FRS-194.4 The Call Report shall filter by call date, product, customer, city, allotted engineer, UCN and call type on any part of the value, and by call status on the WHOLE value. FRS-194.5 The Customer Feedback Report shall list one row per feedback with each question as its own column, and shall offer a column carrying every answer as it was given. FRS-194.6 The Customer Feedback Report shall filter by the feedback’s own date, never the date it was loaded, and by product, customer, state, engineer, UCN, call type and source (Uploaded / Entered here). FRS-194.7 The Customer Feedback Report file shall state that a blank answer is a question not asked of that kind of visit rather than a question unanswered, and that the register holds one feedback per call. FRS-194.8 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall filter by dispatched date range, engineer (chosen from the engineers in the report itself, or typed where that list cannot be built), product and part code, and shall provide a control that clears the filter. FRS-194.9 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall display the first 25 matching rows before any file is taken. FRS-194.10 The Not Consumed Against this Call .xlsx shall carry an About sheet stating its scope, its filter, its rows and the time taken. RATIONALE: .4 matches the status whole because a status is a code — "Solved" as a part-match also takes "Solved - Report Pending", which is an open call. .6 because a migrated feedback loaded in 2026 was given in 2023, and a filter on the load date puts every one of them in the wrong year.

**FRS-062.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The visit report writes every consumption line the engineer has entered, including the line still in the entry control at the moment of saving; the same validation applies to it as to a line already added. “Add Consumption?” offers Yes or None Consumed: Yes requires at least one line before the report will save, and None Consumed withdraws the section. Lines are written in one statement, so a report cannot keep some of its spares and drop the rest.

Where a balance stands below zero — from such a booking, migrated history, or an issue that was never recorded — it shall be shown as a finding to be investigated, never hidden or reset.

FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). **FRS-030.** *(v0.10.141 · 08-Oct-2026)* A consumption line, reported or reconciled, exceeding the engineer’s hand-stock balance for that part shall be BOOKED, the balance going below zero, and every active profile whose role is Spare Coordinator shall receive an in-app notification naming the engineer, the part, the balance before, the quantity consumed, the balance after and the UCN (0401, `notify_negative_handstock`); an increase on amendment is treated the same on the delta. Until 0401 such a line was refused (0061). The visit form lists the parts on the engineer’s hand stock including those at or below zero, accepts any quantity, and warns before saving which parts will go below zero. A line carrying an import reference (source_ref) is exempt from the cap only when written by a holder of bulk.upload or import.panel, or with no signed-in user; anyone else’s reference is discarded before the cap is read, and raising an imported line’s quantity asks the same (0339, D-119).

**FRS-042.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Four database views (0101) compute the analysis: `spare_usage` joins each consumed part to its call for the cover and to the engineer’s User Master row for the region; `spare_usage_rollup` groups it by cover, region and product; `failure_rate_by_product` divides calls in the last 365 days by the machines of that product in the Product Register, giving calls per 100 machines; `failure_modes_by_product` groups calls by standard complaint. All four are security_invoker, so the figures a person reads are computed from exactly the records they may read. The install-base denominator is NOT scoped — it is a property of the fleet — so a user without full call visibility sees their own share of a whole-fleet denominator, and the screen states this rather than leaving it to be inferred. A product with no machines on record shows no rate at all instead of a rate divided by a guess.

### URS-047 — Spares sent to a call are accounted for against it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

FRS-194.6 The Customer Feedback Report shall filter by the feedback’s own date, never the date it was loaded, and by product, customer, state, engineer, UCN, call type and source (Uploaded / Entered here). FRS-194.7 The Customer Feedback Report file shall state that a blank answer is a question not asked of that kind of visit rather than a question unanswered, and that the register holds one feedback per call. FRS-194.8 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall filter by dispatched date range, engineer (chosen from the engineers in the report itself, or typed where that list cannot be built), product and part code, and shall provide a control that clears the filter. **FRS-055.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `unused_spare_report` lists spare lines DISPATCHED or RECEIVED against a call whose part code is not fully accounted for in that call’s consumption — NOT USED where none was booked, SHORT where less was booked than sent. Quantities are aggregated per call and part, so a part sent twice and booked once is not two false findings. Refused and dropped lines are excluded: nothing arrived. Matched on the part CODE, the description being unstable. Only calls in a solved state are assessed, an open call’s parts being legitimately still in the van. `security_invoker`, so a reader sees only the calls their role allows.

### URS-118 — A spare request says what is asked for, for which call or which stock, and is numbered by the system

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let an engineer, or a manager for an engineer in their team, request spare parts either against a call or to replenish the engineer's own hand stock (a HandStock request), and a HandStock request shall state why it is needed. A request against a call shall carry the customer, product, serial, complaint and cover that the call records, copied from the call rather than typed again, and a request raised from within a call shall not be movable to a different call. Each part shall be chosen from the Part Master and never typed, offered first from the parts that fit the call's product with the whole master available on request, and asked for in a whole quantity of at least one. The request number and its date shall be assigned by the system. Re-keying what a call already records is where the request and the call stop describing the same machine, and a part typed freehand is a part no stock figure will ever find.

| **FRS-146** — Raising a spare request | High | OQ-242, OQ-138 |
| **FRS-247** — A spare request on a call with no visit files the visit it implies | High | OQ-239 |

**FRS-146.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-146.1 The Spare Requests screen shall offer the New Spare Request action only to a holder of `spare.request`. FRS-146.2 The request form shall offer two request types, Call Based and HandStock. FRS-146.3 The request form shall require a HandStock reason for a HandStock request and shall refuse the submission with "Enter the reason for the HandStock request." where it is empty. FRS-146.4 The request form shall find the call of a Call Based request by its UCN, call number, party or serial once three characters are typed, and shall offer at most 25 calls. FRS-146.5 The request form shall copy the party, product, serial, complaint and item status (cover) of the chosen call onto the request and shall not offer them for editing. FRS-146.6 The request form shall fix the call, and offer no "Change call", when it is opened from a call. FRS-146.7 The request form shall offer as parts only Part Master entries, chosen from a pick list that takes no free text, and shall state why the list is disabled while the master is empty or still loading. FRS-146.8 The request form shall offer, for a Call Based request, the parts mapped to the call's product, its accessories and the common parts, with a "Show all parts" option offering the whole Part Master; it shall offer the whole Part Master to a HandStock request. FRS-146.9 The request form shall accept a quantity per part as a whole number of at least one, and shall treat a blank or lower value as one. FRS-146.10 The request form shall accept at most 20 spare rows on one request. FRS-146.11 The request form shall accept optional additional remarks. FRS-146.12 The request form shall refuse a submission with no spare ("Add at least one spare."), with no engineer, or of a Call Based request with no UCN ("A Call-Based request needs a call (UC Number)."). FRS-146.13 The database shall assign the OR number (OR-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month) and the OR request date on insert; the form shall show "OR No assigned on submit" and shall not accept either. FRS-146.14 The request form shall generate the request reference WA-yyyymmdd-xxxx when it opens; the reference is the request's primary key, so a colliding reference is refused by the database and never merged into another request. FRS-146.15 The request form shall disable Submit, and say why, while the database is not connected. FRS-146.16 On success the screen shall name the OR number and the reference, reload the register and write an audit entry `spare.request`. RATIONALE: .5 because the request is read downstream (cover-based routing under FRS-147.8, the unused-spare report) through the call's own identity, and a re-typed serial is where the two stop agreeing. .14 records that the reference is made in the browser: that is acceptable only because the database key refuses a duplicate rather than overwriting.

**FRS-247.** *(v0.10.67 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-247.1 When a Call Based spare request and its lines have saved, the Spare Request form shall ask the database to file a visit for the request's call (`file_visit_for_spare_request`, 0333). FRS-247.2 The database shall file that visit only where the call has no visit at all, and shall file nothing for a HandStock request or a UCN that is not a call. FRS-247.3 The visit shall read Call Status Unsolved, the requesting engineer, the request's date (India) as the visit date, the Call Pending Reason master entry meaning spare not available (matched on its letters, so SPARE / SPARES and NOT AVAILABLE / UNAVAILABLE all qualify; SPARES NOT AVAILABLE where the master holds none), Update Visit Work Details? = No, and the OR number as Spare Request; the call shall then read Unsolved. FRS-247.4 A second request on the same call, or a retry, shall file nothing more. FRS-247.5 Only the person who raised the request, holding spare.request, may call it; the public key may not. FRS-247.6 Where the visit cannot be filed, the screen shall say the request was submitted but its visit entry was not added, naming the error. RATIONALE: .1 calls it after the lines rather than from a trigger on the request, because a request whose lines fail stays behind (D-044) and must not turn its call Unsolved, and because the bulk import of request history must not file visits for past requests.

### URS-119 — A spare moves to the next approver only on an answer that means yes

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each spare line shall pass an approval stage only when that stage's recorded answer means yes — Approved, Auto-Approved, or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing — and any other answer, however it is worded, shall hold the line with that approver. Which of the Commercial and NSM stages a line needs shall be settled once, when the Reporting Manager approves it: a line under AMC or OGP needs both, a HandStock request needs NSM, and any other line needs neither. A stage that is not needed shall be recorded as Auto-Approved and shall name no approver. A line that has been rejected, dropped, dispatched or received shall read as such wherever its stage is shown. Before the rule was whole-word, "Not Approved" read as approved and parts reached Stores that nobody had cleared.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-147** — The stage of a spare line is read from its answers, whole-word | High | OQ-217, OQ-139 |

**FRS-147.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-147.1 The system shall compute the stage of a spare line in this order: Rejected where any of the RM, Commercial or NSM answers is a rejection; Received where the line has a receipt time; Dropped where Stores dropped it; Dispatched where Stores dispatched it in full; otherwise the first of RM Approval, Commercial and NSM whose answer does not mean yes; otherwise Stores. FRS-147.2 An answer shall mean yes only when, ignoring case and surrounding space, it is exactly Approved, Auto-Approved (with or without the hyphen) or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing. FRS-147.3 Any other answer — "Not Approved", "Approval Pending", "Not cleared for stores processing", a word from an imported sheet — shall hold the line at that stage. FRS-147.4 The database (`spare_line_stage`, 0256 and 0270) shall compute the stored stage by the same rule as the screen (`APPROVED_RE` in src/lib/spareflow.ts), and `check:ui` shall hold the two patterns together. FRS-147.5 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the Commercial answer unless the line is AMC or OGP (`spare_needs_commercial`). FRS-147.6 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the NSM answer unless the line is AMC or OGP or belongs to a HandStock request (`spare_needs_nsm`, 0210). FRS-147.7 An Auto-Approved answer shall be written with no approver name and no approval time. FRS-147.8 The RM approval dialog shall state, before the approval is written, which later stages the line will skip and which it will stop at. FRS-147.9 The Spare Upload shall keep an unrecognised approval word exactly as written (`approvalWord`), so that it holds the line rather than being guessed into Approved or Rejected. RATIONALE: .2 is whole-word because finding 20 was a substring test that read every way of saying no as yes. .7 because inventing an approver on a quality record is worse than an outcome with no name against it. The rule is settled at RM approval and then READ from the record, which is why `spare_line_stage` keeps its six arguments.

### URS-124 — Stores books spares out to one engineer at a time, whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Stores shall be shown every spare that has cleared its approvals and is still owed, grouped by the engineer it is going to, longest-waiting first, and a queue read to a limit shall say where it stopped. A booking out shall go to one engineer; shall record the quantity sent of each line, which may be less than was asked; shall record the challan date, the courier and remarks; and shall be written whole or not at all, with the stock-out and challan numbers assigned by the system. The parts shall count in the engineer's hand stock from the moment they are booked out: the engineer's acknowledgement confirms their arrival and does not decide it. | **FRS-153** — The Stores queue and booking out | High | OQ-145 |

FRS-153.7 Pending Dispatch shall accept a quantity per line between one and the quantity still owed, and shall mark a line already partly sent "N of M sent". FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. ### URS-129 — A hand-over of stock names two real engineers and is made by somebody who may make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall record a hand-over of spares from one engineer to another, naming both from the User Master's active engineers, never the same person twice. An engineer shall hand over only their own stock; a hand-over of another engineer's stock shall be recorded only by somebody holding an authority to act for others. No hand-over shall exceed what the giving engineer holds. The hand-over shall be recorded in the audit trail, and the register of hand-overs shall be readable in full. What the screen says about where stock comes from shall agree with how stock is counted. A hand-over to a name that is not a person is stock no engineer holds, and a hand-over anyone can make of anyone's stock moves a balance nobody decided to move.

### URS-130 — A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. In particular a movement dated inside a stock period that has already been closed shall be refused, because the closing figure was fixed without it. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-163** — A back-dated movement is counted, or refused | High | OQ-155 |

**FRS-163.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050).

### URS-131 — A spare or stock record is saved whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A spare request, a material return and a stock hand-over, each written as a header and its lines, shall be saved whole or not at all: where any part of one cannot be written, nothing of it shall remain, and the person shall be told that nothing was saved. A header with no lines, or a return with some of its lines, is a record that says less than happened — and for a return, stock has already been taken off an engineer for parts the record does not list.

FRS-164.2 A material return and all its lines shall be written by one database call that writes all or none. FRS-164.3 A stock transfer and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.4 Where such a call fails, the screen shall say that nothing was saved. FRS-164.5 A stock out is already written this way by `dispatch_spare_lines()` (FRS-153.9). RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. ### URS-138 — A spare part keeps its identity, and a machine is offered the parts that fit it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Part Master shall accept a new part only with a code in the agreed form, a description, a category of Spare or Consumable, and either the products it fits or a deliberate statement that it is common to all products, and shall refuse a code that already exists. A part shall never be deleted; it shall be deactivated. A change to a part's code or description shall carry every record that names the part, in one act, after stating what will move, because hand stock is derived from those records and a part renamed in the catalogue alone changes an engineer's balance. The products a part is mapped to, and the accessories mapped to a main product, decide which parts a call offers; they shall be maintainable only by those who maintain masters, in bulk as well as singly, with any failure named, and a mapping that names a product the register does not hold shall be flagged.

### URS-153 — A migrated stock movement is recorded as history, and loaded once

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where material returns, stock transfers and stock issues are loaded from the superseded system, they shall be recorded as having happened — exempt from the check that an engineer holds what they return or transfer, that check being a control on ENTRY — and shall be marked as imported so that the exemption applies to them and to nothing else. Each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, so that loading a file a second time corrects it rather than moving the stock again. A line whose parent record is absent shall be held back and counted. Hand stock is derived from these movements, so a movement loaded twice is not a duplicate row — it is an engineer holding parts that do not exist.

FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

### URS-077 — A stock report is complete, or it is not a report

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall provide a Hand Stock Report of the stock held by each engineer, showing the movements the balance is composed of and not the balance alone. The system shall load every line of that report before permitting it to be exported. A stock figure is RECONCILED AGAINST, so a file cut short is not a shorter answer but a wrong one — parts read as absent and balances as short, with nothing in the file saying that rows were still arriving when it was written. The balance shall be derived from the recorded movements rather than stored, so the report and the register it is taken from cannot disagree.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-160** — The Hand Stock Report says what its file holds | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-152 |
| **FRS-091** — The Hand Stock Report loads whole before it can be exported | Medium | OQ-79 |

**FRS-160.** *(v0.10.116 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-160.1 Hand Stock Report shall be an administrator's screen by default and grantable to any role (`admin: true`). FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. RATIONALE: .2 because a .csv can carry no second sheet, so a searched file is otherwise indistinguishable from the whole register — the silent partial file URS-077 exists to prevent (D-047).

**FRS-091.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The Hand Stock Report reads `handstock_balance` — the same derived view the Hand Stock register reads, so the two cannot disagree — through `handstock_balance_all()` (0384), ONE request returning the whole balance as one array, because the view costs the same for a page as for everything and paging it was one full aggregate per page. The row count carries a “+” until that one result is in. Every download control is disabled while rows are still arriving, and the writer refuses as well as the button. The file is named HandStock_dd-MMM-yyyy_HHmmss with the extension of the format chosen — the month NAMED, as every date in this system is, and the clock stripped of the colons a file name may not carry. The .csv carries dates as text, being all a CSV can carry; the .xlsx carries a number as a number and a date as a serial plus a format; the .xls is SpreadsheetML 2003, chosen over an HTML table so that it too keeps the types. Every workbook carries a second sheet stating its scope, its row count and the time it was taken, a file whose filter is not written down being one somebody later mistakes for the whole register. The export is recorded in the audit trail.

### URS-022 — Acknowledged receipt

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The engineer shall confirm each delivery of a spare as it is received, and a spare shall be recorded as received only when the whole quantity has been confirmed. Only the engineer who raised the request shall confirm it. The confirmation records the parts' arrival; they count in the engineer's hand stock from the moment they were dispatched.

| **FRS-152** — Only the engineer who raised a spare acknowledges it, and only after it is sent | Medium | OQ-144 |
| **FRS-027** — Per-shipment receipt | Medium | OQ-18 |

**FRS-152.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-152.1 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of receipt by anybody other than the engineer named on the request (`is_spare_requester`, 0217). FRS-152.2 The database shall refuse an acknowledgement of a line that has not been dispatched. FRS-152.3 The database shall require `spare.receive` for an acknowledgement. FRS-152.4 The Spare Requests screen shall offer Mark received per line and for every line of one order at that stage, with optional receipt remarks. FRS-152.5 An acknowledgement shall confirm every delivery on the line not yet confirmed, and the line shall read Received only when the confirmed quantity reaches the quantity requested (FRS-027). FRS-152.6 "Needs my action" shall offer an acknowledgement only on the reader's own requests. FRS-152.7 The acknowledgement shall not change the engineer's hand stock, which counts the parts from dispatch (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: .1 is enforced in the database because `sr_update` lets the requester write their own request, so a rule held only by the screen is one a direct call walks past; .7 restates the counting rule so that nobody reads the receipt as the moment the stock arrives.

**FRS-027.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* receive_spare_shipments() stamps each delivery with who confirmed it and when, accumulating spare_request_lines.received_qty. The line is marked Received (received_at) only when the acknowledged quantity reaches the requested quantity, so a part-delivered line remains at the Stores stage.

### URS-024 — Stock integrity

*v0.10.141 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A spare fitted shall be recorded as consumed even where it exceeds the quantity the engineer holds at the moment it is recorded; the hand stock then stands below zero and the Spare Coordinator shall be notified at once, naming the engineer, the part, the quantities and the call, so the stock is corrected afterwards (the user, 2026-10-08: "Allow even if it's negative but notify the Spare Coordinator about the negative spare"). Where a balance stands below zero — from such a booking, migrated history, or an issue that was never recorded — it shall be shown as a finding to be investigated, never hidden or reset.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-137** — Saving a visit, its spares and its feedback | High | OQ-127 |
| **FRS-030** — Consumption beyond hand stock is booked and notified | High | OQ-242, OQ-15 |

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

**FRS-030.** *(v0.10.141 · 08-Oct-2026)* A consumption line, reported or reconciled, exceeding the engineer’s hand-stock balance for that part shall be BOOKED, the balance going below zero, and every active profile whose role is Spare Coordinator shall receive an in-app notification naming the engineer, the part, the balance before, the quantity consumed, the balance after and the UCN (0401, `notify_negative_handstock`); an increase on amendment is treated the same on the delta. Until 0401 such a line was refused (0061). The visit form lists the parts on the engineer’s hand stock including those at or below zero, accepts any quantity, and warns before saving which parts will go below zero. Stock transfers and material returns still move only what is held (0339). Rows naming no engineer or part are not checked, having no balance to check against. A line carrying an import reference (source_ref) is exempt from the cap only when written by a holder of bulk.upload or import.panel, or with no signed-in user; anyone else’s reference is discarded before the cap is read, and raising an imported line’s quantity asks the same (0339, D-119).

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

My Workload shall gather, on one page, the counts of the work waiting in every register the reader may open — spare requests by stage and those awaiting the reader, RM approvals, pending dispatch with its ageing, hand stock, material returns, stock transfers, the daily complaint review by stage, and installations awaiting Commercial — and shall request nothing from a register the reader may not open. Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-117** — My Workload | Medium | OQ-105 |

FRS-117.3 Loading shall begin only once the reader’s reporting team is known. FRS-117.4 Spare Requests shall show Awaiting me, In approval, Awaiting dispatch, Dispatched, Received and Rejected, computed with the register’s own stage rule, each opening Spare Requests filtered to that stage. FRS-117.8 Material Returns shall show MRNs, lines, good quantity and defective quantity; Stock Transfer shall show transfers, lines, units moved and engineers involved. FRS-117.9 Daily Complaint Review shall show exact counts of Review 1, 2 and 3 Pending, Any Potential Effect, Completed and Calls in view, each opening the register filtered to the rows counted — Any Potential Effect to the potential-effect calls (D-022). FRS-117.10 A count taken over a read that stopped at its 4,000-row budget shall carry a “+”. FRS-117.11 A card that is a figure shall open nothing and shall not be styled as a link. FRS-117.12 Each section shall offer Open the register; the page shall offer Refresh, the time of the last read and the number of cards, say Counting N more registers while sections load, say when not connected, and say when no register is open to the reader.
