### URS-130 — A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. In particular a movement dated inside a stock period that has already been closed shall be refused, because the closing figure was fixed without it. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-163** — A back-dated movement is counted, or refused | High | OQ-155 |

**FRS-163.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050).

### URS-131 — A spare or stock record is saved whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A spare request, a material return and a stock hand-over, each written as a header and its lines, shall be saved whole or not at all: where any part of one cannot be written, nothing of it shall remain, and the person shall be told that nothing was saved. A header with no lines, or a return with some of its lines, is a record that says less than happened — and for a return, stock has already been taken off an engineer for parts the record does not list.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-164** — A header and its lines are written in one transaction | High | OQ-156 |

**FRS-164.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-164.1 A spare request and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.2 A material return and all its lines shall be written by one database call that writes all or none. FRS-164.3 A stock transfer and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.4 Where such a call fails, the screen shall say that nothing was saved. FRS-164.5 A stock out is already written this way by `dispatch_spare_lines()` (FRS-153.9). RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-153 — A migrated stock movement is recorded as history, and loaded once

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where material returns, stock transfers and stock issues are loaded from the superseded system, they shall be recorded as having happened — exempt from the check that an engineer holds what they return or transfer, that check being a control on ENTRY — and shall be marked as imported so that the exemption applies to them and to nothing else. Each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, so that loading a file a second time corrects it rather than moving the stock again. A line whose parent record is absent shall be held back and counted. Hand stock is derived from these movements, so a movement loaded twice is not a duplicate row — it is an engineer holding parts that do not exist.

| --- | --- | --- |

FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

### URS-094 — My Workload counts every queue the reader may act on, and each count opens the list it counts

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

My Workload shall gather, on one page, the counts of the work waiting in every register the reader may open — spare requests by stage and those awaiting the reader, RM approvals, pending dispatch with its ageing, hand stock, material returns, stock transfers, the daily complaint review by stage, and installations awaiting Commercial — and shall request nothing from a register the reader may not open. Each count that is a queue shall open that register filtered to exactly the rows counted; a count that is only a figure shall not look as though it opens anything; a count taken over a partial read shall carry a “+”; and a section that fails to load shall be named without stopping the others.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-117** — My Workload | Medium | OQ-105 |

FRS-117.2 Each section shall load on its own and in a fixed order, and a section that fails shall show its own error while the others arrive. FRS-117.3 Loading shall begin only once the reader’s reporting team is known. FRS-117.4 Spare Requests shall show Awaiting me, In approval, Awaiting dispatch, Dispatched, Received and Rejected, computed with the register’s own stage rule, each opening Spare Requests filtered to that stage. FRS-117.5 RM Approval shall show the number waiting, the engineers waiting and the longest wait in days. FRS-117.6 Pending Dispatch shall show spares waiting, those waiting a week or more, units, engineers and orders. FRS-117.7 Hand Stock shall show Short (opening Hand Stock filtered to short lines), units in the field, engineers holding, part codes, stock out, consumed and returned. FRS-117.8 Material Returns shall show MRNs, lines, good quantity and defective quantity; Stock Transfer shall show transfers, lines, units moved and engineers involved. FRS-117.9 Daily Complaint Review shall show exact counts of Review 1, 2 and 3 Pending, Any Potential Effect, Completed and Calls in view, each opening the register filtered to the rows counted — Any Potential Effect to the potential-effect calls (D-022). FRS-117.10 A count taken over a read that stopped at its 4,000-row budget shall carry a “+”. FRS-117.11 A card that is a figure shall open nothing and shall not be styled as a link. FRS-117.12 Each section shall offer Open the register; the page shall offer Refresh, the time of the last read and the number of cards, say Counting N more registers while sections load, say when not connected, and say when no register is open to the reader.

### URS-127 — An engineer's hand stock can be read down to the movements that make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A user shall be able to read, for each engineer and part they may see, the stock in hand and every term it is made of — opening balance, migrated history, stock out, consumption, transfers in and out, returns and office adjustments — such that the terms shown add up to the figure shown; and to open the movements behind any figure, every one of them or a statement that the list is incomplete. A balance below zero shall be shown and explained as a finding rather than hidden. The whole register shall be searchable, not only the part already read. A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's stock with the person. A drill-down whose arithmetic does not add up teaches its reader to stop checking.

| **FRS-160** — The Hand Stock Report says what its file holds | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-152 |

FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. ### URS-129 — A hand-over of stock names two real engineers and is made by somebody who may make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall record a hand-over of spares from one engineer to another, naming both from the User Master's active engineers, never the same person twice. An engineer shall hand over only their own stock; a hand-over of another engineer's stock shall be recorded only by somebody holding an authority to act for others. No hand-over shall exceed what the giving engineer holds. The hand-over shall be recorded in the audit trail, and the register of hand-overs shall be readable in full. What the screen says about where stock comes from shall agree with how stock is counted. A hand-over to a name that is not a person is stock no engineer holds, and a hand-over anyone can make of anyone's stock moves a balance nobody decided to move.

### URS-130 — A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. In particular a movement dated inside a stock period that has already been closed shall be refused, because the closing figure was fixed without it. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-163** — A back-dated movement is counted, or refused | High | OQ-155 |

**FRS-163.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050).

### URS-131 — A spare or stock record is saved whole or not at all

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A spare request, a material return and a stock hand-over, each written as a header and its lines, shall be saved whole or not at all: where any part of one cannot be written, nothing of it shall remain, and the person shall be told that nothing was saved. A header with no lines, or a return with some of its lines, is a record that says less than happened — and for a return, stock has already been taken off an engineer for parts the record does not list.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-164** — A header and its lines are written in one transaction | High | OQ-156 |

**FRS-164.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-164.1 A spare request and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.2 A material return and all its lines shall be written by one database call that writes all or none. FRS-164.3 A stock transfer and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. FRS-164.4 Where such a call fails, the screen shall say that nothing was saved. FRS-164.5 A stock out is already written this way by `dispatch_spare_lines()` (FRS-153.9). RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-153 — A migrated stock movement is recorded as history, and loaded once

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where material returns, stock transfers and stock issues are loaded from the superseded system, they shall be recorded as having happened — exempt from the check that an engineer holds what they return or transfer, that check being a control on ENTRY — and shall be marked as imported so that the exemption applies to them and to nothing else. Each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, so that loading a file a second time corrects it rather than moving the stock again. A line whose parent record is absent shall be held back and counted. Hand stock is derived from these movements, so a movement loaded twice is not a duplicate row — it is an engineer holding parts that do not exist.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |

**FRS-199.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-199.1 The MRN Register upload shall stamp source = import on every row, and the return shortfall check shall pass a row carrying that provenance. FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

RATIONALE: .3 and .4 replace URS-024's old claim that a balance cannot go negative: a consumption line cannot exceed the balance when it is written (FRS-030), but a level can stand below zero where migrated history or an issue never recorded says so, and FRS-044 keeps such a figure exactly — so the register shows it as a finding. FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-161.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-161.1 Material Returns shall offer New MRN only to a holder of `stock.return`. FRS-161.2 The form shall fix the engineer to the signed-in person, and shall let a holder of `users.manage`, `spare.dispatch` or `spare.approve_rm` choose another engineer from the User Master. FRS-161.3 The database shall accept a return for another engineer only from an administrator or a holder of an approval or dispatch authority (`mr_insert`, `can_approve_spares`), and otherwise only a return of the caller's own stock. FRS-161.4 The form shall require the MRN No from the paper slip and keep it as written; the database shall assign the unique reference MRN-YYMM-NNNN. FRS-161.5 The form shall take an MRN date defaulting to today (see FRS-163). FRS-161.6 The form shall offer only parts the engineer holds, and shall not offer a part already on another line. FRS-161.7 The form shall take a good and a defective quantity per line, capped together at what the engineer holds less the other lines, and shall say why a typed value was reduced. FRS-161.8 The database shall refuse a return exceeding the engineer's holding (0039). FRS-161.9 The form shall refuse a submission with no engineer, no MRN No, no spare, a line of zero, or a line or part total above what is held, each with its own message; and shall say, with the hand-stock formula, when the engineer holds nothing. FRS-161.10 The form shall take remarks. FRS-161.11 The database shall refuse an edit of a return (0039). FRS-161.12 On success the screen shall name the reference and write an audit entry `stock.return`. FRS-161.13 A row shall open the MRN: its number, date, reference, engineer, total good and defective, and each item with customer, report number and remarks. FRS-161.14 The register shall list returned items newest MRN first, one row per item, and shall search the MRN number, reference, engineer, spare, description, customer, report number and remarks, with an engineer filter. FRS-161.15 A return shall name the returner’s own stock -- their profile or User Master name -- unless they hold stock.return.others; a return marked import by anybody but an importer is an ordinary, checked return (0339, D-119, D-123). RATIONALE: .4 keeps the slip number as written and does not key on it, because the slips are not issued by this system and two engineers' slips can carry one number; the reference is the identity. The defective quantity is recorded (.7) but raises no nonconforming-material record — that is SR-017, a process gap, and is not claimed here.

**FRS-162.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-162.1 Stock Transfer shall offer New Transfer only to a holder of `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.2 The From engineer shall default to the signed-in person, and shall be changeable only by a holder of an authority to act for others. FRS-162.3 The database shall accept a transfer whose From is not the caller only from an administrator or a holder of that authority. FRS-162.4 The From and To engineers shall be chosen from the active engineers of the User Master, and the database shall refuse a To that is not one. FRS-162.5 The form and the database shall refuse a transfer whose From and To are the same person. FRS-162.6 The form shall offer only parts the From engineer holds, re-read when From changes, shall not offer a part twice, and shall take a quantity from one to what is held; the database shall refuse more than is held (0020). FRS-162.7 The form shall take a transfer date defaulting to today (see FRS-163) and remarks. FRS-162.8 Where the From engineer holds nothing, the form shall say so and state that stock comes from what Stores has dispatched to them, less what they have consumed, handed on or returned. FRS-162.9 On success the screen shall name the transfer number and write an audit entry `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.10 The register shall list every transfer line the reader may see (either engineer in their scope), in pages with Load more, with "+" on its count while more remain, searchable by transfer number, engineers, part and remarks. FRS-162.11 A recorded transfer’s From, To and date are not changed afterwards, except by an importer re-loading it or a User Master rename; a transfer marked import by anybody else is an ordinary, checked transfer (0339, D-119, D-120). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 are the database's because the insert policy today asks only for `stock.transfer`, so anybody holding it can move anybody's stock to any name (D-049); .8 because the screen says stock comes from an acknowledged receipt, which is not how it is counted (D-052).

**FRS-199.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-199.1 The MRN Register upload shall stamp source = import on every row, and the return shortfall check shall pass a row carrying that provenance. FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

**FRS-094.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* 0266: `handstock_adjustments` holds engineer, part, a SIGNED quantity, a mandatory reason and an optional reference (the MTN number); it is the tenth arm of `handstock_movements` (Adjustment, IN when positive, OUT when negative), so the balance and every guard reading the movements include it. The database refuses an engineer who is not an ACTIVE User Master name, a part not on the Part Master, and a minus that would take the engineer below zero, and stamps who recorded it. Insert needs `consumption.reconcile`; there is no update or delete policy, so a wrong adjustment is reversed by another. 0267 adds the table to the User Master rename list (0259). Replaces WinMax's eBizWiz Admin account, whose opening rows 0266 removes. Proved by `handstock_adjustments_test`.

**FRS-013.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock = opening balance + stock-out (from the moment of dispatch) − consumption − transfer-out + transfer-in − returned ± office stock adjustments (0266), with the migrated stock outs and consumption as their own arms (FRS-043). A guard prevents a transfer/return exceeding holdings, counting every movement regardless of visibility. Lowering a stock-out line’s quantity or an opening balance, or deleting either, is refused when it would leave the engineer below zero, and both tables are imaged in record_audit; corrections are Hand Stock adjustments (0339, D-124).

**FRS-014.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock, transfers and returns are scoped to the reporting tree at the database, so a user sees only their own and their team’s stock.

# Indoor Service

## Indoor Service Register `/indoor`

Opened by `mod:/indoor`.

### URS-116 — What is recorded about equipment in the workshop is kept and attributed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every record made about equipment in the workshop — the parts recovered from it, the accessories it came with, each check made on it and its verdict — shall be retained once made and corrected by a further record rather than removed. Who cleaned the equipment, and every later change to the job, shall be recorded by the system from the signed-in person rather than taken from what the screen sends. Damage shall be recordable together with when and by whom it was reported to the owner.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-143** — The Indoor Service Register: list, intake and retained records | High | OQ-136 |

**FRS-143.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-143.1 The register shall list every job the reader may see, newest first, paged, and its count shall carry a “+” while more exist. FRS-143.2 Status, activity and kind chips with counts shall narrow the list and be remembered; dispatched, closed and condemned jobs may be shown or hidden. FRS-143.3 A banner shall count DEMO units out past their expected return. FRS-143.4 Receive shall file a job at once as Customer property / Repair / Received with a database-issued job number, stamped received by and at, and open it; the condition on arrival is recorded on that job. FRS-143.5 Each field shall be saved when the operator leaves it, and a save that fails shall be shown. FRS-143.6 Marking the unit cleaned shall record the work instruction and its revision (default WI/SER/01) and set status Cleaned; the person and the time shall be stamped by the database from the session, any value the browser sends being discarded. FRS-143.7 A harvested part shall be recorded with its code, description, quantity, condition grade and destination, entered on screen. FRS-143.8 Harvested parts, accessories and checks shall not be deletable through the application; an entry made in error shall be marked void with the reason, the person and the time retained. FRS-143.9 Damage shall be recorded with the date it was reported to the owner and by whom. FRS-143.10 Every change to a job and to its parts, accessories and checks shall be captured by the database's row audit (`record_audit`). FRS-143.11 Receiving a unit shall be written to `audit_log` as `indoor.receive`. FRS-143.12 Where the database is not connected the screen shall say that it reads live data only. RATIONALE: .1 because `listIndoorJobs(limit = 500)` and `countMore={false}` make the 501st job disappear under an exact-looking count (D-040). .6–.10 are D-039: `markIndoorCleaned` sends `cleaned_by: uid` and 0158 only fills the time; the three child tables are `FOR ALL` with DELETE granted; a part is added with a blank code and cannot be edited; `reported_to_customer_at`/`_by` exist and are on no screen; and none of the indoor tables is in 0225’s audited list.

### URS-117 — Each kind of workshop job records what that kind of work requires

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A rework shall record the nonconformity it answers, the instruction and revision it followed, who authorised it, who re-verified the product and the result, its disposition and whether any adverse effect was assessed. A pre-delivery inspection shall record its checklist and revision, the firmware and its result. A demonstration loan shall record where the unit went, who holds it and when it is due back, and overdue loans shall be counted. Work of any other kind shall be described.

FRS-144.2 The status shall be settable from nine states, the database refusing Ready, Dispatched or Closed as FRS-059 states. FRS-144.3 A quality check of Fail shall return the job to Under repair; the signer and time shall be shown, and a check signed by the person who received the unit shall be flagged, not blocked. FRS-144.4 A rework shall record the nonconformity reference, the instruction and revision, authorised by, re-verified by and the result, the disposition, and whether an adverse effect was assessed with a note. ### URS-169 — The Indoor Service register carries the R/SER/07 record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The workshop register shall carry every column of the controlled record R/SER/07 INDOOR SERVICE EQUIPMENT FAILURE REGISTER — incoming date, UC No, Field Service Report No, engineer, customer name and place, product and serial, accessories received, problem reported, cleaned as per WI/SER/01, the machine's cover (WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC) as the record's Status, Indoor Service Report No, DC No. and date, dispatch date, remarks and verified by — and shall produce it as the record is kept: a Customer – Devices sheet and a Demo sheet, viewed on screen, downloaded as Excel and printed. A completed entry shall be verifiable by a supervisor holding a permission of its own, the verifier and the time recorded by the system.

**FRS-225.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-225.1 An indoor job shall carry Field Service Report No, Engineer Name, Customer Place, Problem Reported, Indoor Service Report No, DC date, Remarks and Status (cover) as fields of their own, in the record's words; the workflow status and the condition on arrival shall keep their meanings. FRS-225.2 Status (cover) shall be read from the Product Database by model and serial when the product or serial of a job changes, normalised to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC (coverCode; cover_code() in the database), stay editable, and be left unchanged with a message where no single machine matches. FRS-225.3 Receiving a unit from a call shall fill the job from it (FRS-232); entering a UCN on a job afterwards shall prefill Engineer Name from the call's allocated engineer, Customer Place from its city and Customer Name from its party, only into fields still blank. FRS-225.4 A job made a DEMO unit with no engineer named shall read “Indoor Service” in Engineer Name. FRS-225.5 Verifying an entry shall require indoor.verify, shall be refused unless the job is Dispatched, Closed or Condemned, and shall record the verifier and time from the session, discarding any value sent; indoor.verify shall be granted to no role by migration. FRS-225.6 The screen shall show the register in the R/SER/07 column order, one sheet at a time (Customer – Devices: Customer property; Demo: DEMO units), S.No running within the sheet in incoming-date order, optionally bounded by an incoming-date range; Cleaned as per WI/SER/01 shall read Yes when the cleaning is recorded; Accessories Received shall list the accessory names, each followed by “x” and the quantity received where that is not 1, or read Nil; DC No./Date shall join the dispatch reference and DC date; Verified By shall show the verifier's name. FRS-225.7 The Excel download shall carry the two sheets in that order and those headings, Incoming Date and Dispatch Date as Excel dates, and an About sheet; it shall be refused without export.data and written to audit_log as indoor.register_download. FRS-225.8 The printable register (/indoor-register/<sheet>) shall be landscape A4 with the company's mark, the organisation, SERVICE, the record's title, the sheet title and PAGE NO, the eighteen columns with their header repeated on every printed page, the property notice and “TMPL No: R/SER/07 Rev: AUG 2025”; it shall require the Indoor Service Register's module key and export.data, write indoor.register_print to audit_log, and reproduce a stored signature beside Verified By only for the person printing (URS-057). FRS-225.9 The R/SER/07 view shall be the screen's default; on screen only it shall carry a Stage column (FRS-233) and, in Indoor Service Report No, a link to the uploaded report or — once the unit is cleaned and to a holder of indoor.work — an Upload button (FRS-233). RATIONALE: the paper record's Status column is the cover, not the workshop stage, which is why it is a new field rather than a second meaning of `status` (0320).

**FRS-232.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-232.1 “Receive equipment” shall open an intake form, not file a blank job. FRS-232.2 Field Return (renamed from “From a call”, 2026-10-04): picking Product Name (the Product Register's names) and Serial Number (searched within that product) shall list the machine's OPEN calls (`openCallsFor`, pending_calls); choosing one, or typing a UCN, shall fill UC No, Customer Name, Customer Place (the call's city), Engineer Name (the engineer the call is allotted to), Product Name, Product Sl. No, Problem Reported (the call's Complaint Reported), the call's Standard Complaint (shown read only, kept on the job as `standard_complaint`) and Status (cover) — the machine's cover now from the Product Database through coverCode(), else the call's item status; every filled value shall stay editable. FRS-232.3 A DEMO / new device shall be received with no call, as a DEMO unit, Engineer Name “Indoor Service”. FRS-232.4 The accessories received shall be an add-item list — item, quantity, serial, tag — the quantity stored on `indoor_job_accessories.qty`, default 1, refused at 0 or below by the database. FRS-232.5 Filing shall need indoor.receive and create the job (numbered by the database) and its accessory lines, then open it. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02; the open-call lookup is the one Pending Registrations uses, not a copy. FRS-232.9 (2026-10-04) A Field Return shall be received as a Troubleshooting job, the activity fixed and not chosen; a Troubleshooting job shall not be dispatched or closed before its quality check, as a Repair (0370). The Identification tag of the unit and of each accessory shall be chosen as Yes, Identified or Not Identified, a value typed before being kept; an accessory received shall record its item, quantity and tag, without a serial. FRS-232.10 The cleaning work instruction's revision shall be a number of two digits, 01 when none is given. FRS-232.11 (2026-10-04, 0372) A job with a call shall carry, at the top of its Repair page, a Call Status (the visit form's three) and a Call Pending Reason by the visit form's rules — required while Unsolved, Report Pending for a pending report, none for a completed one — and they shall be the visit's values, the visit filing with them; an Unsolved job with no reason shall not have its Indoor DC approved. The job's status shall be derived from them once cleaned: Solved → Ready (a Repair, Rework or Troubleshooting first needing its QC Pass, until then QC); Unsolved with spares not available → Awaiting spares; otherwise Under repair; never once Dispatched, Closed or Condemned. A DEMO / new device shall keep its Status chosen by hand. FRS-232.12 Create Indoor DC shall not ask for the MIRN No. / Customer Ref No., its date, or the mode of despatch; the printed Indoor DC shall carry no SERVICE CENTER line and three signature boxes: ISSUED BY, AUTHORISED BY and RECEIVED BY (WITH DATE). FRS-232.13 While the Create Indoor DC form is open beside a job, the job's DC page shall show a read-only summary of the unit — customer, product and serial, call and its Call Status, job status, report number, and accessories still to go back — and no fields to fill. FRS-232.14 (0374) The intake shall offer three ways in — Field Return, Demo and New Device — each fixing the job's kind and activity: Customer property / Troubleshooting, DEMO unit / Demo, New device / Troubleshooting. A New device shall be its own kind, consigned like a DEMO unit to the party it is going to, and shall have its own sheet (New Devices) on the R/SER/07 register.

### URS-170 — A DEMO unit of an imported product is pre-delivery tested before it leaves

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A DEMO unit whose product is imported shall not leave the workshop until the controlled record R/SER/QC/007 PRE DELIVERY TESTING is complete and every check reads OK, the inspector recorded by the system with their designation, and the record shall be printable as the form is kept. The Product Master shall say whether each product line is imported; where that is not known, the test shall not be demanded and the screen shall say it is not known. Equipment manufactured in-house, and customer property, are not subject to it.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-226** — R/SER/QC/007 Pre-Delivery Testing for a DEMO unit of an imported product | High | OQ-221, OQ-222 |
| **FRS-227** — The Product Master says whether a line is imported | Medium | OQ-221 |

**FRS-226.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-226.1 A job shall have at most one Pre-Delivery Testing record (`indoor_pdt`) holding Date, Measuring Equipment ID No, Software Version, HV and HT as printed on the form, checks 1–5 each OK or NOT OK, and the measured Volume (Vte), Peep and O2% (CMV/ACMV) and PIP, Peep and O2% (PCMV) at FiO2 21, 60 and 100 %; it shall be read with the module key, written with indoor.work or indoor.receive, and never deleted. FRS-226.2 Signing it shall record the inspector from the session with their name and designation at that moment and the time, discarding any value sent; a later edit shall not change them. FRS-226.3 Whether a job owes the test shall be decided by `indoor_job_is_imported()`: the machine's own product code (Product Database, model + serial) and its Product Master line first, else the product name where every code of that name gives the same non-blank answer; otherwise unknown. FRS-226.4 A DEMO unit whose product is imported shall be refused the move to Dispatched or Closed while it has no test, while any field is blank or it is unsigned (naming what is blank), or while any of checks 1–5 reads NOT OK (naming which). FRS-226.5 A DEMO unit whose product is in-house, or whose imported-ness is unknown, and every customer-property job, shall not be asked for the test; the screen shall say in-house, or say unknown and that the Product Master should be set. FRS-226.6 The screen shall show the test only for a DEMO unit of an imported product, laid out as the form (the two mode tables as grids with FiO2 21 / 60 / 100 % columns and the set values printed), and shall say what is still blank or NOT OK. FRS-226.7 The printable form (/indoor-pdt/<job>) shall reproduce R/SER/QC/007 — the company's mark, the organisation, QUALITY CONTROL, PRE DELIVERY TESTING, PAGE NO, the fields, checks 1–6 with OK / NOT OK boxes (6 an instruction, unboxed), the two mode tables, Inspected by Name / Designation / Sign, the property notice and “TMPL No: R/SER/QC/007 Rev: AUG 2025”; it shall print a blank or partial test with a band saying it is not complete; it shall require the module key, write indoor.pdt_print to audit_log, and reproduce a stored signature only where the inspector is the person printing (URS-057). RATIONALE: the rule is asked on the MOVE into Dispatched or Closed, not on every later edit, so a unit already out before it existed can still be remarked and verified; unknown does not require the test by the user's decision (2026-10-02), and saying so on the job is what gets the master filled.

**FRS-227.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-227.1 A product line shall carry Imported (Yes / No), blank until set. FRS-227.2 The Product Master screen shall show it as a column and let a holder of masters.edit.records set it; a save the database refuses or matches nothing shall be reported. FRS-227.3 The Product Master bulk upload shall read an “Imported” column as Yes / No; a blank cell or an absent column shall leave the stored value alone. RATIONALE: no default either way — Yes would demand a test of in-house equipment, No would let an imported unit out untested (0319).

### URS-171 — A unit leaves the workshop on a delivery challan of its own

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Equipment leaving the Indoor Service workshop shall go out on a delivery challan of the workshop's own (Indoor_DC), separate from the spare-parts challan and printed as the template is laid out. The challan number shall be issued by the system in its own series (IDC-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month by the challan date) and shall not be settable by anybody. One challan may carry several units going to the same consignee and no others; each unit, with each of its accessories, shall be a line. Issuing a challan shall record its number and date against every unit on it as the register's DC No. and date, shall require the dispatch permission, and shall be refused for a unit that is not Ready, that is already on a challan, or that the workshop's rules would not let leave — in the words of the rule that refuses it. A challan, once issued, shall not be deleted, and shall be re-printable from the register.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-228** — Indoor_DC: issued by the database, one consignee, stamped on each unit, never a way round a dispatch rule | High | OQ-223, OQ-224, OQ-226 |
| **FRS-235** — The Indoor DC is approved by its Authorised By; rejection releases the units | High | OQ-223, OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-234, OQ-244 |
| **FRS-239** — The Indoor job as a window with the DC beside it, the DC in the form's language, and the register in the app's table | Medium | OQ-229 |

**FRS-228.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-228.1 An Indoor DC (`indoor_dcs`, `indoor_dc_lines`, 0321, 0323) shall carry DC No., DATE (the date of entry, India; no date is accepted from the caller), To, AUTHORISED BY and its approval (FRS-235), MIRN No. / CUSTOMER REF No. and its DATE, Mode of Despatch, PURPOSE and the issuer's name; its number shall be IDC-YYMM-NNNN, issued by the database from a monthly counter by the DC date (`next_indoor_dc_no()`), a number sent with it being discarded even from a trusted role, and an edit shall not change the number or the issuer. FRS-228.2 It shall be written only by `create_indoor_dc()`: the tables shall be readable with the Indoor Service Register's module key and shall have no write policy and no insert, update or delete grant for a signed-in user, and the counter and the number generator shall not be callable through the API. FRS-228.3 `create_indoor_dc()` shall require indoor.dispatch, a consignee (To), and at least one unit; it shall refuse units whose consignees differ (the party for customer property, the going-to party for a DEMO unit, compared ignoring case and surrounding space), a unit that is not Ready, a unit already carrying a DC No., a unit whose Indoor Service Report is not uploaded (FRS-233), and a blank AUTHORISED BY or one `indoor_dc_authorisers()` does not offer the issuer (FRS-235). FRS-228.4 Each unit shall be tried against `indoor_jobs_guard()` by a move to Dispatched that is always rolled back, and a unit the guard refuses shall be refused with the guard's message prefixed by the job number, nothing of the DC being kept. FRS-228.5 The lines shall be, per unit in the order chosen, the equipment — PART No. the machine's product code from the Product Database by model and serial, else the one code its name has on the Product Master, else blank (`indoor_job_product_code()`); DESCRIPTION the product and “Sl.No” and the serial — then each accessory with a name or serial (DESCRIPTION its name and serial, PART No. blank); QTY 1 for the equipment and, for an accessory, the quantity received (0323); PURPOSE the DC's, overridable per line. FRS-228.6 Issuing shall set each unit's DC No. (dispatch_ref) to the DC number and its DC date to the DC date, shall not change its status, and the dispatch time and person shall be stamped by the existing guard. FRS-228.7 A DC shall not be deleted (no delete grant, and `no_hard_delete`). FRS-228.8 The Indoor Service screen shall let a holder of indoor.dispatch tick Ready units with no DC No., say when the ticked units go to different consignees, and open Create Indoor DC: To prefilled from the Party Master (name, address, city, state and pincode) and editable, DATE shown as the date of entry and not editable, AUTHORISED BY chosen from the issuer's list (FRS-235), the customer reference and its date, Mode of Despatch, PURPOSE once and per line, and a preview of the lines; creating shall open the print. FRS-228.9 The screen shall list every Indoor DC (number, date, To, units, lines, mode, issuer), each re-printable, and a unit's drawer shall offer the print of the DC it is on. FRS-228.10 The print (/indoor-dc/<DC No.>) shall reproduce the template: the company's mark and the Service Center's letterhead text (one constant, not the spare DC's), DELIVERY CHALLAN (DC), GSTIN, DC No. and DATE, To, MIRN No. / CUSTOMER REF No. and DATE, Mode of Despatch, S.No. / PART No. / DESCRIPTION / QTY. / PURPOSE, the boxes ISSUED BY (Stores), AUTHORISED BY, RECEIVED BY (WITH DATE) and PACKED & DESPATCH BY, and the note to return a signed copy; ISSUED BY shall print the issuer's name; AUTHORISED BY shall print empty with a PENDING APPROVAL band naming whom the DC waits for until it is approved, and the approver's name once approved; a rejected DC shall print a REJECTED band with its reason; the other two shall print empty, and a stored signature shall appear only where the issuer is the person printing (URS-057); it shall require the module key and write indoor.dc_print to audit_log. RATIONALE: .4 asks the guard rather than copying its rules, so whatever the guard is changed to say, the DC says; .2 because a DC written straight through the API would be a challan whose units were never stamped or tried.

FRS-235.2 `create_indoor_dc()` shall require one of them as AUTHORISED BY, store it as the list spells it, and create the DC Pending approval; the units keep their DC No. as a reservation. FRS-235.3 `approve_indoor_dc()` and `reject_indoor_dc()` shall be allowed only to the person named — their User Master name or profile name matching, ignoring case — or an administrator (`indoor_dc_may_approve()`), only while the DC is pending; approval shall file every unit's drafted visit (FRS-234.3) in the same transaction, refuse the DC's own issuer unless an administrator, and stamp approved_by, approved_by_name and approved_at from the session; a check-only call shall ask who, state and that every unit with a UCN has its visit drafted. ### URS-173 — Indoor Service runs in stages, from intake to the approved delivery challan

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Indoor Service workflow shall run in stages — Intake, Cleaning, Repair, Service Report, Delivery Challan (pending approval) and Dispatched — shown on each job and on each row of the register, each job showing only the fields of its current and completed stages. Intake shall start from the call the unit came in on (chosen from the open calls of the machine, or by its UCN) and fill the job from that call — the customer and place, the engineer the call is allotted to, the machine, its current cover, the complaint — or receive a DEMO / new device with no call, and shall record the accessories received with their quantities. The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded only after the unit is cleaned, with its report number, the stored file named after that number and the uploader recorded by the system; for a unit with a call the same step shall capture the Visit Entry for that call so the work is not entered twice. A spare shall be requestable from the job through the Spare Request workflow without changing the call.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-232** — Indoor intake: from a call, or a DEMO / new device, with the accessories counted | Medium | OQ-226, OQ-227 |
| **FRS-233** — The Indoor stages: the stepper, what each stage shows, and the report uploaded after cleaning | High | OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-247 |
| **FRS-234** — The visit drafted with the Indoor report, and filed against the call at the DC's approval | High | OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-234 |
| **FRS-236** — Request spare from an Indoor job | Low | OQ-227 |
| **FRS-237** — The Indoor visit's Visiting Service Engineer is picked from the User Master | Medium | OQ-228, OQ-229 |
| **FRS-239** — The Indoor job as a window with the DC beside it, the DC in the form's language, and the register in the app's table | Medium | OQ-229 |

**FRS-232.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-232.1 “Receive equipment” shall open an intake form, not file a blank job. FRS-232.2 Field Return (renamed from “From a call”, 2026-10-04): picking Product Name (the Product Register's names) and Serial Number (searched within that product) shall list the machine's OPEN calls (`openCallsFor`, pending_calls); choosing one, or typing a UCN, shall fill UC No, Customer Name, Customer Place (the call's city), Engineer Name (the engineer the call is allotted to), Product Name, Product Sl. No, Problem Reported (the call's Complaint Reported), the call's Standard Complaint (shown read only, kept on the job as `standard_complaint`) and Status (cover) — the machine's cover now from the Product Database through coverCode(), else the call's item status; every filled value shall stay editable. FRS-232.3 A DEMO / new device shall be received with no call, as a DEMO unit, Engineer Name “Indoor Service”. FRS-232.4 The accessories received shall be an add-item list — item, quantity, serial, tag — the quantity stored on `indoor_job_accessories.qty`, default 1, refused at 0 or below by the database. FRS-232.5 Filing shall need indoor.receive and create the job (numbered by the database) and its accessory lines, then open it. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02; the open-call lookup is the one Pending Registrations uses, not a copy. FRS-232.9 (2026-10-04) A Field Return shall be received as a Troubleshooting job, the activity fixed and not chosen; a Troubleshooting job shall not be dispatched or closed before its quality check, as a Repair (0370). The Identification tag of the unit and of each accessory shall be chosen as Yes, Identified or Not Identified, a value typed before being kept; an accessory received shall record its item, quantity and tag, without a serial. FRS-232.10 The cleaning work instruction's revision shall be a number of two digits, 01 when none is given. FRS-232.11 (2026-10-04, 0372) A job with a call shall carry, at the top of its Repair page, a Call Status (the visit form's three) and a Call Pending Reason by the visit form's rules — required while Unsolved, Report Pending for a pending report, none for a completed one — and they shall be the visit's values, the visit filing with them; an Unsolved job with no reason shall not have its Indoor DC approved. The job's status shall be derived from them once cleaned: Solved → Ready (a Repair, Rework or Troubleshooting first needing its QC Pass, until then QC); Unsolved with spares not available → Awaiting spares; otherwise Under repair; never once Dispatched, Closed or Condemned. A DEMO / new device shall keep its Status chosen by hand. FRS-232.14 (0374) The intake shall offer three ways in — Field Return, Demo and New Device — each fixing the job's kind and activity: Customer property / Troubleshooting, DEMO unit / Demo, New device / Troubleshooting. A New device shall be its own kind, consigned like a DEMO unit to the party it is going to, and shall have its own sheet (New Devices) on the R/SER/07 register.

FRS-233.3 “Mark cleaning done” shall record the cleaning against WI/SER/01 and its revision. FRS-233.4 The Indoor Service Report shall be uploaded with its number: the file sent to Drive through the bridge every upload uses (uploadToDrive) and named “<Indoor Service Report No>_<original file name>”, characters a file name cannot carry replaced by “-”; the job shall store the link and file name; the database (`indoor_jobs_guard`, 0323) shall refuse it before the unit is cleaned, without a report number, and without indoor.work, and shall stamp report_uploaded_by / report_uploaded_at from the session, discarding values sent, an unrelated edit keeping them. FRS-233.5 The upload shall be offered on the drawer's Repair page — reached also from the register's Indoor Service Report No cell — only once cleaned and only while the unit is on no DC; it is a form on that page, not a second drawer. FRS-233.6 While a job carries an uploaded report file, its Indoor Service Report No shall not be blanked; a correction to another number shall be allowed (0352, D-115). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-02: show only relevant fields; the order cleaning → report → DC is enforced by the database, and no time is imposed between stages.

### URS-174 — Only the Indoor delivery challan is approved, and its approval files the visit

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

An Indoor delivery challan shall be created pending approval, naming who authorises it — the issuer's Reporting Manager, Regional Manager or an NSM — and only that person or an administrator shall approve or reject it, with the decision, who made it and when recorded by the system and printed on the challan. A unit shall not be dispatched while its challan is pending. Approving shall file, against each unit's call, the Visit Entry drafted with its Indoor Service Report — the call left Unsolved, pending Return to Field, with the work details and the uploaded report — through the same path and rules as a visit entered on the call, and shall not complete while any of those visits is unfiled. Rejecting shall need a reason, keep the challan and release its units for a new one. The spare-parts challan is not affected.

| **FRS-235** — The Indoor DC is approved by its Authorised By; rejection releases the units | High | OQ-223, OQ-226, OQ-227, OQ-234, OQ-244 |
| **FRS-237** — The Indoor visit's Visiting Service Engineer is picked from the User Master | Medium | OQ-228, OQ-229 |

### URS-175 — An Indoor Service job received in error can be deleted, before it has left a trace

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A job on the Indoor Service Register that was received in error — the wrong unit, a duplicate intake, a test entry — shall be deletable permanently, with its accessories, parts, checks and pre-delivery test, by a person given that right (an administrator by default, any other role only where Roles & Permissions grants it), who shall state why and confirm the job number. A job shall not be deletable once it has gone on an Indoor delivery challan, whatever became of the challan, or once its visit has been filed against its call. Each deletion shall be recorded by the system with the job number, product, serial, call, the reason, who and when; a deleted job's number shall not be issued again.

**FRS-238.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-238.1 `delete_indoor_job(job_id, reason)` (0324, SECURITY DEFINER) shall be the only way to delete an Indoor Service job: it shall require indoor.delete (granted to no role by migration; an administrator passes has_perm()) and a non-blank reason; refuse a job carrying a DC No., a job named on any indoor_dc_lines row (an approved, pending or rejected DC), and a job whose visit_uid is set, each in its own words; otherwise delete the job's accessories, harvested parts, checks and Pre-Delivery Testing and then the job, leave indoor_job_counters untouched so the number is not reissued, and write audit_log `indoor.job_delete` naming the job no., product, serial, UCN, kind, activity, status, the reason and the counts deleted, who and when stamped from the session. FRS-238.2 It shall not be callable by the public key; signed-in users may call it (it asks the key itself). FRS-238.3 DELETE on indoor_jobs and indoor_pdt shall be revoked from the API roles, so a direct DELETE is refused for every signed-in user, an administrator included. FRS-238.4 The job window shall offer “Delete job” only to a holder of indoor.delete; it shall say why a job a DC or a filed visit names is kept, and otherwise ask for the reason and for the job number typed to confirm before calling the function, and write its own audit row only for a REFUSED attempt, as indoor.job_delete_refused, since delete_indoor_job() already records the deletion (D-147). FRS-238.5 A job that has been verified or re-verified, PDT-signed, reported to the customer, condemned or disposed of, or whose report is uploaded is a quality record and shall not be deleted; a QC result, checks, parts, accessories and an unsigned PDT do not stop the deletion (0336, D-142). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03, chose permanent deletion over keep-and-hide: “Allow Admin by default, rest I will update from Roles & Permissions”.

Work performed on equipment before it is returned shall be subject to a recorded quality check held as its own record, attributable to the person who performed it. Equipment whose check has failed, and work of a kind that requires a check and has none, shall not leave.

FRS-144.3 A quality check of Fail shall return the job to Under repair; the signer and time shall be shown, and a check signed by the person who received the unit shall be flagged, not blocked. FRS-144.4 A rework shall record the nonconformity reference, the instruction and revision, authorised by, re-verified by and the result, the disposition, and whether an adverse effect was assessed with a note. FRS-144.5 A pre-delivery inspection shall record the source reference, checklist and revision, firmware, result (Pass, Pass with observation, Fail), a held reason and the accessories per packing list. The quality check (FRS-144 QC, 4.5.6) is unchanged. FRS-144.9 Dispatch shall record a reference, warn (not block) while accessories are outstanding, and show who dispatched and when. FRS-144.10 Condemnation shall be as FRS-060 states.

**FRS-059.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `qc_result` / `qc_by` / `qc_at` / `qc_notes` are columns of the job, not sentences in the work text. `indoor.qc` is a permission distinct from `indoor.work` and is enforced by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger, so a person holding every other authority in the module is refused the check by the database rather than by a hidden button. A trigger refuses any move to Ready, Dispatched or Closed while `qc_result` is Fail, refuses a Repair or Rework reaching Dispatched with no result at all, and refuses a failed pre-delivery inspection leaving. Whether the check must be signed by somebody OTHER than the person who received the unit is NOT enforced: the procedure does not require it, both identities are recorded, and the screen states plainly when they are the same.

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-099.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-099.1 The review drawer shall list the Field Failure Reports already raised on the call, as Already reported, above the Raise FFR action. FRS-099.2 Raise FFR (on the review) and ＋ Raise FFR (on the register) shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage, and the database (ffr_write) shall refuse an insert from anybody else. FRS-099.3 Raise FFR on the review shall open the Field Failure Register form filled from the review and the call. FRS-099.4 The form so filled shall warn where the call is not yet solved. FRS-099.5 ＋ Raise FFR on the register shall open a blank form. FRS-099.6 A report raised by hand shall be numbered, stamped and validated exactly as FRS-109 states for every report. FRS-099.7 A report raised by hand shall also start with CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status blank, the table defaults included.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

### URS-148 — A report is taken from the whole register, and says what it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each file shall carry with it what one row of it means, the filter applied, the number of rows and columns, and when it was taken. A date shall arrive in the file as a date and a number as a number. A file is opened days later by somebody who never saw the screen it came from; one whose filter is not written down is later taken for the whole register, and a date held as text sorts, filters and subtracts wrongly without refusing.

FRS-264.2 It shall list one row per spare line dispatched (`stores_dispatch_report`, 0385) in the AppSheet Stores format, its columns in that order: Spare Request NO|Part Number, SO NO, Timestamp, TO, ADDRESS, Stores Status, DETAILS, Spare Request NO, Part Number, Part Description, Dispatched Qty, Pending QTY, SO(n), Spare, OR Date, Request Final Approval Date, IND/IMP, Item Status, Dispatched in (Days), Dispatched in (Days - Group), Year, Month, YY - MM, Sl No; and offer Requested Qty, the part as dispatched and the dispatch line id as optional columns. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.5 Year, Month and YY - MM shall be of the dispatch in India time; Pending QTY the line's quantity still to send after every dispatch; ADDRESS the engineer's address, city, state and phone from the User Master; IND/IMP the part's from the Part Master. FRS-264.6 It shall filter by dispatch date, engineer, part, Spare Request NO, band, IND/IMP and Item Status, and export to a holder of `spare.dispatch` or `reports.view`. FRS-264.7 The Part Master shall carry IND/IMP (Indigenous / Imported / TBD) on its add and edit forms and its bulk upload. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |
