FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-202.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-202.1 Data Export shall open only for a holder of mod:/data-export and export.tables or export.schedules: the table list for either, the download for export.tables, the schedules for export.schedules (0306); anyone else shall be told which right is needed. FRS-202.2 Data Export shall list only the tables exportable_tables() returns — no audit table — with their approximate row counts labelled as estimates. FRS-202.3 Data Export shall provide a search over table names, a control selecting every table shown, a control clearing the selection, and the approximate total of rows selected. FRS-202.4 Data Export shall read each chosen table as the signed-in person, row-level security in force, in pages of 1,000 under a stated order (D-065). FRS-202.5 Data Export shall state, for a table that reached the limit of 200,000 rows, that its file is cut short, and name it in the result (D-065). FRS-202.6 Data Export shall write one CSV per table — dates as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, structured values verbatim — into one ZIP named rithi-export-<date>. FRS-202.7 Data Export shall refuse the ZIP to a role without export.data (D-065). FRS-202.8 Data Export shall write an audit entry for each ZIP naming the tables and the rows of each (D-065). FRS-202.9 Data Export shall download nothing where any table fails, and say so. FRS-202.10 Data Export shall allow an administrator to amend a schedule, its tables becoming the ones ticked. FRS-202.11 Data Export shall allow an administrator to pause and resume a schedule; a paused schedule sends nothing and shows "paused" in place of its next run. FRS-202.12 Data Export shall allow an administrator to delete a schedule after confirmation, the record of its past runs being retained (export_runs.schedule_id set null). FRS-202.13 Data Export shall list each schedule with its name, tables, recurrence, next run, and last run with its status and detail. FRS-202.14 Data Export shall state separately a failure to list the tables and a failure to read the schedules, naming data_export.sql, and shall state that nothing is mailed until the mail function is deployed. RATIONALE: .4 — a paged read with no order can return a row on two pages or on neither, and the file then looks complete; .5 — the pager stops at its cap without a word, which is the silent truncation this project has had thirteen times.

**FRS-249.** *(v0.10.70 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-249.1 Every CSV and Excel download, from whichever screen, shall ask where the export goes once the export permission and the partial-data warning have passed: Download the file to this device, or Save as Google Sheet. FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. FRS-249.4 The screen shall give a link to the sheet when it is saved, and when it is not shall say why and offer the file download instead. FRS-249.5 Each save shall be recorded in the audit log as export.google_sheet with the file name, the row count and the link, and a failed save recorded as failed. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

### URS-150 — A report says what one row is and how each derived figure is reached

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each report shall define what one of its rows stands for — a spare booked, a call, a feedback, a part sent and not accounted for — and shall state in the file how each figure it derives is reached, where the figure is not simply a value recorded elsewhere. A figure that means one thing on the screen and another in the workbook it is compared with is a KPI decision taken on the wrong number; and a date that is a fallback, or a blank that means "not asked", shall say so in the file rather than read as the thing it is standing in for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-194** — What each report holds | Medium | OQ-187 |
| **FRS-195** — The KPI export reproduces the workbook’s Field_INST tab from the register | Medium | OQ-188 |
| **FRS-264** — The Stores Dispatch Report | Medium | OQ-261 |

**FRS-194.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-194.1 The Consumption Report shall list one row per spare booked, with its call and that call’s latest visit, filterable by call date range, product, customer, city, engineer, part (code or name), UCN and call type. FRS-194.2 The Consumption Report file shall state that its two visit dates are the call’s LATEST visit; that where the call has no visit they fall back to the import file’s date and then to when the spare was booked, and are to be read as "no later than"; and that Visit UID is blank on exactly those rows. FRS-194.3 The Call Report shall list one row per CALL, never one per visit, carrying its latest visit by ENTRY and the spares booked on it, voided lines excluded. FRS-194.4 The Call Report shall filter by call date, product, customer, city, allotted engineer, UCN and call type on any part of the value, and by call status on the WHOLE value. FRS-194.5 The Customer Feedback Report shall list one row per feedback with each question as its own column, and shall offer a column carrying every answer as it was given. FRS-194.6 The Customer Feedback Report shall filter by the feedback’s own date, never the date it was loaded, and by product, customer, state, engineer, UCN, call type and source (Uploaded / Entered here). FRS-194.7 The Customer Feedback Report file shall state that a blank answer is a question not asked of that kind of visit rather than a question unanswered, and that the register holds one feedback per call. FRS-194.8 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall filter by dispatched date range, engineer (chosen from the engineers in the report itself, or typed where that list cannot be built), product and part code, and shall provide a control that clears the filter. FRS-194.9 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall display the first 25 matching rows before any file is taken. FRS-194.10 The Not Consumed Against this Call .xlsx shall carry an About sheet stating its scope, its filter, its rows and the time taken. RATIONALE: .4 matches the status whole because a status is a code — "Solved" as a part-match also takes "Solved - Report Pending", which is an open call. .6 because a migrated feedback loaded in 2026 was given in 2023, and a filter on the load date puts every one of them in the wrong year.

**FRS-195.** *(v0.10.127 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-195.1 The KPI export shall produce the Field_INST tab’s columns A to AG, in the workbook’s order and under its headings, followed by Pending Days. FRS-195.2 The KPI export shall include Field, Installation and PM calls (PM since 0390, the user 2026-10-06: "Add PM Calls also"), and shall exclude cancelled calls entirely. FRS-195.3 The KPI export shall compute Call Attended On as the earlier of the first visit and the first spare request, or whichever of the two exists. FRS-195.4 The KPI export shall compute Call Solved Date & Time as the visit date of the entry that moved the call to Solved - Report Completed, the latest such entry on a call re-opened and resolved. FRS-195.5 The KPI export shall mark a call Close only when it is Solved - Report Completed, and every other call Open, Solved - Report Pending included. FRS-195.6 The KPI export shall compute Attended in Days, Solved in Days, TTA, TTS and Failure Month by the workbook’s own formulas — days from the later of complaint and registration, never negative. FRS-195.7 The KPI export shall compute Pending Days as the days a call has been waiting. FRS-195.8 The KPI export shall filter by registered-from and registered-to date and offer the whole register. FRS-195.9 The KPI export shall display the number of matching calls on its download controls, and shall state where that count could not be taken that the export will still read them. FRS-195.10 The KPI export shall read in pages of 1,000 and offer .xlsx, with dates as dates, and .csv. FRS-195.11 The KPI export shall display the list of its columns. FRS-195.12 The KPI export shall be read as the reader, so an engineer’s export holds that engineer’s calls. FRS-195.13 The export, its sheet and its file shall be named Field_INST_PM (the user, 2026-10-06), since it holds PM calls as well. RATIONALE: .2 — the workbook counted cancellations as Close, so its 581 Close rows were 563 completed calls and 18 cancellations; .7 — the workbook’s own formula returns 0 for a call nobody has attended, so every unattended call read as attended and solved the day it was raised. Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

**FRS-264.** *(v0.10.123 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-264.1 Reports shall offer a Stores Dispatch Report, its own page key `mod:/exports/stores-dispatch` (inheriting from `mod:/exports`), granted by 0385 to Admin, Technical Support, Stores Incharge and Spare Coordinator. FRS-264.2 It shall list one row per spare line dispatched (`stores_dispatch_report`, 0385) in the AppSheet Stores format, its columns in that order: Spare Request NO|Part Number, SO NO, Timestamp, TO, ADDRESS, Stores Status, DETAILS, Spare Request NO, Part Number, Part Description, Dispatched Qty, Pending QTY, SO(n), Spare, OR Date, Request Final Approval Date, IND/IMP, Item Status, Dispatched in (Days), Dispatched in (Days - Group), Year, Month, YY - MM, Sl No; and offer Requested Qty, the part as dispatched and the dispatch line id as optional columns. FRS-264.3 Request Final Approval Date shall be the latest of the line's RM, Commercial and NSM decision times; Dispatched in (Days) shall be the exact time from it to the dispatch in days to one decimal; the band shall be 00-03D up to 3, 04-07D up to 7, 08-15D up to 15, 16-30D up to 30, 31-60D up to 60 and >60D beyond, a negative figure in 00-03D. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.5 Year, Month and YY - MM shall be of the dispatch in India time; Pending QTY the line's quantity still to send after every dispatch; ADDRESS the engineer's address, city, state and phone from the User Master; IND/IMP the part's from the Part Master. FRS-264.6 It shall filter by dispatch date, engineer, part, Spare Request NO, band, IND/IMP and Item Status, and export to a holder of `spare.dispatch` or `reports.view`. FRS-264.7 The Part Master shall carry IND/IMP (Indigenous / Imported / TBD) on its add and edit forms and its bulk upload. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

### URS-054 — Consumption recorded against a call is complete

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every part fitted during a visit shall be recorded against that call. Recording shall not depend on a further confirming action by the engineer once the part has been entered, and where no part was used that shall be a STATED answer rather than an unanswered field.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-137** — Saving a visit, its spares and its feedback | High | OQ-127 |
| **FRS-158** — What the consumption register shows of a reconciliation, and what one may do | High | OQ-150 |

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

**FRS-158.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-158.1 The reconciliation form shall fill the call number, the engineer and that engineer's hand stock from the UCN when the UCN is left, and shall say "No call found for X" where there is none. FRS-158.2 The reconciliation form shall let the office change the engineer from the call's, re-reading the named engineer's hand stock, and the database shall take the stock off, and cap the line at, the engineer named on the line. FRS-158.3 The reconciliation form shall take a GRIR / traceability value (batch, goods receipt or serial) per part and the database shall keep it on the line (`grir`). FRS-158.4 The database shall accept a Reconciliation line against a call that has no visit (0243), and `cons_write` shall refuse `source = Reconciliation` to anybody without `consumption.reconcile`. FRS-158.5 The register shall mark a Reconciliation line as such and a reported line as Report. FRS-158.6 The register shall show a voided line's quantity as "Voided" and an adjusted line's as its quantity with "was N", naming who adjusted it. FRS-158.7 The adjust dialog shall accept a quantity from 0 up to the current quantity plus what the engineer holds, shall require a reason, and shall refuse a line with no database id ("Refresh and try again"). FRS-158.8 The form shall reword a permission refusal as "Your role cannot add a reconciliation line (needs consumption.reconcile)" and shall repeat an error inside the open drawer. FRS-158.9 The register shall show dates dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-158.10 The register shall search every column of the loaded rows, and shall build its columns from the data, the first nine in a preferred order and every field selectable. RATIONALE: .2 is the office correcting whose van the part came out of, and is safe only because the cap in .2 is the database's. .4 is not a hole: the reconciliation exists for a part fitted and never reported, which under 0214 alone could not be booked on exactly the calls it was built for.

FRS-194.7 The Customer Feedback Report file shall state that a blank answer is a question not asked of that kind of visit rather than a question unanswered, and that the register holds one feedback per call. **FRS-062.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The visit report writes every consumption line the engineer has entered, including the line still in the entry control at the moment of saving; the same validation applies to it as to a line already added. “Add Consumption?” offers Yes or None Consumed: Yes requires at least one line before the report will save, and None Consumed withdraws the section. Lines are written in one statement, so a report cannot keep some of its spares and drop the rest.

**FRS-108.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-108.1 The Review Desk shall present the calls, the review and the call details in three panes whose dividers can be dragged and whose widths are remembered per device. FRS-108.2 The desk list shall be grouped by review stage and then call status, with expand all and collapse all, and shall mark first-year failures with their age. FRS-108.3 A row click, or its Review or View button, shall open that call’s review in a drawer. FRS-108.4 Without review.edit the register, the desk and the drawer shall be read-only, shall show no tick boxes and no save, and shall say which permission is missing; the database (call_reviews_write) shall refuse the write regardless. FRS-108.5 Export DCCR shall read every page of the filtered set and write a CSV in the register’s own columns and order, the Export tab listing those columns. FRS-108.6 Export DCCR shall be available only to holders of export.data (FRS-018). FRS-108.7 A review save, an automatic save, a bulk answer, an export and a change of the organisation auto-save default shall each be written to the audit trail. FRS-108.8 A review shall be written only on a call that exists and that the writer can see, except by a holder of bulk.upload loading history (0342, D-129).

**FRS-112.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-112.1 xlsxDownload shall refuse, exactly as csvExport does, when the user does not hold export.data. FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-138.2 Every download shall be preceded by the partial-load question (`mayExport`) where the rows are a partial load or a capped search. FRS-138.3 A workbook shall carry dates as serials with a date format and numbers as numbers, and an About sheet stating the report, its scope, its row count, whether more rows exist and when it was taken. FRS-138.4 The Visit Reports export shall carry every column the loaded visits carry, including every answer on the visit form. FRS-138.5 A download from Solved Without a Report or Feedback Without a Report shall be written to `audit_log` with rows, scope and format. RATIONALE: `csvExport` checks `canExportData()` and `xlsxDownload` and `xlsDownload` do not, so on Visit Reports, Solved Without a Report and Feedback Without a Report a role refused the CSV takes the same rows as Excel (D-018).

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-192.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-192.1 The Reports screen shall offer each report only to a role holding that report’s own key (mod:/exports/<report>); a role holding mod:/exports shall hold all of them. FRS-192.2 The Reports screen shall open the first report the role may open where the address names no report or a report the role may not open. FRS-192.3 The Reports screen shall state, where the role may open no report, that an administrator grants reports one by one under Roles & Permissions → Reports. FRS-192.4 The Reports screen shall mount only the report on show, so a report not on show reads nothing. FRS-192.5 Each report shall apply its filter in the database over the whole register, text fields matching on any part of the value. FRS-192.6 Each report shall display the exact number of rows matching the filter, counted in the database as the filter changes, and shall state when the count could not be taken. FRS-192.7 Each report shall describe the applied filter in words and shall provide a control that clears it. FRS-192.8 Each report shall include its mandatory columns in every file and display them ticked and locked. FRS-192.9 Each report shall offer its optional columns for selection, its default columns ticked to start with and removable. FRS-192.10 Each report shall provide controls that select every column, only the mandatory columns, and the default columns. FRS-192.11 Each report shall write its columns in the order of the report’s view, whatever the order they were ticked in, and an absent value as an empty cell. FRS-192.12 Each report shall read every matching row, in pages of 1,000, before writing a file, displaying the number read. FRS-192.13 Each .xlsx file shall carry a second sheet stating the report, what one row is, the filter applied, the number of rows, the number of columns (mandatory and chosen), the time of download and the report’s notes. FRS-192.14 Each .xlsx file shall carry a timestamp as an Excel date serial under a date format and a JSON number as a number; a text value of digits (a serial, a UCN, a contract number) shall remain text. FRS-192.15 Each .csv file shall carry a timestamp as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss in the reader’s time. FRS-192.16 Each report shall disable its download controls while the database is not connected, while a file is being built, when the role may not take the file, and when no row matches. FRS-192.17 Each report shall state "Nothing matches that filter" when the read returns no row, and the error when the file cannot be built. FRS-192.18 Each report shall state when the database is not connected, and shall state to a role that may open the report but not take the file which right it lacks. FRS-192.19 The report builder shall reset the filter and the column choice when a different report is opened. RATIONALE: .1 because the report tabs are separately grantable and the hub’s own check is what enforces it; .6 carries no "+" because the count is the database’s whole aggregate, not a page; .14 tests the TYPE of the value rather than whether a string looks numeric, since a serial of all digits would otherwise lose its leading zeros; .19 so a filter set on one register is never silently applied to another.

**FRS-193.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-193.1 The export gate shall refuse a .csv, an .xlsx, an .xls and a .zip file alike to a role without export.data. FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

FRS-195.3 The KPI export shall compute Call Attended On as the earlier of the first visit and the first spare request, or whichever of the two exists. FRS-195.4 The KPI export shall compute Call Solved Date & Time as the visit date of the entry that moved the call to Solved - Report Completed, the latest such entry on a call re-opened and resolved. FRS-195.5 The KPI export shall mark a call Close only when it is Solved - Report Completed, and every other call Open, Solved - Report Pending included. FRS-195.6 The KPI export shall compute Attended in Days, Solved in Days, TTA, TTS and Failure Month by the workbook’s own formulas — days from the later of complaint and registration, never negative. FRS-195.7 The KPI export shall compute Pending Days as the days a call has been waiting. FRS-195.8 The KPI export shall filter by registered-from and registered-to date and offer the whole register. FRS-195.9 The KPI export shall display the number of matching calls on its download controls, and shall state where that count could not be taken that the export will still read them. FRS-195.10 The KPI export shall read in pages of 1,000 and offer .xlsx, with dates as dates, and .csv. FRS-195.11 The KPI export shall display the list of its columns. FRS-195.12 The KPI export shall be read as the reader, so an engineer’s export holds that engineer’s calls. FRS-195.13 The export, its sheet and its file shall be named Field_INST_PM (the user, 2026-10-06), since it holds PM calls as well. RATIONALE: .2 — the workbook counted cancellations as Close, so its 581 Close rows were 563 completed calls and 18 cancellations; .7 — the workbook’s own formula returns 0 for a call nobody has attended, so every unattended call read as attended and solved the day it was raised. Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

### URS-081 — A potential effect raises a Field Failure Report, and its CAPA is left for the person who handles it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a completed Review 2 finds a potential effect (any of its three answers YES), the system shall raise a Field Failure Report for that call without anybody having to remember to, filled from the call, its visits and its spares, and dated the day Review 2 was completed. It shall raise one report per call however often the review is saved again, and shall not withdraw the report if the answer is later changed; such a report is closed with a remark by a person. The CAPA responsibility, CAPA number and CAPA status of a report raised this way shall be left BLANK, to be filled in later by the person handling the CAPA: a value written there by the system reads as a CAPA decision nobody made. A report may also be raised by hand, from the review or from the register, but only by a person authorised to raise and complete Field Failure Reports, and the review shall show the reports already raised on the call before offering another.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-098** — The Field Failure Report a review raises | High | OQ-86 |
| **FRS-099** — Raising a Field Failure Report by hand | High | OQ-87 |

**FRS-098.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-098.1 The database shall raise a Field Failure Report (trigger zz_ffr_from_review → raise_ffr()) when a review is written whose Any Potential Effect reads YES, that is when all three Review 2 answers are given and any one is YES. FRS-098.2 It shall raise at most one report per UCN; a further save, a correction or a second YES on a call that already has a report shall raise nothing. FRS-098.3 The FFR date shall be the Review 2 completion date. FRS-098.4 The report shall be filled from the call (customer, place, product, serial, cover, installation date, problem reported, call type, current call status), from its visits (date and job done, newest first) and from its spares consumed excluding voided lines, read from the base call tables so that the reviewer’s own visibility cannot prevent the report being raised. FRS-098.5 The report shall carry which of the three answers was YES, and the Review 2 reviewer, with the record. FRS-098.6 CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status shall be left blank, and FFR status shall be Open. FRS-098.7 A later change of the review to NO shall not delete, cancel or alter the report. FRS-098.8 While the report’s Service Dept Observation is blank, the Review 3 observation shall be copied onto it when Review 3 is answered; an observation already written on the report shall never be overwritten. FRS-098.9 A review loaded from a historical file (FRS-100) shall raise no report. RATIONALE: .6 is the user’s decision (2026-09-30) — today raise_ffr() writes “No closed in FFR”, “NA” and “Not required”, which read as a CAPA decision nobody took (D-029). .7 because a quality record is not deleted because somebody revised an opinion (0049). .8 because the report is where that text is finished.

**FRS-099.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-099.1 The review drawer shall list the Field Failure Reports already raised on the call, as Already reported, above the Raise FFR action. FRS-099.2 Raise FFR (on the review) and ＋ Raise FFR (on the register) shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage, and the database (ffr_write) shall refuse an insert from anybody else. FRS-099.3 Raise FFR on the review shall open the Field Failure Register form filled from the review and the call. FRS-099.4 The form so filled shall warn where the call is not yet solved. FRS-099.5 ＋ Raise FFR on the register shall open a blank form. FRS-099.6 A report raised by hand shall be numbered, stamped and validated exactly as FRS-109 states for every report. FRS-099.7 A report raised by hand shall also start with CAPA responsibility, CAPA No and CAPA status blank, the table defaults included.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

### URS-148 — A report is taken from the whole register, and says what it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall provide reports whose filter is applied to the whole of the register they report, not to the rows already on a screen, and shall state before a file is taken exactly how many rows it will hold. Each report shall have a fixed format that is always included, to which a reader may add columns. Each file shall carry with it what one row of it means, the filter applied, the number of rows and columns, and when it was taken. A date shall arrive in the file as a date and a number as a number. A file is opened days later by somebody who never saw the screen it came from; one whose filter is not written down is later taken for the whole register, and a date held as text sorts, filters and subtracts wrongly without refusing.

FRS-192.4 The Reports screen shall mount only the report on show, so a report not on show reads nothing. ### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |
| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |

FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-202.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-202.1 Data Export shall open only for a holder of mod:/data-export and export.tables or export.schedules: the table list for either, the download for export.tables, the schedules for export.schedules (0306); anyone else shall be told which right is needed. FRS-202.2 Data Export shall list only the tables exportable_tables() returns — no audit table — with their approximate row counts labelled as estimates. FRS-202.3 Data Export shall provide a search over table names, a control selecting every table shown, a control clearing the selection, and the approximate total of rows selected. FRS-202.4 Data Export shall read each chosen table as the signed-in person, row-level security in force, in pages of 1,000 under a stated order (D-065). FRS-202.5 Data Export shall state, for a table that reached the limit of 200,000 rows, that its file is cut short, and name it in the result (D-065). FRS-202.6 Data Export shall write one CSV per table — dates as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, structured values verbatim — into one ZIP named rithi-export-<date>. FRS-202.7 Data Export shall refuse the ZIP to a role without export.data (D-065). FRS-202.8 Data Export shall write an audit entry for each ZIP naming the tables and the rows of each (D-065). FRS-202.9 Data Export shall download nothing where any table fails, and say so. FRS-202.10 Data Export shall allow an administrator to amend a schedule, its tables becoming the ones ticked. FRS-202.11 Data Export shall allow an administrator to pause and resume a schedule; a paused schedule sends nothing and shows "paused" in place of its next run. FRS-202.12 Data Export shall allow an administrator to delete a schedule after confirmation, the record of its past runs being retained (export_runs.schedule_id set null). FRS-202.13 Data Export shall list each schedule with its name, tables, recurrence, next run, and last run with its status and detail. FRS-202.14 Data Export shall state separately a failure to list the tables and a failure to read the schedules, naming data_export.sql, and shall state that nothing is mailed until the mail function is deployed. RATIONALE: .4 — a paged read with no order can return a row on two pages or on neither, and the file then looks complete; .5 — the pager stops at its cap without a word, which is the silent truncation this project has had thirteen times.

**FRS-249.** *(v0.10.70 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-249.1 Every CSV and Excel download, from whichever screen, shall ask where the export goes once the export permission and the partial-data warning have passed: Download the file to this device, or Save as Google Sheet. FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. FRS-249.4 The screen shall give a link to the sheet when it is saved, and when it is not shall say why and offer the file download instead. FRS-249.5 Each save shall be recorded in the audit log as export.google_sheet with the file name, the row count and the link, and a failed save recorded as failed. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

### URS-150 — A report says what one row is and how each derived figure is reached

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each report shall define what one of its rows stands for — a spare booked, a call, a feedback, a part sent and not accounted for — and shall state in the file how each figure it derives is reached, where the figure is not simply a value recorded elsewhere. A figure that means one thing on the screen and another in the workbook it is compared with is a KPI decision taken on the wrong number; and a date that is a fallback, or a blank that means "not asked", shall say so in the file rather than read as the thing it is standing in for.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-194** — What each report holds | Medium | OQ-187 |
| **FRS-195** — The KPI export reproduces the workbook’s Field_INST tab from the register | Medium | OQ-188 |
| **FRS-264** — The Stores Dispatch Report | Medium | OQ-261 |

**FRS-194.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-194.1 The Consumption Report shall list one row per spare booked, with its call and that call’s latest visit, filterable by call date range, product, customer, city, engineer, part (code or name), UCN and call type. FRS-194.2 The Consumption Report file shall state that its two visit dates are the call’s LATEST visit; that where the call has no visit they fall back to the import file’s date and then to when the spare was booked, and are to be read as "no later than"; and that Visit UID is blank on exactly those rows. FRS-194.3 The Call Report shall list one row per CALL, never one per visit, carrying its latest visit by ENTRY and the spares booked on it, voided lines excluded. FRS-194.4 The Call Report shall filter by call date, product, customer, city, allotted engineer, UCN and call type on any part of the value, and by call status on the WHOLE value. FRS-194.5 The Customer Feedback Report shall list one row per feedback with each question as its own column, and shall offer a column carrying every answer as it was given. FRS-194.6 The Customer Feedback Report shall filter by the feedback’s own date, never the date it was loaded, and by product, customer, state, engineer, UCN, call type and source (Uploaded / Entered here). FRS-194.7 The Customer Feedback Report file shall state that a blank answer is a question not asked of that kind of visit rather than a question unanswered, and that the register holds one feedback per call. FRS-194.8 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall filter by dispatched date range, engineer (chosen from the engineers in the report itself, or typed where that list cannot be built), product and part code, and shall provide a control that clears the filter. FRS-194.9 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall display the first 25 matching rows before any file is taken. FRS-194.10 The Not Consumed Against this Call .xlsx shall carry an About sheet stating its scope, its filter, its rows and the time taken. RATIONALE: .4 matches the status whole because a status is a code — "Solved" as a part-match also takes "Solved - Report Pending", which is an open call. .6 because a migrated feedback loaded in 2026 was given in 2023, and a filter on the load date puts every one of them in the wrong year.

**FRS-195.** *(v0.10.127 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-195.1 The KPI export shall produce the Field_INST tab’s columns A to AG, in the workbook’s order and under its headings, followed by Pending Days. FRS-195.2 The KPI export shall include Field, Installation and PM calls (PM since 0390, the user 2026-10-06: "Add PM Calls also"), and shall exclude cancelled calls entirely. FRS-195.3 The KPI export shall compute Call Attended On as the earlier of the first visit and the first spare request, or whichever of the two exists. FRS-195.4 The KPI export shall compute Call Solved Date & Time as the visit date of the entry that moved the call to Solved - Report Completed, the latest such entry on a call re-opened and resolved. FRS-195.5 The KPI export shall mark a call Close only when it is Solved - Report Completed, and every other call Open, Solved - Report Pending included. FRS-195.6 The KPI export shall compute Attended in Days, Solved in Days, TTA, TTS and Failure Month by the workbook’s own formulas — days from the later of complaint and registration, never negative. FRS-195.7 The KPI export shall compute Pending Days as the days a call has been waiting. FRS-195.8 The KPI export shall filter by registered-from and registered-to date and offer the whole register. FRS-195.9 The KPI export shall display the number of matching calls on its download controls, and shall state where that count could not be taken that the export will still read them. FRS-195.10 The KPI export shall read in pages of 1,000 and offer .xlsx, with dates as dates, and .csv. FRS-195.11 The KPI export shall display the list of its columns. FRS-195.12 The KPI export shall be read as the reader, so an engineer’s export holds that engineer’s calls. FRS-195.13 The export, its sheet and its file shall be named Field_INST_PM (the user, 2026-10-06), since it holds PM calls as well. RATIONALE: .2 — the workbook counted cancellations as Close, so its 581 Close rows were 563 completed calls and 18 cancellations; .7 — the workbook’s own formula returns 0 for a call nobody has attended, so every unattended call read as attended and solved the day it was raised. Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

**FRS-264.** *(v0.10.123 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-264.1 Reports shall offer a Stores Dispatch Report, its own page key `mod:/exports/stores-dispatch` (inheriting from `mod:/exports`), granted by 0385 to Admin, Technical Support, Stores Incharge and Spare Coordinator. FRS-264.2 It shall list one row per spare line dispatched (`stores_dispatch_report`, 0385) in the AppSheet Stores format, its columns in that order: Spare Request NO|Part Number, SO NO, Timestamp, TO, ADDRESS, Stores Status, DETAILS, Spare Request NO, Part Number, Part Description, Dispatched Qty, Pending QTY, SO(n), Spare, OR Date, Request Final Approval Date, IND/IMP, Item Status, Dispatched in (Days), Dispatched in (Days - Group), Year, Month, YY - MM, Sl No; and offer Requested Qty, the part as dispatched and the dispatch line id as optional columns. FRS-264.3 Request Final Approval Date shall be the latest of the line's RM, Commercial and NSM decision times; Dispatched in (Days) shall be the exact time from it to the dispatch in days to one decimal; the band shall be 00-03D up to 3, 04-07D up to 7, 08-15D up to 15, 16-30D up to 30, 31-60D up to 60 and >60D beyond, a negative figure in 00-03D. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.5 Year, Month and YY - MM shall be of the dispatch in India time; Pending QTY the line's quantity still to send after every dispatch; ADDRESS the engineer's address, city, state and phone from the User Master; IND/IMP the part's from the Part Master. FRS-264.6 It shall filter by dispatch date, engineer, part, Spare Request NO, band, IND/IMP and Item Status, and export to a holder of `spare.dispatch` or `reports.view`. FRS-264.7 The Part Master shall carry IND/IMP (Indigenous / Imported / TBD) on its add and edit forms and its bulk upload. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

It shall never show a record the person could not open on the register itself.

FRS-218.3 Each register shall be shown as its own read returns; a register whose read fails shall be named as not searched rather than read as empty. FRS-218.4 Choosing a hit shall open that record: a call in its register’s read-only view (fetched by UCN when not loaded); a pending request in Pending Registrations; a spare request in its detail (fetched by UID when not loaded); a consumption line in a read-only detail; a party in its editor for a holder of masters.edit.records and in a read-only view otherwise; a machine in Machine History; a part in Part Search; a document by its Drive link; an article in Field Solutions (fetched by id when older than those listed); an FFR in its report. FRS-218.5 ↑ ↓ shall move through the hits and Enter shall open the highlighted one; the search term shall be stripped of the characters that delimit a PostgREST filter. FRS-218.6 Where a register holds more matches than the five shown, its group shall say so rather than read as complete (D-117).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-138.2 Every download shall be preceded by the partial-load question (`mayExport`) where the rows are a partial load or a capped search. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. **FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-195.** *(v0.10.127 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-195.1 The KPI export shall produce the Field_INST tab’s columns A to AG, in the workbook’s order and under its headings, followed by Pending Days. FRS-195.2 The KPI export shall include Field, Installation and PM calls (PM since 0390, the user 2026-10-06: "Add PM Calls also"), and shall exclude cancelled calls entirely. FRS-195.3 The KPI export shall compute Call Attended On as the earlier of the first visit and the first spare request, or whichever of the two exists. FRS-195.4 The KPI export shall compute Call Solved Date & Time as the visit date of the entry that moved the call to Solved - Report Completed, the latest such entry on a call re-opened and resolved. FRS-195.6 The KPI export shall compute Attended in Days, Solved in Days, TTA, TTS and Failure Month by the workbook’s own formulas — days from the later of complaint and registration, never negative. FRS-195.7 The KPI export shall compute Pending Days as the days a call has been waiting. FRS-195.8 The KPI export shall filter by registered-from and registered-to date and offer the whole register. FRS-195.9 The KPI export shall display the number of matching calls on its download controls, and shall state where that count could not be taken that the export will still read them. FRS-195.13 The export, its sheet and its file shall be named Field_INST_PM (the user, 2026-10-06), since it holds PM calls as well. RATIONALE: .2 — the workbook counted cancellations as Close, so its 581 Close rows were 563 completed calls and 18 cancellations; .7 — the workbook’s own formula returns 0 for a call nobody has attended, so every unattended call read as attended and solved the day it was raised. Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

**FRS-264.** *(v0.10.123 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-264.1 Reports shall offer a Stores Dispatch Report, its own page key `mod:/exports/stores-dispatch` (inheriting from `mod:/exports`), granted by 0385 to Admin, Technical Support, Stores Incharge and Spare Coordinator. FRS-264.2 It shall list one row per spare line dispatched (`stores_dispatch_report`, 0385) in the AppSheet Stores format, its columns in that order: Spare Request NO|Part Number, SO NO, Timestamp, TO, ADDRESS, Stores Status, DETAILS, Spare Request NO, Part Number, Part Description, Dispatched Qty, Pending QTY, SO(n), Spare, OR Date, Request Final Approval Date, IND/IMP, Item Status, Dispatched in (Days), Dispatched in (Days - Group), Year, Month, YY - MM, Sl No; and offer Requested Qty, the part as dispatched and the dispatch line id as optional columns. FRS-264.3 Request Final Approval Date shall be the latest of the line's RM, Commercial and NSM decision times; Dispatched in (Days) shall be the exact time from it to the dispatch in days to one decimal; the band shall be 00-03D up to 3, 04-07D up to 7, 08-15D up to 15, 16-30D up to 30, 31-60D up to 60 and >60D beyond, a negative figure in 00-03D. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

### URS-148 — A report is taken from the whole register, and says what it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall provide reports whose filter is applied to the whole of the register they report, not to the rows already on a screen, and shall state before a file is taken exactly how many rows it will hold. Each report shall have a fixed format that is always included, to which a reader may add columns. Each file shall carry with it what one row of it means, the filter applied, the number of rows and columns, and when it was taken. A date shall arrive in the file as a date and a number as a number. A file is opened days later by somebody who never saw the screen it came from; one whose filter is not written down is later taken for the whole register, and a date held as text sorts, filters and subtracts wrongly without refusing.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-192** — Reports: a tab per report, each filtered and counted in the database | Medium | OQ-185 |
| **FRS-264** — The Stores Dispatch Report | Medium | OQ-261 |

**FRS-192.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-192.1 The Reports screen shall offer each report only to a role holding that report’s own key (mod:/exports/<report>); a role holding mod:/exports shall hold all of them. FRS-192.2 The Reports screen shall open the first report the role may open where the address names no report or a report the role may not open. FRS-192.3 The Reports screen shall state, where the role may open no report, that an administrator grants reports one by one under Roles & Permissions → Reports. FRS-192.4 The Reports screen shall mount only the report on show, so a report not on show reads nothing. FRS-192.5 Each report shall apply its filter in the database over the whole register, text fields matching on any part of the value. FRS-192.6 Each report shall display the exact number of rows matching the filter, counted in the database as the filter changes, and shall state when the count could not be taken. FRS-192.7 Each report shall describe the applied filter in words and shall provide a control that clears it. FRS-192.8 Each report shall include its mandatory columns in every file and display them ticked and locked. FRS-192.9 Each report shall offer its optional columns for selection, its default columns ticked to start with and removable. FRS-192.10 Each report shall provide controls that select every column, only the mandatory columns, and the default columns. FRS-192.11 Each report shall write its columns in the order of the report’s view, whatever the order they were ticked in, and an absent value as an empty cell. FRS-192.12 Each report shall read every matching row, in pages of 1,000, before writing a file, displaying the number read. FRS-192.13 Each .xlsx file shall carry a second sheet stating the report, what one row is, the filter applied, the number of rows, the number of columns (mandatory and chosen), the time of download and the report’s notes. FRS-192.14 Each .xlsx file shall carry a timestamp as an Excel date serial under a date format and a JSON number as a number; a text value of digits (a serial, a UCN, a contract number) shall remain text. FRS-192.15 Each .csv file shall carry a timestamp as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss in the reader’s time. FRS-192.16 Each report shall disable its download controls while the database is not connected, while a file is being built, when the role may not take the file, and when no row matches. FRS-192.17 Each report shall state "Nothing matches that filter" when the read returns no row, and the error when the file cannot be built. FRS-192.18 Each report shall state when the database is not connected, and shall state to a role that may open the report but not take the file which right it lacks. FRS-192.19 The report builder shall reset the filter and the column choice when a different report is opened. RATIONALE: .1 because the report tabs are separately grantable and the hub’s own check is what enforces it; .6 carries no "+" because the count is the database’s whole aggregate, not a page; .14 tests the TYPE of the value rather than whether a string looks numeric, since a serial of all digits would otherwise lose its leading zeros; .19 so a filter set on one register is never silently applied to another.

### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-112** — Every file download is gated, scoped and recorded | High | OQ-100 |
| **FRS-138** — One gate for every download | High | OQ-129 |
| **FRS-193** — One export gate for every format, and a record of each file | High | OQ-186 |
| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |
| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |

**FRS-112.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-112.1 xlsxDownload shall refuse, exactly as csvExport does, when the user does not hold export.data. FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-138.2 Every download shall be preceded by the partial-load question (`mayExport`) where the rows are a partial load or a capped search. FRS-138.3 A workbook shall carry dates as serials with a date format and numbers as numbers, and an About sheet stating the report, its scope, its row count, whether more rows exist and when it was taken. FRS-138.4 The Visit Reports export shall carry every column the loaded visits carry, including every answer on the visit form. FRS-138.5 A download from Solved Without a Report or Feedback Without a Report shall be written to `audit_log` with rows, scope and format. RATIONALE: `csvExport` checks `canExportData()` and `xlsxDownload` and `xlsDownload` do not, so on Visit Reports, Solved Without a Report and Feedback Without a Report a role refused the CSV takes the same rows as Excel (D-018).

**FRS-193.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-193.1 The export gate shall refuse a .csv, an .xlsx, an .xls and a .zip file alike to a role without export.data. FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-202.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-202.1 Data Export shall open only for a holder of mod:/data-export and export.tables or export.schedules: the table list for either, the download for export.tables, the schedules for export.schedules (0306); anyone else shall be told which right is needed. FRS-202.2 Data Export shall list only the tables exportable_tables() returns — no audit table — with their approximate row counts labelled as estimates. FRS-202.3 Data Export shall provide a search over table names, a control selecting every table shown, a control clearing the selection, and the approximate total of rows selected. FRS-202.4 Data Export shall read each chosen table as the signed-in person, row-level security in force, in pages of 1,000 under a stated order (D-065). FRS-202.5 Data Export shall state, for a table that reached the limit of 200,000 rows, that its file is cut short, and name it in the result (D-065). FRS-202.6 Data Export shall write one CSV per table — dates as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, structured values verbatim — into one ZIP named rithi-export-<date>. FRS-202.7 Data Export shall refuse the ZIP to a role without export.data (D-065). FRS-202.8 Data Export shall write an audit entry for each ZIP naming the tables and the rows of each (D-065). FRS-202.9 Data Export shall download nothing where any table fails, and say so. FRS-202.10 Data Export shall allow an administrator to amend a schedule, its tables becoming the ones ticked. FRS-202.11 Data Export shall allow an administrator to pause and resume a schedule; a paused schedule sends nothing and shows "paused" in place of its next run. FRS-202.12 Data Export shall allow an administrator to delete a schedule after confirmation, the record of its past runs being retained (export_runs.schedule_id set null). FRS-202.13 Data Export shall list each schedule with its name, tables, recurrence, next run, and last run with its status and detail. FRS-202.14 Data Export shall state separately a failure to list the tables and a failure to read the schedules, naming data_export.sql, and shall state that nothing is mailed until the mail function is deployed. RATIONALE: .4 — a paged read with no order can return a row on two pages or on neither, and the file then looks complete; .5 — the pager stops at its cap without a word, which is the silent truncation this project has had thirteen times.

**FRS-249.** *(v0.10.70 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-249.1 Every CSV and Excel download, from whichever screen, shall ask where the export goes once the export permission and the partial-data warning have passed: Download the file to this device, or Save as Google Sheet. FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. FRS-249.4 The screen shall give a link to the sheet when it is saved, and when it is not shall say why and offer the file download instead. FRS-249.5 Each save shall be recorded in the audit log as export.google_sheet with the file name, the row count and the link, and a failed save recorded as failed. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

### URS-150 — A report says what one row is and how each derived figure is reached

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each report shall define what one of its rows stands for — a spare booked, a call, a feedback, a part sent and not accounted for — and shall state in the file how each figure it derives is reached, where the figure is not simply a value recorded elsewhere. A figure that means one thing on the screen and another in the workbook it is compared with is a KPI decision taken on the wrong number; and a date that is a fallback, or a blank that means "not asked", shall say so in the file rather than read as the thing it is standing in for.

| **FRS-264** — The Stores Dispatch Report | Medium | OQ-261 |

FRS-194.2 The Consumption Report file shall state that its two visit dates are the call’s LATEST visit; that where the call has no visit they fall back to the import file’s date and then to when the spare was booked, and are to be read as "no later than"; and that Visit UID is blank on exactly those rows. FRS-194.3 The Call Report shall list one row per CALL, never one per visit, carrying its latest visit by ENTRY and the spares booked on it, voided lines excluded. FRS-194.4 The Call Report shall filter by call date, product, customer, city, allotted engineer, UCN and call type on any part of the value, and by call status on the WHOLE value. FRS-194.5 The Customer Feedback Report shall list one row per feedback with each question as its own column, and shall offer a column carrying every answer as it was given. FRS-194.6 The Customer Feedback Report shall filter by the feedback’s own date, never the date it was loaded, and by product, customer, state, engineer, UCN, call type and source (Uploaded / Entered here). FRS-194.8 The Not Consumed Against this Call report shall filter by dispatched date range, engineer (chosen from the engineers in the report itself, or typed where that list cannot be built), product and part code, and shall provide a control that clears the filter.
