FRS-264.3 Request Final Approval Date shall be the latest of the line's RM, Commercial and NSM decision times; Dispatched in (Days) shall be the exact time from it to the dispatch in days to one decimal; the band shall be 00-03D up to 3, 04-07D up to 7, 08-15D up to 15, 16-30D up to 30, 31-60D up to 60 and >60D beyond, a negative figure in 00-03D. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.5 Year, Month and YY - MM shall be of the dispatch in India time; Pending QTY the line's quantity still to send after every dispatch; ADDRESS the engineer's address, city, state and phone from the User Master; IND/IMP the part's from the Part Master. FRS-264.6 It shall filter by dispatch date, engineer, part, Spare Request NO, band, IND/IMP and Item Status, and export to a holder of `spare.dispatch` or `reports.view`. FRS-264.7 The Part Master shall carry IND/IMP (Indigenous / Imported / TBD) on its add and edit forms and its bulk upload. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

### URS-071 — Two records of one visit shall not contradict each other

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where the system holds a customer’s feedback about a visit, it shall also hold a completed service report for that visit, and every instance where it does not shall be visible as a list naming which record is absent. Feedback is collected after a visit has taken place, so its existence is evidence that the work occurred; the completed report is the record of what was done. The two disagreeing means a device was serviced and the servicing was never written up — a gap that is invisible from either record read on its own, because neither record is wrong in itself.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-140** — Solved Without a Report, and the two lists' chips and wording | Medium | OQ-131, OQ-132 |
| **FRS-083** — Feedback Without a Report | Medium | OQ-72 |

**FRS-140.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-140.1 Solved Without a Report shall list, from a `security_invoker` view, every call reading Solved whose record has no visit, no visit date, no service report, or a visit entry date equal to its import stamp, naming every gap on the row and omitting unsolved calls and complete ones. FRS-140.2 Gap chips (and on Feedback Without a Report, finding chips) shall show exact counts, a record counting under each of its gaps, and a click shall narrow the list. FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. FRS-140.5 A load failure shall name the missing migration or grant, or show the error verbatim. FRS-140.6 Each list shall export to Excel, with an About sheet explaining each gap and the scope, or to CSV, through FRS-138. FRS-140.7 Refresh shall re-read the list. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-083.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `feedback_without_report` (0229) lists every customer feedback with no visit reading “Solved - Report Completed” behind it, and names WHICH of four things is absent, because each needs a different fix: the feedback records no UCN; no call carries that UCN; the call has no visit at all; or the call has visits and none of them is the completed one. The last is the commonest, and the row carries `latest_visit_status` beside it so that “Solved - Report Pending” — the system stating a known absence — is distinguishable from “Unsolved”, which is a different problem. THE STATUS IS MATCHED ON ITS LETTERS AND DIGITS, not as a string: `is_report_completed()` reduces to lower-case alphanumerics, so a trailing space, a lower-case spelling and an en-dash all read as completed, and `isCompletedVisit()` in src/lib/reportMapping.ts is the client copy of the same rule. That is not defensive coding — the export this was written for carried “Solved - Report Completed ” with a trailing space in all 378 rows, and a string comparison would have reported every one of those calls as missing its report. ANY visit reading completed is enough rather than the latest one: a call written up and then re-visited still has its report. A false entry here sends somebody to re-file a report that exists, which is wasted work and teaches them the list may mean nothing — the same argument as a `_status.sql` row that answers NO for nothing — so both rules are tested with the spellings that actually arrive. The view is `security_invoker`, so the ordinary call and feedback policies decide the rows; the SCREEN is restricted to administrators by `mod:/feedback-without-report`, at the user’s direction (2026-09-22).

### URS-013 — Reports & analytics

**FRS-108.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-108.1 The Review Desk shall present the calls, the review and the call details in three panes whose dividers can be dragged and whose widths are remembered per device. FRS-108.2 The desk list shall be grouped by review stage and then call status, with expand all and collapse all, and shall mark first-year failures with their age. FRS-108.3 A row click, or its Review or View button, shall open that call’s review in a drawer. FRS-108.4 Without review.edit the register, the desk and the drawer shall be read-only, shall show no tick boxes and no save, and shall say which permission is missing; the database (call_reviews_write) shall refuse the write regardless. FRS-108.5 Export DCCR shall read every page of the filtered set and write a CSV in the register’s own columns and order, the Export tab listing those columns. FRS-108.6 Export DCCR shall be available only to holders of export.data (FRS-018). FRS-108.7 A review save, an automatic save, a bulk answer, an export and a change of the organisation auto-save default shall each be written to the audit trail. FRS-108.8 A review shall be written only on a call that exists and that the writer can see, except by a holder of bulk.upload loading history (0342, D-129).

**FRS-112.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-112.1 xlsxDownload shall refuse, exactly as csvExport does, when the user does not hold export.data. FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-138.2 Every download shall be preceded by the partial-load question (`mayExport`) where the rows are a partial load or a capped search. FRS-138.3 A workbook shall carry dates as serials with a date format and numbers as numbers, and an About sheet stating the report, its scope, its row count, whether more rows exist and when it was taken. FRS-138.4 The Visit Reports export shall carry every column the loaded visits carry, including every answer on the visit form. FRS-138.5 A download from Solved Without a Report or Feedback Without a Report shall be written to `audit_log` with rows, scope and format. RATIONALE: `csvExport` checks `canExportData()` and `xlsxDownload` and `xlsDownload` do not, so on Visit Reports, Solved Without a Report and Feedback Without a Report a role refused the CSV takes the same rows as Excel (D-018).

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-192.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-192.1 The Reports screen shall offer each report only to a role holding that report’s own key (mod:/exports/<report>); a role holding mod:/exports shall hold all of them. FRS-192.2 The Reports screen shall open the first report the role may open where the address names no report or a report the role may not open. FRS-192.3 The Reports screen shall state, where the role may open no report, that an administrator grants reports one by one under Roles & Permissions → Reports. FRS-192.4 The Reports screen shall mount only the report on show, so a report not on show reads nothing. FRS-192.5 Each report shall apply its filter in the database over the whole register, text fields matching on any part of the value. FRS-192.6 Each report shall display the exact number of rows matching the filter, counted in the database as the filter changes, and shall state when the count could not be taken. FRS-192.7 Each report shall describe the applied filter in words and shall provide a control that clears it. FRS-192.8 Each report shall include its mandatory columns in every file and display them ticked and locked. FRS-192.9 Each report shall offer its optional columns for selection, its default columns ticked to start with and removable. FRS-192.10 Each report shall provide controls that select every column, only the mandatory columns, and the default columns. FRS-192.11 Each report shall write its columns in the order of the report’s view, whatever the order they were ticked in, and an absent value as an empty cell. FRS-192.12 Each report shall read every matching row, in pages of 1,000, before writing a file, displaying the number read. FRS-192.13 Each .xlsx file shall carry a second sheet stating the report, what one row is, the filter applied, the number of rows, the number of columns (mandatory and chosen), the time of download and the report’s notes. FRS-192.14 Each .xlsx file shall carry a timestamp as an Excel date serial under a date format and a JSON number as a number; a text value of digits (a serial, a UCN, a contract number) shall remain text. FRS-192.15 Each .csv file shall carry a timestamp as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss in the reader’s time. FRS-192.16 Each report shall disable its download controls while the database is not connected, while a file is being built, when the role may not take the file, and when no row matches. FRS-192.17 Each report shall state "Nothing matches that filter" when the read returns no row, and the error when the file cannot be built. FRS-192.18 Each report shall state when the database is not connected, and shall state to a role that may open the report but not take the file which right it lacks. FRS-192.19 The report builder shall reset the filter and the column choice when a different report is opened. RATIONALE: .1 because the report tabs are separately grantable and the hub’s own check is what enforces it; .6 carries no "+" because the count is the database’s whole aggregate, not a page; .14 tests the TYPE of the value rather than whether a string looks numeric, since a serial of all digits would otherwise lose its leading zeros; .19 so a filter set on one register is never silently applied to another.

**FRS-193.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-193.1 The export gate shall refuse a .csv, an .xlsx, an .xls and a .zip file alike to a role without export.data. FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-195.** *(v0.10.127 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-195.1 The KPI export shall produce the Field_INST tab’s columns A to AG, in the workbook’s order and under its headings, followed by Pending Days. FRS-195.2 The KPI export shall include Field, Installation and PM calls (PM since 0390, the user 2026-10-06: "Add PM Calls also"), and shall exclude cancelled calls entirely. FRS-195.3 The KPI export shall compute Call Attended On as the earlier of the first visit and the first spare request, or whichever of the two exists. FRS-195.4 The KPI export shall compute Call Solved Date & Time as the visit date of the entry that moved the call to Solved - Report Completed, the latest such entry on a call re-opened and resolved. FRS-195.5 The KPI export shall mark a call Close only when it is Solved - Report Completed, and every other call Open, Solved - Report Pending included. FRS-195.6 The KPI export shall compute Attended in Days, Solved in Days, TTA, TTS and Failure Month by the workbook’s own formulas — days from the later of complaint and registration, never negative. FRS-195.7 The KPI export shall compute Pending Days as the days a call has been waiting. FRS-195.8 The KPI export shall filter by registered-from and registered-to date and offer the whole register. FRS-195.9 The KPI export shall display the number of matching calls on its download controls, and shall state where that count could not be taken that the export will still read them. FRS-195.10 The KPI export shall read in pages of 1,000 and offer .xlsx, with dates as dates, and .csv. FRS-195.11 The KPI export shall display the list of its columns. FRS-195.12 The KPI export shall be read as the reader, so an engineer’s export holds that engineer’s calls. FRS-195.13 The export, its sheet and its file shall be named Field_INST_PM (the user, 2026-10-06), since it holds PM calls as well. RATIONALE: .2 — the workbook counted cancellations as Close, so its 581 Close rows were 563 completed calls and 18 cancellations; .7 — the workbook’s own formula returns 0 for a call nobody has attended, so every unattended call read as attended and solved the day it was raised. Proved by supabase/tests/kpi_field_inst_test.sql.

**FRS-249.** *(v0.10.70 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-249.1 Every CSV and Excel download, from whichever screen, shall ask where the export goes once the export permission and the partial-data warning have passed: Download the file to this device, or Save as Google Sheet. FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. FRS-249.4 The screen shall give a link to the sheet when it is saved, and when it is not shall say why and offer the file download instead. FRS-249.5 Each save shall be recorded in the audit log as export.google_sheet with the file name, the row count and the link, and a failed save recorded as failed. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

**FRS-264.** *(v0.10.123 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-264.1 Reports shall offer a Stores Dispatch Report, its own page key `mod:/exports/stores-dispatch` (inheriting from `mod:/exports`), granted by 0385 to Admin, Technical Support, Stores Incharge and Spare Coordinator. FRS-264.3 Request Final Approval Date shall be the latest of the line's RM, Commercial and NSM decision times; Dispatched in (Days) shall be the exact time from it to the dispatch in days to one decimal; the band shall be 00-03D up to 3, 04-07D up to 7, 08-15D up to 15, 16-30D up to 30, 31-60D up to 60 and >60D beyond, a negative figure in 00-03D. FRS-264.4 A line with no approval time recorded shall show a blank approval date, blank days and the band No approval date. FRS-264.5 Year, Month and YY - MM shall be of the dispatch in India time; Pending QTY the line's quantity still to send after every dispatch; ADDRESS the engineer's address, city, state and phone from the User Master; IND/IMP the part's from the Part Master. FRS-264.6 It shall filter by dispatch date, engineer, part, Spare Request NO, band, IND/IMP and Item Status, and export to a holder of `spare.dispatch` or `reports.view`. FRS-264.7 The Part Master shall carry IND/IMP (Indigenous / Imported / TBD) on its add and edit forms and its bulk upload. FRS-264.8 It shall also list the stock outs dated from 1 January 2025 (India time) onwards from the historical stock-out record (`spare_issue_history`, 0387, 0388), dated by the stock out's own date or, failing that, the day-first Timestamp the file carried; their OR and approval dates read day-first from the file, their days and band worked out by .3 and .4, Requested Qty blank; a stock out that is also a dispatch made in RITHI shown once, as RITHI's; an optional Source column saying RITHI or Historical; and a stock out with no readable date not shown. RATIONALE: .3 is exact elapsed time at the user's choice (2026-10-05), not date-minus-date; .4 because AppSheet subtracted an empty date and filed such lines under >5 yrs, a missing value presented as a measurement; .8 at the user's request (2026-10-06, "I need for the Whole year. Fetch it from the Historical Data" -- calendar 2025; 2026 added the same day, "add the 2026 historical stock outs too"), the days re-worked rather than copied so one column holds one rule.

**FRS-018.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Visit history is retrievable with field filters; CSV export is blocked unless the user holds export.data.

### URS-111 — A visit is recorded as it happened

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The record of a visit shall be dated no later than today and no earlier than the complaint, because the latest visit decides whether the call is closed. It shall state why an unsolved call is pending, carry the signed service report where the call is completed, record the customer's feedback on a solved call, and record the parts fitted with the traceability of each. Where only part of a visit could be saved the person shall be told exactly which part, and shall be able to complete it without entering the visit twice.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-136** — The visit form | High | OQ-237, OQ-126, OQ-127 |
| **FRS-137** — Saving a visit, its spares and its feedback | High | OQ-127 |

**FRS-136.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-136.1 The visit date shall be no later than today (IST) and no earlier than the call's complaint date, checked on save by `visitDateProblem()` and refused by the database for every visit entered on the form (`uid WEB-…`, 0115); imported history is exempt. FRS-136.2 The Visit Entry Date shall be stamped by the application at the moment of entry and shall not be editable. FRS-136.3 The Visiting Service Engineer shall be required; a manager or administrator may choose an engineer of their team, whose hand stock is then used, while the visit records the signed-in person as its author (`engineer_email`). FRS-136.4 Call Status shall be one of three values. FRS-136.5 Call Pending Reason shall be required from the pending-reason master when the status is Unsolved, and fixed to Report Pending when the report is pending. FRS-136.6 Update Visit Work Details? shall be answered, and shall be Yes when the status is Solved - Report Completed; No shall omit the service report fields. FRS-136.7 The service report shall require software version and filter changed, take the complaint from the master, and offer the accessory serial from the party's CPX/ASU units. FRS-136.8 On an installation, Warranty Start Date? shall be required and answered by choosing one of the customer feedback's two answers — Installation Call Solved Date or Invoice Date — with no default, and be stored on the feedback (FRS-082, FRS-245). FRS-136.9 The manual report shall be a PDF or photo up to 10 MB uploaded to the call type's Drive folder, never a pasted link, and shall be required when the status is Solved - Report Completed; it may be shown, opened, replaced or removed before save. FRS-136.10 On a solved call the feedback questions shall be those for the call type, rating and yes/no answers required, and the customer sign-off name, number and designation optional. FRS-136.11 The form shall show the previous visits (status, engineer, date) and open the last manual report. FRS-136.12 A missing hand-stock view shall be reported as needing its migration.

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

**FRS-224.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-224.1 The database shall, once, write into each warranty machine line whose INST Call holds no call number the UCN of an installation call found by, in turn: the call number WI-<Product>-<Serial>; the product, serial and the sale's party; the product and serial alone, each compared trimmed and case-insensitive, and only where that rule finds exactly one installation call. FRS-224.5 The list and its data shall require mod:/install-calls-unmapped, granted to the administrator role and to Technical Support (which carries every page the administrator holds) and assignable on Roles & Permissions; the public key shall not reach it. If it does not have an installation call give it as a separate list in reports - view only for Admins", and "Map only installation call". Exactly one or nothing, as 0234: a guessed mapping is a false record of which call installed a machine. Proved by supabase/tests/install_call_mapping_once_test.sql (0319).

### URS-071 — Two records of one visit shall not contradict each other

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where the system holds a customer’s feedback about a visit, it shall also hold a completed service report for that visit, and every instance where it does not shall be visible as a list naming which record is absent. Feedback is collected after a visit has taken place, so its existence is evidence that the work occurred; the completed report is the record of what was done. The two disagreeing means a device was serviced and the servicing was never written up — a gap that is invisible from either record read on its own, because neither record is wrong in itself.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-140** — Solved Without a Report, and the two lists' chips and wording | Medium | OQ-131, OQ-132 |
| **FRS-083** — Feedback Without a Report | Medium | OQ-72 |

**FRS-140.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-140.1 Solved Without a Report shall list, from a `security_invoker` view, every call reading Solved whose record has no visit, no visit date, no service report, or a visit entry date equal to its import stamp, naming every gap on the row and omitting unsolved calls and complete ones. FRS-140.2 Gap chips (and on Feedback Without a Report, finding chips) shall show exact counts, a record counting under each of its gaps, and a click shall narrow the list. FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. FRS-140.5 A load failure shall name the missing migration or grant, or show the error verbatim. FRS-140.6 Each list shall export to Excel, with an About sheet explaining each gap and the scope, or to CSV, through FRS-138. FRS-140.7 Refresh shall re-read the list. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-083.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `feedback_without_report` (0229) lists every customer feedback with no visit reading “Solved - Report Completed” behind it, and names WHICH of four things is absent, because each needs a different fix: the feedback records no UCN; no call carries that UCN; the call has no visit at all; or the call has visits and none of them is the completed one. The last is the commonest, and the row carries `latest_visit_status` beside it so that “Solved - Report Pending” — the system stating a known absence — is distinguishable from “Unsolved”, which is a different problem. THE STATUS IS MATCHED ON ITS LETTERS AND DIGITS, not as a string: `is_report_completed()` reduces to lower-case alphanumerics, so a trailing space, a lower-case spelling and an en-dash all read as completed, and `isCompletedVisit()` in src/lib/reportMapping.ts is the client copy of the same rule. That is not defensive coding — the export this was written for carried “Solved - Report Completed ” with a trailing space in all 378 rows, and a string comparison would have reported every one of those calls as missing its report. ANY visit reading completed is enough rather than the latest one: a call written up and then re-visited still has its report. A false entry here sends somebody to re-file a report that exists, which is wasted work and teaches them the list may mean nothing — the same argument as a `_status.sql` row that answers NO for nothing — so both rules are tested with the spellings that actually arrive. The view is `security_invoker`, so the ordinary call and feedback policies decide the rows; the SCREEN is restricted to administrators by `mod:/feedback-without-report`, at the user’s direction (2026-09-22).

### URS-119 — A spare moves to the next approver only on an answer that means yes

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each spare line shall pass an approval stage only when that stage's recorded answer means yes — Approved, Auto-Approved, or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing — and any other answer, however it is worded, shall hold the line with that approver. Which of the Commercial and NSM stages a line needs shall be settled once, when the Reporting Manager approves it: a line under AMC or OGP needs both, a HandStock request needs NSM, and any other line needs neither. A stage that is not needed shall be recorded as Auto-Approved and shall name no approver. A line that has been rejected, dropped, dispatched or received shall read as such wherever its stage is shown. Before the rule was whole-word, "Not Approved" read as approved and parts reached Stores that nobody had cleared.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-147** — The stage of a spare line is read from its answers, whole-word | High | OQ-217, OQ-139 |

**FRS-147.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-147.1 The system shall compute the stage of a spare line in this order: Rejected where any of the RM, Commercial or NSM answers is a rejection; Received where the line has a receipt time; Dropped where Stores dropped it; Dispatched where Stores dispatched it in full; otherwise the first of RM Approval, Commercial and NSM whose answer does not mean yes; otherwise Stores. FRS-147.2 An answer shall mean yes only when, ignoring case and surrounding space, it is exactly Approved, Auto-Approved (with or without the hyphen) or the whole phrase Cleared for Stores Processing. FRS-147.3 Any other answer — "Not Approved", "Approval Pending", "Not cleared for stores processing", a word from an imported sheet — shall hold the line at that stage. FRS-147.4 The database (`spare_line_stage`, 0256 and 0270) shall compute the stored stage by the same rule as the screen (`APPROVED_RE` in src/lib/spareflow.ts), and `check:ui` shall hold the two patterns together. FRS-147.5 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the Commercial answer unless the line is AMC or OGP (`spare_needs_commercial`). FRS-147.6 RM approval of a line shall write Auto-Approved into the NSM answer unless the line is AMC or OGP or belongs to a HandStock request (`spare_needs_nsm`, 0210). FRS-147.7 An Auto-Approved answer shall be written with no approver name and no approval time. FRS-147.8 The RM approval dialog shall state, before the approval is written, which later stages the line will skip and which it will stop at. FRS-147.9 The Spare Upload shall keep an unrecognised approval word exactly as written (`approvalWord`), so that it holds the line rather than being guessed into Approved or Rejected. RATIONALE: .2 is whole-word because finding 20 was a substring test that read every way of saying no as yes. .7 because inventing an approver on a quality record is worse than an outcome with no name against it. The rule is settled at RM approval and then READ from the record, which is why `spare_line_stage` keeps its six arguments.

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A balance below zero shall be shown and explained as a finding rather than hidden. The whole register shall be searchable, not only the part already read. ### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. ### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

### URS-077 — A stock report is complete, or it is not a report

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall provide a Hand Stock Report of the stock held by each engineer, showing the movements the balance is composed of and not the balance alone. The system shall load every line of that report before permitting it to be exported. A stock figure is RECONCILED AGAINST, so a file cut short is not a shorter answer but a wrong one — parts read as absent and balances as short, with nothing in the file saying that rows were still arriving when it was written. The balance shall be derived from the recorded movements rather than stored, so the report and the register it is taken from cannot disagree.

FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. **FRS-091.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The Hand Stock Report reads `handstock_balance` — the same derived view the Hand Stock register reads, so the two cannot disagree — through `handstock_balance_all()` (0384), ONE request returning the whole balance as one array, because the view costs the same for a page as for everything and paging it was one full aggregate per page. The row count carries a “+” until that one result is in. Every download control is disabled while rows are still arriving, and the writer refuses as well as the button. The file is named HandStock_dd-MMM-yyyy_HHmmss with the extension of the format chosen — the month NAMED, as every date in this system is, and the clock stripped of the colons a file name may not carry. The .csv carries dates as text, being all a CSV can carry; the .xlsx carries a number as a number and a date as a serial plus a format; the .xls is SpreadsheetML 2003, chosen over an HTML table so that it too keeps the types. Every workbook carries a second sheet stating its scope, its row count and the time it was taken, a file whose filter is not written down being one somebody later mistakes for the whole register. The export is recorded in the audit trail.

### URS-179 — A product failure is a field call within months of installation, measured over a rolling period

*v0.10.87 · 04-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The number of months and the rolling period shall be maintainable by an administrator, or by a role the administrator grants, on an SLA / Objective Configuration page under Admin, without a code change, defaulting to 3 and 12; every change shall be recorded with the old and new value, who and when; and a change shall alter no figure already written until the objectives are re-calculated. By default only the Admin role shall be given that page. The user, 2026-10-04: "For Product Failures, The Concept is - Failure Within 3 Months, But a Rolling Average for 12 Months".

### URS-136 — A customer is known by one name, and the person who looks after them is a real person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master shall let an authorised user add a customer, giving at least its name, city and state, and shall refuse a name it already holds. It shall let an authorised user maintain a customer's type, profile, Serviceman, route, installation and billing addresses and contacts, and KYC details. It shall NOT allow the customer's name to be changed by editing, on the screen or through the data interface, because every machine, call and contract names the customer by that text and has no other link to it; a change of name shall be made only by a function that carries every record naming it. The Serviceman shall be a person on the User Master, because a new call is allotted to that name. Correcting a Serviceman's spelling across every customer carrying it shall be one act that changes all or none, shall say beforehand how many customers it will change, and shall offer only User Master names or nobody. Marking a customer's KYC Verified shall be attributed by the system to the person who did it, shall not be re-attributable by anybody else, and shall be cleared when the customer is no longer verified.

**FRS-174.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-174.1 The KYC status shall be one of Pending, Verified or Rejected, anything else refused by a CHECK constraint (0201), and a new party with none shall read Pending. **FRS-175.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-175.1 ✎ Change engineer shall list every Serviceman spelling on the Party Master with the number of customers carrying it, counted over the whole register rather than the page loaded. ### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-142 — A cover entry is raised, filled and priced by one rule wherever it is entered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The cover registers shall state for every entry whether it is Active, About to expire or Inactive, by one rule shared with the database, an entry with no readable end date being Not covered and never Active. A new entry shall be offered the next number in its series, which may be changed and shall be refused if already used. The customer shall be chosen from the Party Master, a customer the master does not hold being allowed; choosing a customer on a sale shall fill the address, contact and tax fields from the master, blanks included. A contract line's tax and total shall be derived from its rate by the one GST rule. A renewal shall be re-priced: no price shall be carried from the predecessor, a price entered shall be checked before anything is written, and a revision of the old price by a percentage shall be offered. The installation call for one machine may be raised from that machine, and its call number written back onto that machine only. Starting a call from a cover register shall be offered only to those who may register one.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-184** — Entry state, numbering, the customer and the price on a cover entry | Medium | OQ-177 |
| **FRS-185** — A renewal is priced by what is entered, never by what was paid | Medium | OQ-178 |
| **FRS-186** — The installation call for one machine, raised from the machine | Medium | OQ-179 |
| **FRS-231** — A warranty machine still waiting for its installation call is marked and can be filtered | Low | OQ-225 |
| **FRS-244** — The sale, the contract and the transfer fill the Product Database by product + serial | High | OQ-236 |

**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-184.4 A Sale Entry shall default its warranty start to today and stamp its entry date when created. FRS-184.5 The party picker shall search the Party Master in the database and shall accept a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.6 Choosing a different party on a sale shall fill its eleven address, contact and tax fields from the Party Master, blanks included, and shall fill nothing for a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). Proved by `supabase/tests/cover_expiry_test.sql` (.1) and `npm run check:cover-party` (.6).

**FRS-185.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-185.1 The Renew panel shall show each carried machine's old rate beside an empty rate box. FRS-185.2 It shall offer to revise every ticked machine's old rate by a stated percentage, and to clear every entered rate. FRS-185.3 It shall preview the total with GST. FRS-185.4 A blank rate shall mean “price it later” and be saved as no rate, tax or total. FRS-185.5 Every entered rate shall be checked before anything is written, and a rate that is not a number, or is negative, shall refuse the whole renewal. FRS-185.6 A machine's tax and total shall be derived from its entered rate by the rule of FRS-184.7. FRS-185.7 No rate shall be copied from the predecessor's machines. FRS-185.8 The success message shall say which machines were priced and which were left blank. FRS-185.9 The Renew panel's dates shall read dd-MMM-yyyy and store a date (FRS-089). RATIONALE: .5 before anything because a contract that exists carrying some of its prices is much harder to walk back than one refused. .7 because a price carried forward silently is a price nobody agreed that looks exactly like one they did. .8 and .9 are open (D-064).

**FRS-186.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-186.1 The Register tab (formerly By machine) of the Warranty Register shall offer + Installation call on a saved machine with a model and a serial and no call number, to holders of install.create or cover.edit. FRS-186.2 The confirmation shall list the fixed answers the call will carry (FRS-085.2 to .8) and name the INST Call placeholder it will replace. FRS-186.3 The call number shall be written back through `link_install_call()` (0258), which shall refuse a caller without install.create, cover.edit or administrator. FRS-186.4 It shall refuse to replace a call number already recorded on the machine; a placeholder shall be replaced. FRS-186.5 It shall refuse a call that is not an installation call for that machine's product and serial. FRS-186.6 Calling it with that call number already in place shall change nothing. FRS-186.7 It shall write no other field of the warranty line. FRS-186.8 The row and this device's copy shall show the call number without a reload. RATIONALE: a function rather than a second UPDATE policy, because row-level security cannot grant one column and a policy letting an install.create holder write the link would let them rewrite the whole warranty line. Proved by `supabase/tests/link_install_call_test.sql`.

**FRS-231.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-231.1 The Register tab of the Warranty Register shall mark each machine line Pending when it carries a product and a serial and its INST Call holds no call number, show the call number where one is mapped, and carry the same value to Excel and CSV. FRS-231.2 It shall offer a filter for those machines with their count, applied by the database across the whole register, combining with the search and the cover-state filters. FRS-231.3 The Entries tab shall show, per sale, how many of its machines are pending, counted by the database, and shall offer the same filter there, narrowing to the sales with at least one, with their count; a sale whose count has not been read shall show a dash, not 0. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-02: "In Warranty, Add a Identifier [Should be Filterable as well] for Pending Installation Call Generation". The rule is the one the + Installation call button already uses (machinesNeedingInstallCall), so the mark and the button cannot disagree; a "To Check" placeholder is Pending.

**FRS-244.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-244.1 Every write to a sale line or entry, a contract line or entry, an ownership transfer or an additional entry shall re-sync the Product Database row of that machine — product and serial together, never the serial alone — through sync_product_machine() (0330). FRS-244.2 From the machine's latest sale line (by warranty end; the line's value, else its entry's): Warranty No., start, end, PM visits, Invoice No., Invoice Date, Warranty Years, Warranty Months and Accessories Included. FRS-244.3 From its latest contract line (by contract end; line, else entry): Contract No., start, end, type and status, and its PM visits, which overwrite the sale's (the user's choice) and survive the sale being saved again. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). FRS-244.6 A contract or warranty number a machine carries that a register line holds for ANOTHER model sharing its serial shall be cleared with its dates and type; one no register holds is left. FRS-244.7 Status: a current contract is its type, a current warranty WGP, a machine the registers know with neither OGP. FRS-244.8 A one-time re-sync shall apply this to every machine, the old values of each changed row kept in products_resync_backup. RATIONALE: .1 because a serial is shared by different models — the ORION-G 2410 / CPX CARE MC5521 case — and a contract on one is not cover on the other. ### URS-144 — A change of owner, and cover recovered by hand, name the machine they concern

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

An ownership transfer and an additional entry shall identify the machine by its model together with its serial, and the form shall ask for both. Recording a transfer shall move the recorded owner of that machine only, never of another model that shares the serial; the previous owner shall be completed only where the machine is identified without doubt, and left empty otherwise. The person recording a transfer shall be taken from the signed-in session. The customer a machine goes to shall be chosen from the Party Master. FRS-188.3 A blank previous party shall be completed from the machine's current owner only where exactly one machine carries that model and serial, left empty otherwise, and left empty where it would equal the destination (0182, 0183). ### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

It shall never show a record the person could not open on the register itself.
