**FRS-218.** *(v0.10.104 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-218.1 The header search shall list matching screens the person may open, and from three characters shall search, after a 300 ms pause in typing, calls (UCN, call number, party, serial, product), pending call requests (REQID, party, serial, product), spare requests (UID, OR number, UCN, party, serial, and the part on any line), spare consumption (UCN, call number, part), parties (name, key, city), machines (product, serial, party), active parts (code, description), active documents (title, number, product, tags, file name), knowledge-base articles (title, product, tags, category) and field failure reports (FFR number, UCN, customer, serial, product), warranty entries (SA number, party, invoice number, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry) and contract entries (MC number, party, and the serial or model of any machine on the entry), up to five of each; a warranty or contract hit shall open its register's Entries tab searched to the entry's own number (v0.10.104). FRS-218.2 Each register shall be read as the signed-in person, so row-level security bounds the results; a register shall be searched only where the person may open its screen, and each hit shall be offered only where they may open the screen it leads to (Field Solutions, open to everyone, excepted). FRS-218.3 Each register shall be shown as its own read returns; a register whose read fails shall be named as not searched rather than read as empty. FRS-218.4 Choosing a hit shall open that record: a call in its register’s read-only view (fetched by UCN when not loaded); a pending request in Pending Registrations; a spare request in its detail (fetched by UID when not loaded); a consumption line in a read-only detail; a party in its editor for a holder of masters.edit.records and in a read-only view otherwise; a machine in Machine History; a part in Part Search; a document by its Drive link; an article in Field Solutions (fetched by id when older than those listed); an FFR in its report. FRS-218.5 ↑ ↓ shall move through the hits and Enter shall open the highlighted one; the search term shall be stripped of the characters that delimit a PostgREST filter. FRS-218.6 Where a register holds more matches than the five shown, its group shall say so rather than read as complete (D-117).

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |

**FRS-242.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-242.1 Parties, parts and product lines shall be written under masters.parties.*, masters.parts.* and masters.product_master.* (add / edit / delete), each its own INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policy (0325), with no FOR ALL write policy. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. FRS-242.3 A value list shall carry master.<list>.add beside .edit and .delete; adding shall be admitted by the add key, the list's edit key or masters.edit.records. FRS-242.4 Each of the four registers shall show an Actions column — ✎ Edit and 🗑 Delete, and on the Part Master and the lists Deactivate — each button only to the holder of its key; Add entry only to the holder of the add key. FRS-242.5 The Product Master's Edit shall change every field but the Product Code; a list's Edit shall rename the value and change its columns, saying before it is saved that records already carrying the old wording keep it. FRS-242.6 master_delete_guard() (security definer, not callable through the API) shall refuse deleting a party named on any machine, call, call request, pending registration, sale, contract, ownership transfer, additional entry, feedback, spare request, consumption history or Indoor job; a part named on any spare request, dispatch, consumption, issue history, opening stock, adjustment, transfer or material return line; and a product line whose code any machine, sale line or contract line carries — counting as the owner, and naming the count. FRS-242.7 A delete or edit that matches no row shall be reported as not done, never as done. FRS-242.8 A party’s name, a part’s code or description and a product line’s code shall not be changed except through Rename part or by an importer, so a row cannot be renamed and then deleted (0335, D-136). FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). RATIONALE: .2 so nobody gains or loses on the day it ships; .6 counts as the owner because under the caller's row-level security a count sees only what the caller may read and would pass a party a thousand other calls name. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

### URS-074 — A decision to supply rests on evidence that is retained

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall record, for each customer, whether that customer has been verified. The system shall retain the records on which that verification rests. The system shall show both wherever the decision to supply is taken. A verification with no record behind it is an assertion, and the person relying on it downstream cannot check it.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-174** — KYC values, how two of them are derived, and the verification stamp | Medium | OQ-167 |
| **FRS-090** — What the period suggests, and what the customer register holds | Medium | OQ-78 |
| **FRS-088** — The installations awaiting Commercial | Low | OQ-76 |
| **FRS-086** — KYC records attached to a customer | Medium | OQ-74 |

**FRS-174.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-174.1 The KYC status shall be one of Pending, Verified or Rejected, anything else refused by a CHECK constraint (0201), and a new party with none shall read Pending. FRS-174.2 The database shall fill a blank GSTIN from the tax fields the party carries, found by its shape, and a blank PAN from the GSTIN (characters 3 to 12) or the tax fields, and shall never overwrite a value already entered. FRS-174.3 The drawer shall take a GSTIN of fifteen characters and, on entry, fill a blank PAN from it. FRS-174.4 When the status becomes Verified the database shall stamp the verifier from the session and the time, discarding values the caller sent in that write. FRS-174.5 When the status leaves Verified the database shall clear both. FRS-174.6 Attaching a KYC record whose link is already attached shall keep one record. RATIONALE: .5 because a party that is no longer verified was not verified by anybody, and leaving the name on it says it was. Proved by `supabase/tests/party_kyc_test.sql` (.1, .2, .4, .5) and `npm run check:kyc` (.6).

**FRS-090.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-090.1 The cover registers shall calculate a PM visit count from the recorded period. FRS-090.2 The cover registers shall accept a PM visit count entered by the operator. FRS-090.3 The cover registers shall retain an entered PM visit count when the period or the start date is subsequently changed. FRS-090.4 The warranty register shall re-read the address, the contact details and the tax registrations of the named customer from the customer register when the operator requests it. FRS-090.5 The warranty register shall state each field that request would change, with its present and its proposed value, before changing any. FRS-090.6 The warranty register shall change no field where the customer register holds no such customer. RATIONALE: .1 and .3 together are the requirement — three visits a year is the standard OFFER and what was sold is on the purchase order, so a count that keeps reverting to the offer whenever a start date is corrected is a field somebody re-types until they give up, and one that never follows the period makes every ordinary sale a manual entry. The test for "has it been changed" is whether it still equals what the period suggested BEFORE the edit, which is the same rule a machine uses to pin a field away from its entry. .5 because the installation address on a sale legitimately differs from the registered one: a sale whose address changed silently under an operator who had corrected it by hand is worse than one that is visibly out of date, because the first is wrong and nobody knows. .6 because blanking a sale on the ground that the customer register has never heard of the customer would destroy the only address anybody has.

**FRS-088.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-088.1 My Workload shall list the number of installation requests for which no call has been raised. FRS-088.2 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is verified. FRS-088.3 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is not verified. FRS-088.4 My Workload shall state, of those, the number whose customer is absent from the customer register. FRS-088.5 My Workload shall open the request register filtered to the stated subset when the operator selects a count. FRS-088.6 The request register shall display the verification status of the customer named by each request. RATIONALE: FRS-088.4 is separate from FRS-088.3 because the two need opposite actions — a customer who is absent is added, a customer who is present is verified — and a figure that merges them sends somebody to verify a customer who does not exist. The section is offered to every operator who may open the request register rather than to one department, because a count over a list the reader may not open is both useless and a disclosure of its size.

**FRS-086.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-086.1 The customer register shall attach a document to a customer and shall record its name, its location, the operator who attached it and the time. FRS-086.2 The customer register shall display the verification status of each customer in its list. FRS-086.3 The customer register shall display a link to each attached record in that list. FRS-086.4 The system shall treat a customer as verified on the recorded status alone. FRS-086.5 The system shall treat no customer as verified by the presence of an attached record. FRS-086.6 The customer register shall state, for a verified customer with no attached record, that the record is absent. FRS-086.7 The customer register shall retain a removed record in the document store. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 are the two halves of one asymmetry. The status is a DECISION a person made, and withholding it because the paperwork was filed elsewhere would make the system stricter than the people it serves; attaching a file is not a decision, so it can never make a customer verified. .7 because a KYC record somebody relied on is worth keeping wherever it sits.

**FRS-155.** *(v0.10.73 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-155.1 The Declaration shall find a stock out by the rule of FRS-154.1 and FRS-154.2. FRS-155.2 The Declaration shall list each part once, the quantities of the same part on several lines summed. FRS-155.3 The Declaration shall take, before printing and without printing them, To, Address, City, State, Contact No, Approximate value (Rs.), Purpose and Sent by; To, Address and Approximate value are mandatory. FRS-155.4 The Declaration shall pre-fill the address from the engineer's User Master row and the courier from the stock out. FRS-155.8 The printed sheet shall carry the company mark, the form title, the date, the SO No, the GST No, the area code, the declaration text with the purpose and value, and the statement that no transaction is involved. FRS-155.9 The grid shall carry SNO, part number, description and quantity with totals, 18 rows per sheet, with the heading and the sender block on every sheet and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. **FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.

**FRS-015.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Party/Product/Part/User masters and value lists are editable by authorised roles; edits are gated by masters.edit, or per value list by master.<list>.edit / master.<list>.delete, enforced by row-level security. Every row records the login that created and last changed it (sys columns, 0244). A value in use SHALL be deactivated rather than deleted, and the database SHALL refuse the deletion of a value any record carries (FRS-180.6; OPEN until D-056 is fixed). A part is never deleted (FRS-177.10); a party's name is not changed by editing (FRS-173).

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-139 — A controlled value that is in use is withdrawn, never erased

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Each value list shall be maintainable by those granted that list, a duplicate being refused and each entry attributable to the person who added it. A value that any record carries shall not be deleted; it shall be deactivated, so it stops being offered and the records carrying it still read correctly, and the refusal shall be the database's and not only the screen's. The Standard Complaint list shall be scoped by product, a complaint mapped to no product applying to every product, so a call is offered the complaints that belong to its machine. A value may be renamed by those granted the list; the records already carrying the old wording keep it. An overview shall show every master with its size and whether it loaded.

**FRS-180.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-180.1 An entry shall be added only by a holder of `master.<list>.add` (or its parents `master.<list>.edit`, `masters.edit.records`, `masters.edit`), the database refusing anybody else (0067, 0325; corrected 2026-10-03). FRS-180.2 A value already in the list shall be refused with “already in this list”. FRS-180.3 An entry's Added On shall be the day it was added, and its author shall be recorded by the database from the session (`sys_created_by`, 0244); the Added By shown is a label. FRS-180.4 An entry shall be deactivated or reactivated after a confirmation stating that it stays on the records carrying it and stops being offered. FRS-180.5 🗑 Delete shall be offered only to a holder of `master.<list>.delete`. FRS-180.6 The database shall refuse the deletion of a value that any record carries, and shall say to deactivate it instead. FRS-180.7 Without the right to edit a list, the screen shall name the permission needed. FRS-180.8 ↻ Refresh on a list shall clear that list's dropdown cache, so forms offer the change without a reload; ↻ Refresh all shall clear every one. FRS-180.9 Where the registry of lists (`master_lists`) is absent, the built-in lists shall be used and the screen shall say which bundle to run. FRS-180.10 All Masters shall list the four registers with a row count each, and every value list with its entry count, whether it Loaded, is Empty or failed, and where it is used; a list may be opened in place or on its own page, and an unknown list address shall return to the overview. RATIONALE: .6 in the database because every count and filter downstream matches the stored value, and a deleted value leaves records carrying a word no list holds. Today a hard DELETE is offered with no such check and nothing in the database refuses it (D-056). FRS-180.11 An entry shall be added through an Add entry form opened by a button, naming each field and marking the required ones, and refusing an empty value; on the DCCR Complaint Grouping and Root Cause Key Word lists the Product shall be required and picked from the Product Master, or COMM for every product.

**FRS-181.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-181.1 Each Standard Complaint shall carry the products it applies to in `extra.products`, and a complaint mapped to none shall apply to every product. FRS-181.2 The mapping shall be edited singly, or for ticked complaints set, added to or removed in bulk, ten at a time with every failure named, by holders of `master.complaint.edit` only. FRS-181.3 Changing the mapping shall keep every other value in `extra`. FRS-181.4 The editor shall offer every product in the register and every product already mapped, so a mapping cannot vanish from its own editor. FRS-181.5 The list shall be filterable by complaint and by product, including “All products (no mapping)”. FRS-181.6 Its export shall carry the key and the products so the file can be re-loaded, and shall stop at 5,000 rows saying so. FRS-181.7 After a change the complaint caches shall be cleared, so the call forms offer the new scope.

**FRS-242.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-242.1 Parties, parts and product lines shall be written under masters.parties.*, masters.parts.* and masters.product_master.* (add / edit / delete), each its own INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policy (0325), with no FOR ALL write policy. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. FRS-242.3 A value list shall carry master.<list>.add beside .edit and .delete; adding shall be admitted by the add key, the list's edit key or masters.edit.records. FRS-242.4 Each of the four registers shall show an Actions column — ✎ Edit and 🗑 Delete, and on the Part Master and the lists Deactivate — each button only to the holder of its key; Add entry only to the holder of the add key. FRS-242.5 The Product Master's Edit shall change every field but the Product Code; a list's Edit shall rename the value and change its columns, saying before it is saved that records already carrying the old wording keep it. FRS-242.6 master_delete_guard() (security definer, not callable through the API) shall refuse deleting a party named on any machine, call, call request, pending registration, sale, contract, ownership transfer, additional entry, feedback, spare request, consumption history or Indoor job; a part named on any spare request, dispatch, consumption, issue history, opening stock, adjustment, transfer or material return line; and a product line whose code any machine, sale line or contract line carries — counting as the owner, and naming the count. FRS-242.7 A delete or edit that matches no row shall be reported as not done, never as done. FRS-242.8 A party’s name, a part’s code or description and a product line’s code shall not be changed except through Rename part or by an importer, so a row cannot be renamed and then deleted (0335, D-136). FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). RATIONALE: .2 so nobody gains or loses on the day it ships; .6 counts as the owner because under the caller's row-level security a count sees only what the caller may read and would pass a party a thousand other calls name. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. FRS-182.2 It shall filter by party, product, serial and status, the status being the derived cover status rather than a stored one. FRS-182.7 It shall state that an Inactive line takes no new Sale Entry and still takes contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback, and where it is empty shall point to Bulk Uploads and name the permission needed. FRS-182.8 The Sale Entry's product picker shall offer only Active lines, pair code and name where the catalogue gives one answer, count the retired lines it does not offer and say why, and accept a product the catalogue does not hold. **FRS-227.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-227.1 A product line shall carry Imported (Yes / No), blank until set. ### URS-141 — The assembled machine record says how current it is, and who may read it is a decision on record

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Product Database 2.0 shall state when it was last assembled and, where a source register has changed since, that it is being updated and within what time. It shall be re-assembled automatically after any source register changes, within a stated interval, and on demand only by those authorised to maintain the registers. Who may read it shall be stated as a decision: it assembles warranty and contract detail, and where its readership is wider than that of the registers it reads, that shall be recorded and approved by the system owner rather than inherited from a technical fix. An empty result shall say, for each source register, how many rows it holds and how many lack a serial or a model, and whether the reader is seeing only their own share.

### URS-163 — Only a known person gets in, and every way in is the production one

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall admit a person only through the organisation’s identity provider and shall record every successful and every refused sign-in. A person whose profile cannot be read shall not be admitted. A signed-in person who has neither a profile nor a User Master entry shall hold no authority beyond seeing that their identity is unresolved. Super administrators shall be designated in one list that the application and the database agree on. A password shall meet a stated strength, changing one shall require the current one, and a forgotten one shall have one stated remedy. ### URS-177 — Equipment sold through a dealer is monitored, and its installation call is raised when the dealer sells it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Sold Through shall record the dealer a machine was sold through, chosen only from parties identified as dealers, on the Warranty Sale Entry, on the Ownership Transfer and in the Product Database. A sale may be made to a dealer, but no installation call shall be raised for a dealer. When the dealer sells the machine to a customer an ownership transfer shall be recorded, and the installation call shall be raised from that transfer, for the customer, with the call number OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL so that it is told apart, dated the transfer date. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-03 (“Sold through -- it is to monitor the equipments sold through Dealer … we can not have an installation call for a dealer … then generate an installation call from the ownership transfer entry … OT-PRODUCT-SERIAL NO”).

FRS-243.2 Sold Through on the Warranty Sale Entry and on each machine line shall be chosen only from dealers (no free text). FRS-243.6 The Ownership Transfer register shall show Sold Through and offer, to a holder of install.create, “+ Installation call” on a transfer: one call for the transfer's To party, numbered OT-<product>-<serial>, dated the transfer date, built by the same builder as a sale's installation call with the Party Master's city, state and engineer and the Product Database's cover; a machine that already has its OT- call is not given a second. FRS-243.7 Once, the Sold Through 0318 cleared from machine lines shall be restored from its backup where the line still follows its entry and the entry's value is blank or different (0328). ### URS-181 — The month's PM visits are worked out from the Warranty and Contract Registers, each Generated or Missed

*v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall list, for a chosen month, the machines whose warranty or contract has a PM visit due in that month, worked out from the cover's start date, period and PM visits: visit k falls on the start date plus k times (months x 30 / PM visits) days. Each shall be shown as Generated when a PM call for that visit (reading k / N) exists for the machine and is not cancelled, and as a Missed PM otherwise, and the list shall be filterable by Missed PM / Generated, by Products / Accessories, and by product. A PM call shall be created only for a Missed PM whose machine's installation call is solved, or which has no installation call, and whose party is a customer, and each of those two conditions shall also be a filter. The coordinator shall be able to create those calls, dated the 1st of the month, registered after the month's latest PM call and allotted to the Product Database's engineer. The monthly PM upload shall remain. The user, 2026-10-08: "Can we do PM generation from Contract and warranty register?"; the first visit of a cover starting 10 January with 3 visits in 12 months is due on its 120th day; "it should check the largest registeration date and time for the month, then add 10 secs"; Added On "should capture the actual Date of that call generation"; a visit is generated "when the visit is created - like 1/12, 2/12 like that and it is not in Cancelled state"; "Give me an option to segregate Product and Accessory"; "Give me pending list separately.. like a filter at the top, generated, pending (Or name it Missed PM)"; "Add the product as a filter at the top"; "Add 2 more logics - But add these as rules + Filters: 1. The installation call associated with it should be in solved state 2. Party the device is associated to should be a customer"; "Allow machines with no installation call".

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-269** — PM Due | High | OQ-267 |

**FRS-269.** *(v0.10.146 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-269.1 PM Due shall be listed under Administration beside PM Bulk Upload, opened by mod:/pm-due, and its list read only by a holder of pm.generate, through pm_visits_due() (0404), which refuses anybody else and is not executable by the public key. FRS-269.2 A cover is a Warranty Register line (warranty_sale_details) or a Contract Register line (contract_details) with a product, a serial, a start date, a period in months and PM visits above 0; its end is its end date, else start + months - 1 day. FRS-269.3 Visit k (1 to PM visits) shall be due on start + round(k x months x 30 / PM visits) days, never after the end; it belongs to the month that date falls in. FRS-269.4 Every machine (product + serial, case and spaces ignored) with a visit falling in the month shall be listed, with the last such visit; it shall be Generated when a PM call for that machine, not cancelled, registered from the cover's start month to its end, has a Reported Problem reading k / N with the same visit number and the same number of visits, in whatever month it was registered, and a Missed PM otherwise; the answer shall include calls the reader cannot see, and each row shall show the generating call and the machine's last PM call. FRS-269.5 A machine with a warranty and a contract visit in the same month shall be listed once, from the warranty. FRS-269.6 The party, city, state and engineer shall be the machine's Product Database row (its Service Engineer), the register's party where it has none; a Missed PM with no engineer shall be counted and created unallocated. FRS-269.7 The list shall be filtered at the top by status (Missed PM, the default; Generated; All), by type (All; Products; Accessories, an accessory being a product whose Product Master category is ACCESSORY), by installation (Installation solved or none, the default; Solved; No installation call; Installation not solved; Any), by party (Customer, the default; Not a customer; Any) and by one product, each button counting what it would show with the other filters applied. FRS-269.8 A row may be created only when it is a Missed PM, its machine's installation call (Installation register, product + serial; a Solved call taken over a cancelled or later one) reads Solved or it has no installation call (0404), and its party (the Product Database's, else the register's) has Type CUSTOMER on the Party Master; an installation call that exists and is not Solved, or a party not in the master or with no Type, fails; each row shall show its installation call and state and its party's Type. Only such a row shall be tickable; every one shown starts ticked. Create shall need pm.create, the PM register's insert right, and shall write the ticked rows through the calls view with the PM upload's shaping (shapePmRows): call type P M VISIT, Registration Date, Complaint Date and Breakdown Date the 1st of the month, Added On today, Standard Complaint SCHEDULED PM VISIT, Reported Problem SCHEDULED PM VISIT k / N, the SA number as Warranty Number or the MC number as Contract Number, the cover dates, and Item Status WGP or the contract's type normalised. FRS-269.9 The first call shall be registered 10 seconds after the largest registration date-and-time among ALL PM calls of the month (pm_due_latest_reg_at), read when Create is pressed, and each next 10 seconds later; a month with none starts at 00:30 on the 1st, 5 seconds apart, as on PM Bulk Upload. FRS-269.10 After creating, the list shall be read again, so a created visit reads Generated. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-08; the texts are what all 8,720 PM calls of 2026 carry (_pm_generation_inputs.sql). 0401's count of PM calls since the cover started was replaced (D-157).

### URS-040 — A bulk load shall not silently alter what it does not carry

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Loading a file shall change only the fields that file supplies. A field the file does not carry shall take the value the system defines for it, and shall not be written as empty or null; a load that cannot honour this shall fail rather than write. Where a register is declared to be loaded from a file that is the WHOLE of each record (the Product Database), a cell the file carries under its heading and leaves empty shall empty that field, so a correction made at source can remove a value as well as add one; a stamped or a required column shall never be emptied this way.

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

**FRS-267.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-267.1 Bulk Uploads shall offer "DCCR Register — historical, with its calls", loaded into a staging register keyed on the UC Number, open to a holder of bulk.upload. FRS-267.2 Each row shall file its call — a P M VISIT row as a PM call, any other as a Field call — dated by the file's CALL DATE, with the customer as the party, the place, product, serial, cover, complaint, engineer, warranty number and Review 1 answers; the month-only warranty start shall be kept as text. FRS-267.3 Each row shall file its review marked imported, keeping the file's reviewers and dates and raising no Field Failure Report. FRS-267.4 Each row shall file one visit carrying the CURRENT CALL STATUS (else CALL STATUS), pending reason, engineer and Call Solved Date & Time, entered at the solved date, else the file's Updated Date, else the call date; no visit shall be filed for Unattended or for a Canceled call, which shall be filed cancelled. FRS-267.5 A call already in the register shall not be changed, and only a review it lacks shall be added. FRS-267.6 Loading shall notify nobody. FRS-267.7 Re-loading shall correct the calls the load filed and add no second call or visit; a correction shall need the same edit rights as on screen. FRS-267.8 The outcome for each UC Number shall be recorded on its staging row. RATIONALE: measured on the live project 2026-10-06, 6,051 DCCR rows of 2025 had been loaded while no Field call before 2026 existed, so the DCCR View could show none of them.

**FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-046.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The API writes a batch of rows as ONE insert whose column list is the union of the rows’ keys; a row lacking one of those keys is written as NULL, not as the column default. The loader therefore groups rows by their column set and sends each group separately, so a column no row in the group carries genuinely defaults. Filling absent values in was rejected as a fix: it would defeat a default that carries meaning. A load that violates a NOT NULL constraint fails the batch and writes nothing of it.

### URS-068 — One identified record per machine, assembled from every register that names it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every machine the organisation has sold, contracted or recovered shall appear exactly once in a register of machines, identified by its MODEL together with its SERIAL — never by the serial alone, which repeats across models. That record shall be assembled from the warranty sale register, the contract register, the additional entries, the ownership transfer register and the installation call, and shall state for each of the party, the warranty and the contract WHICH register decided it, so the record can be checked against its evidence. Where the registers disagree, the most recently dated evidence shall decide.

| **FRS-080** — Product Database 2.0 assembles one row per machine from five registers | High | OQ-64 |

**FRS-183.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-183.1 `product_database_v2` shall read from a materialised view (`product_database_v2_mv`, 0220) that is rebuilt only when a source register has changed since the last rebuild, by `refresh_product_database_2_if_stale()` run every five minutes by pg_cron (0223). FRS-183.2 The screen shall show “Live as of <time>” and, where a register has changed since, that it will update within 5 minutes. FRS-183.3 ⟳ Rebuild shall run `refresh_product_database_2()`, which the database shall refuse to anybody without pd2.rebuild (Rebuild Product Database 2.0) or administrator, and which shall clear the stale flag. FRS-183.4 The screen shall offer ⟳ Rebuild to holders of pd2.rebuild, a key copied once to the roles that held masters.edit or cover.edit. FRS-183.5 Every signed-in user who may open the screen shall read every machine and its warranty and contract detail (0221). This is the recorded position, a widening from 0220's masters.view / cover.edit / administrator, and is for the system owner to confirm or narrow; narrowing is one predicate and one grant. FRS-183.6 The screen shall load every machine, so its count and status chips are exact, and shall search on the device by product, serial, party, contract or SA number. FRS-183.7 Where it lists nothing it shall show, for each source register, the rows held and those with no serial or no model, and shall say “your slice too” to a reader who is not an office role. FRS-183.8 The drawer shall link the SA number, the installation UCN, the MC number and the transfer reference to the registers holding them, and show a missing number as plain text. FRS-183.9 A load failure shall give one of the three answers of `loadFailure()` and the error verbatim. FRS-183.10 The materialised view shall not be readable by the public (anon) key (0337, D-127). **FRS-080.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `product_database_v2` (0218) lists every machine named by `warranty_sale_details`, `contract_details` or `product_additional_entries`, keyed by `machine_key(product, serial)` — the SQL twin of `machineKey()` in `src/lib/machine.ts`, squashed so ORION-G and ORION G are one model, and MODEL-plus-SERIAL so the eleven machines numbered 219 stay eleven rows. Ownership Transfer and the installation call are joined in. The party is the most recently DATED claim among the ownership transfer, the additional entry, the contract and the sale, ties breaking towards the transfer. `party_from`, `warranty_from`, `contract_from` and `item_status_reason` name the deciding register on every row. It does not replace `public.products` or `machine_cover`, both of which are left exactly as they are.

### URS-069 — What a machine is covered by today is derived, not typed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Whether a machine is inside its warranty, under a maintenance contract, or covered by neither shall be DERIVED from the recorded warranty and contract periods rather than stored as an opinion that ages. A machine inside its warranty is under warranty (WGP) even where a contract also covers it; a labour contract is AMC and a comprehensive contract is CMC; a machine covered by neither is OGP. A contract whose type was never recorded shall be reported as such and shall never be assumed to be either kind.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-081** — Item status is derived warranty-first, and a typeless contract is flagged | High | OQ-65 |

**FRS-081.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `product_database_v2.item_status` is WGP where the warranty period covers today; otherwise `contract_cover_code(type)` where the contract period covers today — labour/labor to AMC, comprehensive/CMC to CMC, anything else returned UNCHANGED rather than bucketed; otherwise OGP. A contract covering today whose type is blank reads `CONTRACT (TYPE NOT RECORDED)`. This differs from `machine_cover` in both directions on purpose: that view asks the contract FIRST (so a machine inside warranty reads as its contract type) and defaults a blank type to CMC (so a labour contract silently reads as comprehensive).

### URS-070 — A warranty starts when the machine was installed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The warranty period of a machine shall start from the date recorded on its installation — the Warranty Start Date captured when the installation call is reported, or failing that the date that call was solved — and shall fall back to the selling register only where no installation was recorded. The end of the period shall be derived from that start and the recorded period, by the same arithmetic the rest of the application uses.

| **FRS-082** — Warranty start comes from the installation, and the end is computed like the app | High | OQ-66 |

**FRS-245.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-245.1 Where the customer feedback of a machine's latest installation call answers Warranty Start Date? with "Installation Call Solved Date" and the call is Solved, that product + serial's Product Database warranty start shall be the day the call was solved, in India time (0331). FRS-245.2 Its warranty end shall then be that start plus the sale's warranty period — months, else years × 12 — by cover_period_end(), the application's own arithmetic; with no period known the end is left as the sale has it. FRS-245.3 "Invoice Date", any other answer, or an installation not yet solved shall leave the documented start of the PO / Warranty Sale Entry. FRS-245.4 The machine shall be re-synced whenever an installation's feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, and the answer shall survive the sale being saved again. FRS-245.5 Only the product + serial the installation names shall change. FRS-245.6 A one-time apply shall set this for every machine whose installation already answered "Installation Call Solved Date", the old start, end and status kept in products_install_start_backup. RATIONALE: the two answers are the feedback's own, measured on the live register (328 and 78 installations, 2026-10-03); 28 reports carrying a typed date were left as they are, the user's decision. Proved by `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

**FRS-246.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-246.1 public.installation_warranty_starts shall hold one row per installation call, keyed on the UCN (ucn_key, unique), with call_number, product_name, serial, party_name, reg_date, warranty_choice, call_solved_at, solved_date (the India-time day of call_solved_at where not given), engineer, visit_at, remarks, source (RITHI, Feedback or Upload) and the columns the file carries that it does not name in extra (0332). FRS-246.3 machine_install_warranty_start() shall read the machine's latest row here (by solved date), so a loaded 2018 row decides its machine's warranty as a reported call does (FRS-245). FRS-246.4 Saving a row shall re-sync its product + serial, and the old machine where the product or serial changed. FRS-246.5 A RITHI installation shall fill its own row when its feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, once the engineer has answered Warranty Start Date?. FRS-246.6 Loading or correcting a row shall need Bulk Uploads (bulk.upload); reading needs a sign-in. FRS-246.8 On an installation's Visit Entry, below Warranty Start Date?, the system shall show the Product Database warranty of that product + serial as it stands and — when Installation Call Solved Date is chosen on a visit that solves the call — the start and end it will have, computed by the database (machine_warranty_preview). FRS-246.9 The record shall be filled once from every installation feedback already on file. **FRS-082.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Warranty start is the `Warranty Start Date?` answer on the installation call’s feedback, read through `imported_ts()` so a cell holding "n/a" yields nothing rather than failing the whole view; failing that the installation call’s solved date; failing that the additional entry; failing that the warranty sale. Where a start and a period are both known the end is `cover_period_end(start, months)`, which reproduces `addPeriod()` in `src/lib/dates.ts` INCLUDING its JavaScript month overflow — 31 January plus one month is 2 March, where Postgres’s own interval arithmetic clamps to 27 February. 26 of 458 start/period combinations differ between the two.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. ### URS-140 — The install base is read, not typed, and work on a machine starts from the machine

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Product Database shall present the install base read-only — machines are loaded, or follow from the cover registers and ownership transfer — and shall let a person who may register calls start a field call, and a person who may create installation calls start an installation call, from a machine, with the machine's customer, model, serial and cover already filled. The Product Master shall present the catalogue of product lines, saying which lines are still sold, and shall be maintained by hand by those granted it. A retired product line shall not be offered on a new sale, and the reason shall be stated where it is missing; it shall remain available to contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback. A product the catalogue does not hold may still be typed on a sale, the catalogue being kept by hand.

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

### URS-170 — A DEMO unit of an imported product is pre-delivery tested before it leaves

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A DEMO unit whose product is imported shall not leave the workshop until the controlled record R/SER/QC/007 PRE DELIVERY TESTING is complete and every check reads OK, the inspector recorded by the system with their designation, and the record shall be printable as the form is kept. The Product Master shall say whether each product line is imported; where that is not known, the test shall not be demanded and the screen shall say it is not known. Equipment manufactured in-house, and customer property, are not subject to it.

FRS-226.4 A DEMO unit whose product is imported shall be refused the move to Dispatched or Closed while it has no test, while any field is blank or it is unsigned (naming what is blank), or while any of checks 1–5 reads NOT OK (naming which). ### URS-060 — A record is keyed on what identifies it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The key of a quality or servicing record shall be the whole of what identifies it. Where a record concerns a DEVICE, the device is its model together with its serial number, serial numbers being repeated across models. Where one document concerns SEVERAL devices, each device shall hold its own record under that document’s number. A key narrower than the identity does not fail loudly — it silently replaces one record with another — so the sufficiency of such a key shall be established by MEASUREMENT against the data to be loaded, before that data is loaded.

| **FRS-178** — Renaming a part carries its history | High | OQ-213, OQ-171 |
| **FRS-188** — A transfer and an additional entry name the model and the serial | High | OQ-181 |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-072** — A device record is keyed on the model and the serial | High | OQ-54 |

FRS-119.7 A voided spare shall read VOIDED, a cancelled call CANCELLED, and a migrated FFR or uploaded feedback shall be labelled so.
