FRS-178.3 `rename_part()` shall rewrite the part's identity in the catalogue and in all ten tables that carry it — stock adjustments (0266) included since 0309 — in one transaction. FRS-178.4 It shall refuse a rename onto a part that already exists, never merging two parts. FRS-178.7 The spare-request-line guard and the material-return guard shall let through the one change a rename makes — the part, moved exactly as the rename’s ticket names it, nothing else changed — so a rename does not need an administrator (0310); every other change of part on a line, and every other edit of a return, shall still be refused. FRS-178.8 Stock transfers shall move last of the ten, so the transfer stock check sees the part’s full balance under the new name. FRS-178.5 The consumption guard shall admit that rename by a ticket only the function can write, and shall refuse every other change of part on a consumption line. FRS-178.6 Every engineer's hand stock shall be the same after a rename as before, under the new identity. RATIONALE: nothing has a foreign key to `parts`; hand stock is derived from the nine tables, so a catalogue-only rename changes balances rather than links (D-007, D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/rename_part_test.sql`.

**FRS-188.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-188.1 The Record a transfer form shall require the model and the serial. FRS-188.2 The destination party shall be chosen from the Party Master. FRS-188.3 A blank previous party shall be completed from the machine's current owner only where exactly one machine carries that model and serial, left empty otherwise, and left empty where it would equal the destination (0182, 0183). FRS-188.4 Recording a transfer shall set the owner in the Product Database of that model and serial only, and not where a later-dated transfer of the same machine exists. FRS-188.5 The person recording shall be stamped from the session with any caller-supplied value discarded, and shall not change afterwards. FRS-188.6 The Add entry details form shall require the model and the serial, and saving shall insert or correct the entry keyed on `machine_key` (0185). FRS-188.7 A save the database refuses shall say why in words. RATIONALE: 298 serials in the recovered-entries export belong to more than one product. Today the transfer form asks for the serial alone, 0072/0183 fill the model and previous owner from the first `products` row with that serial, the owner of EVERY machine sharing the serial is moved, and `recorded_by` keeps a caller-supplied value (D-060); the entry form asks for the serial alone and upserts on `serial_number`, a target 0185 removed, so every save is refused (D-054).

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-072.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Three registers were keyed on less than their identity, and each was corrected against MEASURED data rather than argument. The field failure register was keyed on the report number alone (0181): eight numbers in the 2016–2019 registers each cover several machines — one covers four — so 20 rows collapsed to 8 and TWELVE machines were lost on a load reporting success. Recovered warranty entries were keyed on the serial alone (0185): of 2,263 rows, 298 serials belong to more than one product — one serial is both an ANAVENT and an ORION, another is four machines — so 640 rows collapsed to 298 and THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO machines were lost. Ownership transfers carried no key at all (0184). Each key is now the pair, held as a GENERATED STORED column with a plain unique index. The rule was already stated in the codebase (src/lib/machine.ts) together with the incident that produced it — a request for one model’s serial 201 was offered an open call for another model’s serial 201, one action from being mapped onto it — and these three registers contradicted it.

### URS-125 — The documents that travel with a stock out are complete and can be produced again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

For every stock out the system shall produce a Delivery Challan and a Declaration on the company's controlled layout, listing exactly what that stock out carried, and shall produce them again on request for any stock out the reader may see, however old it is. The challan shall carry the stock-out and reference numbers and dates, the recipient, the courier, each part and quantity with the total, and the company's statutory identifiers, on sheets each complete in itself; a signature shall appear on it only as URS-057 allows. The Declaration shall state the recipient's address, the parcel's approximate value and its purpose, and each part once with its total quantity, and shall name what is still missing before it is printed. Correcting the engineer's address from the Declaration may update the User Master only for somebody authorised to dispatch, and only the address. A challan that can no longer be found is a shipment whose paperwork cannot be reproduced.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-154** — The Delivery Challan | High | OQ-146 |
| **FRS-155** — The Declaration | High | OQ-147 |

FRS-154.3 The Delivery Challan shall print the quantity sent on THIS stock out for each line (`spare_dispatch_lines`), ordered by spare ID. FRS-154.4 Each sheet shall carry the company mark (`COMPANY_LOGO`), the company's name, address, telephone and e-mail, and the title DELIVERY CHALLAN. FRS-154.6 The grid shall carry Sr.No, Order No., Item Code, Description and Qty; the last sheet shall carry the total and every other sheet "Continued on sheet N". FRS-154.7 The challan shall be cut into A4 sheets of 20 rows, each with its own letterhead and signature block and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-154.8 The challan shall carry the dispatch remarks and the company's GSTIN, CIN and PAN. ### URS-127 — An engineer's hand stock can be read down to the movements that make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A user shall be able to read, for each engineer and part they may see, the stock in hand and every term it is made of — opening balance, migrated history, stock out, consumption, transfers in and out, returns and office adjustments — such that the terms shown add up to the figure shown; and to open the movements behind any figure, every one of them or a statement that the list is incomplete. A balance below zero shall be shown and explained as a finding rather than hidden. The whole register shall be searchable, not only the part already read. A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's stock with the person. A drill-down whose arithmetic does not add up teaches its reader to stop checking.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-159** — Reading hand stock, and the movements behind it | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-151, OQ-158 |
| **FRS-160** — The Hand Stock Report says what its file holds | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-152 |

**FRS-159.** *(v0.10.150 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-159.1 Hand Stock shall show one line per engineer and part with Opening, From history, Stock out, Consumed, Transfer in, Transfer out, Returned, Stock level and Last movement, read from `handstock_balance` (security_invoker). FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.3 Hand Stock shall offer In hand (the default), Short (below zero), Settled (zero) and All, each with its exact count once the balance is loaded ("+" only while a restored device cache cut at its cap is shown, which also offers a reload). FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. FRS-159.12 A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's name on spare requests, dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, MRNs and transfers, so the balance is one balance under the new name (0259–0262). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 replace URS-024's old claim that a balance cannot go negative: a consumption line cannot exceed the balance when it is written (FRS-030), but a level can stand below zero where migrated history or an issue never recorded says so, and FRS-044 keeps such a figure exactly — so the register shows it as a finding. FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-160.** *(v0.10.116 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-160.1 Hand Stock Report shall be an administrator's screen by default and grantable to any role (`admin: true`). FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. RATIONALE: .2 because a .csv can carry no second sheet, so a searched file is otherwise indistinguishable from the whole register — the silent partial file URS-077 exists to prevent (D-047).

### URS-129 — A hand-over of stock names two real engineers and is made by somebody who may make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall record a hand-over of spares from one engineer to another, naming both from the User Master's active engineers, never the same person twice. An engineer shall hand over only their own stock; a hand-over of another engineer's stock shall be recorded only by somebody holding an authority to act for others. No hand-over shall exceed what the giving engineer holds. The hand-over shall be recorded in the audit trail, and the register of hand-overs shall be readable in full. What the screen says about where stock comes from shall agree with how stock is counted. A hand-over to a name that is not a person is stock no engineer holds, and a hand-over anyone can make of anyone's stock moves a balance nobody decided to move.

| **FRS-229** — The Material Transfer Note R/SER/STR/003, and a reason per part | Medium | OQ-224 |

**FRS-162.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-162.1 Stock Transfer shall offer New Transfer only to a holder of `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.2 The From engineer shall default to the signed-in person, and shall be changeable only by a holder of an authority to act for others. FRS-162.3 The database shall accept a transfer whose From is not the caller only from an administrator or a holder of that authority. FRS-162.4 The From and To engineers shall be chosen from the active engineers of the User Master, and the database shall refuse a To that is not one. FRS-162.5 The form and the database shall refuse a transfer whose From and To are the same person. FRS-162.6 The form shall offer only parts the From engineer holds, re-read when From changes, shall not offer a part twice, and shall take a quantity from one to what is held; the database shall refuse more than is held (0020). FRS-162.7 The form shall take a transfer date defaulting to today (see FRS-163) and remarks. FRS-162.8 Where the From engineer holds nothing, the form shall say so and state that stock comes from what Stores has dispatched to them, less what they have consumed, handed on or returned. FRS-162.9 On success the screen shall name the transfer number and write an audit entry `stock.transfer`. FRS-162.10 The register shall list every transfer line the reader may see (either engineer in their scope), in pages with Load more, with "+" on its count while more remain, searchable by transfer number, engineers, part and remarks. FRS-162.11 A recorded transfer’s From, To and date are not changed afterwards, except by an importer re-loading it or a User Master rename; a transfer marked import by anybody else is an ordinary, checked transfer (0339, D-119, D-120). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 are the database's because the insert policy today asks only for `stock.transfer`, so anybody holding it can move anybody's stock to any name (D-049); .8 because the screen says stock comes from an acknowledged receipt, which is not how it is counted (D-052).

**FRS-229.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-229.1 A stock transfer line shall carry an optional Reason (`stock_transfer_lines.reason`, 0322), blank by default; the transfer's common Remarks stay. FRS-229.2 The New Stock Transfer form shall take a reason on each part as well as the common Remarks, and the register shall show it. FRS-229.3 Each transfer shall offer “🖨 MTN”, opening /mtn/<transfer no>, which shall require the Stock Transfer screen's module key and read the transfer by its number under row-level security. FRS-229.4 The print shall reproduce R/SER/STR/003: the company's mark, the organisation, SERVICE and MATERIAL TRANSFER NOTE (MTN), the RECORD block (DOC. REF R/SER/STR/003, ISSUE No./DATE 02 01.11.09, REV. No./DATE 00 01.11.09, PAGE No. n of N), Name & Place of Issuer and of Receiver — the engineer and their City on the User Master, else their Region, blank where the directory holds the name more than once with different places — MTN No. (the transfer number) and Date; S.No. / Part No. / Description / Qty. / Reason for Transfer / Remarks, Reason being the line's reason else the common remarks and Remarks blank; and the boxes Issued By (the sending engineer and the transfer date), Received By (blank: a transfer records no receipt), Authorised By (blank) and Entered By (the name of the login that keyed it). ### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-133 — A login is issued, reset and withdrawn by a person granted the right; a reset password is its owner's alone

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let only a person granted the right create a sign-in login for a person on the User Master, reset a forgotten password (its own right, users.reset_password, which never reaches an administrator's login or that of anyone who can grant permissions), and disable or re-enable a login. A login created with a starting password may keep it: the owner can replace it under My Profile and is not forced to (the system owner's decision, 2026-10-01: “Leave it as it is, it is that way for Ease of Operation”). Until it is replaced, whoever knows the starting password can sign in as that person; this is an accepted risk (D-057, R-80). A reset shall generate a new password, show it once to the administrator and to nobody else, end every session the person holds, and be recorded by the database — whose login, by whom, when — without the password. Disabling a login shall keep every record the person made. A record signed in under a password somebody else also knows is not attributable to the person it names.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-168** — A new login starts with a known starting password its owner may replace | High | OQ-161 |
| **FRS-169** — A reset is generated, shown once, ends every session and is recorded by the database | High | OQ-162 |

**FRS-168.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-168.1 The User Master shall offer to create a sign-in login when a person is added, and the profile it writes shall be accepted by the database only from an administrator (`profiles_admin_write`). FRS-168.2 It shall refuse a login without a valid email address, and a starting password shorter than six characters. FRS-168.3 The drawer shall propose a starting password (a common default, which the administrator may overwrite) and the success message shall say the person signs in with it and can change it under My Profile. FRS-168.4 The first sign-in shall NOT force a change (the system owner's decision, 2026-10-01: “Leave it as it is, it is that way for Ease of Operation”); the owner changes it under My Profile. FRS-168.5 Where the project requires email confirmation, the User Master shall say that the person must confirm before signing in. FRS-168.6 Each creation shall be written to the audit trail with the role granted and never the password. RATIONALE: .3 and .4 are the system owner's accepted choice, for ease of operation. Its cost is stated so it stays a decision rather than an oversight: a starting password every administrator knows, and nothing requires changing, is shared by the office until its owner replaces it, and a record signed under it before then is not attributable to the person it names (D-057, R-80).

**FRS-169.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-169.1 `admin_reset_password()` (0110, 0305) shall refuse a caller who does not hold users.reset_password (an administrator holds it), shall refuse to reset a super administrator's password for a caller who is not one, and shall refuse to reset the password of an administrator or of somebody who can grant permissions for a caller who is not an administrator. FRS-169.2 It shall refuse a password shorter than ten characters. FRS-169.3 The User Master shall generate the password, set it through that function after a confirmation, and show it once with a copy control; it shall not be stored or written to any log. FRS-169.4 The function shall end every session the person holds. FRS-169.5 The function shall write `password_resets` — whose login, by whom, when — readable by administrators and holders of users.reset_password only, and the screen shall write the audit trail without the password. FRS-169.6 Disabling a login shall block sign-in and loading while keeping every record; enabling shall restore it; each shall be written to the audit trail. RATIONALE: .5 in the database because the client trail can be bypassed (FRS-021); .1's second half because an administrator who could reset a super administrator's password could take the project. Proved by `supabase/tests/admin_reset_password_test.sql`.

### URS-134 — Authority given to one person beyond their role is deliberate, visible and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let an administrator grant an individual person a permission their role does not carry, and shall show those individual grants wherever that person's access is set. Creating a login by copying another person shall copy their role and individual grants, shall grant sight of every record only where the administrator ticks it and shall say that it does, and shall be recorded with the person copied. The role written on the User Master shall reach the person's sign-in; a difference between the two shall be visible, correctable one person at a time, and each correction recorded. An individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, so authority that is not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews.

| --- | --- | --- |

FRS-170.2 The Access drawer shall show every individual permission the person holds beside those the role gives. FRS-170.3 ⧉ Clone shall create a new login carrying the source person's role and individual permissions, shall add `data.view_all` only when “can see all records” is ticked, and shall say that ticking it grants sight of every record. FRS-170.4 Every access save, clone and login creation shall be written to the audit trail, a clone naming the person copied. FRS-170.6 The User Master shall count the people whose sign-in role differs from the directory, show “X (now Y)” against each, and offer to apply the directory's role, writing each person separately, naming each failure and auditing each change. RATIONALE: .2 because an individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, and authority not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews. .6 one person at a time so that one failure does not leave the office unsure which of forty changes happened.

### URS-135 — A person's record is complete, agrees with the reporting tree, and is never destroyed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The User Master shall require a name for every person, it being what calls are allotted to, and shall record every field it offers, including the Department from which training audiences are drawn. A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be a name held by a person on the User Master, and a name matching nobody shall be stated as such before it is saved, because the reporting tree is built from those names and a misspelling empties a team without any error. The directory's Active flag shall be labelled as what it does, and kept apart from whether the person's login may sign in. A person who has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities history or a training record shall not be removed from the User Master; they shall be marked inactive instead. An administrator shall be able to see what a person has entered, for a handover.

| **FRS-172** — A person with a history is not removed from the User Master | High | OQ-165 |

FRS-171.3 The Department shall be chosen from the Department value list. FRS-171.4 The Reporting Manager and Regional Manager fields shall suggest the names on the User Master, and a name that matches no row shall be stated as such before saving and saved only on confirmation. FRS-171.5 The directory Active field shall be labelled as the directory flag it is; the login's own Disable / Enable shall be the only control described as deciding sign-in. FRS-171.6 Editing the whole table shall write each changed row separately, name every row that failed and keep its draft, mark changed rows “Edited”, save on Enter and ask before discarding on Esc. FRS-171.7 The 📊 Data drawer shall list, for a holder of users.manage, the calls, spare requests, approvals, dispatches, visit reports and consumption matching the person's name or email, within what the reader may see. FRS-171.8 Without a database connection the User Master shall show the sheet directory read-only. RATIONALE: .2 because training audiences are drawn by Department, and a Department chosen and not saved removes the person from every audience that names it. .4 because the reporting tree is built from these names; 0212 and 0257 record what a name matching nobody does. .5 because “Yes — may sign in” on a flag that governs no sign-in tells an administrator a leaver is locked out when they are not. All three are open (D-053).

**FRS-172.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-172.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a User Master row that has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities period, a training assignment or a training attendance, and the refusal shall say to mark the person inactive instead. ### URS-136 — A customer is known by one name, and the person who looks after them is a real person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master shall let an authorised user add a customer, giving at least its name, city and state, and shall refuse a name it already holds. It shall let an authorised user maintain a customer's type, profile, Serviceman, route, installation and billing addresses and contacts, and KYC details. It shall NOT allow the customer's name to be changed by editing, on the screen or through the data interface, because every machine, call and contract names the customer by that text and has no other link to it; a change of name shall be made only by a function that carries every record naming it. The Serviceman shall be a person on the User Master, because a new call is allotted to that name. Correcting a Serviceman's spelling across every customer carrying it shall be one act that changes all or none, shall say beforehand how many customers it will change, and shall offer only User Master names or nobody. Marking a customer's KYC Verified shall be attributed by the system to the person who did it, shall not be re-attributable by anybody else, and shall be cleared when the customer is no longer verified.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-176.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-176.1 Each register shall load in pages of 1,000 — the Warranty and Contract registers open at 2,000 and double on each Load more — and its count shall carry “+” while more rows exist; a register loaded to the end shall show an exact count. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.6 The ⚙ Columns picker shall offer the register's other fields and shall not offer the five system columns (`isSysColumn()`). FRS-176.7 ⭳ Export CSV shall be refused without export.data. FRS-176.8 Where the register holds more rows than are loaded, the export shall say so and ask before writing a file of the loaded rows. FRS-176.9 The export shall write every date as dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.10 A load, search or count that fails shall say so in words and keep the database's message; a count that could not be made shall read “—”, never 0. FRS-176.11 Arriving from a Product Database 2.0 link shall open the target register on the right tab, already searched for the number. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-146 — A training record, once made, is amended with a trace and ended only for a reason

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A training assignment shall be cancellable only by those responsible for training, with the reason kept, and a cancelled assignment shall read as neither open nor completed. An assignment past its due date and not completed shall read Overdue. A correction to a recorded attendance, assessment result, score, or Roles & Responsibilities period shall keep the value it replaced, who changed it and when: a training record is evidence of competence, and an edit that leaves no trace makes it evidence of nothing. The list of training sessions may be read by every signed-in user; who attended and how they were assessed shall be read only as URS-079 states.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-190** — Cancelling, Overdue, and amending a training record | High | OQ-183 |

**FRS-190.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-190.1 An open assignment shall be cancelled only by a holder of training.manage, with a reason, the database refusing anybody else (`tg_update`); a cancelled assignment shall read Cancelled and keep its reason. FRS-190.2 An assignment not completed and past its due date shall read Overdue (`training_status`, 0264). FRS-190.3 Assigning a document or topic to an audience shall skip anybody already assigned it and report how many were created. FRS-190.4 Re-saving a session shall record, for each attendance, assessment result, score or remark it changes, the previous value, who changed it and when, in a history no user can edit or delete. FRS-190.5 Changing a Roles & Responsibilities period's From or To shall be recorded the same way. FRS-190.6 The Sessions list shall be readable by every signed-in user (`ts_read`); a person's attendance and assessment only through `may_see_person()`. FRS-190.7 The assignments shall be searchable and counted by status with exact counts; where nothing is visible the screen shall say “No training assigned that you may see”, and a load failure shall name the bundle to run. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 because a Pass that was a Fail, or a period that moved, cannot be told from one recorded correctly once the edit leaves no trace; today both are overwritten in place and neither table is audited by `record_audit` (D-062).

### URS-163 — Only a known person gets in, and every way in is the production one

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall admit a person only through the organisation’s identity provider and shall record every successful and every refused sign-in. A person whose profile cannot be read shall not be admitted. A signed-in person who has neither a profile nor a User Master entry shall hold no authority beyond seeing that their identity is unresolved. Super administrators shall be designated in one list that the application and the database agree on. A password shall meet a stated strength, changing one shall require the current one, and a forgotten one shall have one stated remedy. A change to a person’s permissions shall reach a session already open within a stated time. An unknown login admitted with an engineer’s authority is an unknown login able to write quality records.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-210** — Sign-in, identity and passwords | High | OQ-203 |
| **FRS-216** — My Profile: the account, the R&R period, and what I can do | Medium | OQ-214, OQ-209 |

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-216.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-216.1 My Profile shall show the account: name, e-mail, designation, Permission (the role) and region. FRS-216.2 My Profile shall state, where the person’s profile did not load, that it did not and what they may do until it exists (FRS-210.5). FRS-216.3 A holder of users.manage or training.manage shall be able to change the period of a recorded R&R document, From remaining required and To not before it, the database stamping who last changed the row and when (sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on). FRS-216.4 My Profile shall show the role in effect, whether its permissions are stored or the built-in fallback, any personal extra permissions, and the actions and pages they grant, and shall say when an administrator is previewing another person. FRS-216.5 My Profile shall present its sections as tabs, one per section — Account, Details & R&R, Training, My Team (only where somebody reports to the person), What I can do, Signature, Password and Appearance — remembering the tab last opened on that device and opening Account when the remembered tab is not offered. FRS-216.6 My Team shall list the people reporting to the person in two groups by their User Master status (Active): Active / Current and Ex Employees, each with its count, the tab counting the current ones, and an ex employee’s profile, R&R and training remaining viewable. RATIONALE: .4 because a person told they cannot do something needs to see whether the role or the fallback is the reason, and the wrong answer there sends an administrator to tick the wrong box.

### URS-172 — A stock hand-over and a stock return print as the stores records they are

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A stock transfer shall print as the MATERIAL TRANSFER NOTE (R/SER/STR/003) and a material return as the MATERIAL RETURN NOTE (R/SER/STR/002), laid out as the paper records with their record block, from what the system already holds — the engineers' names with their place from the User Master, the parts and quantities, the transfer or return number and date — and with the name the system knows in each signature box it can fill and the others left to be signed by hand. A transfer shall take a reason for each part as well as one common remark, the part's own reason printing where one was given. A stored signature shall be reproduced only in a box naming the person printing.

**FRS-110.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-110.1 A report shall be editable from its table row or from Edit / weekly review on the desk, and both shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage; the database (ffr_update) shall refuse anybody else. FRS-110.5 The live call shall be shown beside each report, marked — withdrawn where the review no longer answers YES. FRS-110.6 ffr_read shall give a holder of ffr.view the whole register, and anybody else the reports on calls they may see or reports they raised (0165, 0176). **FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. **FRS-170.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-170.1 The 🔐 Access drawer shall let an administrator set a person's role and tick individual permissions, held in `profiles.extra_permissions` and honoured by `has_perm()` on top of the role; the database shall accept the write only from an administrator.
