FRS-170.6 The User Master shall count the people whose sign-in role differs from the directory, show “X (now Y)” against each, and offer to apply the directory's role, writing each person separately, naming each failure and auditing each change. RATIONALE: .2 because an individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, and authority not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews. .6 one person at a time so that one failure does not leave the office unsure which of forty changes happened.

**FRS-203.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-203.1 Roles & Permissions shall allow change to a holder of rbac.manage, display the matrix read-only to a holder of admin.view, and state to anyone else that they lack permission. FRS-203.2 Roles & Permissions shall display the permissions stored for each role and shall not re-seed the matrix over an edit in progress. FRS-203.3 Roles & Permissions shall group pages by menu heading, then page, then action, each level expandable, with controls expanding and collapsing every level. FRS-203.4 Roles & Permissions shall grant the right to open a page (View) and each action on it separately per role, and shall provide a control granting or removing every right on one page for one role. FRS-203.5 Roles & Permissions shall display the administrator role holding every permission, and shall not allow it to be narrowed. FRS-203.6 Roles & Permissions shall, on Save, write only the roles the operator changed, re-assert the administrator’s full set where it has fallen behind, and state "Nothing was changed" when nothing was. FRS-203.7 Roles & Permissions shall refuse to save a role left with no permission (URS-056). FRS-203.8 The system shall record each saved change with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when (D-067). FRS-203.9 Roles & Permissions shall export the matrix as .xlsx — a Matrix sheet (group, page, route, grant, key, Yes / No per role), a Roles sheet (permissions held, stored or NOT CONFIGURED fallback) and a How to read this sheet (who, when, saved or UNSAVED) — recorded as rbac.export and available to rbac.manage and admin.view. FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.11 Each page's row shall list every key its controls test, including a key of another module used on that page, so a control is governed by a tick shown where the control is (findings 63 and 64). FRS-203.12 The Installation Call and PM Call registers, the Contract Register, the Objective page, chart sharing, validation results, shared table layouts, the Product Database 2.0 rebuild, deleting a Tracker item and returning stock in another engineer's name shall each be governed by keys of their own, and each screen shall ask the key the database asks. FRS-203.13 A key may have parent keys; holding a parent shall grant its children in the database and in the application alike, from one list held in both (public.perm_parents, PERM_PARENTS), and the matrix shall show a child held through its parent as held; unticking it shall untick the parent and tick the parent's other children in their own right, so the role loses only that child (the user, 2026-10-02: “All Greyed out Permissions should be editable”). Manage users, Edit masters, Edit sales / warranties, Edit contracts and each register's Edit and Report keys shall be parents of their parts (finding 67). FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). FRS-203.15 A new per-page key shall be granted once to exactly the roles and people holding the key it replaces, and a re-run shall not restore a key an administrator has since removed. RATIONALE: .6 because permsForRole() returns the STORED set whenever it is non-empty, so a save that rewrote every role would replace an administrator’s tuning with whatever the screen held; .8 because rbac.save records only the role keys, and app_roles is not one of the ten tables record_audit covers — today nothing can say what a role could do on a given day.

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-212.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-212.1 An administrator shall be able to choose any profile (searchable, the first 60 shown) and see the application with that person’s permissions until Exit, the choice surviving a reload, with a banner throughout. FRS-212.2 While previewing, the application shall refuse every write — insert, update, delete, a function call that writes, a file upload — stating that a preview is read-only (D-069). FRS-212.3 The system shall record each start and end of a preview with the administrator and the person previewed (D-069). FRS-212.4 A screen that narrows its rows to the previewed person (Hand Stock, Stock Transfer, MRN, Spare Requests) shall do so by that person’s name and address. RATIONALE: .2 — the component’s own comment says "Nothing is written — a read-only preview" and nothing enforces it; a write made during a preview runs under the administrator’s session while the screen shows another person, so the record is attributed to the administrator and believed to be the other person’s.

**FRS-213.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-213.1 The menu shall show an entry exactly when the route guard would open its page for that person. FRS-213.2 The route guard shall state, for a known screen the person may not open, that they lack access and whom to ask, and shall send an unknown address to the Dashboard. FRS-213.3 The address /users shall open the User Master. FRS-213.4 The printable routes (/dc/, /declaration/, /ffr/, /indoor-pdt/, /indoor-register/, /indoor-dc/, /mtn/, /mrn-print/) shall render without the menu, their rows bounded by row-level security; /ffr/ shall require the Field Failure Register's module key, the three indoor routes the Indoor Service Register's, /mtn/ the Stock Transfer screen's and /mrn-print/ the Material Returns screen's. FRS-213.5 A screen that fails to render shall show an error in its own place, the menu and header remaining. FRS-213.6 While a saved session is restored the application shall show Loading rather than the sign-in screen. FRS-213.7 The menu shall be grouped, each group and the whole menu collapsible, the sidebar collapsible to icons and remembered per device, and shown as a drawer on a narrow screen; the Knowledge Base heading shall flash until a page in it has been opened on the device. FRS-213.8 The header search shall list the screens the person may open, and from three characters the records they may open (FRS-218); Enter shall open the highlighted entry, the first by default. FRS-213.9 The header shall show a breadcrumb (group · screen), the person’s name and designation, "Permission · <role>", and a menu offering My Profile, Clear Cache and Update, and Sign out. FRS-213.10 A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be able to switch between team calls and own calls, the choice remembered. FRS-213.11 The counts beside menu entries shall carry "+" where they are taken from a partial read. FRS-213.12 The update banner shall check version.json when the tab gains focus and every 5 minutes, name the new version only where it differs from the running one and otherwise say the running build is older, and Update now shall clear the screen caches, keep the offline registers and reload. FRS-213.13 Clear Cache and Update shall clear the screen and dropdown caches, the browser caches and service workers, and reload, keeping the offline registers. FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. RATIONALE: .1 because an entry shown on admin.view for a page that asks its own key is a menu that offers what the page then refuses; .12 because a banner that announces the version already running teaches people to dismiss it.

**FRS-003.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each role maps to a permission set (app_roles). Data visibility is scoped by a reporting tree resolved from User Master; enforced in the client and, authoritatively, by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.

**FRS-004.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every read/write is governed by RLS policies keyed on the authenticated user (auth.uid()) and SECURITY DEFINER helper functions; the UI gate is secondary.

**FRS-014.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock, transfers and returns are scoped to the reporting tree at the database, so a user sees only their own and their team’s stock.

**FRS-050.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every view over a table carrying row-level security is created `security_invoker`, so the policies are evaluated for the READER. `create or replace view` does not carry the setting over, and a view running as its owner returns everything with no error and no warning. `npm run check:views` fails on any view over an RLS-protected table that lacks it, and `_status.sql` reports it on a live project; views intentionally readable by every signed-in user are enumerated with their reason.

### URS-010 — Master data

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Party, product, part and user master data, and configurable value lists, shall be maintained under control.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-155** — The Declaration | High | OQ-147 |
| **FRS-177** — Adding and editing a part | Medium | OQ-170 |
| **FRS-180** — Adding to, withdrawing from and deleting from a value list | Medium | OQ-173 |
| **FRS-182** — The install base and the catalogue are read here, and a call starts from a machine | Medium | OQ-244, OQ-175 |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-201** — The legacy importer on Admin Config | High | OQ-194 |
| **FRS-015** — Master maintenance | Medium | OQ-26 |

**FRS-155.** *(v0.10.73 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-155.1 The Declaration shall find a stock out by the rule of FRS-154.1 and FRS-154.2. FRS-155.2 The Declaration shall list each part once, the quantities of the same part on several lines summed. FRS-155.3 The Declaration shall take, before printing and without printing them, To, Address, City, State, Contact No, Approximate value (Rs.), Purpose and Sent by; To, Address and Approximate value are mandatory. FRS-155.4 The Declaration shall pre-fill the address from the engineer's User Master row and the courier from the stock out. FRS-155.5 The Declaration shall name, above the sheet, each mandatory field still empty ("Still to fill in: ..."). FRS-155.6 The Declaration shall offer "Save to the User Master as <engineer>'s address" when the address has been edited, and shall write only the address, city, state and telephone of that engineer's row. FRS-155.7 The database shall refuse that write without `spare.dispatch` and shall refuse, to anybody but an administrator, a change to any other column of the User Master (`user_directory_address_guard`, 0030). FRS-155.8 The printed sheet shall carry the company mark, the form title, the date, the SO No, the GST No, the area code, the declaration text with the purpose and value, and the statement that no transaction is involved. FRS-155.9 The grid shall carry SNO, part number, description and quantity with totals, 18 rows per sheet, with the heading and the sender block on every sheet and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-155.10 The recipient block shall carry the courier line and the recipient's name and address; the sender block shall carry no signature image, and shall name the person who booked the stock out (spare_dispatches.dispatched_by, stamped from the session by 0211) under the department -- never a fixed name; where an old stock out recorded nobody, the name is left blank and the page says so (D-155). FRS-155.11 The page shall offer Back to dispatch, Challan and Print, and the error states of FRS-154.11. RATIONALE: .5 warns and does not block, because the declaration is sometimes completed by hand at the packing bench; whether an incomplete declaration may be printed at all is the owner's decision and is recorded here as open. .7 is what makes .6 safe: the page can change an address and nothing else, and only for somebody who packs parcels.

**FRS-177.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-177.1 ＋ Add part shall be offered to holders of masters.edit only, and the database shall refuse a write to `parts` from anybody else. FRS-177.2 The code shall be converted to upper case and refused if empty, if it contains “|”, or if it does not begin with a letter or digit followed only by letters, digits and - _ . /. FRS-177.3 A description shall be required. FRS-177.4 Spare or Consumable shall be required on a new part. FRS-177.5 The product(s) the part fits, or “Common to all products”, shall be required on a new part, Common being stored as no product. FRS-177.6 A purchase cost shall be a number where entered, and a blank shall be stored as not recorded, never as 0. FRS-177.7 A code that already exists shall be refused. FRS-177.8 The form shall show the part as it will be listed, CODE|Description. FRS-177.9 Editing a part shall allow its category, products and cost to change, shall keep a category the Item Master file brought even where it is not one of those offered, and shall allow an older part with those fields blank to be saved. FRS-177.10 A part shall be deactivated or reactivated after confirmation, and shall never be deleted. RATIONALE: .2 because “|” separates the code from the description in the identity every stock table carries. .6 because 0 is a price and “not recorded” is not one.

**FRS-180.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-180.1 An entry shall be added only by a holder of `master.<list>.add` (or its parents `master.<list>.edit`, `masters.edit.records`, `masters.edit`), the database refusing anybody else (0067, 0325; corrected 2026-10-03). FRS-180.2 A value already in the list shall be refused with “already in this list”. FRS-180.3 An entry's Added On shall be the day it was added, and its author shall be recorded by the database from the session (`sys_created_by`, 0244); the Added By shown is a label. FRS-180.4 An entry shall be deactivated or reactivated after a confirmation stating that it stays on the records carrying it and stops being offered. FRS-180.5 🗑 Delete shall be offered only to a holder of `master.<list>.delete`. FRS-180.6 The database shall refuse the deletion of a value that any record carries, and shall say to deactivate it instead. FRS-180.7 Without the right to edit a list, the screen shall name the permission needed. FRS-180.8 ↻ Refresh on a list shall clear that list's dropdown cache, so forms offer the change without a reload; ↻ Refresh all shall clear every one. FRS-180.9 Where the registry of lists (`master_lists`) is absent, the built-in lists shall be used and the screen shall say which bundle to run. FRS-180.10 All Masters shall list the four registers with a row count each, and every value list with its entry count, whether it Loaded, is Empty or failed, and where it is used; a list may be opened in place or on its own page, and an unknown list address shall return to the overview. RATIONALE: .6 in the database because every count and filter downstream matches the stored value, and a deleted value leaves records carrying a word no list holds. Today a hard DELETE is offered with no such check and nothing in the database refuses it (D-056). FRS-180.11 An entry shall be added through an Add entry form opened by a button, naming each field and marking the required ones, and refusing an empty value; on the DCCR Complaint Grouping and Root Cause Key Word lists the Product shall be required and picked from the Product Master, or COMM for every product.

**FRS-182.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-182.1 The Product Database shall have no path that writes a machine. FRS-182.2 It shall filter by party, product, serial and status, the status being the derived cover status rather than a stored one. FRS-182.3 A search that times out shall say how to narrow it and keep the database's message. FRS-182.4 “+ Field” shall be offered on a machine only to holders of calls.create, and “+ Install” only to holders of install.create; each shall open its call form filled with the machine's customer, product, serial and cover. FRS-182.5 The database shall refuse an installation call from anybody without install.create, whatever screen it was started from (FRS-008). FRS-182.6 The Product Master shall list every product line — code, name, type, category, short form, still sold, added on, added by — with All / Active / Inactive counts that are exact, shall be searchable, and shall have no path that writes a line other than its Imported column (FRS-227). FRS-182.7 It shall state that an Inactive line takes no new Sale Entry and still takes contracts, calls, visits, spares and feedback, and where it is empty shall point to Bulk Uploads and name the permission needed. FRS-182.8 The Sale Entry's product picker shall offer only Active lines, pair code and name where the catalogue gives one answer, count the retired lines it does not offer and say why, and accept a product the catalogue does not hold. FRS-182.9 No signed-in user shall delete a machine through the API: adding and editing stay with masters.edit.records, and a machine is removed only from the SQL editor (D-139). RATIONALE: .8 is guidance and not a control, and is stated as such: a trigger refusing a retired line would also refuse the historical sales import, in which 30 of 53 lines are retired and the sales really happened, and a catalogue kept by hand may lack a real line. `product_line_sellable()` (0193) holds the same rule in SQL. .4 is open for “+ Install”, offered today to calls.create (D-063).

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.

**FRS-015.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Party/Product/Part/User masters and value lists are editable by authorised roles; edits are gated by masters.edit, or per value list by master.<list>.edit / master.<list>.delete, enforced by row-level security. Every row records the login that created and last changed it (sys columns, 0244). A value in use SHALL be deactivated rather than deleted, and the database SHALL refuse the deletion of a value any record carries (FRS-180.6; OPEN until D-056 is fixed). A part is never deleted (FRS-177.10); a party's name is not changed by editing (FRS-173).

### URS-079 — Roles, responsibilities and training are recorded per person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each person shall have a record of the Roles & Responsibilities document in force for them, with the period it applies to; a new one shall end the previous one without deleting it. When a controlled QMS document is issued, the people who must be trained on it shall be chosen and the training assigned to each. Training shall be recorded as sessions with the attendees, the trainer, the method, any assessment result and the attendance evidence, or as the person's own acknowledgement of having read the document; a failed assessment shall keep the training open. A person's profile shall list every past training they received, and shall be visible to the person, their managers and those responsible for users and training only.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-172** — A person with a history is not removed from the User Master | High | OQ-165 |
| **FRS-190** — Cancelling, Overdue, and amending a training record | High | OQ-183 |
| **FRS-216** — My Profile: the account, the R&R period, and what I can do | Medium | OQ-214, OQ-209 |
| **FRS-093** — Profile, R&R periods and training, bounded by one visibility rule | High | OQ-81 |

**FRS-172.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-172.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a User Master row that has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities period, a training assignment or a training attendance, and the refusal shall say to mark the person inactive instead. FRS-172.2 No deletion of a User Master row shall remove a `user_profile` or `user_rr` row by cascade. FRS-172.3 The User Master shall offer 🗑 Delete only on a row with no such history — a duplicate or a mistaken entry — and only after a confirmation. FRS-172.4 Every deletion shall be written to the audit trail with the name removed. RATIONALE: 0264 declares `user_profile` and `user_rr` ON DELETE CASCADE and the two training tables not, so today a person with training cannot be deleted while a person with only an R&R history is deleted together with it — the one record URS-079 says must be ended without being deleted, and FRS-093 says is not deletable (D-059).

**FRS-190.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-190.1 An open assignment shall be cancelled only by a holder of training.manage, with a reason, the database refusing anybody else (`tg_update`); a cancelled assignment shall read Cancelled and keep its reason. FRS-190.2 An assignment not completed and past its due date shall read Overdue (`training_status`, 0264). FRS-190.3 Assigning a document or topic to an audience shall skip anybody already assigned it and report how many were created. FRS-190.4 Re-saving a session shall record, for each attendance, assessment result, score or remark it changes, the previous value, who changed it and when, in a history no user can edit or delete. FRS-190.5 Changing a Roles & Responsibilities period's From or To shall be recorded the same way. FRS-190.6 The Sessions list shall be readable by every signed-in user (`ts_read`); a person's attendance and assessment only through `may_see_person()`. FRS-190.7 The assignments shall be searchable and counted by status with exact counts; where nothing is visible the screen shall say “No training assigned that you may see”, and a load failure shall name the bundle to run. RATIONALE: .4 and .5 because a Pass that was a Fail, or a period that moved, cannot be told from one recorded correctly once the edit leaves no trace; today both are overwritten in place and neither table is audited by `record_audit` (D-062).

**FRS-216.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-216.1 My Profile shall show the account: name, e-mail, designation, Permission (the role) and region. FRS-216.2 My Profile shall state, where the person’s profile did not load, that it did not and what they may do until it exists (FRS-210.5). FRS-216.3 A holder of users.manage or training.manage shall be able to change the period of a recorded R&R document, From remaining required and To not before it, the database stamping who last changed the row and when (sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on). FRS-216.4 My Profile shall show the role in effect, whether its permissions are stored or the built-in fallback, any personal extra permissions, and the actions and pages they grant, and shall say when an administrator is previewing another person. FRS-216.5 My Profile shall present its sections as tabs, one per section — Account, Details & R&R, Training, My Team (only where somebody reports to the person), What I can do, Signature, Password and Appearance — remembering the tab last opened on that device and opening Account when the remembered tab is not offered. FRS-216.6 My Team shall list the people reporting to the person in two groups by their User Master status (Active): Active / Current and Ex Employees, each with its count, the tab counting the current ones, and an ex employee’s profile, R&R and training remaining viewable. RATIONALE: .4 because a person told they cannot do something needs to see whether the role or the fallback is the reason, and the wrong answer there sends an administrator to tick the wrong box.

**FRS-093.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* 0264: `user_profile` (employee code, joining date), `user_rr` (a trigger closes the previous open period the day before the new From), `training_sessions` + `training_attendance` (bulk, Pass/Fail, score, attachments) and `training_assignments` (one per person per document). `training_status` derives Completed = attended without a Fail OR acknowledged with no Fail recorded; Overdue = open past its due date; Cancelled = cancelled by training.manage with its reason kept. Every per-person row is read through `may_see_person()`: the person, their reporting tree, users.manage, training.manage; the Sessions list is readable by every signed-in user. The trainee acknowledges only their own assignment through `acknowledge_training()`. No row SHALL be deleted, by the application or by a cascade from the User Master (FRS-172; OPEN until D-059 is fixed), and an amendment to attendance, assessment or an R&R period SHALL keep the value it replaced, the author and the time (FRS-190; record_audit keeps both images since 0314, D-062). Proved in part by `people_training_test`.

## Part Master `/parts`

Opened by `mod:/parts`.

### URS-118 — A spare request says what is asked for, for which call or which stock, and is numbered by the system

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let an engineer, or a manager for an engineer in their team, request spare parts either against a call or to replenish the engineer's own hand stock (a HandStock request), and a HandStock request shall state why it is needed. A request against a call shall carry the customer, product, serial, complaint and cover that the call records, copied from the call rather than typed again, and a request raised from within a call shall not be movable to a different call. Each part shall be chosen from the Part Master and never typed, offered first from the parts that fit the call's product with the whole master available on request, and asked for in a whole quantity of at least one. The request number and its date shall be assigned by the system. Re-keying what a call already records is where the request and the call stop describing the same machine, and a part typed freehand is a part no stock figure will ever find.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-146** — Raising a spare request | High | OQ-242, OQ-138 |
| **FRS-247** — A spare request on a call with no visit files the visit it implies | High | OQ-239 |

**FRS-146.** *(v0.10.72 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-146.1 The Spare Requests screen shall offer the New Spare Request action only to a holder of `spare.request`. FRS-146.2 The request form shall offer two request types, Call Based and HandStock. FRS-146.3 The request form shall require a HandStock reason for a HandStock request and shall refuse the submission with "Enter the reason for the HandStock request." where it is empty. FRS-146.4 The request form shall find the call of a Call Based request by its UCN, call number, party or serial once three characters are typed, and shall offer at most 25 calls. FRS-146.5 The request form shall copy the party, product, serial, complaint and item status (cover) of the chosen call onto the request and shall not offer them for editing. FRS-146.6 The request form shall fix the call, and offer no "Change call", when it is opened from a call. FRS-146.7 The request form shall offer as parts only Part Master entries, chosen from a pick list that takes no free text, and shall state why the list is disabled while the master is empty or still loading. FRS-146.8 The request form shall offer, for a Call Based request, the parts mapped to the call's product, its accessories and the common parts, with a "Show all parts" option offering the whole Part Master; it shall offer the whole Part Master to a HandStock request. FRS-146.9 The request form shall accept a quantity per part as a whole number of at least one, and shall treat a blank or lower value as one. FRS-146.10 The request form shall accept at most 20 spare rows on one request. FRS-146.11 The request form shall accept optional additional remarks. FRS-146.12 The request form shall refuse a submission with no spare ("Add at least one spare."), with no engineer, or of a Call Based request with no UCN ("A Call-Based request needs a call (UC Number)."). FRS-146.13 The database shall assign the OR number (OR-YYMM-NNNN, restarting each month) and the OR request date on insert; the form shall show "OR No assigned on submit" and shall not accept either. FRS-146.14 The request form shall generate the request reference WA-yyyymmdd-xxxx when it opens; the reference is the request's primary key, so a colliding reference is refused by the database and never merged into another request. FRS-146.15 The request form shall disable Submit, and say why, while the database is not connected. FRS-146.16 On success the screen shall name the OR number and the reference, reload the register and write an audit entry `spare.request`. FRS-146.17 Once the RM has decided a line, its part and quantity shall not be changed by anybody, the requester included, except by a part rename; Item Status shall be taken from the call when the request is raised and change afterwards only to the call’s own value, and the request type shall not change (0340, D-121, D-122). RATIONALE: .5 because the request is read downstream (cover-based routing under FRS-147.8, the unused-spare report) through the call's own identity, and a re-typed serial is where the two stop agreeing. .14 records that the reference is made in the browser: that is acceptable only because the database key refuses a duplicate rather than overwriting.

**FRS-247.** *(v0.10.67 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-247.1 When a Call Based spare request and its lines have saved, the Spare Request form shall ask the database to file a visit for the request's call (`file_visit_for_spare_request`, 0333). FRS-247.2 The database shall file that visit only where the call has no visit at all, and shall file nothing for a HandStock request or a UCN that is not a call. FRS-247.3 The visit shall read Call Status Unsolved, the requesting engineer, the request's date (India) as the visit date, the Call Pending Reason master entry meaning spare not available (matched on its letters, so SPARE / SPARES and NOT AVAILABLE / UNAVAILABLE all qualify; SPARES NOT AVAILABLE where the master holds none), Update Visit Work Details? = No, and the OR number as Spare Request; the call shall then read Unsolved. FRS-247.4 A second request on the same call, or a retry, shall file nothing more. FRS-247.5 Only the person who raised the request, holding spare.request, may call it; the public key may not. FRS-247.6 Where the visit cannot be filed, the screen shall say the request was submitted but its visit entry was not added, naming the error. RATIONALE: .1 calls it after the lines rather than from a trigger on the request, because a request whose lines fail stays behind (D-044) and must not turn its call Unsolved, and because the bulk import of request history must not file visits for past requests.

### URS-125 — The documents that travel with a stock out are complete and can be produced again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

For every stock out the system shall produce a Delivery Challan and a Declaration on the company's controlled layout, listing exactly what that stock out carried, and shall produce them again on request for any stock out the reader may see, however old it is. The challan shall carry the stock-out and reference numbers and dates, the recipient, the courier, each part and quantity with the total, and the company's statutory identifiers, on sheets each complete in itself; a signature shall appear on it only as URS-057 allows. The Declaration shall state the recipient's address, the parcel's approximate value and its purpose, and each part once with its total quantity, and shall name what is still missing before it is printed. Correcting the engineer's address from the Declaration may update the User Master only for somebody authorised to dispatch, and only the address. A challan that can no longer be found is a shipment whose paperwork cannot be reproduced.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-154** — The Delivery Challan | High | OQ-146 |
| **FRS-155** — The Declaration | High | OQ-147 |

**FRS-154.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-154.1 The Delivery Challan shall be opened by stock-out number from Stock Out, from Pending Dispatch and after booking; the page sits outside the module guard and shows a stock out only where the reader's row-level access admits it. FRS-154.2 The Delivery Challan shall find any stock out the reader may see, however many have been booked since it. FRS-154.3 The Delivery Challan shall print the quantity sent on THIS stock out for each line (`spare_dispatch_lines`), ordered by spare ID. FRS-154.4 Each sheet shall carry the company mark (`COMPANY_LOGO`), the company's name, address, telephone and e-mail, and the title DELIVERY CHALLAN. FRS-154.5 Each sheet shall carry the recipient engineer, the courier, the Stock Out No., the Stock Out Date, the Ref No. and the Ref Date. FRS-154.6 The grid shall carry Sr.No, Order No., Item Code, Description and Qty; the last sheet shall carry the total and every other sheet "Continued on sheet N". FRS-154.7 The challan shall be cut into A4 sheets of 20 rows, each with its own letterhead and signature block and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-154.8 The challan shall carry the dispatch remarks and the company's GSTIN, CIN and PAN. FRS-154.9 The company signature block shall carry the printer's saved signature only where the printer booked the stock out, and the customer block shall always be blank (FRS-067). FRS-154.10 The page shall offer Print, Declaration and Back to dispatch, and state the number of sheets. FRS-154.11 The page shall state, in place of the challan, that the database is not connected, that the stock out was not found or cannot be viewed, or the read error verbatim. RATIONALE: .1 is deliberate — the engineer receiving the parcel and Commercial chasing it are legitimate readers who hold neither dispatch module — and is for RA/QA to confirm. .2 is the requirement the page does not meet: it searches the 500 most recent stock outs, so an older one reads as "not found" (D-045).

**FRS-155.** *(v0.10.73 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-155.1 The Declaration shall find a stock out by the rule of FRS-154.1 and FRS-154.2. FRS-155.2 The Declaration shall list each part once, the quantities of the same part on several lines summed. FRS-155.3 The Declaration shall take, before printing and without printing them, To, Address, City, State, Contact No, Approximate value (Rs.), Purpose and Sent by; To, Address and Approximate value are mandatory. FRS-155.4 The Declaration shall pre-fill the address from the engineer's User Master row and the courier from the stock out. FRS-155.5 The Declaration shall name, above the sheet, each mandatory field still empty ("Still to fill in: ..."). FRS-155.6 The Declaration shall offer "Save to the User Master as <engineer>'s address" when the address has been edited, and shall write only the address, city, state and telephone of that engineer's row. FRS-155.7 The database shall refuse that write without `spare.dispatch` and shall refuse, to anybody but an administrator, a change to any other column of the User Master (`user_directory_address_guard`, 0030). FRS-155.8 The printed sheet shall carry the company mark, the form title, the date, the SO No, the GST No, the area code, the declaration text with the purpose and value, and the statement that no transaction is involved. FRS-155.9 The grid shall carry SNO, part number, description and quantity with totals, 18 rows per sheet, with the heading and the sender block on every sheet and "Sheet X of Y". FRS-155.10 The recipient block shall carry the courier line and the recipient's name and address; the sender block shall carry no signature image, and shall name the person who booked the stock out (spare_dispatches.dispatched_by, stamped from the session by 0211) under the department -- never a fixed name; where an old stock out recorded nobody, the name is left blank and the page says so (D-155). FRS-155.11 The page shall offer Back to dispatch, Challan and Print, and the error states of FRS-154.11. RATIONALE: .5 warns and does not block, because the declaration is sometimes completed by hand at the packing bench; whether an incomplete declaration may be printed at all is the owner's decision and is recorded here as open. .7 is what makes .6 safe: the page can change an address and nothing else, and only for somebody who packs parcels.

### URS-127 — An engineer's hand stock can be read down to the movements that make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A user shall be able to read, for each engineer and part they may see, the stock in hand and every term it is made of — opening balance, migrated history, stock out, consumption, transfers in and out, returns and office adjustments — such that the terms shown add up to the figure shown; and to open the movements behind any figure, every one of them or a statement that the list is incomplete. A balance below zero shall be shown and explained as a finding rather than hidden. The whole register shall be searchable, not only the part already read. A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's stock with the person. A drill-down whose arithmetic does not add up teaches its reader to stop checking.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-159** — Reading hand stock, and the movements behind it | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-151, OQ-158 |
| **FRS-160** — The Hand Stock Report says what its file holds | Medium | OQ-260, OQ-152 |

**FRS-159.** *(v0.10.150 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-159.1 Hand Stock shall show one line per engineer and part with Opening, From history, Stock out, Consumed, Transfer in, Transfer out, Returned, Stock level and Last movement, read from `handstock_balance` (security_invoker). FRS-159.2 A line's drawer shall show an arithmetic line whose terms are every component of the level, including the opening balance, the migrated history and any stock adjustment (0266), and whose result is the level shown. FRS-159.3 Hand Stock shall offer In hand (the default), Short (below zero), Settled (zero) and All, each with its exact count once the balance is loaded ("+" only while a restored device cache cut at its cap is shown, which also offers a reload). FRS-159.4 The drawer shall explain a level below zero as more consumed or handed on than was issued, and Hand Stock Report shall show a negative On Hand inverted. FRS-159.5 Hand Stock shall offer an engineer list of every active engineer on the reader's team with their total in hand, plus anybody holding stock who is not in the directory. FRS-159.6 Hand Stock shall read the whole balance in ONE request (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384 — security invoker, so the reader's own visibility applies) and search it on the device (engineer, part, code; two characters or more), replacing the list with the matches and stating "searching the whole register — N matches" with an exact N (v0.10.116: the balance was paged a thousand at a time and every search keystroke was a further full aggregate in the database). FRS-159.7 The drawer shall list every movement behind the line — stock out, consumed, received, returned, handed over, with reference, date, UCN, party and remarks — or state that the list stops at its limit. FRS-159.8 The Movements tab shall list the ledger newest first in pages of 1,000, filter by engineer in the database, offer a chip per movement kind with counts, and colour a quantity by its sign. FRS-159.9 Hand Stock shall offer Transfer stock, and Transfer this spare on a line above zero, to a holder of `stock.transfer`, opening Stock Transfer. FRS-159.10 The History included / History ignored switch (FRS-043) shall be remembered in the browser. FRS-159.11 Hand Stock opened from My Workload's Short card shall open on Short. FRS-159.12 A User Master rename shall carry the engineer's name on spare requests, dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, MRNs and transfers, so the balance is one balance under the new name (0259–0262). RATIONALE: .3 and .4 replace URS-024's old claim that a balance cannot go negative: a consumption line cannot exceed the balance when it is written (FRS-030), but a level can stand below zero where migrated history or an issue never recorded says so, and FRS-044 keeps such a figure exactly — so the register shows it as a finding. FRS-159.13 (2026-10-08) A line's movements shall be shown as a table -- number, date and time, movement, In, Out, the balance after each (from the opening balance, oldest first; left out when the trail is cut at its cap), reference, UCN, party and remarks -- and shall be downloadable as Excel (a movements sheet with real dates, and a stock level sheet) and as CSV, each saying whether it holds every movement.

**FRS-160.** *(v0.10.116 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-160.1 Hand Stock Report shall be an administrator's screen by default and grantable to any role (`admin: true`). FRS-160.2 A download taken while a search is applied shall say so in the file: the .xlsx and .xls on their About sheet, the .csv in its file name. FRS-160.3 Refresh shall restart the load, and a result still arriving from the earlier load shall be discarded (run token); the load is ONE request for the whole balance (`handstock_balance_all()`, 0384), complete the moment it lands. FRS-160.4 The subtitle, the file scope and the empty message shall say "every engineer" or "your own stock, and your team's" by `seesEveryRecord`. FRS-160.5 A failed load shall name the missing views and the bundle to run, a missing grant, or the error verbatim. RATIONALE: .2 because a .csv can carry no second sheet, so a searched file is otherwise indistinguishable from the whole register — the silent partial file URS-077 exists to prevent (D-047).

### URS-132 — A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-166** — A rename carries the team, and only an administrator makes one | High | OQ-159 |
| **FRS-167** — A rename carries the records filed under the name, and not the signatures on them | High | OQ-160 |

**FRS-166.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`.

**FRS-167.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-167.1 When a User Master name changes, 0259 shall rewrite the old name to the new, in the same transaction, in: `allocated_to` on field, installation and PM calls; `engineer` on call requests, pending registrations, spare requests, spare dispatches, spare consumption, consumption history, opening stock, spare issue history and material returns; `from_engineer` and `to_engineer` on stock transfers; and `service_engineer` on parties and products. FRS-167.2 Each column shall be matched as its own read policy matches it, lower(btrim()) on both sides. FRS-167.3 It shall not rewrite rm_by, commercial_by, nsm_by, dispatched_by, received_by, recorded_by, the engineer on a visit report or a feedback, the engineer on a sale, or `spare_request_engineer_log`. FRS-167.4 It shall move nothing under the limits of FRS-166.3 to .5, the case-only test being made on lower(btrim()). FRS-167.5 The guards that refuse a change of engineer — the frozen answered call request (0260), the consumption line and the dispatched spare request (0261) — shall admit exactly this change, recognised by a ticket only the rename trigger can write (`engineer_rename_ticket`: row-level security on, no policy, no grants), and shall refuse every other change they refused before. FRS-167.6 A call moved by a rename shall not send “Call allotted to you” (0262). FRS-167.7 Each table shall be updated only where it exists, so a project lacking a module still renames what it has. RATIONALE: .3 because those columns record who DID something; rewriting them would sign a record in a name the person was not using when they signed it. .5 uses a ticket rather than a session flag because `set_config` is callable by anybody who can update a row (D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_records_test.sql`.

### URS-135 — A person's record is complete, agrees with the reporting tree, and is never destroyed

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The User Master shall require a name for every person, it being what calls are allotted to, and shall record every field it offers, including the Department from which training audiences are drawn. A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be a name held by a person on the User Master, and a name matching nobody shall be stated as such before it is saved, because the reporting tree is built from those names and a misspelling empties a team without any error. The directory's Active flag shall be labelled as what it does, and kept apart from whether the person's login may sign in. A person who has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities history or a training record shall not be removed from the User Master; they shall be marked inactive instead. An administrator shall be able to see what a person has entered, for a handover.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-171** — What a User Master row records, and what its fields say they do | Medium | OQ-164 |
| **FRS-172** — A person with a history is not removed from the User Master | High | OQ-165 |

**FRS-171.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-171.1 The User Master shall refuse to save a row without a name. FRS-171.2 It shall write every field its form offers, the Department included (0263). FRS-171.3 The Department shall be chosen from the Department value list. FRS-171.4 The Reporting Manager and Regional Manager fields shall suggest the names on the User Master, and a name that matches no row shall be stated as such before saving and saved only on confirmation. FRS-171.5 The directory Active field shall be labelled as the directory flag it is; the login's own Disable / Enable shall be the only control described as deciding sign-in. FRS-171.6 Editing the whole table shall write each changed row separately, name every row that failed and keep its draft, mark changed rows “Edited”, save on Enter and ask before discarding on Esc. FRS-171.7 The 📊 Data drawer shall list, for a holder of users.manage, the calls, spare requests, approvals, dispatches, visit reports and consumption matching the person's name or email, within what the reader may see. FRS-171.8 Without a database connection the User Master shall show the sheet directory read-only. RATIONALE: .2 because training audiences are drawn by Department, and a Department chosen and not saved removes the person from every audience that names it. .4 because the reporting tree is built from these names; 0212 and 0257 record what a name matching nobody does. .5 because “Yes — may sign in” on a flag that governs no sign-in tells an administrator a leaver is locked out when they are not. All three are open (D-053).

**FRS-172.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-172.1 The database shall refuse the deletion of a User Master row that has a profile, a Roles & Responsibilities period, a training assignment or a training attendance, and the refusal shall say to mark the person inactive instead. FRS-172.2 No deletion of a User Master row shall remove a `user_profile` or `user_rr` row by cascade. FRS-172.3 The User Master shall offer 🗑 Delete only on a row with no such history — a duplicate or a mistaken entry — and only after a confirmation. FRS-172.4 Every deletion shall be written to the audit trail with the name removed. RATIONALE: 0264 declares `user_profile` and `user_rr` ON DELETE CASCADE and the two training tables not, so today a person with training cannot be deleted while a person with only an R&R history is deleted together with it — the one record URS-079 says must be ended without being deleted, and FRS-093 says is not deletable (D-059).

### URS-136 — A customer is known by one name, and the person who looks after them is a real person

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master shall let an authorised user add a customer, giving at least its name, city and state, and shall refuse a name it already holds. It shall let an authorised user maintain a customer's type, profile, Serviceman, route, installation and billing addresses and contacts, and KYC details. It shall NOT allow the customer's name to be changed by editing, on the screen or through the data interface, because every machine, call and contract names the customer by that text and has no other link to it; a change of name shall be made only by a function that carries every record naming it. The Serviceman shall be a person on the User Master, because a new call is allotted to that name. Correcting a Serviceman's spelling across every customer carrying it shall be one act that changes all or none, shall say beforehand how many customers it will change, and shall offer only User Master names or nobody. Marking a customer's KYC Verified shall be attributed by the system to the person who did it, shall not be re-attributable by anybody else, and shall be cleared when the customer is no longer verified.

FRS-240.5 A name already on the register, ignoring case and outer spaces, shall be refused by name and nothing written. RATIONALE: .5 because the name is the customer's key (FRS-173); a second entry under the same name is a second customer every machine and call could be filed against.

**FRS-270.** *(v0.10.142 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-270.1 The Party Master edit drawer and Add form shall offer Type, Profile, Serviceman, City, State and Country as type-search-and-select lists. FRS-270.2 Type shall offer CUSTOMER and DEALER, and Profile PRIVATE, GOVERNMENT, DEALER and GENERAL (the Warranty Entry's own lists, one constant), each with the values the Party Master already holds, once regardless of case. ### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. **FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. ### URS-138 — A spare part keeps its identity, and a machine is offered the parts that fit it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Part Master shall accept a new part only with a code in the agreed form, a description, a category of Spare or Consumable, and either the products it fits or a deliberate statement that it is common to all products, and shall refuse a code that already exists. A part shall never be deleted; it shall be deactivated. A change to a part's code or description shall carry every record that names the part, in one act, after stating what will move, because hand stock is derived from those records and a part renamed in the catalogue alone changes an engineer's balance. The products a part is mapped to, and the accessories mapped to a main product, decide which parts a call offers; they shall be maintainable only by those who maintain masters, in bulk as well as singly, with any failure named, and a mapping that names a product the register does not hold shall be flagged.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-177** — Adding and editing a part | Medium | OQ-170 |
| **FRS-178** — Renaming a part carries its history | High | OQ-213, OQ-171 |
| **FRS-179** — Which products a part fits, and which accessories a product takes | Medium | OQ-172 |
| **FRS-219** — A part's HSN code | Medium | OQ-213 |

**FRS-177.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-177.1 ＋ Add part shall be offered to holders of masters.edit only, and the database shall refuse a write to `parts` from anybody else. FRS-177.2 The code shall be converted to upper case and refused if empty, if it contains “|”, or if it does not begin with a letter or digit followed only by letters, digits and - _ . /. FRS-177.3 A description shall be required. FRS-177.4 Spare or Consumable shall be required on a new part. FRS-177.5 The product(s) the part fits, or “Common to all products”, shall be required on a new part, Common being stored as no product. FRS-177.6 A purchase cost shall be a number where entered, and a blank shall be stored as not recorded, never as 0. FRS-177.7 A code that already exists shall be refused. FRS-177.8 The form shall show the part as it will be listed, CODE|Description. FRS-177.9 Editing a part shall allow its category, products and cost to change, shall keep a category the Item Master file brought even where it is not one of those offered, and shall allow an older part with those fields blank to be saved. FRS-177.10 A part shall be deactivated or reactivated after confirmation, and shall never be deleted. RATIONALE: .2 because “|” separates the code from the description in the identity every stock table carries. .6 because 0 is a price and “not recorded” is not one.

FRS-178.2 The drawer shall state, before renaming, how many records in which tables will move. FRS-178.3 `rename_part()` shall rewrite the part's identity in the catalogue and in all ten tables that carry it — stock adjustments (0266) included since 0309 — in one transaction. FRS-178.4 It shall refuse a rename onto a part that already exists, never merging two parts. FRS-178.7 The spare-request-line guard and the material-return guard shall let through the one change a rename makes — the part, moved exactly as the rename’s ticket names it, nothing else changed — so a rename does not need an administrator (0310); every other change of part on a line, and every other edit of a return, shall still be refused. FRS-178.8 Stock transfers shall move last of the ten, so the transfer stock check sees the part’s full balance under the new name. FRS-178.5 The consumption guard shall admit that rename by a ticket only the function can write, and shall refuse every other change of part on a consumption line. FRS-178.6 Every engineer's hand stock shall be the same after a rename as before, under the new identity. **FRS-179.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-179.1 The Part Master shall read a part with no product as “Common (all products)”. FRS-179.8 The Part Master search shall require every typed word to appear in the part, Item Master fields held in `extra` included, and shall filter by code, description, product and active or inactive. ### URS-142 — A cover entry is raised, filled and priced by one rule wherever it is entered

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The cover registers shall state for every entry whether it is Active, About to expire or Inactive, by one rule shared with the database, an entry with no readable end date being Not covered and never Active. A new entry shall be offered the next number in its series, which may be changed and shall be refused if already used. The customer shall be chosen from the Party Master, a customer the master does not hold being allowed; choosing a customer on a sale shall fill the address, contact and tax fields from the master, blanks included. A contract line's tax and total shall be derived from its rate by the one GST rule. A renewal shall be re-priced: no price shall be carried from the predecessor, a price entered shall be checked before anything is written, and a revision of the old price by a percentage shall be offered. The installation call for one machine may be raised from that machine, and its call number written back onto that machine only. Starting a call from a cover register shall be offered only to those who may register one.

| --- | --- | --- |

| **FRS-185** — A renewal is priced by what is entered, never by what was paid | Medium | OQ-178 |
| **FRS-186** — The installation call for one machine, raised from the machine | Medium | OQ-179 |
| **FRS-231** — A warranty machine still waiting for its installation call is marked and can be filtered | Low | OQ-225 |
| **FRS-244** — The sale, the contract and the transfer fill the Product Database by product + serial | High | OQ-236 |

**FRS-184.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-184.1 Each entry shall read ACTIVE where its end date is more than 30 days away, ABOUT TO EXPIRE within 30 days, INACTIVE once passed, and NOT COVERED where there is no readable end date, by `coverStatus()` and its SQL twin `cover_state()` (0187), which shall agree. FRS-184.2 The three state tiles shall count and filter by that state. FRS-184.3 + New entry shall offer the next number continuing the highest recent number in the series, editable and not reserved; the unique key shall refuse a number already used. FRS-184.4 A Sale Entry shall default its warranty start to today and stamp its entry date when created. FRS-184.5 The party picker shall search the Party Master in the database and shall accept a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.6 Choosing a different party on a sale shall fill its eleven address, contact and tax fields from the Party Master, blanks included, and shall fill nothing for a name the master does not hold. FRS-184.7 On a contract line, entering a rate shall derive the tax as GST_PERCENT (18) of the rate and the total as rate plus tax, through `itemTaxAmount()` and `totalAfterTax()`, the one copy of the rule; a sale line shall carry no rate. FRS-184.8 The contract type shall be chosen from CMC or AMC. FRS-184.9 + Field call on a machine shall be offered only to holders of calls.create, and shall open the Field Call form filled with the party, the machine and its cover. RATIONALE: .1 NOT COVERED because “active” is the one wrong answer for an unknown; the sheet's blank-reads-active was a comparison artefact. .6 blanks included because keeping the last party's address where the new one has none puts another customer's address on a sale with nothing saying so. .9 is open (D-063). Proved by `supabase/tests/cover_expiry_test.sql` (.1) and `npm run check:cover-party` (.6).

**FRS-185.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-185.1 The Renew panel shall show each carried machine's old rate beside an empty rate box. FRS-185.2 It shall offer to revise every ticked machine's old rate by a stated percentage, and to clear every entered rate. FRS-185.3 It shall preview the total with GST. FRS-185.4 A blank rate shall mean “price it later” and be saved as no rate, tax or total. FRS-185.5 Every entered rate shall be checked before anything is written, and a rate that is not a number, or is negative, shall refuse the whole renewal. FRS-185.6 A machine's tax and total shall be derived from its entered rate by the rule of FRS-184.7. FRS-185.7 No rate shall be copied from the predecessor's machines. **FRS-244.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-244.1 Every write to a sale line or entry, a contract line or entry, an ownership transfer or an additional entry shall re-sync the Product Database row of that machine — product and serial together, never the serial alone — through sync_product_machine() (0330). FRS-243.2 Sold Through on the Warranty Sale Entry and on each machine line shall be chosen only from dealers (no free text). FRS-243.3 An ownership transfer shall record as Sold Through its From party when that party is a dealer, and nothing otherwise, stamped by the database with any value sent discarded. FRS-243.4 The Product Database's Sold Through shall be the dealer on the machine's latest transfer that names one, else the sale line's, else the sale entry's, and re-saving the sale shall not change it. FRS-243.5 The Warranty Register shall offer no installation call for a sale whose Type is DEALER — on the entry or on a Register line — shall say instead that the call is raised from the Ownership Transfer, and shall not count a dealer's machines as waiting for a call; the database shall refuse any signed-in insert of an installation call, or change of its party, to a dealer, however raised. FRS-243.6 The Ownership Transfer register shall show Sold Through and offer, to a holder of install.create, “+ Installation call” on a transfer: one call for the transfer's To party, numbered OT-<product>-<serial>, dated the transfer date, built by the same builder as a sale's installation call with the Party Master's city, state and engineer and the Product Database's cover; a machine that already has its OT- call is not given a second. FRS-243.7 Once, the Sold Through 0318 cleared from machine lines shall be restored from its backup where the line still follows its entry and the entry's value is blank or different (0328). FRS-243.8 A re-load of an installation call that already exists under the same party shall not be refused as a new call for a dealer; a new call, or a re-load that moves a call onto a dealer, shall still be refused (0351, D-148). The Sold Through picker shall read a party as a dealer the way the database does, ignoring outer spaces (D-152). RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-03, and their choices: Sold Through on a transfer is the From party when a dealer; the transfer's call is dated the transfer date; the dealer rule is kept by the database as well as the screen; the 249 cleared values are restored.

**FRS-244.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-244.1 Every write to a sale line or entry, a contract line or entry, an ownership transfer or an additional entry shall re-sync the Product Database row of that machine — product and serial together, never the serial alone — through sync_product_machine() (0330). FRS-244.2 From the machine's latest sale line (by warranty end; the line's value, else its entry's): Warranty No., start, end, PM visits, Invoice No., Invoice Date, Warranty Years, Warranty Months and Accessories Included. FRS-244.3 From its latest contract line (by contract end; line, else entry): Contract No., start, end, type and status, and its PM visits, which overwrite the sale's (the user's choice) and survive the sale being saved again. FRS-244.4 A contract line for a machine the Product Database does not hold shall insert it, for the owner the registers name and with that owner's Party Master address. FRS-244.5 From its latest transfer: Transfer Ref and Transfer Date; the owner moves for that machine only (D-060's move half). FRS-244.6 A contract or warranty number a machine carries that a register line holds for ANOTHER model sharing its serial shall be cleared with its dates and type; one no register holds is left. FRS-244.7 Status: a current contract is its type, a current warranty WGP, a machine the registers know with neither OGP. FRS-244.8 A one-time re-sync shall apply this to every machine, the old values of each changed row kept in products_resync_backup. RATIONALE: .1 because a serial is shared by different models — the ORION-G 2410 / CPX CARE MC5521 case — and a contract on one is not cover on the other. Proved by `supabase/tests/registers_fill_product_database_test.sql`.

Record a transfer shall show the OT Number as given on save, not typed, and report the number given. FRS-266.2 Record a transfer shall take an optional Invoice No. and Invoice Date; the machine (product + serial) shall show the latest transfer's invoice on the Product Database while it is dated (by its invoice date, else the transfer date) on or after the sale's invoice, with or without a fresh warranty (sync_product_machine). FRS-266.3 Record a transfer shall take optional files, each uploaded to the "Ownership Transfers" Drive folder (the drive root until that folder exists and the bridge is redeployed) and kept on the transfer as {name, url, at, by}; the transfers list shall show the OT Number, Invoice No., Invoice Date and the files, each opening in the app's document preview. FRS-266.4 Since FRS-266.1, a fresh warranty (FRS-263.3) always has a Reference no. to carry. Proved by `supabase/tests/transfer_ot_number_invoice_test.sql`.

**FRS-263.** *(v0.10.115 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-263.1 Record a transfer shall show the machine's Invoice No. and Invoice Date in its Sale Entry block, as stored on the Product Database (0330). FRS-263.3 A fresh warranty shall need a period above 0 and the Reference no.; the database shall refuse either missing, shall work out the years and the end itself, discarding values sent, and shall clear months, years and end where no start is given (0383, ownership_transfer_warranty). The sale entry shall not be changed. FRS-263.5 The transfers list shall show each fresh warranty's start and end. Proved by `supabase/tests/transfer_fresh_warranty_test.sql`.
