FRS-262.2 It shall open Record a transfer on Ownership Transfer with that machine picked by model and serial, its details shown as FRS-260.2 describes, leaving the To party and the date to be entered; saving shall follow FRS-260 unchanged.

**FRS-260.** *(v0.10.108 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-260.1 Record a transfer shall pick the machine from the Product Database by serial (this device's copy first, else the server), each choice naming the serial, the model and the current party, and shall not accept a serial typed outside it. FRS-260.2 Choosing the machine shall show, as the Product Database has them, its current details (party, address, city, state, Service Engineer), its Sale Entry (SA Number, Sold Through) and its warranty (start date, end date, item status, contract number), none of them editable. FRS-260.3 The To party shall be picked from the Party Master (this device's copy first, else the server) and shall show that party's address, city, state, type and Service Engineer; a name not on the Party Master shall not be accepted, and a To party equal to the current party shall be refused. FRS-260.4 Saving shall record the model with the serial and the machine's current party as From, and shall keep the details of .2 on the transfer, so what the machine carried when it changed hands stays on record. Pull all Details from the Product Database in regards to Sale Entry, Warranty Details [Start Date, End Date]". A serial alone was resolved by the database with the first matching machine, which on a serial shared by several models is a guess. Invoice No and Date are not shown: the Product Database view does not yet publish them.

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |

**FRS-242.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-242.1 Parties, parts and product lines shall be written under masters.parties.*, masters.parts.* and masters.product_master.* (add / edit / delete), each its own INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policy (0325), with no FOR ALL write policy. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. FRS-242.3 A value list shall carry master.<list>.add beside .edit and .delete; adding shall be admitted by the add key, the list's edit key or masters.edit.records. FRS-242.4 Each of the four registers shall show an Actions column — ✎ Edit and 🗑 Delete, and on the Part Master and the lists Deactivate — each button only to the holder of its key; Add entry only to the holder of the add key. FRS-242.5 The Product Master's Edit shall change every field but the Product Code; a list's Edit shall rename the value and change its columns, saying before it is saved that records already carrying the old wording keep it. FRS-242.6 master_delete_guard() (security definer, not callable through the API) shall refuse deleting a party named on any machine, call, call request, pending registration, sale, contract, ownership transfer, additional entry, feedback, spare request, consumption history or Indoor job; a part named on any spare request, dispatch, consumption, issue history, opening stock, adjustment, transfer or material return line; and a product line whose code any machine, sale line or contract line carries — counting as the owner, and naming the count. FRS-242.7 A delete or edit that matches no row shall be reported as not done, never as done. FRS-242.8 A party’s name, a part’s code or description and a product line’s code shall not be changed except through Rename part or by an importer, so a row cannot be renamed and then deleted (0335, D-136). FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). RATIONALE: .2 so nobody gains or loses on the day it ships; .6 counts as the owner because under the caller's row-level security a count sees only what the caller may read and would pass a party a thousand other calls name. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

### URS-172 — A stock hand-over and a stock return print as the stores records they are

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A stock transfer shall print as the MATERIAL TRANSFER NOTE (R/SER/STR/003) and a material return as the MATERIAL RETURN NOTE (R/SER/STR/002), laid out as the paper records with their record block, from what the system already holds — the engineers' names with their place from the User Master, the parts and quantities, the transfer or return number and date — and with the name the system knows in each signature box it can fill and the others left to be signed by hand. A transfer shall take a reason for each part as well as one common remark, the part's own reason printing where one was given. A stored signature shall be reproduced only in a box naming the person printing.

**FRS-155.** *(v0.10.73 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-155.1 The Declaration shall find a stock out by the rule of FRS-154.1 and FRS-154.2. FRS-155.2 The Declaration shall list each part once, the quantities of the same part on several lines summed. FRS-155.3 The Declaration shall take, before printing and without printing them, To, Address, City, State, Contact No, Approximate value (Rs.), Purpose and Sent by; To, Address and Approximate value are mandatory. **FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.

**FRS-015.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Party/Product/Part/User masters and value lists are editable by authorised roles; edits are gated by masters.edit, or per value list by master.<list>.edit / master.<list>.delete, enforced by row-level security. Every row records the login that created and last changed it (sys columns, 0244). A value in use SHALL be deactivated rather than deleted, and the database SHALL refuse the deletion of a value any record carries (FRS-180.6; OPEN until D-056 is fixed). A part is never deleted (FRS-177.10); a party's name is not changed by editing (FRS-173).

### URS-027 — Refurbished spares

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Where a recycled spare is issued in place of a new one, it shall be identified by its own part number, held and consumed as that part, and the engineer shall be told the part is refurbished. Only a part held in Part Master and active may be issued this way.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-033** — Refurbished issue | High | OQ-20 |

**FRS-033.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Stores may mark a line as refurbished when issuing it. The issue records the recycled identity — R + part code, description unchanged — while the request keeps what was asked for. Hand stock is derived from the ISSUE, so the refurbished part is held and consumed under its own code. A database check refuses the swap unless that code exists in Part Master and is active, and the engineer’s dispatch notification states that the part is refurbished.

Opened by `mod:/masters`.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-176.2 A register opened from the copy on this device shall say “Showing cached data” and how long ago it was synchronised. FRS-176.3 It shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes, and only while no filter or search is applied. FRS-176.4 ↻ Refresh shall re-read the register from the database and replace the copy. FRS-176.5 A filter or search typed into the Party Master, the Product Database or a cover register shall be run by the database 300 ms after the last keystroke, and clearing it shall restore the unfiltered list. FRS-176.12 Every date shown on these registers shall read dd-MMM-yyyy. FRS-176.13 A reply arriving after the reader has opened another entry shall be discarded. FRS-176.14 Status and state chips shall show exact counts where the whole register is loaded, and act as filters. FRS-176.15 Without a database connection, the Party, Part and User Masters shall say so and, where a sheet copy exists, show it read-only. FRS-176.16 A register paged by a column that is not unique (a cover register by its end date) shall order by its unique id last, so no machine appears on two pages or on none (D-103). RATIONALE: .1 and .8 because a count or a file that looks whole and is not is worse than none — somebody acts on it. .3 because a background refresh replacing a filtered view is a register changing while it is being read. .13 because a late reply seeding Renew with another contract's machines would renew the wrong machines.

**FRS-248.** *(v0.10.68 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-248.1 The shared register table shall draw its first 150 rows, and 300 more each time the last drawn row comes within reach of the scroll, with a "Showing N of M — scroll for more · Show more" row while any are not yet drawn. FRS-248.2 Sorting, filtering, grouping, the row and group counts, select-all and the export shall work on every row the register holds, not only the rows drawn. FRS-248.3 A new sort, filter or grouping shall start drawing from the top. FRS-248.4 Sorting shall read each row's value once and compare with one collator, in the same order as before: blanks last, numbers by value, text with its digits read as numbers. RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. ### URS-138 — A spare part keeps its identity, and a machine is offered the parts that fit it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Part Master shall accept a new part only with a code in the agreed form, a description, a category of Spare or Consumable, and either the products it fits or a deliberate statement that it is common to all products, and shall refuse a code that already exists. A part shall never be deleted; it shall be deactivated. A change to a part's code or description shall carry every record that names the part, in one act, after stating what will move, because hand stock is derived from those records and a part renamed in the catalogue alone changes an engineer's balance. The products a part is mapped to, and the accessories mapped to a main product, decide which parts a call offers; they shall be maintainable only by those who maintain masters, in bulk as well as singly, with any failure named, and a mapping that names a product the register does not hold shall be flagged.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-177** — Adding and editing a part | Medium | OQ-170 |
| **FRS-178** — Renaming a part carries its history | High | OQ-213, OQ-171 |
| **FRS-179** — Which products a part fits, and which accessories a product takes | Medium | OQ-172 |
| **FRS-219** — A part's HSN code | Medium | OQ-213 |

**FRS-177.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-177.1 ＋ Add part shall be offered to holders of masters.edit only, and the database shall refuse a write to `parts` from anybody else. FRS-177.2 The code shall be converted to upper case and refused if empty, if it contains “|”, or if it does not begin with a letter or digit followed only by letters, digits and - _ . /. FRS-177.3 A description shall be required. FRS-177.4 Spare or Consumable shall be required on a new part. FRS-177.5 The product(s) the part fits, or “Common to all products”, shall be required on a new part, Common being stored as no product. FRS-177.6 A purchase cost shall be a number where entered, and a blank shall be stored as not recorded, never as 0. FRS-177.7 A code that already exists shall be refused. FRS-177.8 The form shall show the part as it will be listed, CODE|Description. FRS-177.9 Editing a part shall allow its category, products and cost to change, shall keep a category the Item Master file brought even where it is not one of those offered, and shall allow an older part with those fields blank to be saved. FRS-177.10 A part shall be deactivated or reactivated after confirmation, and shall never be deleted. RATIONALE: .2 because “|” separates the code from the description in the identity every stock table carries. .6 because 0 is a price and “not recorded” is not one.

**FRS-178.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-178.1 A change to a part's code or description shall be made only through `rename_part()` (0196), which shall refuse a caller without masters.edit.rename_part (0289); the work behind it, `rename_part_records()` (0309), shall not be callable by any signed-in user or the public key. FRS-178.2 The drawer shall state, before renaming, how many records in which tables will move. FRS-178.3 `rename_part()` shall rewrite the part's identity in the catalogue and in all ten tables that carry it — stock adjustments (0266) included since 0309 — in one transaction. FRS-178.4 It shall refuse a rename onto a part that already exists, never merging two parts. FRS-178.7 The spare-request-line guard and the material-return guard shall let through the one change a rename makes — the part, moved exactly as the rename’s ticket names it, nothing else changed — so a rename does not need an administrator (0310); every other change of part on a line, and every other edit of a return, shall still be refused. FRS-178.8 Stock transfers shall move last of the ten, so the transfer stock check sees the part’s full balance under the new name. FRS-178.5 The consumption guard shall admit that rename by a ticket only the function can write, and shall refuse every other change of part on a consumption line. FRS-178.6 Every engineer's hand stock shall be the same after a rename as before, under the new identity. RATIONALE: nothing has a foreign key to `parts`; hand stock is derived from the nine tables, so a catalogue-only rename changes balances rather than links (D-007, D-008). Proved by `supabase/tests/rename_part_test.sql`.

**FRS-179.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-179.1 The Part Master shall read a part with no product as “Common (all products)”. FRS-179.2 It shall flag in red, with ⚠, a product named on a part that the Product Database does not hold, and shall offer “⚠ Unrecognised” as a filter. FRS-179.3 A holder of masters.edit shall be able to tick several parts and set, add or remove products, or set Spare or Consumable, after confirmation, written ten at a time with every failure named. FRS-179.5 The Main product → Accessories panel shall offer as main products the Product Master lines not categorised ACCESSORY, and as accessories the ACCESSORY lines. FRS-179.6 One list shall be held per main product however its name is typed, a re-save replacing it, with an optional note. FRS-179.7 The database shall refuse every write to the accessory lists, deletion included, from anybody without masters.edit (`pa_insert`, `pa_update`, `pa_delete`, 0255), and every access from a caller not signed in. FRS-179.8 The Part Master search shall require every typed word to appear in the part, Item Master fields held in `extra` included, and shall filter by code, description, product and active or inactive. RATIONALE: .1 and .2 because these mappings decide which spares a call offers (`partfit`), so a product named in a spelling the register lacks makes a part vanish from every call on that product. Proved in part by `supabase/tests/product_accessories_test.sql` (.6, .7).

**FRS-219.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-219.1 The Part Master shall carry an HSN Code per part, shown as a column, set on Add part and on the edit drawer by a holder of masters.edit.records, and filled by an "HSN Code" (or HSN, HSN No, HSN/SAC) column in the Part Master upload. FRS-219.2 It shall accept digits only, of any length, or blank. FRS-219.3 Changing it shall be an ordinary edit, never a rename. ### URS-139 — A controlled value that is in use is withdrawn, never erased

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Each value list shall be maintainable by those granted that list, a duplicate being refused and each entry attributable to the person who added it. A value that any record carries shall not be deleted; it shall be deactivated, so it stops being offered and the records carrying it still read correctly, and the refusal shall be the database's and not only the screen's. The Standard Complaint list shall be scoped by product, a complaint mapped to no product applying to every product, so a call is offered the complaints that belong to its machine. A value may be renamed by those granted the list; the records already carrying the old wording keep it. An overview shall show every master with its size and whether it loaded.

| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |

**FRS-180.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-180.1 An entry shall be added only by a holder of `master.<list>.add` (or its parents `master.<list>.edit`, `masters.edit.records`, `masters.edit`), the database refusing anybody else (0067, 0325; corrected 2026-10-03). FRS-180.2 A value already in the list shall be refused with “already in this list”. FRS-180.3 An entry's Added On shall be the day it was added, and its author shall be recorded by the database from the session (`sys_created_by`, 0244); the Added By shown is a label. FRS-180.4 An entry shall be deactivated or reactivated after a confirmation stating that it stays on the records carrying it and stops being offered. FRS-180.5 🗑 Delete shall be offered only to a holder of `master.<list>.delete`. FRS-180.6 The database shall refuse the deletion of a value that any record carries, and shall say to deactivate it instead. FRS-180.7 Without the right to edit a list, the screen shall name the permission needed. FRS-180.8 ↻ Refresh on a list shall clear that list's dropdown cache, so forms offer the change without a reload; ↻ Refresh all shall clear every one. FRS-180.9 Where the registry of lists (`master_lists`) is absent, the built-in lists shall be used and the screen shall say which bundle to run. FRS-180.10 All Masters shall list the four registers with a row count each, and every value list with its entry count, whether it Loaded, is Empty or failed, and where it is used; a list may be opened in place or on its own page, and an unknown list address shall return to the overview. RATIONALE: .6 in the database because every count and filter downstream matches the stored value, and a deleted value leaves records carrying a word no list holds. Today a hard DELETE is offered with no such check and nothing in the database refuses it (D-056). FRS-180.11 An entry shall be added through an Add entry form opened by a button, naming each field and marking the required ones, and refusing an empty value; on the DCCR Complaint Grouping and Root Cause Key Word lists the Product shall be required and picked from the Product Master, or COMM for every product.

FRS-181.4 The editor shall offer every product in the register and every product already mapped, so a mapping cannot vanish from its own editor. FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). ### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |

**FRS-242.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-242.1 Parties, parts and product lines shall be written under masters.parties.*, masters.parts.* and masters.product_master.* (add / edit / delete), each its own INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policy (0325), with no FOR ALL write policy. FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. FRS-242.3 A value list shall carry master.<list>.add beside .edit and .delete; adding shall be admitted by the add key, the list's edit key or masters.edit.records. FRS-242.4 Each of the four registers shall show an Actions column — ✎ Edit and 🗑 Delete, and on the Part Master and the lists Deactivate — each button only to the holder of its key; Add entry only to the holder of the add key. FRS-242.5 The Product Master's Edit shall change every field but the Product Code; a list's Edit shall rename the value and change its columns, saying before it is saved that records already carrying the old wording keep it. FRS-242.6 master_delete_guard() (security definer, not callable through the API) shall refuse deleting a party named on any machine, call, call request, pending registration, sale, contract, ownership transfer, additional entry, feedback, spare request, consumption history or Indoor job; a part named on any spare request, dispatch, consumption, issue history, opening stock, adjustment, transfer or material return line; and a product line whose code any machine, sale line or contract line carries — counting as the owner, and naming the count. FRS-242.7 A delete or edit that matches no row shall be reported as not done, never as done. FRS-242.8 A party’s name, a part’s code or description and a product line’s code shall not be changed except through Rename part or by an importer, so a row cannot be renamed and then deleted (0335, D-136). FRS-242.9 The delete guard shall also count a party named as Sold Through, an Indoor DC consignee, an indoor job's demo party, or a Field Failure Report's or material return's customer, and a part on an indoor job (0350, D-137). RATIONALE: .2 so nobody gains or loses on the day it ships; .6 counts as the owner because under the caller's row-level security a count sees only what the caller may read and would pass a party a thousand other calls name. Proved by `supabase/tests/master_add_edit_delete_test.sql`.

### URS-040 — A bulk load shall not silently alter what it does not carry

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Loading a file shall change only the fields that file supplies. A field the file does not carry shall take the value the system defines for it, and shall not be written as empty or null; a load that cannot honour this shall fail rather than write. Where a register is declared to be loaded from a file that is the WHOLE of each record (the Product Database), a cell the file carries under its heading and leaves empty shall empty that field, so a correction made at source can remove a value as well as add one; a stamped or a required column shall never be emptied this way.

| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-074** — Every loadable register has a key its interface can infer | Medium | OQ-54 |
| **FRS-267** — The old DCCR register loads with its calls | High | OQ-265 |
| **FRS-071** — The field failure register is loaded year by year, whatever shape each year is | Medium | OQ-63 |
| **FRS-046** — A batch is one shape | High | OQ-33 |

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

**FRS-267.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-267.1 Bulk Uploads shall offer "DCCR Register — historical, with its calls", loaded into a staging register keyed on the UC Number, open to a holder of bulk.upload. FRS-267.2 Each row shall file its call — a P M VISIT row as a PM call, any other as a Field call — dated by the file's CALL DATE, with the customer as the party, the place, product, serial, cover, complaint, engineer, warranty number and Review 1 answers; the month-only warranty start shall be kept as text. FRS-267.3 Each row shall file its review marked imported, keeping the file's reviewers and dates and raising no Field Failure Report. FRS-267.4 Each row shall file one visit carrying the CURRENT CALL STATUS (else CALL STATUS), pending reason, engineer and Call Solved Date & Time, entered at the solved date, else the file's Updated Date, else the call date; no visit shall be filed for Unattended or for a Canceled call, which shall be filed cancelled. FRS-267.5 A call already in the register shall not be changed, and only a review it lacks shall be added. FRS-267.6 Loading shall notify nobody. FRS-267.7 Re-loading shall correct the calls the load filed and add no second call or visit; a correction shall need the same edit rights as on screen. FRS-267.8 The outcome for each UC Number shall be recorded on its staging row. RATIONALE: measured on the live project 2026-10-06, 6,051 DCCR rows of 2025 had been loaded while no Field call before 2026 existed, so the DCCR View could show none of them.

**FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-046.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The API writes a batch of rows as ONE insert whose column list is the union of the rows’ keys; a row lacking one of those keys is written as NULL, not as the column default. The loader therefore groups rows by their column set and sends each group separately, so a column no row in the group carries genuinely defaults. Filling absent values in was rejected as a fix: it would defeat a default that carries meaning. A load that violates a NOT NULL constraint fails the batch and writes nothing of it.

### URS-082 — Old Daily Complaint Reviews load as they were, and raise nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall load historical Daily Complaint Reviews in bulk from a file (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) as they were: the reviewer names and review dates the file records shall be kept, the person loading the file shall not be recorded as the reviewer of any review, and every row loaded shall be marked as imported so it stays distinguishable from a review answered in this system. Loading them shall NOT raise Field Failure Reports: the reports of those years are loaded from their own register, so raising them again from the reviews would issue a second report, under a new number, for a failure decided on years ago. Re-loading a corrected file shall update the same calls, matched on the UCN, rather than adding them again.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

A row that cannot meet this shall be held back and named rather than written.

FRS-142.2 A CSV template may be downloaded. FRS-142.3 Headings shall be matched by alias; a row with none of party, product and serial shall be dropped as blank and counted. FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.7 The due month shall default to this month, earlier months being loadable; every call shall be dated the 1st of it (`reg_date`) and today recorded as `added_on` (FRS-032). FRS-142.8 The first registration time and the gap between calls shall be prefilled from the latest PM call of that month and editable. FRS-142.9 Unrecognised columns shall be kept on the call in `extra`. FRS-142.10 The first eight calls and the count shall be previewed before import. ### URS-040 — A bulk load shall not silently alter what it does not carry

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Loading a file shall change only the fields that file supplies. A field the file does not carry shall take the value the system defines for it, and shall not be written as empty or null; a load that cannot honour this shall fail rather than write. Where a register is declared to be loaded from a file that is the WHOLE of each record (the Product Database), a cell the file carries under its heading and leaves empty shall empty that field, so a correction made at source can remove a value as well as add one; a stamped or a required column shall never be emptied this way.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-196** — Bulk Uploads: pick, preview, confirm, write, report | High | OQ-189 |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-074** — Every loadable register has a key its interface can infer | Medium | OQ-54 |
| **FRS-267** — The old DCCR register loads with its calls | High | OQ-265 |
| **FRS-071** — The field failure register is loaded year by year, whatever shape each year is | Medium | OQ-63 |
| **FRS-046** — A batch is one shape | High | OQ-33 |

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

**FRS-267.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-267.1 Bulk Uploads shall offer "DCCR Register — historical, with its calls", loaded into a staging register keyed on the UC Number, open to a holder of bulk.upload. FRS-267.2 Each row shall file its call — a P M VISIT row as a PM call, any other as a Field call — dated by the file's CALL DATE, with the customer as the party, the place, product, serial, cover, complaint, engineer, warranty number and Review 1 answers; the month-only warranty start shall be kept as text. FRS-267.3 Each row shall file its review marked imported, keeping the file's reviewers and dates and raising no Field Failure Report. FRS-267.4 Each row shall file one visit carrying the CURRENT CALL STATUS (else CALL STATUS), pending reason, engineer and Call Solved Date & Time, entered at the solved date, else the file's Updated Date, else the call date; no visit shall be filed for Unattended or for a Canceled call, which shall be filed cancelled. FRS-267.5 A call already in the register shall not be changed, and only a review it lacks shall be added. FRS-267.6 Loading shall notify nobody. FRS-267.7 Re-loading shall correct the calls the load filed and add no second call or visit; a correction shall need the same edit rights as on screen. FRS-267.8 The outcome for each UC Number shall be recorded on its staging row. RATIONALE: measured on the live project 2026-10-06, 6,051 DCCR rows of 2025 had been loaded while no Field call before 2026 existed, so the DCCR View could show none of them.

**FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-046.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The API writes a batch of rows as ONE insert whose column list is the union of the rows’ keys; a row lacking one of those keys is written as NULL, not as the column default. The loader therefore groups rows by their column set and sends each group separately, so a column no row in the group carries genuinely defaults. Filling absent values in was rejected as a fix: it would defeat a default that carries meaning. A load that violates a NOT NULL constraint fails the batch and writes nothing of it.
