### URS-151 — A bulk load is seen before it is written, and is recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit a register to be loaded from a file only by an administrator. Before anything is written — including any record the load must create for its rows to refer to — the system shall show what will be written, what will be held back and why, and what the file carries that will not be loaded, and shall ask the operator to confirm the number of rows and whether loading the same file again would correct them or add them a second time. A load that stops part-way shall state how much of it was written. Every load shall be recorded with who ran it, into which register, from which file, and how many rows were written and held back. A bulk load writes more quality records in a minute than a person writes in a year: one that is not previewed makes its mistakes at that rate, and one that is not recorded leaves nobody able to say where the records came from.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-196** — Bulk Uploads: pick, preview, confirm, write, report | High | OQ-189 |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-201** — The legacy importer on Admin Config | High | OQ-194 |

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.

### URS-152 — A servicing record loaded from the superseded system says what it said, and nothing is invented

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where calls, visits, spare requests, dispatches, consumption or feedback are loaded from the superseded system, each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, shall carry what the file carries and no attribution the file does not support, and shall be distinguishable from the records this system created. Where loading one record requires another that the file does not supply, the system shall create only what the file’s own values establish, shall mark what it creates as imported, and shall name every row it holds back for want of it. The effect a load will have on the status of the calls it touches shall be stated before the load is confirmed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

### URS-153 — A migrated stock movement is recorded as history, and loaded once

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where material returns, stock transfers and stock issues are loaded from the superseded system, they shall be recorded as having happened — exempt from the check that an engineer holds what they return or transfer, that check being a control on ENTRY — and shall be marked as imported so that the exemption applies to them and to nothing else. Each shall be keyed on what identifies it in that system, so that loading a file a second time corrects it rather than moving the stock again. A line whose parent record is absent shall be held back and counted. Hand stock is derived from these movements, so a movement loaded twice is not a duplicate row — it is an engineer holding parts that do not exist.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |

**FRS-199.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-199.1 The MRN Register upload shall stamp source = import on every row, and the return shortfall check shall pass a row carrying that provenance. FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

### URS-154 — A master loaded from a file keeps each entry’s identity

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a master — the customers, the machines, the product lines, the parts, the value lists, the cover registers or the QMS master list — is loaded from a file, each entry shall be matched on what identifies it; no load shall rename or merge an entry; and a value the file carries that the master cannot express shall be kept rather than guessed. Where the file is the whole of each record, a cell left empty shall empty that field; where it is not, a field the file does not carry shall be left as it is. A Standard Complaint renamed by a load stops matching every call that already carries it, and a machine’s cover left in place after the master was corrected is a machine serviced under somebody else’s contract.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-200** — Loading the masters | High | OQ-193 |
| **FRS-241** — Adding a product line to the Product Master | Medium | OQ-231 |

**FRS-200.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-200.1 The Party Master upload shall key each party on its name, separate the billing block, and give each party a Party key on its first load that no later load changes. FRS-200.2 The Product Database upload shall key each machine on model and serial; a heading the file carries with an empty cell shall clear that field (FRS-197.10), and a heading the file does not carry shall leave it alone. FRS-200.3 The Product Master upload shall key each product line on its code and carry Active as given, Active deciding only whether a new sale may name the line. FRS-200.4 The Part Master upload shall key each part on CODE|Description, normalise its category and keep an unknown category as given, and load an Inactive row as retired. FRS-200.5 Each master value list shall have its own uploader, which stamps the list name and keys each value on list name, value, stage and product. FRS-200.6 The Standard Complaint upload shall match each complaint on its Key (from Export CSV) and shall never rename one; the Products column shall set the complaint’s product mapping, and a file without that column shall leave every mapping as it is. FRS-200.7 The QMS Documents (Master List) upload shall key each document on number and revision, stamp kind = qms, require the URL, and assign no training. FRS-200.8 The Sale Entry, Sale Details, Contract Entry and Contract Details uploads shall shape the four AppSheet exports through the cover importer in any order, creating a stub entry for an item whose entry is not yet loaded and filling it when the entry arrives. RATIONALE: .6 because every count, filter and frequent-failure match runs on the complaint’s stored value — a rename is the calls already carrying it silently leaving every analysis. .7 because assigning training is a decision about PEOPLE (URS-079) that a list of documents cannot make.

**FRS-241.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-241.1 The Product Master shall offer “+ Add entry” only to a holder of `masters.product_master.add` (or its parents; 0325, corrected 2026-10-03), opening a pop-up form. FRS-241.2 Product Code and Product Name shall be required and marked * — the two the register's upload requires; a save with either blank shall be refused naming the blank fields, and nothing written. FRS-241.3 Item Detail, Type, Category, Short Form, Still sold? (Active by default) and Imported (not set by default) shall be optional; Type and Category shall offer the values the catalogue already uses and accept a new one. FRS-241.4 A code already on the register, ignoring case, shall be refused by code and nothing overwritten. FRS-241.5 Added and Added by shall be recorded as the day and the person who added it. RATIONALE: .4 because the code is the line's key and the upload is where an existing line is corrected; an add that overwrote would change a line every machine of that code is read against.

### URS-178 — Each installation's warranty decision is kept, and the old ones can be loaded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

For every installation call the system shall keep, in one record per call, the machine (product and serial), the customer, the registration date, the installing engineer's choice of where the warranty starts — the installation call's solved date or the invoice date — the day the call was solved, the engineer, the visit and the remarks, together with the warranty start and end that choice produced. Installation calls made before the system, back to 2018, shall be loadable into the same record in one file, and shall decide their machine's warranty exactly as a call reported in the system does. The engineer shall see, while reporting an installation, the machine's warranty as it stands and as it will stand after the report.

| --- | --- | --- |

FRS-246.2 warranty_start, warranty_end and period_months shall be written by the system from the Product Database after the choice is applied; a value sent through the API shall be discarded. FRS-246.3 machine_install_warranty_start() shall read the machine's latest row here (by solved date), so a loaded 2018 row decides its machine's warranty as a reported call does (FRS-245). FRS-246.4 Saving a row shall re-sync its product + serial, and the old machine where the product or serial changed. FRS-246.5 A RITHI installation shall fill its own row when its feedback is saved or its call's solved state changes, once the engineer has answered Warranty Start Date?. FRS-246.6 Loading or correcting a row shall need Bulk Uploads (bulk.upload); reading needs a sign-in. FRS-246.7 Bulk Uploads shall offer the register "Installation Warranty Start (old installation calls)", matched on the UCN so a re-loaded file corrects rather than adds, requiring UCN, product and serial. FRS-246.8 On an installation's Visit Entry, below Warranty Start Date?, the system shall show the Product Database warranty of that product + serial as it stands and — when Installation Call Solved Date is chosen on a visit that solves the call — the start and end it will have, computed by the database (machine_warranty_preview). FRS-246.9 The record shall be filled once from every installation feedback already on file. Proved by `supabase/tests/installation_warranty_starts_test.sql` and `supabase/tests/install_warranty_start_test.sql`.

### URS-062 — A loaded register can be corrected by loading it again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Every register that may be populated from a file shall have a natural key drawn from the file itself, so that re-loading a corrected export UPDATES the records it names rather than adding them a second time. The key shall be one the data interface can infer, and its sufficiency shall be verified against a database rather than by inspection. A row not carrying the key shall be refused and the reason given, a row that cannot be matched on a re-run being one that arrives again on every load.

| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |
| **FRS-201** — The legacy importer on Admin Config | High | OQ-194 |
| **FRS-074** — Every loadable register has a key its interface can infer | Medium | OQ-54 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

FRS-142.2 A CSV template may be downloaded. FRS-142.3 Headings shall be matched by alias; a row with none of party, product and serial shall be dropped as blank and counted. FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.11 A PM call shall be keyed on product, serial and due month, so that loading the same file again updates the calls it names rather than creating them again. FRS-142.12 Calls shall be written in batches with progress, the database assigning UCN and Call Number; a stop shall state how many were created. FRS-142.13 The loaded file may be cleared. **FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

### URS-039 — Identifier continuity across a migration

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Record identifiers shall remain unique and continue in sequence after historical records carrying their own identifiers are loaded; the system shall not re-issue an identifier the migrated data already uses.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-045** — Identifier continuity | High | OQ-32 |

**FRS-045.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The call-request trigger assigns a REQID from a sequence when the row does not carry one, and when it DOES carry one advances the sequence past it (0097), so loading historical records cannot leave the counter beneath them. `resync_call_req_seq()` repairs a counter already stranded. Identifiers issued out of sequence before the repair are re-lettered rather than renumbered, so a record people have seen keeps its identity while ceasing to collide.

### URS-040 — A bulk load shall not silently alter what it does not carry

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Loading a file shall change only the fields that file supplies. A field the file does not carry shall take the value the system defines for it, and shall not be written as empty or null; a load that cannot honour this shall fail rather than write. Where a register is declared to be loaded from a file that is the WHOLE of each record (the Product Database), a cell the file carries under its heading and leaves empty shall empty that field, so a correction made at source can remove a value as well as add one; a stamped or a required column shall never be emptied this way.

**FRS-267.** *(v0.10.132 · 06-Oct-2026)* FRS-267.1 Bulk Uploads shall offer "DCCR Register — historical, with its calls", loaded into a staging register keyed on the UC Number, open to a holder of bulk.upload. FRS-267.2 Each row shall file its call — a P M VISIT row as a PM call, any other as a Field call — dated by the file's CALL DATE, with the customer as the party, the place, product, serial, cover, complaint, engineer, warranty number and Review 1 answers; the month-only warranty start shall be kept as text. FRS-267.3 Each row shall file its review marked imported, keeping the file's reviewers and dates and raising no Field Failure Report. FRS-267.7 Re-loading shall correct the calls the load filed and add no second call or visit; a correction shall need the same edit rights as on screen. FRS-267.8 The outcome for each UC Number shall be recorded on its staging row. **FRS-071.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The register exists on paper back to 2016, one spreadsheet TAB per year, and the years do not agree with one another. The Bulk Uploads definition maps each year’s headings onto `field_failure_reports` through the shared header matcher (case- and space-insensitive, several accepted names per column, one date parser), and ANY COLUMN IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS KEPT on the row in `extra` and named on screen as kept — so a format nobody anticipated loses nothing and the unfamiliar heading is something to name later rather than data discarded now. Rows are matched on the FFR number TOGETHER WITH the machine's serial (0181, FRS-072), because in the 2016–2019 registers one report number covers several machines, so a corrected year is re-loaded over itself and the years may be loaded in any order; a row with no number is refused, because without it the same row arrives again on every load. Two properties are enforced in the database rather than by the importer: every loaded row carries `imported_from`, so migrated years stay DISTINGUISHABLE from reports this system raised and any figure over the register can report the split (the Insights tab does); and `ffr_stamp` leaves `raised_by` NULL on a loaded row, because the sheet’s “Raised by” is a name with no user account behind it and stamping the person running the upload would attribute a 2016 report to somebody who never saw it. Loading old years cannot disturb the current year’s number, which is drawn per year.

**FRS-046.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* The API writes a batch of rows as ONE insert whose column list is the union of the rows’ keys; a row lacking one of those keys is written as NULL, not as the column default. The loader therefore groups rows by their column set and sends each group separately, so a column no row in the group carries genuinely defaults. Filling absent values in was rejected as a fix: it would defeat a default that carries meaning. A load that violates a NOT NULL constraint fails the batch and writes nothing of it.

### URS-137 — A register says how much of itself it is showing, and a copy says how old it is

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every master and cover register shall say whether the rows on screen are the whole register or part of it, a count over a partly loaded register being shown as a lower bound. A register read from a copy held on the device shall say so and how old the copy is, and shall refresh itself in the background only while no filter is applied, so a filtered view is never replaced under the person reading it. A search shall be run by the database, not over the rows already on screen, wherever the register is larger than one page. An export shall be refused without the export permission, shall warn and ask before writing a file from a register not fully loaded, and shall write dates in the one written form. A failure shall be reported in words, keeping the database's own message, and never shown as an empty list; an empty result shall report what its sources hold rather than assert that nothing exists.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-156** — The spare and stock registers say how much they show | Medium | OQ-148 |
| **FRS-165** — Who may open the spare and stock screens | Medium | OQ-157 |
| **FRS-176** — Reading, refreshing and exporting a master or cover register | Medium | OQ-169 |
| **FRS-248** — A register of any size opens and sorts without freezing the screen | Medium | OQ-240 |
| **FRS-261** — The device copies: a stored snapshot, refreshed per register, downloadable one at a time; the Contract Entry Date is today | Medium | OQ-257 |

**FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.3 Every such register shall report a failed read as a failure — naming the migration where its table or view is missing (`isMissingTable`), otherwise the error verbatim — and shall never show a failed read as an empty register. FRS-156.4 RM Approval and Pending Dispatch shall state that nothing is waiting only to a reader for whom `seesEveryRecord` is true, and otherwise that nothing is waiting that the reader can see. FRS-156.5 A register that opens on data kept from an earlier read shall do so only within 30 minutes of it, shall label it as cached with its age, shall refresh it in the background every 30 minutes and shall offer Refresh. FRS-156.6 Spare Requests and Spare Consumption shall fall back, while the database is not connected, to a read-only copy of their Google Sheet and shall say so. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

RATIONALE: measured on 20,000 rows, the table took 16.2 s to open and 11.2 s to sort when it drew every row; 0.1 s and 0.2 s drawing what can be seen (D-118).

**FRS-261.** *(v0.10.109 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-261.1 The machine copy kept on a device shall be read from the stored Product Database table (`products`), as saved by the registers (0330), and not from the `product_database` view, so no contract or installation call is re-derived while it downloads. FRS-261.2 The machine copy and the Part Master shall be refreshed every six hours; the Party Master copy and the Standard Complaints once in ten days; each refreshed at once by an edit made on that device. FRS-261.3 The note saying what the device holds shall offer Download again for Machines, Customers, Complaints and Parts separately, each fetching only its own register, and shall be shown in the Record a transfer drawer. FRS-261.4 A new contract entry shall show the Contract Entry Date as today, not editable, and shall be stamped with the moment of saving; an edit shall leave it as it was. RATIONALE: .1 the view timed out for a signed-in person ("canceling statement due to statement timeout") and no machine copy reached any device; the copy therefore carries the stored contract, status and engineer, not the view's party-matched ones.

### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-112** — Every file download is gated, scoped and recorded | High | OQ-100 |
| **FRS-138** — One gate for every download | High | OQ-129 |
| **FRS-193** — One export gate for every format, and a record of each file | High | OQ-186 |
| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |
| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |

**FRS-112.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-112.1 xlsxDownload shall refuse, exactly as csvExport does, when the user does not hold export.data. FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-138.2 Every download shall be preceded by the partial-load question (`mayExport`) where the rows are a partial load or a capped search. FRS-138.3 A workbook shall carry dates as serials with a date format and numbers as numbers, and an About sheet stating the report, its scope, its row count, whether more rows exist and when it was taken. FRS-138.4 The Visit Reports export shall carry every column the loaded visits carry, including every answer on the visit form. FRS-138.5 A download from Solved Without a Report or Feedback Without a Report shall be written to `audit_log` with rows, scope and format. RATIONALE: `csvExport` checks `canExportData()` and `xlsxDownload` and `xlsDownload` do not, so on Visit Reports, Solved Without a Report and Feedback Without a Report a role refused the CSV takes the same rows as Excel (D-018).

**FRS-193.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-193.1 The export gate shall refuse a .csv, an .xlsx, an .xls and a .zip file alike to a role without export.data. FRS-193.2 A report shall require, in addition to export.data, its own right to take the file: consumption.view, calls.view or reports.view for the Consumption, Unused Spares and Call reports; feedback.view or calls.report for the Customer Feedback Report; and calls.view or reports.view for the KPI export. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. FRS-193.4 The system shall write an audit entry for each file produced, naming the report or the tables, the rows, the columns and the filter (report.<key>, kpi.export, report.unused_spares, rbac.export, data.export). FRS-193.5 The system shall write no audit entry, and shall display no "Downloaded" message, for a file the export gate refused or the person cancelled. FRS-193.6 Where a file is taken from a list not yet wholly loaded, the system shall ask before writing it and state how many rows were loaded of how many. RATIONALE: .1 — the gate lives in csvExport alone (src/lib/format.tsx); xlsxDownload and the Data Export zip do not consult it, and the KPI export checks no report-level right at all (D-065). .5 — the report builder writes its audit entry after csvExport returns, whether that call wrote the file or refused it (D-065).

**FRS-202.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-202.1 Data Export shall open only for a holder of mod:/data-export and export.tables or export.schedules: the table list for either, the download for export.tables, the schedules for export.schedules (0306); anyone else shall be told which right is needed. FRS-202.2 Data Export shall list only the tables exportable_tables() returns — no audit table — with their approximate row counts labelled as estimates. FRS-202.3 Data Export shall provide a search over table names, a control selecting every table shown, a control clearing the selection, and the approximate total of rows selected. FRS-202.4 Data Export shall read each chosen table as the signed-in person, row-level security in force, in pages of 1,000 under a stated order (D-065). FRS-202.5 Data Export shall state, for a table that reached the limit of 200,000 rows, that its file is cut short, and name it in the result (D-065). FRS-202.6 Data Export shall write one CSV per table — dates as dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, structured values verbatim — into one ZIP named rithi-export-<date>. FRS-202.7 Data Export shall refuse the ZIP to a role without export.data (D-065). FRS-202.8 Data Export shall write an audit entry for each ZIP naming the tables and the rows of each (D-065). FRS-202.9 Data Export shall download nothing where any table fails, and say so. FRS-202.10 Data Export shall allow an administrator to amend a schedule, its tables becoming the ones ticked. FRS-202.11 Data Export shall allow an administrator to pause and resume a schedule; a paused schedule sends nothing and shows "paused" in place of its next run. FRS-202.12 Data Export shall allow an administrator to delete a schedule after confirmation, the record of its past runs being retained (export_runs.schedule_id set null). FRS-202.13 Data Export shall list each schedule with its name, tables, recurrence, next run, and last run with its status and detail. FRS-202.14 Data Export shall state separately a failure to list the tables and a failure to read the schedules, naming data_export.sql, and shall state that nothing is mailed until the mail function is deployed. RATIONALE: .4 — a paged read with no order can return a row on two pages or on neither, and the file then looks complete; .5 — the pager stops at its cap without a word, which is the silent truncation this project has had thirteen times.

**FRS-249.** *(v0.10.70 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-249.1 Every CSV and Excel download, from whichever screen, shall ask where the export goes once the export permission and the partial-data warning have passed: Download the file to this device, or Save as Google Sheet. FRS-249.2 Save as Google Sheet shall create a Google Sheet holding the same rows and columns as the file, in a folder of the exporter's own inside the RITHI export folder on Google Drive; the folder shall be created on the person's first export and the same folder used on every later one (remembered by email, and found by its name if the remembered folder is gone), never a second. FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. FRS-249.4 The screen shall give a link to the sheet when it is saved, and when it is not shall say why and offer the file download instead. FRS-249.5 Each save shall be recorded in the audit log as export.google_sheet with the file name, the row count and the link, and a failed save recorded as failed. RATIONALE: .1 sits in the three file writers so no screen can offer a download without the choice; .2 is the user's rule, 2026-10-04: "When the same user is exporting for the 2nd time ... dont create again, instead save it in the existing folder".

### URS-155 — Whole tables leave only as an authorised, complete and recorded file

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall allow whole tables to be taken out as files only by an administrator holding the authority to export. Each table shall be read as that person, with their access rules in force, and shall be written entirely or with a statement that it was cut short. Each such export shall be recorded with who took it, when, which tables and how many rows of each. A schedule that sends tables on a timer shall be amended, paused, resumed or deleted only by an administrator, and deleting one shall not remove the record of what it sent. A whole-table export is the customer base, every serial and every contract leaving the building in one file; it is the export most worth recording, and a file silently cut short at a row limit is a backup that is not one.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |

### URS-062 — A loaded register can be corrected by loading it again

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Every register that may be populated from a file shall have a natural key drawn from the file itself, so that re-loading a corrected export UPDATES the records it names rather than adding them a second time. The key shall be one the data interface can infer, and its sufficiency shall be verified against a database rather than by inspection. A row not carrying the key shall be refused and the reason given, a row that cannot be matched on a re-run being one that arrives again on every load.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-100** — Loading historical reviews (Bulk Uploads → DCCR Register) | High | OQ-88 |
| **FRS-142** — The PM batch load | High | OQ-135 |
| **FRS-196** — Bulk Uploads: pick, preview, confirm, write, report | High | OQ-189 |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-198** — Loading the servicing registers | High | OQ-191 |
| **FRS-199** — Loading the stock movement registers | High | OQ-192 |
| **FRS-201** — The legacy importer on Admin Config | High | OQ-194 |
| **FRS-074** — Every loadable register has a key its interface can infer | Medium | OQ-54 |

**FRS-100.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-100.1 The DCCR Register upload shall write to call_reviews on the conflict target ucn, so that re-loading a corrected file updates the reviews of the calls it names. FRS-100.2 A row with no UCN shall be refused and named. FRS-100.3 The Review 2 by and Review 3 by names and the Date of Review 2 and Date of Review 3 in the file shall be stored as given. FRS-100.4 The database shall stamp no identity of the person loading the file on an imported row — neither review2_by_uid nor review3_by_uid, nor a reviewer name the file leaves blank — and a review date the file leaves blank shall stay blank rather than become the day of loading. FRS-100.5 Every row written by the load shall carry a marker that it was imported (imported), set by the load and not alterable from the review screen. FRS-100.6 An imported row shall raise no Field Failure Report, whatever its Any Potential Effect. FRS-100.7 Review Status, Any Potential Effect, Action Taken and the Review N Completed flags shall be derived from the answers loaded, and the file’s own copies of them ignored. FRS-100.8 The register shall show an imported review as imported. FRS-100.9 Only an administrator shall be able to mark a review imported; the marker sent by anybody else shall be discarded, because it switches off the Field Failure Report rule for that call. RATIONALE: .4 because 0173 stamps the reviewer from the session on every write path, and on a load the session is the loader — a 2019 review would be attributed to somebody who never saw it; the same reasoning FRS-071 applies to loaded Field Failure Reports. .6 because the reports of those years arrive through their own upload, and raising them again from the reviews would issue a second number for one failure (D-029).

**FRS-142.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-142.1 PM Bulk Upload shall refuse any user who does not hold pm.bulk_upload (an administrator holds it; 0302 made it a grantable key), and each call it creates shall still pass the PM register’s own insert policy. FRS-142.2 A CSV template may be downloaded. FRS-142.3 Headings shall be matched by alias; a row with none of party, product and serial shall be dropped as blank and counted. FRS-142.4 A row with no serial shall be held back and named, not created. FRS-142.5 The Standard Complaint shall be checked against the product's complaint master and the engineer against the active User Master; a row carrying a value on neither shall be held back and named. FRS-142.6 Item status shall be normalised through `coverCode()` to WGP, OGP, CMC or AMC, an unrecognised value kept as written. FRS-142.7 The due month shall default to this month, earlier months being loadable; every call shall be dated the 1st of it (`reg_date`) and today recorded as `added_on` (FRS-032). FRS-142.8 The first registration time and the gap between calls shall be prefilled from the latest PM call of that month and editable. FRS-142.9 Unrecognised columns shall be kept on the call in `extra`. FRS-142.10 The first eight calls and the count shall be previewed before import. FRS-142.11 A PM call shall be keyed on product, serial and due month, so that loading the same file again updates the calls it names rather than creating them again. FRS-142.12 Calls shall be written in batches with progress, the database assigning UCN and Call Number; a stop shall state how many were created. FRS-142.13 The loaded file may be cleared. RATIONALE: `pmImport.ts` keeps any row with a party OR a product, so a PM call with no serial is created (URS-053), and the writer is insert-only with “no key to re-run against”, so a file loaded twice is every call twice (URS-062) (D-038).

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-198.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-198.1 The Field, Installation and PM Calls uploads shall key each call on its UCN, stamp its call type, let the database assign a call number and registration date where the file carries none, and leave both registrant columns empty where the file cannot name a person (FRS-051). FRS-198.2 The Field, Installation and PM Reports uploads shall key each visit on the file’s uid or, where it has none, on a uid derived from the UCN and the visit date; shall require the visit date; and shall write Visit Entry Date to updated_at. FRS-198.3 The preview of a visit load shall state that each call’s status becomes that of its latest loaded entry, and that a visit with a blank status leaves its call reading Report pending. FRS-198.4 The Spare Request upload shall key each request on its OR number and shall not send the table’s own uid. FRS-198.5 The Spare Request Lines upload shall number each line within its request, re-point a line to the request already holding its OR number, and carry the RM, Commercial and NSM decisions the file records. FRS-198.6 The Spare Request Lines upload shall, for a line naming an OR number no request holds, create a request with status Imported and a remark saying why, and shall state in the confirmation how many it will create. FRS-198.7 The Stock Out Register upload shall key each dispatch on its uid, the person on it being stamped by the database (0211). FRS-198.8 The Consumption upload shall key each line on the file’s source row id and, for a call with no visit, shall file ONE visit per UCN from the file’s Visit Date & Time, the first dated row deciding, under the uid the visit registers derive. FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. FRS-198.11 The Customer Feedback upload shall key each feedback on its UCN, stamp imported_from, and take the feedback date from Visit Entry Date. RATIONALE: .3 because a visit load moves the status of every call it touches and a blank status is itself an answer; .6 because the header export does not reach back as far as the lines (58 OR numbers on 8,675 lines are in neither file), and a request created from a line is a quality record created from a file, which the operator is told about before agreeing to it. .8 records the 0214 guard’s requirement rather than evading it: nothing is invented, and no date means no visit.

**FRS-199.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-199.1 The MRN Register upload shall stamp source = import on every row, and the return shortfall check shall pass a row carrying that provenance. FRS-199.2 The Stock Transfer Register upload shall stamp source = import, the transfer stock check passing that provenance, and shall hold back by name a row transferring to the same engineer. FRS-199.3 The Stock Transfer Lines upload shall hold back, and count in the confirmation, each line whose transfer is not in the register. FRS-199.4 An imported movement shall remain subject to every check other than the shortfall check. FRS-199.5 The MRN Register and Stock Transfer Lines uploads shall each be keyed on a natural key drawn from the file, so a second load corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-199.6 Until FRS-199.5 holds, Bulk Uploads shall warn before confirmation that a re-run of either adds every row again (FRS-196.9). RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are 0089’s rule — an import is a record, not a request, so it is exempt from the shortfall check AND FROM NOTHING ELSE; the issue that covered a historical return may be in a file not yet loaded. .5 because URS-062 requires a key of every loadable register and these two have none; a second run moves the stock again. Partly proved by supabase/tests/spare_import_exemption_test.sql (.1, .2, .4).

**FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.

**FRS-074.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Ownership transfers are keyed on the hand-over document AND the machine (0184); recovered warranty entries on the model AND the serial (0185); customer feedback on the call (0186). Each is a GENERATED STORED column carrying a plain unique index, because the data interface can infer neither an expression index nor a partial one — `npm run check:upserts` verifies every declared target against a real database and refused a partial index written during this very revision. A row carrying no key is refused and named at the point of loading. Where a row has no key VALUE but must be retained — feedback naming no call — the key falls back to the row’s own identifier, so it is unique by construction and no record is deleted to permit an index. Existing duplicates are collapsed by the migration keeping the most recent, a second record of one thing being a correction of the first.

### URS-078 — The register of machines is searchable with no signal, and the office can see who has it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall keep a copy of the register of machines and of the customer register on each device a person signs in on, so that selecting a product, a serial and the customer it belongs to works on a weak or absent network connection. The copy shall be replaced only by a complete newer copy, never by a partial one, and shall state its age to the person using it. The system shall let an administrator see, for every person, which devices hold a copy, how many machines and customers each holds, when each copy was taken and the last failure to refresh it — including every person who has never reported a copy — so that an engineer about to travel without a usable copy can be found before the visit rather than during it.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-118** — Product & Party Search | Medium | OQ-106 |
| **FRS-211** — Sign-out leaves nothing on the device | High | OQ-204 |
| **FRS-215** — Device Cache Status: what each copy is, and how old | Medium | OQ-208 |
| **FRS-092** — Each device reports its own copy; the report lists everybody | Medium | OQ-80 |

**FRS-118.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-118.1 Where the product list cannot be read from the register, the screen shall fall back to the product value list and shall show the error with a Refresh hint. FRS-118.2 A serial given with no product shall be searched as a match on any part of the serial. FRS-118.3 The machine search shall show at most 200 results and say so when more matched. FRS-118.4 Where exactly one machine, or one party, matches, its party shall open at once. FRS-118.5 The party drop-down shall be searched on the server over the customers named on the Product Register (those holding a machine), and the box beside it shall take any part of a name; the party card shall prefer the party whose name matches exactly. FRS-118.6 ＋ Field call on a machine row shall be offered only to holders of calls.create and shall open the Field Call Register filled with that machine’s customer, product and serial. FRS-118.7 Download again shall take a fresh full copy of the machine and customer registers for the device, the copy being replaced only when the new one is complete (URS-078). FRS-118.8 The result tables shall be sortable and resizable, with columns shown or hidden, remembered per device. FRS-118.9 The screen shall say Give a product or a serial, Give a party name, No machine matched and No party matched where each applies, show a search error until dismissed, and say when not connected. FRS-118.10 Opening a party shall find it by its exact name (ignoring case and outer spaces), and the party search shall say when it shows only the first 50 (D-133).

**FRS-211.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-211.1 Sign-out shall record logout, clear the person’s notifications, report and then delete the offline machine and party copy, and end any preview. FRS-211.2 Sign-out shall remove every screen cache (rithi.cache.*, rithi.sync.*), the cached Audit Log rows included (D-070). FRS-211.3 The counts beside menu entries shall be held per person, shown only to that person, and removed at sign-out (D-070). RATIONALE: .2 and .3 — the offline registers were wiped at sign-out, and the screen caches beside them were not; on a shared device the next person opens the Audit Log to the previous person’s cached rows and reads the previous person’s counts beside the menu.

**FRS-215.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-215.1 Device Cache Status shall show, per person per device: the person (marked where inactive), the role, the device label with its browser identification on hover, the app version, the machines held and when downloaded, the customers held and when, the standard complaints held and when, the problem (storage refused, download errors) and when the device last reported. FRS-215.2 Device Cache Status shall give each row a state: Current (under 6 hours), Due a refresh (6 to 24 hours), Older than a day, No copy on the device, or Never reported. FRS-215.3 Device Cache Status shall show a chip per state with its exact count, selecting a chip filtering the list. FRS-215.4 Device Cache Status shall search by person, e-mail, role or device. FRS-215.5 Device Cache Status shall state the number of people and devices and how the reports arrive. FRS-215.6 Device Cache Status shall provide a refresh stating when it last synchronised, and a failure to load shall name device_cache.sql. RATIONALE: .1 names "storage refused" because a browser that will not keep a copy is an engineer who has none however often it downloads.

**FRS-092.** *(v0.10.106 · 05-Oct-2026)* FRS-092.1 Each device shall record what it holds of the offline registers in `device_cache_status`, one row per person per device, upserted on (user_id, device_id). FRS-092.2 The person on that row shall be stamped by the database from the session, any value sent by the device being discarded. FRS-092.3 A device shall write only its own row, and a person shall read only their own rows unless they hold `mod:/device-cache`. FRS-092.4 `device_cache_report()` shall refuse a caller without `mod:/device-cache`, shall not be callable without signing in, and shall return every profile including those with no device reported. FRS-092.5 A device shall report after each download completes or fails and when its user signs out, and shall not re-send an unchanged report within six hours. FRS-092.6 The report shall carry, beside the machines and customers, how many Standard Complaints (0253) and how many Part Master parts (0380) the device holds and when each was stored; the device shall keep the parts list, with each part's products and each product's accessories, for six hours and serve the spare pickers from it with no signal; the Spare Requests page and its new-request form shall show how many parts this device holds and when they were cached, with Download now to fetch a fresh copy at once, a failed download keeping the copy already held. RATIONALE: .2 because a report somebody else could file is a report nobody can rely on; .4 because the engineer most worth finding is the one with no copy anywhere, and a list of reports cannot show an absence. Proved by `supabase/tests/device_cache_status_test.sql`.

### URS-111 — A visit is recorded as it happened

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The record of a visit shall be dated no later than today and no earlier than the complaint, because the latest visit decides whether the call is closed. It shall state why an unsolved call is pending, carry the signed service report where the call is completed, record the customer's feedback on a solved call, and record the parts fitted with the traceability of each. Where only part of a visit could be saved the person shall be told exactly which part, and shall be able to complete it without entering the visit twice.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-136** — The visit form | High | OQ-237, OQ-126, OQ-127 |
| **FRS-137** — Saving a visit, its spares and its feedback | High | OQ-127 |

**FRS-136.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-136.1 The visit date shall be no later than today (IST) and no earlier than the call's complaint date, checked on save by `visitDateProblem()` and refused by the database for every visit entered on the form (`uid WEB-…`, 0115); imported history is exempt. FRS-136.2 The Visit Entry Date shall be stamped by the application at the moment of entry and shall not be editable. FRS-136.3 The Visiting Service Engineer shall be required; a manager or administrator may choose an engineer of their team, whose hand stock is then used, while the visit records the signed-in person as its author (`engineer_email`). FRS-136.4 Call Status shall be one of three values. FRS-136.5 Call Pending Reason shall be required from the pending-reason master when the status is Unsolved, and fixed to Report Pending when the report is pending. FRS-136.6 Update Visit Work Details? shall be answered, and shall be Yes when the status is Solved - Report Completed; No shall omit the service report fields. FRS-136.7 The service report shall require software version and filter changed, take the complaint from the master, and offer the accessory serial from the party's CPX/ASU units. FRS-136.8 On an installation, Warranty Start Date? shall be required and answered by choosing one of the customer feedback's two answers — Installation Call Solved Date or Invoice Date — with no default, and be stored on the feedback (FRS-082, FRS-245). FRS-136.9 The manual report shall be a PDF or photo up to 10 MB uploaded to the call type's Drive folder, never a pasted link, and shall be required when the status is Solved - Report Completed; it may be shown, opened, replaced or removed before save. FRS-136.10 On a solved call the feedback questions shall be those for the call type, rating and yes/no answers required, and the customer sign-off name, number and designation optional. FRS-136.11 The form shall show the previous visits (status, engineer, date) and open the last manual report. FRS-136.12 A missing hand-stock view shall be reported as needing its migration.

**FRS-137.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-137.1 A save shall write the visit, then every spare line in one insert (FRS-062), then the feedback. FRS-137.2 Where a later step fails, the form shall state what was saved and what was not, and a further Save shall retry only the part not saved. FRS-137.3 The call's state shall follow from the visit by trigger (FRS-007); the status stamp written afterwards to `calls.status` shall not be what decides whether the call is closed. FRS-137.4 The spare picker shall offer only the engineer's hand stock, narrowed to the call's product, its accessories and common parts, with Show all parts to widen it; the quantity offered shall be capped at the balance across the lines (FRS-030). FRS-137.5 Each spare line may carry a GRIR / traceability reference, stored in `spare_consumption.grir`. FRS-137.6 A successful save shall be written to `audit_log` as `call.report`, a spare failure as `call.report.consumption` and a feedback failure as `call.report.feedback`. RATIONALE: .2 is the whole of what can be promised: the three writes are separate statements, so a visit can stand without its spares if the form is closed after a failure. `unused_spare_report` (FRS-055) is what then makes a dispatched part visible as unaccounted for.

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall list every call that reads as solved but whose visit record is incomplete, and every customer feedback with no completed service report behind it, naming each gap on each row, counting each exactly, and allowing each to be exported with an explanation of what was counted. FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-224.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-224.1 The database shall, once, write into each warranty machine line whose INST Call holds no call number the UCN of an installation call found by, in turn: the call number WI-<Product>-<Serial>; the product, serial and the sale's party; the product and serial alone, each compared trimmed and case-insensitive, and only where that rule finds exactly one installation call. FRS-224.2 It shall consider installation calls only, shall not map a call already mapped to a machine, shall not map a call two machine lines both want, and shall leave a line already holding a call number alone. FRS-224.3 It shall log every change with the value replaced and the rule that made it, record that it ran, and change nothing on a later run. FRS-224.4 Machines Without an Installation Call shall list, live, every warranty machine line whose INST Call holds no call number, with its sale, party, product, serial and warranty dates, the reason (no product or serial; no installation call; the call already mapped to another line; one match not mapped; several matches) and the candidate installation calls with their parties, filterable by reason and exportable to Excel with dates as dates. FRS-224.5 The list and its data shall require mod:/install-calls-unmapped, granted to the administrator role and to Technical Support (which carries every page the administrator holds) and assignable on Roles & Permissions; the public key shall not reach it. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-10-02: "look for all installation calls using this - Product, Serial No, Party Name or WI-<Product>-<SerialNo>. And map it. If it does not have an installation call give it as a separate list in reports - view only for Admins", and "Map only installation call". Exactly one or nothing, as 0234: a guessed mapping is a false record of which call installed a machine. Proved by supabase/tests/install_call_mapping_once_test.sql (0319).

### URS-065 — A recovered quality record is reviewed before it is written

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where records of work already done are recovered from a superseded system, each shall be resolved to the record it belongs to AND SHOWN TO AN OPERATOR BEFORE ANY OF IT IS WRITTEN, and only rows that resolved cleanly shall be written. A visit attached to the wrong call, or carrying another machine’s photograph, is a worse outcome than a visit still missing: the first is a false record of what was done to a device, the second is a gap that is visible as a gap. Rows that did not resolve shall be reported with the reason and left unwritten rather than written with a guess.

| **FRS-077** — Bulk Report Mapping reads, resolves and only then writes | High | OQ-58 |

FRS-140.3 Each list may be searched by UCN, call number, party, product and serial (and engineer on Feedback Without a Report). FRS-140.4 The empty message shall claim that every record is complete only to a reader who sees every record, and otherwise say that nothing incomplete is visible to them. FRS-140.5 A load failure shall name the missing migration or grant, or show the error verbatim. FRS-140.6 Each list shall export to Excel, with an About sheet explaining each gap and the scope, or to CSV, through FRS-138. FRS-140.7 Refresh shall re-read the list. RATIONALE: .4 because both views are `security_invoker` and the module key can be granted to a scoped role, to whom “Every solved call has a dated visit and a service report behind it” is a statement about calls it cannot see (D-040).

**FRS-145.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-145.1 Bulk Report Mapping shall be open only to an administrator or a holder of `calls.report`, with the database connected, and shall say so to anyone else. FRS-145.2 The preview may be narrowed to the rows with a problem. FRS-145.3 A column of the file the screen does not recognise shall be kept on the visit written, under its own heading. FRS-145.4 A row with no attachment resolved shall be skipped at write, not written without its report, whether or not step 2 was run.

**FRS-077.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* The screen runs in three stated steps and in this order: READ the sheet and work out which call each row belongs to; RESOLVE the superseded system’s file references into links; WRITE only the rows that came through both cleanly. Nothing is written until the operator has SEEN what each row resolved to, and rows that did not resolve are listed with the reason and are not written. The register it writes into is the visit history, whose records are never deleted, so a wrong write cannot be taken back — which is why the review is a step rather than a confirmation dialogue. Bulk Report Mapping shall count a visit as attached only when the update changed it, and stop, naming the visit, when row-level security matched nothing (D-091).
