**FRS-207.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-207.1 Software Validation shall offer result recording (Pass / Fail / N/A and the actual result) only to a person the database permits to record — an administrator or a holder of config.manage (D-068). FRS-207.2 validation_results shall hold one row per EXECUTION of a test, each with its own result, actual result, executor and execution time, a new execution adding a row (D-068). FRS-207.3 The executor shall be stamped from auth.uid() and displayed with the result; a typed tester name, where kept, shall be shown beside it and never in place of it (D-068). FRS-207.4 The execution time shall be the time of that execution (D-068). FRS-207.5 A refused or failed save shall be stated on screen with the database’s reason (D-068). FRS-207.6 The Test Protocol shall display, per test, the latest execution and the number of earlier ones, and summarise recorded against total, passes and failures. FRS-207.7 A person who may not record shall see the results read-only, the screen saying so. FRS-207.8 The approval, CAPA and checklist evidence tables shall print blank for wet signature. RATIONALE: 0046 keys the table on test_id alone and sets executed_at only when it is empty, so a re-test overwrites the earlier result and keeps the FIRST date; the tester is free text; and a save the database refuses is ignored by the screen.

**FRS-208.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-208.1 Software Validation shall open by mod:/software-validation and present the package in tabs, each tab holding its own key and showing its own section and no other. FRS-208.2 The Requirements by Module tab shall list, per module, its requirements and their gaps — user requirements with no system requirement, system requirements with no test, user requirements with no test — and the screens with no requirement, each with its written reason. FRS-208.3 The Traceability Matrix shall list one row per link between a user requirement, a system requirement and a test, with counts, and shall name the tests outside it. FRS-208.4 The Traceability Summary shall state, counted from the package, how many user requirements have no system requirement and how many have no test, and mark each; only where both counts are zero shall it state that all have both. FRS-208.5 Software Validation shall print the tab on show, or every section as the full package. RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are D-073 — two tabs shared the key ‘trace’, so pressing either showed both, and the summary asserted "every requirement is covered" whatever the table beneath it showed.

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

**FRS-213.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-213.1 The menu shall show an entry exactly when the route guard would open its page for that person. FRS-213.2 The route guard shall state, for a known screen the person may not open, that they lack access and whom to ask, and shall send an unknown address to the Dashboard. FRS-213.3 The address /users shall open the User Master. FRS-213.4 The printable routes (/dc/, /declaration/, /ffr/, /indoor-pdt/, /indoor-register/, /indoor-dc/, /mtn/, /mrn-print/) shall render without the menu, their rows bounded by row-level security; /ffr/ shall require the Field Failure Register's module key, the three indoor routes the Indoor Service Register's, /mtn/ the Stock Transfer screen's and /mrn-print/ the Material Returns screen's. FRS-213.5 A screen that fails to render shall show an error in its own place, the menu and header remaining. FRS-213.6 While a saved session is restored the application shall show Loading rather than the sign-in screen. FRS-213.7 The menu shall be grouped, each group and the whole menu collapsible, the sidebar collapsible to icons and remembered per device, and shown as a drawer on a narrow screen; the Knowledge Base heading shall flash until a page in it has been opened on the device. FRS-213.8 The header search shall list the screens the person may open, and from three characters the records they may open (FRS-218); Enter shall open the highlighted entry, the first by default. FRS-213.9 The header shall show a breadcrumb (group · screen), the person’s name and designation, "Permission · <role>", and a menu offering My Profile, Clear Cache and Update, and Sign out. FRS-213.10 A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be able to switch between team calls and own calls, the choice remembered. FRS-213.11 The counts beside menu entries shall carry "+" where they are taken from a partial read. FRS-213.12 The update banner shall check version.json when the tab gains focus and every 5 minutes, name the new version only where it differs from the running one and otherwise say the running build is older, and Update now shall clear the screen caches, keep the offline registers and reload. FRS-213.13 Clear Cache and Update shall clear the screen and dropdown caches, the browser caches and service workers, and reload, keeping the offline registers. FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. RATIONALE: .1 because an entry shown on admin.view for a page that asks its own key is a menu that offers what the page then refuses; .12 because a banner that announces the version already running teaches people to dismiss it.

**FRS-024.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each build carries a version, build number and build ID shown in the footer; an in-app Version History lists changes; source and schema changes are version-controlled.

### URS-086 — The date a review was completed is corrected only by a person granted that right, and the correction is recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The date on which Review 1, 2 or 3 was completed is the date a reviewer is held to and the date a Field Failure Report raised from the review carries. The system shall set it itself when the stage completes, shall allow it to be corrected only by a person granted that right (an administrator, or a role given it on Roles & Permissions), and shall record every correction with the previous date, the new date, who made it and when. Holding the authority to complete a review shall not by itself allow the date of its completion to be changed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-106** — Correcting a review completion date | High | OQ-94 |

**FRS-106.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-106.1 The database shall stamp review2_at and review3_at with the day the stage completes, where the column is empty (0044); Review 1's date is the call's registration date (the register shows reg_date for it) and is not stored on the review, so it is corrected on the call, not here. FRS-106.2 The review drawer shall offer the set-date control only to holders of review.correct_date (an administrator holds it). FRS-106.3 The database shall refuse any change to review2_at or review3_at, other than the stamp of .1 and the clearing of a stage that becomes incomplete, from a caller without review.correct_date, a review imported by a holder of bulk.upload excepted (0302; review1_at is derived, not stored). FRS-106.4 The database shall record every change of a review completion date with the previous and new value, the person and the time, independently of the screen. RATIONALE: until 0302 the restriction was on the screen only, and a holder of review.edit could set any date through the API with nothing but a client-written audit entry behind it (D-020); .4 is still open.

### URS-134 — Authority given to one person beyond their role is deliberate, visible and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall let an administrator grant an individual person a permission their role does not carry, and shall show those individual grants wherever that person's access is set. Creating a login by copying another person shall copy their role and individual grants, shall grant sight of every record only where the administrator ticks it and shall say that it does, and shall be recorded with the person copied. The role written on the User Master shall reach the person's sign-in; a difference between the two shall be visible, correctable one person at a time, and each correction recorded. An individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, so authority that is not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-170** — Individual grants, clones, and the role on the sign-in | High | OQ-163 |

**FRS-170.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-170.1 The 🔐 Access drawer shall let an administrator set a person's role and tick individual permissions, held in `profiles.extra_permissions` and honoured by `has_perm()` on top of the role; the database shall accept the write only from an administrator. FRS-170.2 The Access drawer shall show every individual permission the person holds beside those the role gives. FRS-170.3 ⧉ Clone shall create a new login carrying the source person's role and individual permissions, shall add `data.view_all` only when “can see all records” is ticked, and shall say that ticking it grants sight of every record. FRS-170.4 Every access save, clone and login creation shall be written to the audit trail, a clone naming the person copied. FRS-170.5 Saving a User Master row whose role differs from the person's sign-in shall write the role to the sign-in, or say that it could not and which role the sign-in keeps; a person with no sign-in shall be told they receive it on first sign-in. FRS-170.6 The User Master shall count the people whose sign-in role differs from the directory, show “X (now Y)” against each, and offer to apply the directory's role, writing each person separately, naming each failure and auditing each change. RATIONALE: .2 because an individual grant does not appear on the role matrix, and authority not shown where access is set is authority nobody reviews. .6 one person at a time so that one failure does not leave the office unsure which of forty changes happened.

### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-112** — Every file download is gated, scoped and recorded | High | OQ-100 |
| **FRS-138** — One gate for every download | High | OQ-129 |
| **FRS-193** — One export gate for every format, and a record of each file | High | OQ-186 |
| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |
| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |

**FRS-112.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-112.1 xlsxDownload shall refuse, exactly as csvExport does, when the user does not hold export.data. FRS-112.2 A download control shall not be offered to a user who does not hold export.data. FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-193.3 The permission matrix export shall be permitted to a holder of rbac.manage or admin.view and shall pass the same export gate. ### URS-156 — A change to what a role may do is deliberate, confined to the roles changed, and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let an authorised administrator grant and remove, per role, the right to open each screen and each action on it; shall show every other administrator the same matrix read-only; and shall write, on saving, only the roles the administrator changed. The administrator role shall always hold every permission. Each change shall be recorded with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when. A person shall be able to see the permissions actually in effect for them and where they come from. A save that rewrites every role writes an administrator’s untouched tuning back to whatever the screen happened to hold, and a permission change recorded without what changed cannot answer the question an assessor asks of it: who could do this, on which day.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-203** — The permission matrix: stored, edited per role, saved per role, recorded | High | OQ-210, OQ-196 |
| **FRS-216** — My Profile: the account, the R&R period, and what I can do | Medium | OQ-214, OQ-209 |

**FRS-203.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-203.1 Roles & Permissions shall allow change to a holder of rbac.manage, display the matrix read-only to a holder of admin.view, and state to anyone else that they lack permission. FRS-203.2 Roles & Permissions shall display the permissions stored for each role and shall not re-seed the matrix over an edit in progress. FRS-203.3 Roles & Permissions shall group pages by menu heading, then page, then action, each level expandable, with controls expanding and collapsing every level. FRS-203.4 Roles & Permissions shall grant the right to open a page (View) and each action on it separately per role, and shall provide a control granting or removing every right on one page for one role. FRS-203.5 Roles & Permissions shall display the administrator role holding every permission, and shall not allow it to be narrowed. FRS-203.6 Roles & Permissions shall, on Save, write only the roles the operator changed, re-assert the administrator’s full set where it has fallen behind, and state "Nothing was changed" when nothing was. FRS-203.7 Roles & Permissions shall refuse to save a role left with no permission (URS-056). FRS-203.8 The system shall record each saved change with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when (D-067). FRS-203.9 Roles & Permissions shall export the matrix as .xlsx — a Matrix sheet (group, page, route, grant, key, Yes / No per role), a Roles sheet (permissions held, stored or NOT CONFIGURED fallback) and a How to read this sheet (who, when, saved or UNSAVED) — recorded as rbac.export and available to rbac.manage and admin.view. FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.11 Each page's row shall list every key its controls test, including a key of another module used on that page, so a control is governed by a tick shown where the control is (findings 63 and 64). FRS-203.12 The Installation Call and PM Call registers, the Contract Register, the Objective page, chart sharing, validation results, shared table layouts, the Product Database 2.0 rebuild, deleting a Tracker item and returning stock in another engineer's name shall each be governed by keys of their own, and each screen shall ask the key the database asks. FRS-203.13 A key may have parent keys; holding a parent shall grant its children in the database and in the application alike, from one list held in both (public.perm_parents, PERM_PARENTS), and the matrix shall show a child held through its parent as held; unticking it shall untick the parent and tick the parent's other children in their own right, so the role loses only that child (the user, 2026-10-02: “All Greyed out Permissions should be editable”). Manage users, Edit masters, Edit sales / warranties, Edit contracts and each register's Edit and Report keys shall be parents of their parts (finding 67). FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). FRS-203.15 A new per-page key shall be granted once to exactly the roles and people holding the key it replaces, and a re-run shall not restore a key an administrator has since removed. RATIONALE: .6 because permsForRole() returns the STORED set whenever it is non-empty, so a save that rewrote every role would replace an administrator’s tuning with whatever the screen held; .8 because rbac.save records only the role keys, and app_roles is not one of the ten tables record_audit covers — today nothing can say what a role could do on a given day.

**FRS-216.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-216.1 My Profile shall show the account: name, e-mail, designation, Permission (the role) and region. FRS-216.2 My Profile shall state, where the person’s profile did not load, that it did not and what they may do until it exists (FRS-210.5). FRS-216.3 A holder of users.manage or training.manage shall be able to change the period of a recorded R&R document, From remaining required and To not before it, the database stamping who last changed the row and when (sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on). FRS-216.4 My Profile shall show the role in effect, whether its permissions are stored or the built-in fallback, any personal extra permissions, and the actions and pages they grant, and shall say when an administrator is previewing another person. FRS-216.5 My Profile shall present its sections as tabs, one per section — Account, Details & R&R, Training, My Team (only where somebody reports to the person), What I can do, Signature, Password and Appearance — remembering the tab last opened on that device and opening Account when the remembered tab is not offered. FRS-216.6 My Team shall list the people reporting to the person in two groups by their User Master status (Active): Active / Current and Ex Employees, each with its count, the tab counting the current ones, and an ex employee’s profile, R&R and training remaining viewable. RATIONALE: .4 because a person told they cannot do something needs to see whether the role or the fallback is the reason, and the wrong answer there sends an administrator to tick the wrong box.

### URS-175 — An Indoor Service job received in error can be deleted, before it has left a trace

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

A job on the Indoor Service Register that was received in error — the wrong unit, a duplicate intake, a test entry — shall be deletable permanently, with its accessories, parts, checks and pre-delivery test, by a person given that right (an administrator by default, any other role only where Roles & Permissions grants it), who shall state why and confirm the job number. A job shall not be deletable once it has gone on an Indoor delivery challan, whatever became of the challan, or once its visit has been filed against its call. Each deletion shall be recorded by the system with the job number, product, serial, call, the reason, who and when; a deleted job's number shall not be issued again.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-238** — delete_indoor_job(): permanent, by its own key, refused once a DC or a filed visit names the job | High | OQ-228, OQ-229 |

**FRS-238.** *(v0.10.79 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-238.1 `delete_indoor_job(job_id, reason)` (0324, SECURITY DEFINER) shall be the only way to delete an Indoor Service job: it shall require indoor.delete (granted to no role by migration; an administrator passes has_perm()) and a non-blank reason; refuse a job carrying a DC No., a job named on any indoor_dc_lines row (an approved, pending or rejected DC), and a job whose visit_uid is set, each in its own words; otherwise delete the job's accessories, harvested parts, checks and Pre-Delivery Testing and then the job, leave indoor_job_counters untouched so the number is not reissued, and write audit_log `indoor.job_delete` naming the job no., product, serial, UCN, kind, activity, status, the reason and the counts deleted, who and when stamped from the session. FRS-238.2 It shall not be callable by the public key; signed-in users may call it (it asks the key itself). FRS-238.3 DELETE on indoor_jobs and indoor_pdt shall be revoked from the API roles, so a direct DELETE is refused for every signed-in user, an administrator included. FRS-238.4 The job window shall offer “Delete job” only to a holder of indoor.delete; it shall say why a job a DC or a filed visit names is kept, and otherwise ask for the reason and for the job number typed to confirm before calling the function, and write its own audit row only for a REFUSED attempt, as indoor.job_delete_refused, since delete_indoor_job() already records the deletion (D-147). FRS-238.5 A job that has been verified or re-verified, PDT-signed, reported to the customer, condemned or disposed of, or whose report is uploaded is a quality record and shall not be deleted; a QC result, checks, parts, accessories and an unsigned PDT do not stop the deletion (0336, D-142). RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-03, chose permanent deletion over keep-and-hide: “Allow Admin by default, rest I will update from Roles & Permissions”.

### URS-176 — Each master is added to, changed and deleted under rights of its own, and a row in use is never deleted

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The Party Master, the Product Master, the Part Master and each value list shall each have a right to add, a right to edit and a right to delete, granted role by role on Roles & Permissions, with edit and delete offered as buttons on each row of the register to those who hold them. Granting these rights shall take nothing from a role that could already add and edit masters. A party, a part or a product line that any machine, call, sale, contract, spare or stock record still names shall not be deleted, the refusal being the database's and saying how many records name it; deactivating or marking it inactive remains the way to withdraw it. The Product Database shall remain read-only.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-242** — One key to add, one to edit, one to delete per master, and the delete guard | High | OQ-232, OQ-242, OQ-247 |

FRS-242.2 Each add and edit key shall have masters.edit.records and masters.edit as parents, and each delete key masters.edit only, in public.perm_parents and PERM_PARENTS alike; no grant shall be written. ### URS-067 — Authority over a quality record is held section by section

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The authority to amend a call in progress shall be grantable SEPARATELY for each part of the record whose amendment means a different thing: the complaint as reported, the customer and device it names, the vigilance answers, and the customer’s contact details. Re-allocating a call to another engineer, and cancelling or restoring one, shall each be their own authority. A single “edit” right cannot express the distinction the record requires — correcting a telephone number and re-answering whether a patient was harmed are not the same act — and each shall be attributable to the person who performed it.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-132** — Editing a call, by section, and never once it is closed | High | OQ-120 |

| **FRS-079** — The call edit rights are four sections, plus allotment and cancellation | High | OQ-60 |

**FRS-132.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-132.1 Edit shall be offered on a call to any role holding `calls.edit` or any one of `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance`, `calls.edit.contact` or `calls.allot`. FRS-132.2 Fields outside the sections the role holds shall be read-only on the form, each naming the right it needs. FRS-132.3 A call whose state is Solved or Cancelled shall be read-only to every role, administrators included; the way back is Re-open (FRS-133.4) or Restore (FRS-133.3). **FRS-133.** *(v0.10.71 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-133.1 Cancel shall be offered only on a call whose state is Unattended or Unsolved, and `cancel_call()` shall refuse any other state. **FRS-079.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* `calls.edit.complaint`, `calls.edit.customer`, `calls.edit.vigilance` and `calls.edit.contact` each gate one part of the record and are granted independently; `calls.allot` gates re-allocation to another engineer and `calls.cancel` gates cancelling and restoring a call. `calls.edit` remains the parent, so a role holding it holds the four sections — `parentAction()` resolves a section key to it — and a role may instead be given one section alone. `cover.edit` is the equivalent authority over the warranty and contract registers, and `admin.view` opens the administration pages READ-ONLY, so somebody may inspect configuration without the right to change users.

### URS-063 — A read-only role holds no authority to write, and a derived role does not track its source

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Where a role is described as read-only it shall hold no permission that any write policy names, so that a refusal is the database’s and not a hidden control. Where a role is created by COPYING another, the copy shall be a one-time act and the two shall not thereafter be kept in step, so that granting an authority on one role cannot confer it on another. A periodic report shall state the write authority each such role holds; it shall present that as a matter for review rather than as a defect, because a grant may be deliberate and no re-application of configuration can remove one.

FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.11 Each page's row shall list every key its controls test, including a key of another module used on that page, so a control is governed by a tick shown where the control is (findings 63 and 64). FRS-203.12 The Installation Call and PM Call registers, the Contract Register, the Objective page, chart sharing, validation results, shared table layouts, the Product Database 2.0 rebuild, deleting a Tracker item and returning stock in another engineer's name shall each be governed by keys of their own, and each screen shall ask the key the database asks. FRS-203.13 A key may have parent keys; holding a parent shall grant its children in the database and in the application alike, from one list held in both (public.perm_parents, PERM_PARENTS), and the matrix shall show a child held through its parent as held; unticking it shall untick the parent and tick the parent's other children in their own right, so the role loses only that child (the user, 2026-10-02: “All Greyed out Permissions should be editable”). Manage users, Edit masters, Edit sales / warranties, Edit contracts and each register's Edit and Report keys shall be parents of their parts (finding 67). FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). FRS-203.15 A new per-page key shall be granted once to exactly the roles and people holding the key it replaces, and a re-run shall not restore a key an administrator has since removed. RATIONALE: .6 because permsForRole() returns the STORED set whenever it is non-empty, so a save that rewrote every role would replace an administrator’s tuning with whatever the screen held; .8 because rbac.save records only the role keys, and app_roles is not one of the ten tables record_audit covers — today nothing can say what a role could do on a given day.

**FRS-075.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* 0180 removes `review.edit` from the Zoho Migration role. It had arrived by copying: 0155 merged the Technical Support permission row into Zoho Migration on EVERY application of the RBAC bundle, so an authority granted deliberately on one role crossed to another silently. What it conferred was established against a database rather than read from the policy — `review.edit` grants ALL commands on `call_reviews`, and a user holding it answered a review, fired the trigger and raised a field failure report in their own name, a record the retention guard means can never be deleted. 0155 now SEEDS the role once and leaves it alone: two roles kept identical are one role with two names, and a separate role exists in order to diverge and be revoked without touching the other. The Technical Support grant is RETAINED, being the system owner’s decision. The status report tests only what the configuration bundle provides; the write authority each read-only role holds is reported by a diagnostic as a question for review, because a status row that reads NO on a deliberate grant sends somebody to re-apply configuration that cannot remove it.

### URS-056 — An access role always has a defined permission set

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

A role by which access is granted shall never exist without an explicit set of permissions. Where a role is added by configuration it shall be derived from an existing role, so that no role can be brought into use whose effective authority is implied rather than stated.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-203** — The permission matrix: stored, edited per role, saved per role, recorded | High | OQ-210, OQ-196 |
| **FRS-065** — A role is created only by derivation | High | OQ-50 |

**FRS-203.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-203.1 Roles & Permissions shall allow change to a holder of rbac.manage, display the matrix read-only to a holder of admin.view, and state to anyone else that they lack permission. FRS-203.2 Roles & Permissions shall display the permissions stored for each role and shall not re-seed the matrix over an edit in progress. FRS-203.3 Roles & Permissions shall group pages by menu heading, then page, then action, each level expandable, with controls expanding and collapsing every level. FRS-203.4 Roles & Permissions shall grant the right to open a page (View) and each action on it separately per role, and shall provide a control granting or removing every right on one page for one role. FRS-203.5 Roles & Permissions shall display the administrator role holding every permission, and shall not allow it to be narrowed. FRS-203.6 Roles & Permissions shall, on Save, write only the roles the operator changed, re-assert the administrator’s full set where it has fallen behind, and state "Nothing was changed" when nothing was. FRS-203.7 Roles & Permissions shall refuse to save a role left with no permission (URS-056). FRS-203.8 The system shall record each saved change with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when (D-067). FRS-203.9 Roles & Permissions shall export the matrix as .xlsx — a Matrix sheet (group, page, route, grant, key, Yes / No per role), a Roles sheet (permissions held, stored or NOT CONFIGURED fallback) and a How to read this sheet (who, when, saved or UNSAVED) — recorded as rbac.export and available to rbac.manage and admin.view. FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.11 Each page's row shall list every key its controls test, including a key of another module used on that page, so a control is governed by a tick shown where the control is (findings 63 and 64). FRS-203.12 The Installation Call and PM Call registers, the Contract Register, the Objective page, chart sharing, validation results, shared table layouts, the Product Database 2.0 rebuild, deleting a Tracker item and returning stock in another engineer's name shall each be governed by keys of their own, and each screen shall ask the key the database asks. FRS-203.13 A key may have parent keys; holding a parent shall grant its children in the database and in the application alike, from one list held in both (public.perm_parents, PERM_PARENTS), and the matrix shall show a child held through its parent as held; unticking it shall untick the parent and tick the parent's other children in their own right, so the role loses only that child (the user, 2026-10-02: “All Greyed out Permissions should be editable”). Manage users, Edit masters, Edit sales / warranties, Edit contracts and each register's Edit and Report keys shall be parents of their parts (finding 67). FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). FRS-203.15 A new per-page key shall be granted once to exactly the roles and people holding the key it replaces, and a re-run shall not restore a key an administrator has since removed. RATIONALE: .6 because permsForRole() returns the STORED set whenever it is non-empty, so a save that rewrote every role would replace an administrator’s tuning with whatever the screen held; .8 because rbac.save records only the role keys, and app_roles is not one of the ten tables record_audit covers — today nothing can say what a role could do on a given day.

**FRS-065.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Roles may be added from Roles & Permissions by a holder of rbac.manage. The form requires a source role and copies its permissions; a role cannot be created with an empty set, because has_perm() treats an empty permission array as unconfigured and falls back to the engineer defaults — an “empty” role would therefore grant an engineer’s authority. The key is derived as a slug from the name and cannot collide with an existing or reserved key. Roles are not deleted from this screen; a role in use is emptied or its users moved. Every role the database holds is drawn in the matrix and offered wherever a role is chosen.

**FRS-110.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-110.1 A report shall be editable from its table row or from Edit / weekly review on the desk, and both shall be offered only to holders of ffr.manage; the database (ffr_update) shall refuse anybody else. FRS-110.2 The edit form shall carry the weekly review date, the reviewer and the attachment, so that recording a weekly review clears Due a review. FRS-110.3 The update log (FRS-070) shall be shown with the report. FRS-110.4 The desk shall list reports with search and the chips All, Open and Due a review (open and not reviewed within 7 days), and shall show the report and the call as it stands now, in panes whose widths are remembered. FRS-110.5 The live call shall be shown beside each report, marked — withdrawn where the review no longer answers YES. FRS-110.6 ffr_read shall give a holder of ffr.view the whole register, and anybody else the reports on calls they may see or reports they raised (0165, 0176). FRS-110.7 An empty register shown to a reader without ffr.view shall say that it may be their access rather than an empty register. FRS-110.8 No report shall be deletable (0166). FRS-110.9 Year and product filters (opening on the current year, by FFR date, products limited to the chosen years) shall apply to the register and to Insights alike, and a filter matching nothing shall offer to clear them. FRS-110.10 The table view shall offer search, status buttons All, Open, Closed and Cancelled, and a CSV export available only to holders of export.data, warning when more than 5,000 rows were read.

**FRS-111.** *(v0.10.81 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-111.1 ffr_call_context() (0178) shall return the visits and spares of a report’s call to a caller holding ffr.view, an office role or administration, even where the caller cannot see the call itself. FRS-111.2 It shall return nothing for a UCN that carries no Field Failure Report, and nothing to a caller without that authority, so that it is not a general reader of calls. FRS-111.3 It shall leave the call’s own engineer and team with everything they could see before. FRS-111.4 The printable report (/ffr/:ffrNo) shall open only for a reader who may open the Field Failure Register (mod:/failure-report), and shall otherwise say that the reader cannot open it; within that, row-level security shall decide which report is found. FRS-111.5 The printable report shall lay out R-SER-03 Rev 02 from the same form definition as the Word copy (FRS-067), with Print, a Word copy download written to the audit trail, and Back to the register. FRS-111.6 The register's count shall carry a + once it reaches the 5,000 the register reads, and a failed read of the call report reviews shall be reported rather than read as no review (D-135). RATIONALE: .1 deliberately widens visibility (the user, 2026-09-12: a right to read a failure report that does not carry the visits it was raised from is not much of a right), so .2 is what keeps it to that and nothing more. .4 because the print route sits outside the module guard today (D-026).

**FRS-117.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-117.1 A section shall appear only when the reader holds the module key of the register behind it, tested before anything is requested, so that no request is made otherwise. FRS-117.2 Each section shall load on its own and in a fixed order, and a section that fails shall show its own error while the others arrive. FRS-117.3 Loading shall begin only once the reader’s reporting team is known. FRS-117.4 Spare Requests shall show Awaiting me, In approval, Awaiting dispatch, Dispatched, Received and Rejected, computed with the register’s own stage rule, each opening Spare Requests filtered to that stage. FRS-117.5 RM Approval shall show the number waiting, the engineers waiting and the longest wait in days. FRS-117.6 Pending Dispatch shall show spares waiting, those waiting a week or more, units, engineers and orders. FRS-117.7 Hand Stock shall show Short (opening Hand Stock filtered to short lines), units in the field, engineers holding, part codes, stock out, consumed and returned. FRS-117.8 Material Returns shall show MRNs, lines, good quantity and defective quantity; Stock Transfer shall show transfers, lines, units moved and engineers involved. FRS-117.9 Daily Complaint Review shall show exact counts of Review 1, 2 and 3 Pending, Any Potential Effect, Completed and Calls in view, each opening the register filtered to the rows counted — Any Potential Effect to the potential-effect calls (D-022). FRS-117.10 A count taken over a read that stopped at its 4,000-row budget shall carry a “+”. FRS-117.11 A card that is a figure shall open nothing and shall not be styled as a link. FRS-117.12 Each section shall offer Open the register; the page shall offer Refresh, the time of the last read and the number of cards, say Counting N more registers while sections load, say when not connected, and say when no register is open to the reader.

**FRS-131.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-131.1 Each register shall show the 800 most recent calls, Load more adding 800, and its count shall carry a “+” while more exist. FRS-131.2 Of the calls the database returns, an engineer shall be shown their own and a manager their team's; a call with no allottee shall be shown to every reader the database returns it to, so that the desk which must allot it can find it. FRS-131.11 Arriving with a UCN to edit shall open that call whether or not it is among the rows loaded, and arriving with a search shall open the register already searched. FRS-131.12 The same actions shall be offered in one order on the row and at the top of an opened call. FRS-131.13 A manager without `calls.allot` shall be told where the right is granted. **FRS-156.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-156.1 Spare Requests, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns and Stock Transfer shall read in pages of 1,000 with Load more, and shall mark their count with "+" while another page may exist. FRS-156.2 RM Approval (2,000), Pending Dispatch (2,000) and Stock Out (5,000) shall mark their count with "+" when their read reaches its limit. FRS-156.7 While an administrator previews another person's view ("View as"), a register shall show only the previewed person's rows, and never more than the administrator's own read returned. FRS-156.8 A register shall show the rows the database returns for the reader and apply no further role filter of its own. FRS-156.9 An export taken while more rows remain shall be preceded by a statement that it is partial (`exportscope`), and shall be refused without `export.data` (FRS-018). RATIONALE: .8 exists because Spare Consumption filters the rows row-level security already scoped a second time, by whichever engineer or e-mail column the data happens to carry — hiding rows the policy allowed, or none at all when the column is absent (D-047). .3 because Stock Out swallows any error but a missing table and reads "No stock outs yet" (D-046).

**FRS-165.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-165.1 Spare Requests, RM Approval, Pending Dispatch, Stock Out, Spare Consumption, Hand Stock, Material Returns (MRN) and Stock Transfer shall each open only for a holder of its own module key (`mod:/spare-requests`, `mod:/spare-rm-approval`, `mod:/spare-dispatch`, `mod:/stock-out`, `mod:/spare-consumption`, `mod:/handstock`, `mod:/mrn`, `mod:/stock-transfer`), granted per role on Roles & Permissions. FRS-165.2 Stock Out shall carry its own key, separate from Pending Dispatch's, and no action key. FRS-165.3 Hand Stock Report shall open for an administrator by default and for another role only by grant (FRS-160.1). FRS-165.4 Each action on these screens shall require its action key — `spare.request`, `spare.approve_rm`, `spare.approve_commercial`, `spare.approve_nsm`, `spare.drop`, `spare.dispatch`, `spare.receive`, `consumption.reconcile`, `stock.return`, `stock.transfer`, `export.data` — and the database shall refuse the write without it. FRS-165.5 The Delivery Challan and Declaration pages shall carry no module key and shall show only a stock out the reader's row-level access admits (FRS-154.1). RATIONALE: the module key opens a screen; the read policies decide its rows, so granting a key correctly and seeing an empty page is the other half, not a fault in the grant.

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-212.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-212.1 An administrator shall be able to choose any profile (searchable, the first 60 shown) and see the application with that person’s permissions until Exit, the choice surviving a reload, with a banner throughout. FRS-212.2 While previewing, the application shall refuse every write — insert, update, delete, a function call that writes, a file upload — stating that a preview is read-only (D-069). FRS-212.3 The system shall record each start and end of a preview with the administrator and the person previewed (D-069). FRS-212.4 A screen that narrows its rows to the previewed person (Hand Stock, Stock Transfer, MRN, Spare Requests) shall do so by that person’s name and address. RATIONALE: .2 — the component’s own comment says "Nothing is written — a read-only preview" and nothing enforces it; a write made during a preview runs under the administrator’s session while the screen shows another person, so the record is attributed to the administrator and believed to be the other person’s.

**FRS-213.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-213.1 The menu shall show an entry exactly when the route guard would open its page for that person. FRS-213.2 The route guard shall state, for a known screen the person may not open, that they lack access and whom to ask, and shall send an unknown address to the Dashboard. FRS-213.3 The address /users shall open the User Master. FRS-213.5 A screen that fails to render shall show an error in its own place, the menu and header remaining. FRS-213.6 While a saved session is restored the application shall show Loading rather than the sign-in screen. FRS-213.7 The menu shall be grouped, each group and the whole menu collapsible, the sidebar collapsible to icons and remembered per device, and shown as a drawer on a narrow screen; the Knowledge Base heading shall flash until a page in it has been opened on the device. FRS-213.8 The header search shall list the screens the person may open, and from three characters the records they may open (FRS-218); Enter shall open the highlighted entry, the first by default. FRS-213.9 The header shall show a breadcrumb (group · screen), the person’s name and designation, "Permission · <role>", and a menu offering My Profile, Clear Cache and Update, and Sign out. FRS-213.10 A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be able to switch between team calls and own calls, the choice remembered. FRS-213.11 The counts beside menu entries shall carry "+" where they are taken from a partial read. FRS-213.12 The update banner shall check version.json when the tab gains focus and every 5 minutes, name the new version only where it differs from the running one and otherwise say the running build is older, and Update now shall clear the screen caches, keep the offline registers and reload. FRS-213.13 Clear Cache and Update shall clear the screen and dropdown caches, the browser caches and service workers, and reload, keeping the offline registers. FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. RATIONALE: .1 because an entry shown on admin.view for a page that asks its own key is a menu that offers what the page then refuses; .12 because a banner that announces the version already running teaches people to dismiss it.

**FRS-003.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each role maps to a permission set (app_roles). Data visibility is scoped by a reporting tree resolved from User Master; enforced in the client and, authoritatively, by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.

**FRS-004.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every read/write is governed by RLS policies keyed on the authenticated user (auth.uid()) and SECURITY DEFINER helper functions; the UI gate is secondary.

**FRS-014.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Hand stock, transfers and returns are scoped to the reporting tree at the database, so a user sees only their own and their team’s stock.

**FRS-050.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Every view over a table carrying row-level security is created `security_invoker`, so the policies are evaluated for the READER. `create or replace view` does not carry the setting over, and a view running as its owner returns everything with no error and no warning. `npm run check:views` fails on any view over an RLS-protected table that lacks it, and `_status.sql` reports it on a live project; views intentionally readable by every signed-in user are enumerated with their reason.

Opened by `mod:/audit`.

### URS-128 — A material return records what came back, from whom, and in what condition

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall record each return of spares from an engineer to Stores against the paper slip it came with, stating each part, how many came back good and how many defective, and the call or customer it came from where known. An engineer shall return only their own stock; a return on another engineer's behalf shall be recorded only by somebody holding an administrator, approval or dispatch authority. No return shall exceed what the engineer holds. The system shall give each return its own unique reference, keep the slip number as written, and record the return in the audit trail. A return, once recorded, shall not be edited; a mistake is corrected by a further entry.

| **FRS-161** — Recording a material return | High | OQ-153 |
| **FRS-230** — The Material Return Note R/SER/STR/002, printed from what the return holds | Medium | OQ-224 |

FRS-161.2 The form shall fix the engineer to the signed-in person, and shall let a holder of `users.manage`, `spare.dispatch` or `spare.approve_rm` choose another engineer from the User Master. FRS-161.3 The database shall accept a return for another engineer only from an administrator or a holder of an approval or dispatch authority (`mr_insert`, `can_approve_spares`), and otherwise only a return of the caller's own stock. FRS-161.4 The form shall require the MRN No from the paper slip and keep it as written; the database shall assign the unique reference MRN-YYMM-NNNN. FRS-161.5 The form shall take an MRN date defaulting to today (see FRS-163). FRS-161.6 The form shall offer only parts the engineer holds, and shall not offer a part already on another line. FRS-161.7 The form shall take a good and a defective quantity per line, capped together at what the engineer holds less the other lines, and shall say why a typed value was reduced. FRS-161.8 The database shall refuse a return exceeding the engineer's holding (0039). FRS-161.9 The form shall refuse a submission with no engineer, no MRN No, no spare, a line of zero, or a line or part total above what is held, each with its own message; and shall say, with the hand-stock formula, when the engineer holds nothing. ### URS-129 — A hand-over of stock names two real engineers and is made by somebody who may make it

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall record a hand-over of spares from one engineer to another, naming both from the User Master's active engineers, never the same person twice. An engineer shall hand over only their own stock; a hand-over of another engineer's stock shall be recorded only by somebody holding an authority to act for others. No hand-over shall exceed what the giving engineer holds. The hand-over shall be recorded in the audit trail, and the register of hand-overs shall be readable in full. What the screen says about where stock comes from shall agree with how stock is counted. A hand-over to a name that is not a person is stock no engineer holds, and a hand-over anyone can make of anyone's stock moves a balance nobody decided to move.

FRS-162.8 Where the From engineer holds nothing, the form shall say so and state that stock comes from what Stores has dispatched to them, less what they have consumed, handed on or returned. FRS-162.10 The register shall list every transfer line the reader may see (either engineer in their scope), in pages with Load more, with "+" on its count while more remain, searchable by transfer number, engineers, part and remarks. ### URS-149 — Every file taken out of the system is authorised and recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit data to leave it as a file only to a person whose role holds the authority to export, whatever the format of the file and whatever screen it is taken from, and shall record each such file — who took it, when, from which report or tables, with what filter and how many rows. A file that was not produced shall not be recorded as produced. An authority checked for one format and not for another is a door locked on one side only, and a trail that shows a download the gate refused cannot be believed about the downloads it does show.

| **FRS-202** — Data Export: whole tables, and the schedules | High | OQ-195 |
| **FRS-249** — Every download can be saved as a Google Sheet in the exporter's own Drive folder | Medium | OQ-241 |

FRS-112.3 .1 and .2 shall apply to the workbooks of Product Failure Analysis (each block and the trend), of Field Failure Register Insights (the trend and the Pareto) and to the Objective evidence workbook, and to any workbook added later. FRS-112.4 Every workbook shall carry a sheet stating its scope, year and filters, the rules applied and its row count. FRS-112.5 A download taken over a partial read shall warn before the file is built (mayExport). FRS-112.6 Every download shall be written to the audit trail. FRS-112.7 A workbook’s raw sheet shall carry every column it builds — the Field Failure Pareto sheet’s “Machine the call named” included. FRS-112.8 check:ui shall refuse a download function that does not test the export permission. RATIONALE: the gate was written for CSV and the workbook writer was added beside it without it, so the raw review and failure rows behind each chart can be taken by a role refused export (D-018).

**FRS-138.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-138.1 Every download shall be refused, in every format, to a person without `export.data`, the refusal made by the shared writers (`csvExport`, `xlsxDownload`, `xlsDownload`) so that no screen can omit it. FRS-202.3 Data Export shall provide a search over table names, a control selecting every table shown, a control clearing the selection, and the approximate total of rows selected. FRS-202.4 Data Export shall read each chosen table as the signed-in person, row-level security in force, in pages of 1,000 under a stated order (D-065). FRS-249.3 Numbers shall arrive as numbers, dates as dates in dd-mmm-yyyy [hh:mm:ss], and everything else as text, so an identifier made of digits keeps its leading zeros. ### URS-157 — The audit trail is read only by those entitled, and is not left on a device

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall let a person entitled to read the audit trail search it by action, person and outcome and take it as a file; shall let nobody else read it; and shall keep no copy of it on a device after the person who fetched it has signed out. Both trails — what a user did and what a record became — shall be readable by the same people and by nobody else. A trail readable by a screen’s audience but not by the database’s is an empty page that reads as "nothing happened".

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-204** — Reading the audit trail | High | OQ-197 |

**FRS-204.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-204.1 The Audit Log shall open for a holder of audit.view, and the database shall return audit_log rows to an administrator or a holder of audit.view and to nobody else (D-066). FRS-204.2 The Audit Log shall list the time, the user, the e-mail, the role, the action, the target, the outcome, the duration and the error. FRS-204.3 The Audit Log shall filter in the database by action and by e-mail on any part of the value, and by outcome. FRS-204.4 The Audit Log shall load further rows 500 at a time. FRS-204.5 The Audit Log shall provide a refresh stating when it last synchronised, and shall re-synchronise every 30 minutes while no filter is set. FRS-204.6 The Audit Log shall keep at most 1,500 rows in the browser for a quick first display, labelled "Showing cached — synced … ago", and those rows shall be removed at sign-out (FRS-211.2) (D-070). FRS-204.7 The Audit Log shall export the rows loaded as CSV through the export gate, asking first where more rows exist than are loaded. FRS-204.8 The Audit Log shall remember its column layout per person. FRS-204.9 The record-level trail (record_audit) shall be readable only by an administrator or a holder of audit.view and writable through no application path. RATIONALE: .1 — the screen admits audit.view while audit_read (0009) admits is_admin() alone, so a non-administrator granted audit.view opens a page that is always empty and reads as "nothing happened"; record_audit_read already admits both, and the two trails should answer to the same audience.

### URS-164 — A device keeps nobody’s records after they leave, and a preview changes nothing

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When a person signs out, the system shall remove from that device every copy of records it holds for them — the offline registers, the screen caches, the audit rows, the counts beside the menu — so that the next person on a shared device sees nothing of theirs. An administrator previewing the system as another person shall see what that person would be shown, shall be unable to write anything while previewing, and each preview shall be recorded. A preview that writes does so under the administrator’s own identity while the screen shows somebody else’s, so the record produced is attributed to neither of the people who believe they made it.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-211** — Sign-out leaves nothing on the device | High | OQ-204 |
| **FRS-212** — View as: a preview that writes nothing | High | OQ-205 |

**FRS-211.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-211.1 Sign-out shall record logout, clear the person’s notifications, report and then delete the offline machine and party copy, and end any preview. FRS-211.2 Sign-out shall remove every screen cache (rithi.cache.*, rithi.sync.*), the cached Audit Log rows included (D-070). FRS-211.3 The counts beside menu entries shall be held per person, shown only to that person, and removed at sign-out (D-070). RATIONALE: .2 and .3 — the offline registers were wiped at sign-out, and the screen caches beside them were not; on a shared device the next person opens the Audit Log to the previous person’s cached rows and reads the previous person’s counts beside the menu.

**FRS-212.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-212.1 An administrator shall be able to choose any profile (searchable, the first 60 shown) and see the application with that person’s permissions until Exit, the choice surviving a reload, with a banner throughout. FRS-212.2 While previewing, the application shall refuse every write — insert, update, delete, a function call that writes, a file upload — stating that a preview is read-only (D-069). FRS-212.3 The system shall record each start and end of a preview with the administrator and the person previewed (D-069). FRS-212.4 A screen that narrows its rows to the previewed person (Hand Stock, Stock Transfer, MRN, Spare Requests) shall do so by that person’s name and address. RATIONALE: .2 — the component’s own comment says "Nothing is written — a read-only preview" and nothing enforces it; a write made during a preview runs under the administrator’s session while the screen shows another person, so the record is attributed to the administrator and believed to be the other person’s.

FRS-204.6 The Audit Log shall keep at most 1,500 rows in the browser for a quick first display, labelled "Showing cached — synced … ago", and those rows shall be removed at sign-out (FRS-211.2) (D-070). FRS-204.7 The Audit Log shall export the rows loaded as CSV through the export gate, asking first where more rows exist than are loaded. FRS-204.8 The Audit Log shall remember its column layout per person. FRS-204.9 The record-level trail (record_audit) shall be readable only by an administrator or a holder of audit.view and writable through no application path. RATIONALE: .1 — the screen admits audit.view while audit_read (0009) admits is_admin() alone, so a non-administrator granted audit.view opens a page that is always empty and reads as "nothing happened"; record_audit_read already admits both, and the two trails should answer to the same audience.

FRS-206.2 The SLA targets, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.87 (FRS-254), shall accept hours of at least 1 and on/off per rule, save only the rules changed, and display the defaults, naming 0044, where the table is missing or empty. FRS-206.3 The Hotline desk shall be chosen from the Hotline profiles, saved on choice, fall back to the single hotline profile when cleared, and display who new calls resolve to now; where no desk exists the card shall say so, and a failure to load shall name call_requests.sql. RATIONALE: .6 because none of the three cards writes an audit entry and neither table is under record_audit, so a Review 2 verdict that differs from last month’s cannot be traced to the rule change that caused it.

**FRS-210.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-210.1 Sign-in shall authenticate against Supabase Auth by e-mail and password and state in plain words a wrong password and an unconfirmed address. FRS-210.2 A released build shall offer no other way in — no local demo account and no sheet-era User Master sign-in — whatever the browser’s stored connection (D-074). FRS-210.3 A person whose profile cannot be read shall be signed out with the error. FRS-210.4 A person with no profile shall have one created from their User Master row, carrying that row’s role. FRS-210.5 A person with neither a profile nor a User Master row shall remain signed in as an unresolved identity holding NO permission, in the application and in the database, with a banner saying so (D-074). FRS-210.6 The client’s list of super administrators shall equal public.app_super_admins, a change to one being made with the other (0156). FRS-210.7 Changing a password shall verify the current password first and require a new one of at least 8 characters, confirmed and different from the current one, and shall be offered to database logins only. FRS-210.8 A reset or invite link shall set a password of at least 8 characters, confirmed; Cancel shall sign out; an expired link shall return to sign-in stating why. FRS-210.9 The sign-in screen and the reset screen shall give one remedy for a forgotten or expired password: ask an administrator (D-074). FRS-210.10 A change to a role’s permissions shall reach an open session when its tab next becomes visible, at most once a minute. FRS-210.11 The system shall record each sign-in as login, each refused sign-in as login_failed with the address typed, the error and the duration, and each sign-out as logout. RATIONALE: .5 — has_perm() fell back to the engineer permissions whenever the caller’s role row was empty or absent, so a login the organisation did not know held an engineer’s write authority (fixed by 0300: a signed-in login with no profile gets FALSE); .2 — a fallback sign-in was reachable by saving a connection that is not a Supabase project URL (removed).

**FRS-211.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-211.1 Sign-out shall record logout, clear the person’s notifications, report and then delete the offline machine and party copy, and end any preview. FRS-211.2 Sign-out shall remove every screen cache (rithi.cache.*, rithi.sync.*), the cached Audit Log rows included (D-070). FRS-211.3 The counts beside menu entries shall be held per person, shown only to that person, and removed at sign-out (D-070). RATIONALE: .2 and .3 — the offline registers were wiped at sign-out, and the screen caches beside them were not; on a shared device the next person opens the Audit Log to the previous person’s cached rows and reads the previous person’s counts beside the menu.

**FRS-212.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-212.1 An administrator shall be able to choose any profile (searchable, the first 60 shown) and see the application with that person’s permissions until Exit, the choice surviving a reload, with a banner throughout. FRS-212.2 While previewing, the application shall refuse every write — insert, update, delete, a function call that writes, a file upload — stating that a preview is read-only (D-069). FRS-212.3 The system shall record each start and end of a preview with the administrator and the person previewed (D-069). FRS-212.4 A screen that narrows its rows to the previewed person (Hand Stock, Stock Transfer, MRN, Spare Requests) shall do so by that person’s name and address. RATIONALE: .2 — the component’s own comment says "Nothing is written — a read-only preview" and nothing enforces it; a write made during a preview runs under the administrator’s session while the screen shows another person, so the record is attributed to the administrator and believed to be the other person’s.

**FRS-021.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* TWO TRAILS AGAIN, as of 0225 (2026-09-21). `audit_log` records what a USER DID — action, target, duration, outcome, actor and time — and its retention is configurable (app_settings.audit_retention_days, default ~10 years), with a daily digest built to archive the day off-database (supabase/functions/daily-digest) THAT HAS NEVER BEEN DEPLOYED — so no off-database archive exists today. Its LIMITS are stated rather than glossed: it is written by the CLIENT, so it can be bypassed by a direct API call, and it is purged when the retention window passes. THE SECOND TRAIL IS BACK ON. `record_audit` records what a ROW BECAME, before and after, in triggers that CANNOT BE BYPASSED and that nothing purges — stopped by 0112 on 2026-09-05 when it was thought to exist only for 21 CFR Part 11, and re-armed by 0225 at the user’s direction on 2026-09-21. The event that settled it was not a regulatory one: on 2026-09-20 a re-applied bundle set 4,222 calls back to Unattended, and NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM COULD SAY WHAT THEY HAD BEEN. A client-written trail cannot answer that, because the write did not come through the client. 0103’s shape is what was restored, not 0048’s: a BULK load is ONE attributable event rather than a row per record, so the trail stays about what people did. The table also still holds everything it captured 2026-08 to 2026-09-05; that gap, 05-Sep to 21-Sep, is real and is not recoverable.

### URS-151 — A bulk load is seen before it is written, and is recorded

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall permit a register to be loaded from a file only by an administrator. Before anything is written — including any record the load must create for its rows to refer to — the system shall show what will be written, what will be held back and why, and what the file carries that will not be loaded, and shall ask the operator to confirm the number of rows and whether loading the same file again would correct them or add them a second time. A load that stops part-way shall state how much of it was written. Every load shall be recorded with who ran it, into which register, from which file, and how many rows were written and held back. A bulk load writes more quality records in a minute than a person writes in a year: one that is not previewed makes its mistakes at that rate, and one that is not recorded leaves nobody able to say where the records came from.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-196** — Bulk Uploads: pick, preview, confirm, write, report | High | OQ-189 |
| **FRS-197** — How a file becomes rows | High | OQ-190 |
| **FRS-201** — The legacy importer on Admin Config | High | OQ-194 |

**FRS-196.** *(v0.10.152 · 08-Oct-2026)* FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.2 Bulk Uploads shall state, where the database is not connected, that it must be connected in Settings first. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158).

**FRS-197.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-197.1 The importer shall hold back and name a row missing any required column, and shall load no fragment of it. FRS-197.2 The importer shall hold back by name the rows a register’s rules declare impossible — a spare line of quantity below one, a return of nothing, a transfer to the same engineer, a dispatch of nothing, an opening balance of nothing — so the rest of the file loads. FRS-197.3 The importer shall, where a file carries several headings for one column, take the heading of highest alias priority and keep the others in the row’s extra data. FRS-197.4 The importer shall write the value a register stamps (call type, list name, source) over the file’s own column of that name, and shall not copy that column into extra. FRS-197.5 The importer shall read a date day-first, reading a date column month-first only where its own values prove it, and the preview shall say so. FRS-197.6 The importer shall keep in extra a cell a typed column cannot read, rather than drop it. FRS-197.7 The importer shall keep a heading the register does not map in the row’s extra data — or report it as not loaded where the register has no extra — and shall drop a heading the register declares unwanted, reporting it as ignored. FRS-197.8 The importer shall resolve rows repeating one key within a file by keeping the last, except where the register adds their quantities (the WinMax opening-stock export). FRS-197.9 The importer shall apply the controlled vocabularies while shaping — cover to WGP / OGP / CMC / AMC, approvals to Approved / Rejected, part category to its title case — and shall pass an unrecognised value through unchanged. FRS-197.10 The importer shall, on a register declared blanksClear (the Product Database), send an empty value where the file carries the heading and leaves the cell blank, and shall never blank a stamped or a required column. RATIONALE: .9 passes an unknown value through because a guess written into a quality record is worse than a value that reads as odd — the odd one gets reported. .10 is the stated exception to URS-040 (amended in this revision) and exists because an upload that could only ADD a value could never carry a correction made at source (D-006). Proved by npm run check:uploads.

**FRS-201.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-201.1 The legacy importer shall show only to an administrator, on Admin Config, with a banner directing every register it does not handle to Bulk Uploads. FRS-201.2 The legacy importer shall display the row counts of user_directory, material_returns and the four cover tables, with a control recounting them, a failed count reading as an error rather than as empty. FRS-201.3 The legacy importer shall detect each chosen file’s table from its headings, mark a file it does not recognise, and explain the MRN form-data tab. FRS-201.4 The legacy importer shall show, before writing, what each file will write, and shall write only on confirmation (D-071). FRS-201.5 The legacy importer shall upsert the four cover tables on their numbers. FRS-201.6 The legacy importer shall match User Master and MRN rows on a natural key, so a re-import corrects rather than adds (D-071). FRS-201.7 The legacy importer shall state, before Normalise cover runs — automatically after a cover import or on demand — how many item values it will hand back to their entry and in which fields, and shall run it only on confirmation (URS-072) (D-071). FRS-201.8 The legacy importer shall record every import and every normalisation in the audit trail (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because a second User Master row for one person changes visible_engineer_names() — who sees whose calls — and a second MRN row changes an engineer’s stock; .7 because URS-072 requires the statement before the discard and this is the one path that discards without it.
