### URS-179 — A product failure is a field call within months of installation, measured over a rolling period

*v0.10.87 · 04-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall compute each product failure rate objective as the share of the machines of that product installed (warranty start) in a rolling period ending at the month’s cut-off that had a field call on their serial within a stated number of months of installation, counting a machine once however many calls it had, and leaving out a cancelled call, a call before installation and a machine with no warranty start. The number of months and the rolling period shall be maintainable by an administrator, or by a role the administrator grants, on an SLA / Objective Configuration page under Admin, without a code change, defaulting to 3 and 12; every change shall be recorded with the old and new value, who and when; and a change shall alter no figure already written until the objectives are re-calculated. By default only the Admin role shall be given that page. The user, 2026-10-04: "For Product Failures, The Concept is - Failure Within 3 Months, But a Rolling Average for 12 Months".

### URS-158 — A fault repeating across the fleet is caught by the review

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

In addition to a repeat failure on one machine (URS-046), the review shall determine whether the same Standard Complaint has arisen on several DIFFERENT machines of one product within a stated number of days, counting distinct serial numbers rather than calls, and shall state which of the two rules fired. The rule shall be switchable, and its window and threshold maintainable by an administrator without a code change; answers already recorded shall be left as they were. A batch, a component or a design fault reaches the review as a first failure on each machine it touches, so a rule about one machine can never see it.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-205** — Frequent failure rule 2: the same complaint across the fleet | High | OQ-198 |

**FRS-205.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-205.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a fleet failure where the same Standard Complaint appears on at least the stated number of distinct serials of the same product within the stated number of days, the call under review counted. FRS-205.2 frequent_failure(ucn) shall count distinct serials, so repeated calls on one serial do not fire the fleet rule. FRS-205.3 frequent_failure(ucn) shall report a call a frequent failure where either rule fires, and shall name which rule fired. FRS-205.4 The fleet rule’s on/off, window (days, at least 1, default 30) and distinct serials (at least 2, default 2) shall be held in app_settings and editable in Admin Config. FRS-205.5 The window of the fleet rule shall be held in DAYS and separately from rule 1’s window in months, so a change to one cannot move the other. FRS-205.6 An answer already recorded in call_reviews.frequent_failure shall not be re-based when a rule changes. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-15: "Rule 2, Same Complaint across same product, but multiple serial nos in the last 30 days." Thirty days and a month differ in February, which is why it is days. Proved by supabase/tests/frequent_failure_rule2_test.sql.

### URS-159 — A change to a rule that decides a quality answer is attributable

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The service-level targets, the Hotline desk that new calls are filed to, and the frequent-failure rules shall be changeable only by an administrator or a holder of the configuration authority, and every change shall be recorded with the previous and the new value, who changed it and when. These settings alter no record already written, but they decide the next thousand: a verdict recorded under one rule and read months later under another can only be explained if the change is on record.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-206** — Admin Config: the settings that decide quality answers | High | OQ-199 |
| **FRS-254** — SLA / Objective Configuration, and the failure-within-months rule | High | OQ-250 |

**FRS-206.** *(v0.10.89 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-206.1 Admin Config shall present the legacy importer, the Hotline desk and Audit Mode on one page, opened by mod:/admin-config. FRS-206.2 The SLA targets, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.87 (FRS-254), shall accept hours of at least 1 and on/off per rule, save only the rules changed, and display the defaults, naming 0044, where the table is missing or empty. FRS-206.3 The Hotline desk shall be chosen from the Hotline profiles, saved on choice, fall back to the single hotline profile when cleared, and display who new calls resolve to now; where no desk exists the card shall say so, and a failure to load shall name call_requests.sql. FRS-206.4 The frequent-failure rules, on SLA / Objective Configuration since 0.10.89 (FRS-254.6), shall be saved by an administrator or a holder of config.manage, the card stating on saving that the rule applies from now on and that recorded answers are unchanged. FRS-206.5 The database shall refuse a change to sla_rules or app_settings from anyone other than an administrator or a holder of config.manage. FRS-206.6 The system shall record each change to an SLA target, the Hotline desk or a frequent-failure rule with the setting, its previous and new value, who changed it and when (D-067). RATIONALE: .6 because none of the three cards writes an audit entry and neither table is under record_audit, so a Review 2 verdict that differs from last month’s cannot be traced to the rule change that caused it.

**FRS-254.** *(v0.10.89 · 04-Oct-2026)* FRS-254.1 SLA / Objective Configuration shall be opened by mod:/sla-objective-config, listed under Administration, and given by default to the Admin role with config.manage and objective.manage, and to Technical Support with the page alone, its cards read-only until those actions are ticked (0358); every other role shall be granted it on Roles & Permissions. FRS-254.2 It shall present the SLA targets (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.2) and the Product Failure rule: the months after installation within which a field call is a failure (default 3) and the rolling period (default 12), each a whole number from 1 to 120, editable by a holder of objective.manage, and the database shall refuse the change from anyone else. FRS-254.3 objective_value() for failure_rate_12m shall return, for the period end E, the machines of the product (and serial pattern) with a serial and a warranty start in (E − rolling months, E] that have a non-cancelled field call on the same serial (trimmed, case-blind) and product pattern registered from the warranty start to the warranty start plus the window months and not after E, over all such machines; NULL when there are none. FRS-254.4 objective_evidence() shall return one failure row per failed machine (its first call in the window, with the installation date, the days after it and the number of calls in the window), the installed machines, and a filter row stating the rule, so the workbook counts to the figure. FRS-254.5 A missing setting shall fall back to 3 and 12; a change shall be stamped with who and when from the session and recorded in the audit trail with the old and new value; no figure shall change until Re-calculate. FRS-254.7 Re-calculating every computed objective of a year shall complete within the database statement time limit on a register of 20,000 machines and 40,000 calls: the failure rate shall be computed as one join of the window’s machines to the window’s calls, planned with its values on every run (0359; measured 0.7 s for six objectives over ten months, against about 47 s for 0357, which timed out on the live project). FRS-254.6 It shall also present the frequent-failure rules Review 2 applies (moved from Admin Config, FRS-206.4), unchanged in behaviour and permission. RATIONALE: the user, 2026-10-04, and the four answers given that day: warranty start is installation; the rate is over machines installed; it replaces the earlier rule (every field call in 12 months over the whole install base); the SLA targets move to the new page. "By Default Grant Permission to Admin - All Actions, Rest let the Admin Decide through the App"; later the same day, "Grant the page to Technical Support as well, Move Frequent Failure -- the rule Review 2 applies also to this Page".

### URS-179 — A product failure is a field call within months of installation, measured over a rolling period

*v0.10.87 · 04-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

The system shall compute each product failure rate objective as the share of the machines of that product installed (warranty start) in a rolling period ending at the month’s cut-off that had a field call on their serial within a stated number of months of installation, counting a machine once however many calls it had, and leaving out a cancelled call, a call before installation and a machine with no warranty start. The number of months and the rolling period shall be maintainable by an administrator, or by a role the administrator grants, on an SLA / Objective Configuration page under Admin, without a code change, defaulting to 3 and 12; every change shall be recorded with the old and new value, who and when; and a change shall alter no figure already written until the objectives are re-calculated. By default only the Admin role shall be given that page. The user, 2026-10-04: "For Product Failures, The Concept is - Failure Within 3 Months, But a Rolling Average for 12 Months".

## Software Validation `/software-validation`

Opened by `mod:/software-validation`.

### URS-160 — Validation evidence is attributable, and every execution is kept

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall record the result of each execution of a validation test with the person who executed it, taken from the authenticated session, and the date it was executed. A later execution of the same test shall be recorded as a further execution and shall not replace the earlier one. A result that could not be saved shall be reported to the person recording it, and a person without the authority to record shall not be offered the means to. Validation evidence that is overwritten on re-test shows a pass where a failure was recorded, dated to the first attempt, under a name anybody could have typed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-207** — Recording the execution of a validation test | High | OQ-200 |

**FRS-207.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-207.1 Software Validation shall offer result recording (Pass / Fail / N/A and the actual result) only to a person the database permits to record — an administrator or a holder of config.manage (D-068). FRS-207.2 validation_results shall hold one row per EXECUTION of a test, each with its own result, actual result, executor and execution time, a new execution adding a row (D-068). FRS-207.3 The executor shall be stamped from auth.uid() and displayed with the result; a typed tester name, where kept, shall be shown beside it and never in place of it (D-068). FRS-207.4 The execution time shall be the time of that execution (D-068). FRS-207.5 A refused or failed save shall be stated on screen with the database’s reason (D-068). FRS-207.6 The Test Protocol shall display, per test, the latest execution and the number of earlier ones, and summarise recorded against total, passes and failures. FRS-207.7 A person who may not record shall see the results read-only, the screen saying so. FRS-207.8 The approval, CAPA and checklist evidence tables shall print blank for wet signature. RATIONALE: 0046 keys the table on test_id alone and sets executed_at only when it is empty, so a re-test overwrites the earlier result and keeps the FIRST date; the tester is free text; and a save the database refuses is ignored by the screen.

### URS-161 — The validation package is shown truthfully in the system

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall present its own validation package — plan, requirements, risk, tests, defects and traceability — to an administrator, section by section, and shall print any section or the whole. Every count and every statement of coverage in it shall be computed from the package itself rather than written as a claim. A summary that states every requirement is covered, beside a table showing otherwise, is the one sentence an assessor reads first.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-208** — The validation package, section by section | Medium | OQ-201 |

**FRS-208.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-208.1 Software Validation shall open by mod:/software-validation and present the package in tabs, each tab holding its own key and showing its own section and no other. FRS-208.2 The Requirements by Module tab shall list, per module, its requirements and their gaps — user requirements with no system requirement, system requirements with no test, user requirements with no test — and the screens with no requirement, each with its written reason. FRS-208.3 The Traceability Matrix shall list one row per link between a user requirement, a system requirement and a test, with counts, and shall name the tests outside it. FRS-208.4 The Traceability Summary shall state, counted from the package, how many user requirements have no system requirement and how many have no test, and mark each; only where both counts are zero shall it state that all have both. FRS-208.5 Software Validation shall print the tab on show, or every section as the full package. RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are D-073 — two tabs shared the key ‘trace’, so pressing either showed both, and the summary asserted "every requirement is covered" whatever the table beneath it showed.

### URS-162 — How a record moves between screens is drawn from the validation, and checked

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall show, as diagrams, how a record moves from one screen to the next — a call through its spares, closure, consumption and feedback; a review to its Field Failure Report and the Objective; an engineer’s hand stock; a sale to its installation, cover and preventive maintenance — with every step naming the screen it happens on and the requirements and tests that state it. The diagrams shall be drawn from one definition held with the validation package, shown both to the people using the system and in the validation package, printed with the package, and checked so that a step naming a screen, a requirement or a test that does not exist cannot be released. A drawn diagram is one more copy of the truth, and the copy nobody checks is the one that goes stale unnoticed.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. RATIONALE: .1 because an entry shown on admin.view for a page that asks its own key is a menu that offers what the page then refuses; .12 because a banner that announces the version already running teaches people to dismiss it.

**FRS-024.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each build carries a version, build number and build ID shown in the footer; an in-app Version History lists changes; source and schema changes are version-controlled.

"By Default Grant Permission to Admin - All Actions, Rest let the Admin Decide through the App"; later the same day, "Grant the page to Technical Support as well, Move Frequent Failure -- the rule Review 2 applies also to this Page".

### URS-166 — Where the system reads and writes its records is not a device preference

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

The system shall read and write its records in the database it was released for. A change of that database, or of the bridge through which documents are filed to the document store, shall be permitted only to an administrator, shall be visible on every screen for as long as it is in force, and shall be recorded. A browser pointed at another project writes every call it registers and every visit it files there, while every screen looks exactly as it did.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-214** — Settings: the database and the document bridge | High | OQ-207 |

**FRS-214.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-214.1 Settings shall allow change to a holder of users.manage.settings (held through Manage users, its parent, or ticked on its own since 0286), and display read-only to a holder of admin.view, and direct anyone else to My Profile. FRS-214.2 The database connection shall take a Supabase project URL and publishable key, save them in this browser, and test them by counting calls. FRS-214.3 Every screen shall display a banner while the browser is connected to a database other than the one the build was released with (D-072). FRS-214.4 The system shall record every change of the database connection or of the CallReg bridge URL with who, when, and the old and new address, and never the key (D-067). FRS-214.5 The CallReg bridge shall take the Web App URL and the Field tab, list the sheet’s tabs on Test, and be saved in this browser; a newer DEFAULT_SHEETS_URL shall supersede a stored one through DEFAULT_URL_VERSION. FRS-214.6 The Design System Defaults section shall be descriptive only. FRS-214.7 Document Templates shall be held in this browser and read by nothing, and Reset Demo Data shall, after confirmation, clear this browser’s demo store except users and reload. RATIONALE: MODULES_WITHOUT_REQUIREMENT recorded Settings as "per-device preferences — nothing about the quality record depends on them". The database connection decides where every record this browser creates is written, and the bridge carries documents to Drive; that statement is withdrawn (D-072).

### URS-084 — The reviewer sees the evidence a failure judgement rests on

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: High. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

When answering Review 2 and Review 3 for a call, the reviewer shall be shown, beside the questions and without leaving the review: the call as registered; the Review 1 vigilance answers given at registration, which the review cannot alter; the machine’s age at failure, flagged where it failed within its first year and stated as not known where it cannot be computed; whether the call is a repeat failure under BOTH rules applied — the same machine failing again, and the same complaint on several machines of the same product — with the earlier calls behind the verdict; the visits recorded, with the latest hour meter, software version and pending reason; the spares consumed; the signed service report; and the machine’s history. The consequence of the answers (Any Potential Effect, and that a Field Failure Report will be raised) shall be shown before they are saved. A judgement on patient risk made without its evidence in view cannot later be defended.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-103** — The evidence beside the review | High | OQ-91 |
| **FRS-104** — Repeat failure across the fleet (rule 2) | High | OQ-92 |

**FRS-103.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-103.1 The review shall show a call card: call number, call date, customer, product and serial, engineer, call status and nature of complaint, the UCN coloured by call state. FRS-103.2 The review shall show Review 1 (public health threat, death, serious incident, completed or pending, date) read-only. FRS-103.3 The review shall show the age at failure under Warranty Failure, with a WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR warning below 366 days and “not known” where no warranty start is recorded. FRS-103.4 The review shall show, from the reports, the hour meter of the latest visit, the software version, the pending reason, and every visit newest first with its status, engineer and job done. FRS-103.5 The review shall display the signed service report inside the screen. FRS-103.6 The review shall list the spares booked against the call with part number, description and quantity. FRS-103.7 The review shall open a Machine History pop-up for the call’s machine under the reader’s own visibility. FRS-103.8 The review shall show Any Potential Effect worked out from the three answers as they are chosen, and state that a Field Failure Report is to be raised when it reads YES, before anything is saved. FRS-103.9 All NO shall fill the three Review 2 answers and shall not save them. FRS-103.10 A context read that fails shall say that it could not be read rather than show an empty list.

**FRS-104.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-104.1 frequent_failure(ucn) shall return a verdict of frequent when rule 1 (FRS-054) or rule 2 holds, and shall say which fired. FRS-104.2 Rule 2 shall hold where the same standard complaint is recorded on at least ffr.rule2_serials DISTINCT serials of the same product (default 2, never fewer than 2) within ffr.rule2_window_days before the call (default 30), counting serials and not calls. FRS-104.3 Rule 2 shall be switchable by ffr.rule2_enabled, and its window and serial count held in app_settings separately from rule 1’s. FRS-104.4 The review shall show, for each rule, the count, the threshold and the earlier UCNs with date, days before, engineer and what they matched on. FRS-104.5 Answers already recorded shall not be re-based when a rule or its settings change. RATIONALE: URS-046 names the procedure’s rule, which is rule 1; rule 2 (0198, the user’s of 2026-09-15) sees the batch, component or design fault that rule 1 cannot, because every one of those calls is a first failure on its own machine.

### URS-090 — What fails and why is analysed from the review record, and says how much of it was read

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because its own words name this screen.*

Authorised users shall be able to analyse the review register by product (as reviewed), cover, root cause, complaint grouping, standard complaint, spare category, machine, software version and age at failure, as ranked charts with their tables, narrowed by clicking any value, and as trends by month, quarter or year; shall be able to build a chart of their own and keep it, or share it with a role or with everyone where authorised to share; and shall be told how many reviews were read, with a “+” where they were not all read, and when a figure includes migrated history. Sharing a chart shall never let a reader see records they could not otherwise see.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-113** — Product Failure Analysis and Field Failure Insights | Medium | OQ-101 |

**FRS-113.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-113.1 Product Failure Analysis shall read field_call_review in pages up to 8,000 rows, and a figure taken over a capped read shall carry a “+”; Refresh and the time of the last read shall be shown. FRS-113.2 It shall open on the current year, dating a review by complaint date or else registration date, and Every year shall warn that migrated history is included. FRS-113.3 Its cards shall be failures reviewed, any potential effect, risk to patient, failed in warranty, frequent failure and product corrected. FRS-113.4 Its built-in analyses shall be which products fail (under the product as reviewed, FRS-105.5), per cover, root cause, complaint grouping, standard complaint, spare category, machines failing more than once (model and serial), software version in version order and age at failure in age order. FRS-113.5 Each analysis shall be a chart with a table beside it (rank, count, share, cumulative) and a Data labels switch. FRS-113.6 Clicking any bar or table row shall narrow every chart, shown as Narrowed to chips with Clear all. FRS-113.7 The trend shall be offered by month, quarter or year, as a line and a table, each period clickable. FRS-113.8 A user shall be able to build a chart from 22 named dimensions and a form (Pareto, share or ordered), name it and keep it; sharing it with everyone or a role shall need charts.share (a part of config.manage since 0286), enforced by the saved_charts policies; the owner shall be stamped by the database; a shared chart shall be drawn from the reader’s own rows; a chart whose dimension no longer exists shall say so. FRS-113.9 Field Failure Insights shall show reports, open, due a review, CAPA in hand, call still open, effect withdrawn, closed, cancelled and migrated. FRS-113.10 Insights shall cross-filter across machine, cover, status, CAPA, root cause, grouping, customer and period, with chips and Clear all. FRS-113.11 Insights shall chart which machines fail, cover, root cause, grouping, customer, report status and CAPA status, the trend by month, quarter or year with change, share and running total, and a Pareto drilled freely through machine, complaint grouping and root cause with the 80% line; its raw sheet shall say of each report whether it was migrated or raised here. FRS-113.12 Both screens shall say when not connected, when a read failed and while reading.

### URS-019 — Controlled change

*v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026 · Risk: Medium. Filed here because the requirement declares this screen.*

Changes to the software shall be version-controlled, tested and approved; each release shall be uniquely identifiable in-app.

| Implemented by | Risk | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FRS-207** — Recording the execution of a validation test | High | OQ-200 |
| **FRS-208** — The validation package, section by section | Medium | OQ-201 |
| **FRS-209** — Data flows defined as data, drawn from it, and checked | Medium | OQ-202 |
| **FRS-213** — The application frame | Medium | OQ-222, OQ-224, OQ-206 |
| **FRS-024** — Release identity & change log | Medium | IQ-01 |

**FRS-207.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-207.1 Software Validation shall offer result recording (Pass / Fail / N/A and the actual result) only to a person the database permits to record — an administrator or a holder of config.manage (D-068). FRS-207.2 validation_results shall hold one row per EXECUTION of a test, each with its own result, actual result, executor and execution time, a new execution adding a row (D-068). FRS-207.3 The executor shall be stamped from auth.uid() and displayed with the result; a typed tester name, where kept, shall be shown beside it and never in place of it (D-068). FRS-207.4 The execution time shall be the time of that execution (D-068). FRS-207.5 A refused or failed save shall be stated on screen with the database’s reason (D-068). FRS-207.6 The Test Protocol shall display, per test, the latest execution and the number of earlier ones, and summarise recorded against total, passes and failures. FRS-207.7 A person who may not record shall see the results read-only, the screen saying so. FRS-207.8 The approval, CAPA and checklist evidence tables shall print blank for wet signature. RATIONALE: 0046 keys the table on test_id alone and sets executed_at only when it is empty, so a re-test overwrites the earlier result and keeps the FIRST date; the tester is free text; and a save the database refuses is ignored by the screen.

**FRS-208.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-208.1 Software Validation shall open by mod:/software-validation and present the package in tabs, each tab holding its own key and showing its own section and no other. FRS-208.2 The Requirements by Module tab shall list, per module, its requirements and their gaps — user requirements with no system requirement, system requirements with no test, user requirements with no test — and the screens with no requirement, each with its written reason. FRS-208.3 The Traceability Matrix shall list one row per link between a user requirement, a system requirement and a test, with counts, and shall name the tests outside it. FRS-208.4 The Traceability Summary shall state, counted from the package, how many user requirements have no system requirement and how many have no test, and mark each; only where both counts are zero shall it state that all have both. FRS-208.5 Software Validation shall print the tab on show, or every section as the full package. RATIONALE: .1 and .4 are D-073 — two tabs shared the key ‘trace’, so pressing either showed both, and the summary asserted "every requirement is covered" whatever the table beneath it showed.

**FRS-209.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-209.1 Each data flow shall be defined as data in src/lib/flows.ts: steps, each with a label, the MODULES route it happens on where it happens on a screen, an area, a detail, the records it reads or writes and the URS / FRS / test IDs that state it; and arrows, each forward, optional or a loop back. FRS-209.2 The diagram shall be laid out from that definition alone, left to right, a step’s column being the longest chain of forward arrows into it, loops drawn beneath and excluded from the ranking. FRS-209.3 The layout shall refuse a definition whose forward arrows form a cycle, naming the step. FRS-209.4 Software Validation shall show every flow on a Data Flows tab, and How RITHI Functions shall show the same flows from the same definition under a Data flows choice. FRS-209.5 Selecting a step shall show its detail, its records, its requirement and test IDs, and a link that opens its screen. FRS-209.6 Printing the full validation package shall include every flow, each with a table of its steps, their screens and their IDs. FRS-209.7 check:ui shall fail when a step names a route that is not in MODULES, a requirement or test ID that does not exist in the package, or when an arrow names a step its flow does not contain. FRS-209.8 Every workflow shall have a flow (fourteen as of 2026-10-02: a call, quality, hand stock, a sale, installation, PM, the HandStock spare route, reconciliation, the workshop, documents and training, the masters, people and access, bulk loading, reports and exports). FRS-209.9 A flow shall play step by step in process order (column, then position) with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Reset: played steps shown, the current step highlighted with its detail, later steps faded, the arrows into the current step animated; with reduced motion requested it shall advance only on Next and animate nothing; selecting a box shall stop the walk and open that step. FRS-209.10 check:ui shall fail when an arrow label lies on a box or on another label. RATIONALE: the system owner, 2026-09-30, asking for the flows to be "defined with the validation". .7 is what makes the diagram evidence rather than illustration: a description that is wrong is worse than none, and one that cannot drift is the only kind worth keeping.

**FRS-213.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* FRS-213.1 The menu shall show an entry exactly when the route guard would open its page for that person. FRS-213.2 The route guard shall state, for a known screen the person may not open, that they lack access and whom to ask, and shall send an unknown address to the Dashboard. FRS-213.3 The address /users shall open the User Master. FRS-213.4 The printable routes (/dc/, /declaration/, /ffr/, /indoor-pdt/, /indoor-register/, /indoor-dc/, /mtn/, /mrn-print/) shall render without the menu, their rows bounded by row-level security; /ffr/ shall require the Field Failure Register's module key, the three indoor routes the Indoor Service Register's, /mtn/ the Stock Transfer screen's and /mrn-print/ the Material Returns screen's. FRS-213.5 A screen that fails to render shall show an error in its own place, the menu and header remaining. FRS-213.6 While a saved session is restored the application shall show Loading rather than the sign-in screen. FRS-213.7 The menu shall be grouped, each group and the whole menu collapsible, the sidebar collapsible to icons and remembered per device, and shown as a drawer on a narrow screen; the Knowledge Base heading shall flash until a page in it has been opened on the device. FRS-213.8 The header search shall list the screens the person may open, and from three characters the records they may open (FRS-218); Enter shall open the highlighted entry, the first by default. FRS-213.9 The header shall show a breadcrumb (group · screen), the person’s name and designation, "Permission · <role>", and a menu offering My Profile, Clear Cache and Update, and Sign out. FRS-213.10 A Reporting or Regional Manager shall be able to switch between team calls and own calls, the choice remembered. FRS-213.11 The counts beside menu entries shall carry "+" where they are taken from a partial read. FRS-213.12 The update banner shall check version.json when the tab gains focus and every 5 minutes, name the new version only where it differs from the running one and otherwise say the running build is older, and Update now shall clear the screen caches, keep the offline registers and reload. FRS-213.13 Clear Cache and Update shall clear the screen and dropdown caches, the browser caches and service workers, and reload, keeping the offline registers. FRS-213.14 The theme shall be chosen per device, from the header or from My Profile. FRS-213.15 Demo data left in a browser shall be cleared once on first sign-in. RATIONALE: .1 because an entry shown on admin.view for a page that asks its own key is a menu that offers what the page then refuses; .12 because a banner that announces the version already running teaches people to dismiss it.

**FRS-024.** *(v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026)* Each build carries a version, build number and build ID shown in the footer; an in-app Version History lists changes; source and schema changes are version-controlled.

## Non-auditable requirements

Recorded here because a feature absent from the specification is the thing an assessor finds. Each is classified by PROVENANCE: it is not derived from a regulatory clause and is not offered as evidence against one. That is a statement about where the requirement came from, NOT a statement that its use goes unrecorded.

### NAR-008 — Spare Recycling: a parallel track under Indoor Service, with its own stock, hidden in Audit Mode

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed) — hidden with its screen while Audit Mode is on* · risk: **Low** · *v0.10.100 · 05-Oct-2026*

NAR-008.1 The system shall register a defective spare for recycling with its part (from the Part Master), quantity, received date, its Source (Service Return or Defective Spare), remarks and an optional call reference held as text only, numbered RCY/YY/NNNN restarting each year. NAR-008.2 The system shall let a holder of recycle.request raise an MRS of one or more parts, optionally against an open recycling request, with no approval, numbered RMRS/YY/NNNN; its spares belong to the person who raised it. NAR-008.3 The system shall let a holder of recycle.issue book an MRS line out with a unit cost, in one or more bookings, never beyond the quantity asked for; the quantity shall go to the raiser's recycling hand stock. NAR-008.4 The recycling hand stock shall be issued less consumed, per person and part, kept apart from the regular hand stock; a part shall not be consumed beyond it. NAR-008.5 On an open request a holder of recycle.close shall record consumption from their own recycling hand stock and other costs (Labour, Courier, Vendor, Other), and may remove either while the request is open. NAR-008.6 A request shall close only with its job done recorded, as Returned (to the Service Store as R<PartNo>, recorded only, the Part Master and regular stock unchanged) or Not recyclable with a reason; a closed request shall not change. NAR-008.7 Each request shall show its parts cost (consumption valued at the holder's average stock-out cost for the part), other cost and total, and the cost of stock booked out on its MRSs. NAR-008.8 Nothing in the track shall read or write calls, spare requests, stock outs, spare consumption or the regular hand stock. NAR-008.9 While Audit Mode is on the menu, the screen, its guide entry, its data flow, its Version History entries and this requirement shall be hidden, and the database shall return none of its rows and refuse every write. NAR-008.11 A request shall record Start Work once, with the date and time it started (not in the future, not before the request was registered), and its SLA shall run only from then: due a configured number of working days later (3 by default), skipping the weekdays configured as holidays (Saturday and Sunday by default), counted in India time; the request shall show On track, Due today, Breached, or, once closed, Met or Breached. NAR-008.12 The working days and the holiday weekdays shall be set on the SLA page by a holder of Admin config, apart from the call SLA rules, and the section shall be hidden while Audit Mode is on. NAR-008.13 A quantity of more than one shall be registered as that many requests of one spare each, numbered together. NAR-008.14 A holder of recycle.register shall import spares from any MRN line — its good and defective quantities, any number of times — each spare becoming its own request carrying the MRN No as a reference, with the Source Defective Spare; the MRN shall not be changed. NAR-008.15 While Audit Mode is on the whole page shall disappear — an open page returns to the home screen — and every open screen shall follow the switch as soon as it is thrown, or within a minute on another device. NAR-008.16 A holder of recycle.delete shall delete one or more requests, open or closed, after confirming; their consumption and other costs shall go with them (the consumption returning to the recycling hand stock) and an MRS raised against them shall be kept, no longer linked. NAR-008.10 Its six recycle.* keys shall be granted to no role (an administrator passes every check); the screen key is held by the administrator and Technical Support only, and opens an empty page without a recycle.* key; every other grant is made on Roles & Permissions.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-10-04: "Create a Complete Work Flow for Spare Recycling, Like Registration, spare request job done details, consumption, handstock -- This is a Parallel Track and should not collide with Regular Calls or Spare or Handstock. Even the Stock should be maintained Separately. This is Non Auditable Requirement and when i enable the Audit mode, it should not show. Keep all this under Indoor Service. In Spare Request, there is no need for approval. But during Stock out, Give a Provision to add Cost." The decisions on stock source (regular stores through an MRS into a separate user's hand stock), outcome (Returned as R<PartNo> or Not recyclable) and numbering were the owner's answers the same day. Proved by supabase/tests/spare_recycling_test.sql.

**No test protocol names this requirement.** That is a gap, not a decision.

**Where it lives:** supabase/migrations/0355_spare_recycling.sql · supabase/migrations/0365_spare_recycling_start_sla_mrn.sql · src/modules/SpareRecycling.tsx · src/modules/SlaRulesCard.tsx · src/lib/auditMode.ts · supabase/tests/spare_recycling_test.sql

### NAR-007 — The cover registers open an entry in a pop-up, details beside products, buttons fixed at the top

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed)* · risk: **Low** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

NAR-007.1 The Warranty Register and the Contract Register shall each display an opened entry in a window over the list of entries. NAR-007.2 The window shall display the entry's details on its left and the list of the entry's machines on its right. NAR-007.3 The window shall display every action on the entry, and on its machines as a whole, in a bar at its top that does not scroll. NAR-007.4 Each of the two halves shall scroll independently of the other. NAR-007.5 The window shall not close on a click outside it. NAR-007.6 The window shall ask for confirmation before closing while the entry or any of its machines holds an unsaved change. NAR-007.7 The window shall display the two halves one above the other where the available width is below 900 pixels. NAR-007.8 The Warranty Register and the Contract Register shall each label their per-machine view Register. NAR-007.9 The window shall display the Renew panel and the Convert to Contract panel in a third column beside the two, widening to make room. NAR-007.10 Selecting a machine line on the Register tab shall open that line's entry in the window, with the selected machine opened, marked and scrolled into view.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-10-02: "Rename "By Machine" to "Register". When I click on the Entry, the Entry should open in a Pop Up Window with 2 Screens - Left Side details of the Entry, Right Side List of Product. Keep all the Action Buttons at the Top [Sticky]." Then, the same day: "Do the same for the Warranty Register" — which replaced NAR-005's side-by-side split on both registers. CLASSIFIED NON-AUDITABLE BY WHAT IT TOUCHES, as NAR-005 was: the same fields, the same validation, the same policies and the same writes, arranged differently. Two parts are not cosmetic and are stated for that reason: NAR-007.5 and NAR-007.6, because a window holding a contract's rates that closed on a stray click would lose them without a trace. A button that acts on ONE machine (Save machine, Remove) stays on that machine's card, and the Renew panel's Create the renewal stays inside the panel it confirms; NAR-007.3 covers the actions on the entry and on its machines as a whole. Should this layout ever be used to withhold a field from one of the two halves, that use is NOT covered by this classification.

**Verified by:** OQ-225 — The Register tab marks and filters machines waiting for an installation call; a line opens its entry; Renew and Convert open in a third column.

**Where it lives:** src/modules/CoverRegister.tsx · src/modules/fieldcalls.css

### NAR-006 — A call's Party and Product details refreshed from the masters — only while Audit Mode is OFF

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed) — the first rule conditioned on Audit Mode (NAR-001)* · risk: **Medium** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

NAR-006.1 The Call View and the call registers shall offer Update Party Details, which sets a call's City and State from the Party Master entry for its party, leaving a call whose party the master does not hold unchanged. NAR-006.2 They shall offer Update Product Details, which sets the Warranty No, Warranty Start and End, Contract No, Contract Start and End, Contract Type and Item Status to what was in force ON THE CALL'S REGISTRATION DATE: the warranty and the contract running on that date; where none was running, the last that had ended before it, with Item Status OGP; where both were running, Item Status WGP. The machine is matched on product and serial together. NAR-006.3 Both shall be available on a call of any status, one call at a time or for many selected calls, to a holder of calls.edit or calls.edit.customer. NAR-006.4 While Audit Mode is ON both controls shall be hidden and the database shall refuse both functions.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-09-30: "Give a Provision to update Party Details and Product Details as Separate Functions in the Call View ... As on the Date of Call registration", and "This Button falls under Audit Mode, this can be enabled when the Audit Mode is disabled and should be hidden when Audit Mode is enabled. It's a Non Auditable Requirement." ASSESSED AGAINST NAR-001's condition: the Audit Mode rule WITHHOLDS a write while the mode is on; it does not alter, conceal or suppress any record, nor change what a record shows an assessor. The refresh itself writes through the calls' ordinary policies and every change is recorded by the calls' record_audit triggers with its before and after values, so a refreshed call remains traceable. Implemented by 0271 (call_cover_as_of, refresh_calls_party, refresh_calls_product) and proved by call_refresh_from_masters_test.

**No test protocol names this requirement.** That is a gap, not a decision.

**Where it lives:** 0271_call_refresh_from_masters.sql · supabase/tests/call_refresh_from_masters_test.sql · src/modules/FieldCalls.tsx · src/lib/auditMode.ts

### NAR-004 — Scheduled export of chosen tables, delivered by electronic mail

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed) — BUILT; THE MAIL SIDE AWAITS ONE DEPLOYMENT* · risk: **High** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

NAR-004.1 The system shall provide an administrator a means to define a named export schedule. NAR-004.2 An export schedule shall identify one or more relations of the public schema. NAR-004.3 The system shall reject an export schedule identifying a relation absent from the public schema. NAR-004.4 The system shall reject an export schedule identifying the relation audit_log, record_audit or audit_mode_changes. NAR-004.5 An export schedule shall specify a recurrence of either every day or one stated day of the week. NAR-004.6 An export schedule shall specify a time of day in the Asia/Kolkata time zone. NAR-004.7 The system shall obtain the delivery addresses of an export from the export service configuration. NAR-004.8 The system shall provide no application interface that changes the delivery addresses of an export. NAR-004.9 The system shall write the contents of each relation identified by a schedule to a separate comma-separated-values file. NAR-004.10 The system shall collect the files of one export into one archive. NAR-004.11 The system shall send one electronic mail message carrying that archive to each delivery address. NAR-004.12 The system shall omit from the archive each file whose inclusion would take the archive above the configured attachment limit. NAR-004.13 The system shall name each relation omitted under NAR-004.12 in the body of that message. NAR-004.14 The system shall send at most one message for one export schedule in one recurrence interval. NAR-004.15 The system shall send one message for a recurrence interval whose stated time has passed and for which it has sent no message. NAR-004.16 The system shall read every row of each identified relation irrespective of the row-level security policies on that relation. NAR-004.17 The system shall record for each export its start time, its completion time, the relations exported, the number of rows exported, the size of the archive and its outcome. NAR-004.18 The system shall send one electronic mail message naming the cause where an export does not complete. NAR-004.19 The system shall refuse every modification and every deletion of an export record received through the application programming interface.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-09-22 ("Export every Table and send it to Email every day by 11pm"), then narrowed by the same person to a CSV export of SELECTED tables ("I need to Export CSV only. Maybe I can select the Tables") and to a schedule set on a screen ("Or can we have Scheduled Export option in the UI itself so that i will schedule which ever is necessary"). The statements above are the narrowed requirement, which is what is built. THE ONE STATEMENT THAT IS NOT A CONVENIENCE IS NAR-004.8. An earlier design of this export held the delivery address in an app_settings row; it was refused as an exfiltration primitive and the refusal was correct — NAR-004.16 makes this the whole customer base, every serial, every contract, every contact, leaving the system on a timer, and a destination any administrator can edit means it can be redirected silently with nothing on any screen looking different the next morning. So the requirement is split by WHERE IT IS KEPT: which relations and at what time are rows an administrator edits (NAR-004.1, .2, .5, .6); the addresses are configuration of the export service, set through the deployment channel by somebody holding the project keys (NAR-004.7), and no application path changes them (NAR-004.8). NAR-004.4 is the second control and exists for the same reason NAR-004.16 does: the export reads past row-level security, so an unchecked relation name would be a way to mail out the audit trail. WHAT IS BUILT AND WHAT IS NOT: the schedules, their guards, the due-time arithmetic and the run record are in 0228 and the screen is Administration → Data Export. The service that sends the mail is supabase/functions/scheduled-export (Deno, Resend), which cannot be deployed from the repository — it needs a Resend key and one CLI deploy. NOTHING IS SENT UNTIL THAT IS DONE, and NAR-004.9 to .19 are therefore SPECIFIED AND UNVERIFIED AS AT THIS REVISION. The transport was the system owner’s choice on 2026-09-22 ("Resend + Supabase Edge Function for the transport"); the addresses agreed are service.almsind@gmail.com and devika.m@airliquide.com. A CORRECTION IS OWED ON THIS ENTRY’S OWN EARLIER TEXT. It stated that a search on 2026-09-22 found "no mail path of any kind — no MailApp, no pg_net, no transport" and withdrew two statements about a daily digest on that basis. THAT SEARCH WAS WRONG: supabase/functions/daily-digest has been in the repository since 2026-09, sends through Resend, attaches the day’s record_audit as a CSV, and ships with a pg_net schedule — and this package’s own supplier appendix names Resend. The true statement is narrower and is the one that matters to an assessor: THAT FUNCTION HAS NEVER BEEN DEPLOYED, so no digest has ever been sent and no off-database archive of the audit trail exists. The claim withdrawn was about a control OPERATING; the reason given for withdrawing it was false. Should this export ever be relied upon as the backup of record, that use is NOT covered by this classification: backup and restore is FRS-023, it is auditable, and PQ-06 verifies it.

**Verified by:** OQ-68 — The daily export runs to time, carries every table, and says so when it does not. · OQ-70 — A schedule names what leaves and when, and cannot name where it goes or reach an audit trail. · OQ-71 — The mail carries every row of the chosen relations, readable, and says what it left out.

**Where it lives:** 0228_export_schedules.sql · supabase/functions/scheduled-export/index.ts · src/modules/DataExport.tsx · supabase/tests/export_schedule_test.sql · scripts/check-scheduled-export.mjs

### NAR-003 — Bulk Report Mapping — attaching a recovered report to its call, and converting the references already loaded

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed)* · risk: **Medium** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

NAR-003.1 Bulk Report Mapping shall identify the call for each imported row by the UC Number, and by the Call Number where the UC Number is empty. NAR-003.2 Bulk Report Mapping shall classify a visit as the completed visit when the visit call status, reduced to lower-case alphanumeric characters, equals "solvedreportcompleted". NAR-003.3 Bulk Report Mapping shall make no change to a call whose completed visit holds a non-empty report link. NAR-003.4 Bulk Report Mapping shall write the report link to the completed visit whose report link is empty. NAR-003.5 Bulk Report Mapping shall select the completed visit with the latest entry timestamp where the call holds more than one completed visit with an empty report link. NAR-003.6 Bulk Report Mapping shall write the report link, the source reference and the call status "Solved - Report Completed" to the visit selected under NAR-003.4. NAR-003.7 Bulk Report Mapping shall preserve every column of that visit other than the three columns named in NAR-003.6. NAR-003.8 Bulk Report Mapping shall create one visit carrying the report link and the call status "Solved - Report Completed" where the call holds no completed visit. NAR-003.9 Bulk Report Mapping shall make no change for an imported row whose report link is empty. NAR-003.10 Bulk Report Mapping shall display for each imported row, before the operator confirms the write, one action from the set {no change, write to existing visit, create visit}. NAR-003.11 Bulk Report Mapping shall complete every write to an existing visit before it creates any visit. NAR-003.12 Bulk Report Mapping shall classify the report column of every visit it can read as one of: a Drive link, a Drive file identifier, an AppSheet link, an AppSheet file path, another link, or unrecognised. NAR-003.13 Bulk Report Mapping shall report the number of visits it classified into each of the six classes named in NAR-003.12 before the operator confirms any write. NAR-003.14 Bulk Report Mapping shall resolve an AppSheet link and an AppSheet file path to a Drive link by the file name each carries. NAR-003.15 Bulk Report Mapping shall make no change to a visit whose file name Google Drive resolves to no file or to more than one file. NAR-003.16 Bulk Report Mapping shall write the visit’s report link and its source reference, and no other column of that visit, when it converts a reference. NAR-003.17 Bulk Report Mapping shall write the reference it replaced to the source reference column of a visit whose source reference column is empty. NAR-003.18 Bulk Report Mapping shall make no change to the source reference column of a visit whose source reference column is not empty. NAR-003.19 Bulk Report Mapping shall state, where the person operating it does not hold sight of every call, that the counts it reports are of the visits that person can read.

**Why it is classified this way.** Stated by the system owner on 2026-09-22: "If the Report is already present, it should not update. If the Report is Absent, then it should update the Report Link on a Existing Visit Entry - with Status ‘Solved - Report Completed’ - with the Report Link. If there is no Visit with ‘Solved - Report Completed’, then it should add Visit Entry." CLASSIFIED NON-AUDITABLE BY PROVENANCE, at the owner’s direction: it is a rule about how a recovery tool behaves, not one derived from a regulatory clause, and it is not offered as evidence against one. THAT IS NOT A STATEMENT THAT ITS USE GOES UNRECORDED — `reports` is one of the ten tables record_audit covers (0225), so every attachment and every filed visit is recorded with the row before and after. NAR-003.3 and NAR-003.7 are the two that carry weight and are written as prohibitions for that reason: a recovered link must never displace one an engineer filed, and a visit being attached to is an engineer’s record whose other columns are theirs. Should this tool ever be used to alter a visit’s date, engineer or work details, that use is NOT covered by this classification and is to be raised as an auditable requirement with its own risk assessment. NAR-003.12 TO .19 WERE ADDED ON 2026-09-22 for the second job the same screen now does. A probe counted 12,254 visits, 7,538 of which hold an AppSheet reference in the report column where a Drive link should be — 5,496 bare file paths and 2,042 AppSheet links — because Bulk Uploads’ visit registers store the cell exactly as the file wrote it. On those calls the report cannot be opened. RE-IMPORTING THE SOURCE SHEET IS NOT THE REMEDY AND IS WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEHAVIOUR: those rows now carry the engineer’s own columns, and an import would write the file over them. NAR-003.15 IS THE ONE THAT CARRIES THE MOST WEIGHT. A reference Drive cannot resolve is left exactly as it is, because an unresolved reference can still be settled by hand while a blanked one has lost the only thing that says which document it was — the same argument as NAR-003.3, one level down. NAR-003.16 EXCLUDES THE CALL STATUS DELIBERATELY, and differs from NAR-003.6 for that reason: attaching a recovered report to a visit that had none is a statement that the report is now complete, whereas changing the FORM of a reference already on the row says nothing new about what the engineer did. A status written here would also move which visit decides its call’s status, on up to 7,538 calls in one pass.

**Verified by:** OQ-67 — A recovered report reaches its call without displacing what an engineer filed. · OQ-69 — A reference already in the register becomes a link, and nothing that cannot be resolved is lost.

**Where it lives:** src/lib/reportMapping.ts · src/modules/ReportMapping.tsx · src/components/report/ConvertLoadedReports.tsx · scripts/check-report-mapping.ts

### NAR-002 — Tracker — the shared activity list

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed)* · risk: **Low** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

An activity list a handful of people keep together: anyone who can open it may add a row, edit any field and delete a row, and every field saves when it loses focus rather than through a form. A deletion removes the row for everybody, after a confirmation that says so. Each row shows who last changed it and when and who raised it, stamped by the database, and a position number with the durable id on hover. Rows marked Done or Dropped are hidden until a tick shows them, with their count. Adding and deleting a row are recorded in the audit trail. It is reached under Administration and is gated by its own module key, so who may open it is an administrator’s decision like any other screen.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-09-08 — "add a tracker page under admin to track activities. something very similar to backlog.. shared between me and a few other. all who have access should be able add, edit". IT IS NOT A QUALITY RECORD AND IS NOT OFFERED AS ONE: nothing in the servicing process reads it, no figure is drawn from it, and no judgement recorded elsewhere depends on it. It is listed here for the reason this section exists — a feature absent from the specification is the thing an assessor finds — and because its edit-in-place behaviour is deliberate and would otherwise read as a control that had been forgotten rather than one that was never required. Should anything a servicing or quality procedure relies on ever be kept here, that use is NOT covered by this classification and is to be raised as an auditable requirement with its own risk assessment: a shared list with no attribution per field and no amendment history cannot carry a record anybody must rely on.

**No test protocol names this requirement.** That is a gap, not a decision.

**Where it lives:** src/modules/Tracker.tsx

### NAR-001 — Audit Mode

*Non-Auditable Requirement (user-originated; no regulatory clause claimed)* · risk: **Medium** · *v0.10.66 · 03-Oct-2026*

The system provides a system-wide Audit Mode that only a holder of audit.mode (an administrator unless one is granted it) may switch on or off. The switch is held in app_settings; it is changed only through set_audit_mode(), which refuses a caller without audit.mode and refuses a change with no reason; every change is written to audit_mode_changes with the new state, the reason, the actor and the time. That table has no insert, update or delete path through the API and is not covered by the audit-log retention purge, so the record of when the mode was on outlives the audit log itself.

**Why it is classified this way.** Requested by the system owner on 2026-09-06, with the rules governing the mode’s BEHAVIOUR to be supplied separately. As at this revision ONE BEHAVIOUR IS CONDITIONED ON THE MODE, and it is NAR-006: while the mode is ON, a call's Party and Product details cannot be refreshed from the masters (the controls are hidden and the database refuses). Nothing else reads it. It is documented now rather than later because an undocumented switch in a validated system is a finding in itself. When the rules arrive, each one is to be assessed on its own merits — any rule that would alter, conceal or suppress a quality record, or change what a record shows to an assessor, is NOT covered by this classification and must be raised as an auditable requirement with its own risk assessment before it is built.

**Verified by:** OQ-38 — Audit Mode is an administrator’s switch, and every throw of it is kept.

**Where it lives:** 0114_audit_mode.sql · supabase/tests/audit_mode_test.sql

# Traceability matrix

**One row per LINK, not per requirement.** A user requirement implemented by
two system requirements, each proved by two tests, is four rows — because what
is being traced is the link: *this need is met by this mechanism, and that is
shown by this test*. Collapsing them into one row with three lists hands the
reader back the very question the matrix exists to answer.

The URS and FRS cells are **left blank on a row that continues the one above**,
so the eye follows a requirement down its own block. Nothing is missing there:
the identifier is the one at the top of the block.

A requirement with no system requirement, or a mechanism with no test, **still
gets a row**, with the gap named in the empty column. Leaving it out would make
this table answer "everything here is traced" by omitting everything that is
not.

| **URS-130** | **A stock movement dated in the past is still counted, and one dated in the future is refused** — Where a hand-over, a return or a challan may be dated earlier than the day it is recorded, the system shall keep the recording time separately from the stated date, shall refuse a stated date in the future, and shall either count a back-dated movement in the engineer's hand stock or refuse it — never record it and leave it out of the balance. A movement that is recorded and not counted is the one error a stock register cannot show. _(Risk: High.)_ | **FRS-163** | FRS-163.1 The database shall refuse a transfer date, an MRN date or a DC date later than the day it is recorded. FRS-163.2 The database shall refuse a transfer or a return whose stated date falls before the hand-stock cutoff (`handstock_cutoff()`, the day after the last closed period). FRS-163.3 Every transfer and return the database accepts shall appear in `handstock_movements` and in the balance. FRS-163.4 The recording time of each movement shall be kept separately from its stated date (`created_at`, `sys_created_on`). FRS-163.5 A stock out shall be dated in the ledger by its booking time, so that the DC date moves no balance (FRS-153.11). RATIONALE: 0096 dates a transfer by `transfer_date` and a return by `mrn_date` and drops every movement dated before the cutoff, on the ground that the closing figure already holds it — which is true only of a movement recorded BEFORE the close. One recorded afterwards and back-dated across it is in neither (D-050). | **OQ-155** | OQ · A back-dated movement is counted or refused, never recorded and dropped. A header with no lines, or a return with some of its lines, is a record that says less than happened — and for a return, stock has already been taken off an engineer for parts the record does not list. _(Risk: High.)_ | **FRS-164** | FRS-164.1 A spare request and its lines shall be written by one database call that writes both or neither. RATIONALE: the three screens write the header, then the lines, and on a failure DELETE the header — a compensating delete the database does not permit: 0049's retention trigger refuses a delete of `spare_requests`, `mr_delete` admits only an administrator, and `stock_transfers` has no delete policy at all. Each delete fails or matches nothing, unchecked, and the half-record stays (D-044). | **OQ-156** | OQ · A spare request, a return and a transfer are saved whole or not at all. | **URS-132** | **A correction to a person's name keeps their team and their work with them** — The system shall allow only an administrator to change the name of a person on the User Master. Where the name changes, the system shall carry the change, in the same act, to every record that identifies that person BY NAME as the one the record belongs to: the people who name them as Reporting or Regional Manager, the calls allotted to them, their call requests and pending registrations, spare requests and dispatches, consumption, opening stock, issue history, material returns, stock transfers, and the customers and machines they look after. It shall NOT rewrite a record of something the person DID — an approval, a dispatch, a receipt, a recorded-by, a visit report, the log of changes of engineer — those being signatures. It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank, where only its case or surrounding space changed, or where another person on the User Master still holds the old name. Before saving, the User Master shall state what the change will move and ask for confirmation. Who may see a call and whose stock a part is are both decided by the name, so a correction that moves the person and leaves their records behind silently hides their calls from them and their manager and splits their hand stock into two balances. _(Risk: High.)_ | **FRS-166** | FRS-166.1 The database shall refuse a change to a User Master name from anybody but an administrator (`user_directory_address_guard`). FRS-166.2 When a name changes, `user_directory_carry_rename()` (0257) shall rewrite, in the same statement, every other User Master row naming the old name as Reporting Manager or Regional Manager, matched with lower() and no trimming, exactly as `visible_engineer_names()` matches. FRS-166.3 It shall carry nothing where the old name was blank. FRS-166.4 It shall carry nothing where only the case changed. FRS-166.5 It shall carry nothing where another User Master row still holds the old name. FRS-166.6 The User Master shall state before saving a changed name — from the drawer and from the whole-table edit — how many people name it as manager and which kinds of record will move, or, where another row holds the old name, that NOTHING will move; and shall save only on confirmation. FRS-166.7 The cascade shall run as the caller, so `sys_updated_by` on every moved row names the administrator who renamed. RATIONALE: .2 matches as the tree matches, because a btrim() here would also move a row naming ' Ravi ', which the tree does not count as Ravi's today — a widening. .5 because two rows with one name are two people the tree already cannot tell apart, and moving their team to one of them would be a guess. Proved as a signed-in administrator by `supabase/tests/directory_rename_carries_team_test.sql`. | **OQ-159** | OQ · Correcting a manager's name keeps their team, within the three limits, and only an administrator can do it. Expected: The non-administrator is refused by the database. The warning names three people and the kinds of record that will move. | **URS-151** | **A bulk load is seen before it is written, and is recorded** — The system shall permit a register to be loaded from a file only by an administrator. A load that stops part-way shall state how much of it was written. Every load shall be recorded with who ran it, into which register, from which file, and how many rows were written and held back. A bulk load writes more quality records in a minute than a person writes in a year: one that is not previewed makes its mistakes at that rate, and one that is not recorded leaves nobody able to say where the records came from. _(Risk: High.)_ | **FRS-196** | FRS-196.1 Bulk Uploads shall open only for a holder of bulk.upload (an administrator holds it); what each load writes is still decided by that table's own policies. FRS-196.3 Bulk Uploads shall display guidance before first use: that the order of loading matters, that the preview comes first, that dates are read day-first, and which registers carry a warning. FRS-196.4 Bulk Uploads shall list the registers in groups (Calls, Visit Reports, Spares, Quality, Masters, Master Value Lists, Cover), and shall show a register's exact current row count after a load into it and, for every register, on request (Count every register) — never a stale or estimated number, and no count at all until one is taken (v0.10.112: the counts were taken on every open, 31 whole-table scans, among the heaviest reads on the live project). FRS-196.5 Bulk Uploads shall locate a file’s header row below any letterhead by the register’s own column names. FRS-196.6 Bulk Uploads shall display, before any write: the rows ready; each row held back with its row number and reason; the headings kept on the row, not loaded, ignored and stamped; the recognised columns with the required ones marked; and one shaped sample row. FRS-196.7 Bulk Uploads shall state, where no row is loadable, which required column every row lacks and ask whether the right register was chosen, and shall write nothing. FRS-196.8 Bulk Uploads shall run a register’s preparation step before the confirmation, so the count confirmed is the count written, and that step shall WRITE nothing until the operator confirms — no stub request and no visit (D-075). FRS-196.9 Bulk Uploads shall ask for confirmation stating the number of rows, the register, what the preparation will create or re-point, and either the column a re-run is matched on or that the register has no key and a re-run adds every row again. FRS-196.10 Bulk Uploads shall write in batches of 300, 500 or 2,000 rows by table, displaying progress, each request holding rows of a single column set. FRS-196.11 Bulk Uploads shall upsert a register that has a natural key and insert into one that has none. FRS-196.12 Bulk Uploads shall state on failure the database’s error, the row it stopped near, how many rows were written before it stopped, and a hint where one is known (a missing index → _status.sql; a timeout → re-run; a missing table). FRS-196.13 Bulk Uploads shall download this device’s offline copy again after a Product Database or Party Master load. FRS-196.14 Bulk Uploads shall write an audit entry for every load, naming the register, the file, the rows written, the rows held back and the outcome (D-067). FRS-196.15 Bulk Uploads shall provide a control that dismisses a result message. RATIONALE: .8 — the preparation step was moved before the confirmation so the number approved is the number written, and in moving it the two steps that CREATE records (stub spare requests, visits from a consumption file) came to write before anybody had agreed to the load; cancelling leaves them in the register. .12 — there is no whole-file rollback, so the count already written is what a person needs to decide whether a re-run is safe, which it is only where the register has a key. FRS-196.16 (2026-10-08) The Spare Request upload shall hold back, and name, a row with no Engineer Name; the Spare Request Lines upload shall hold back, and count and name, a line whose request is not in RITHI, and shall create no request for it (D-158). | **OQ-189** | OQ · A bulk load needs bulk.upload, is previewed and confirmed before it writes anything, reports a part-written failure, and is recorded. Each load appears in the Audit Log with register, file and counts. |

FRS-198.9 The Consumption upload shall hold back and name each row whose call has no visit and whose file gives no date for one. FRS-198.10 The historical and yearly consumption and stock-out uploads shall key each row on its source and reference — the yearly reference being position, UCN and part — derive the source year from the Visit Entry year, and carry the Historical provenance. | **URS-156** | **A change to what a role may do is deliberate, confined to the roles changed, and recorded** — The system shall let an authorised administrator grant and remove, per role, the right to open each screen and each action on it; shall show every other administrator the same matrix read-only; and shall write, on saving, only the roles the administrator changed. |  |  | **FRS-083** | `feedback_without_report` (0229) lists every customer feedback with no visit reading “Solved - Report Completed” behind it, and names WHICH of four things is absent, because each needs a different fix: the feedback records no UCN; no call carries that UCN; the call has no visit at all; or the call has visits and none of them is the completed one. The last is the commonest, and the row carries `latest_visit_status` beside it so that “Solved - Report Pending” — the system stating a known absence — is distinguishable from “Unsolved”, which is a different problem. THE STATUS IS MATCHED ON ITS LETTERS AND DIGITS, not as a string: `is_report_completed()` reduces to lower-case alphanumerics, so a trailing space, a lower-case spelling and an en-dash all read as completed, and `isCompletedVisit()` in src/lib/reportMapping.ts is the client copy of the same rule. That is not defensive coding — the export this was written for carried “Solved - Report Completed ” with a trailing space in all 378 rows, and a string comparison would have reported every one of those calls as missing its report. ANY visit reading completed is enough rather than the latest one: a call written up and then re-visited still has its report. A false entry here sends somebody to re-file a report that exists, which is wasted work and teaches them the list may mean nothing — the same argument as a `_status.sql` row that answers NO for nothing — so both rules are tested with the spellings that actually arrive. The view is `security_invoker`, so the ordinary call and feedback policies decide the rows; the SCREEN is restricted to administrators by `mod:/feedback-without-report`, at the user’s direction (2026-09-22). | **OQ-72** | OQ · Feedback with no completed report behind it is listed, and feedback WITH one is not. | **URS-064** | **A credential cannot be recovered from a log** — No log, error message or build record the system produces shall contain any part of a credential. Where a credential is malformed such that a subsystem would report a fragment of it, the operation shall be REFUSED before that subsystem is reached, and the refusal shall say what to correct without reproducing any part of the value. THAT WAS NOT SUFFICIENT, and a real run proved it twice. Node’s URL parser splits credentials at the LAST “@” and libpq at the FIRST, so a password containing an unencoded “@” makes libpq report a HOST built from a SUFFIX of the password — a string matching neither the password nor the URL, which no exact-value mask can catch. It reached a public build log while the platform’s own masking displayed the secret as masked throughout. scripts/apply-migrations.mjs now REFUSES before psql is invoked when the URL carries more than one “@”, names the correction and prints no part of the value: nothing can leak from a call that is not made. Every tail of the password of three characters or more is additionally masked, for any other tool reporting the same shape. The exposure already made is not undone by this and is recorded as requiring the credential to be rotated. | **OQ-57** | OQ · A malformed database credential is refused before any part of it can be reported. With the credential correctly encoded the run proceeds, showing the refusal tests the malformation and not the presence of a password. |

|  |  | **FRS-068** | user_signature_status() reports, per user, WHETHER a signature has been saved and when — never the image. remove_user_signature() deletes one belonging to another person and is refused to a non-administrator and for the caller’s own row (which the Profile page removes). Both are SECURITY DEFINER functions, not views: a definer view over Row-Level-Security-protected tables reads as its owner and defeats the policies beneath it, which this system shipped three times, and the automated check that now refuses such a view is not weakened to admit these. A plain DELETE policy admitting an administrator was written first and does not work: PostgreSQL applies the SELECT policy to a DELETE that must locate its row, so an administrator unable to read the row reported a successful statement affecting nothing. | **OQ-51** | OQ · A signature is held for, and applied by, its owner alone. FRS-203.4 Roles & Permissions shall grant the right to open a page (View) and each action on it separately per role, and shall provide a control granting or removing every right on one page for one role. FRS-203.5 Roles & Permissions shall display the administrator role holding every permission, and shall not allow it to be narrowed. FRS-203.6 Roles & Permissions shall, on Save, write only the roles the operator changed, re-assert the administrator’s full set where it has fallen behind, and state "Nothing was changed" when nothing was. FRS-203.7 Roles & Permissions shall refuse to save a role left with no permission (URS-056). FRS-203.8 The system shall record each saved change with the role, each permission granted or removed, who changed it and when (D-067). FRS-203.9 Roles & Permissions shall export the matrix as .xlsx — a Matrix sheet (group, page, route, grant, key, Yes / No per role), a Roles sheet (permissions held, stored or NOT CONFIGURED fallback) and a How to read this sheet (who, when, saved or UNSAVED) — recorded as rbac.export and available to rbac.manage and admin.view. FRS-203.10 Roles & Permissions shall report the outcome of a save in a message that can be dismissed. FRS-203.14 Every action on a page, including those that were an administrator's alone, shall be a key on that page's row, tickable for every role but Admin; the Admin column shall be shown greyed, holding everything and not removable (finding 65, and the user's 2026-09-30 request). |  |  | **FRS-021** | TWO TRAILS AGAIN, as of 0225 (2026-09-21). `audit_log` records what a USER DID — action, target, duration, outcome, actor and time — and its retention is configurable (app_settings.audit_retention_days, default ~10 years), with a daily digest built to archive the day off-database (supabase/functions/daily-digest) THAT HAS NEVER BEEN DEPLOYED — so no off-database archive exists today. Its LIMITS are stated rather than glossed: it is written by the CLIENT, so it can be bypassed by a direct API call, and it is purged when the retention window passes. THE SECOND TRAIL IS BACK ON. `record_audit` records what a ROW BECAME, before and after, in triggers that CANNOT BE BYPASSED and that nothing purges — stopped by 0112 on 2026-09-05 when it was thought to exist only for 21 CFR Part 11, and re-armed by 0225 at the user’s direction on 2026-09-21. The event that settled it was not a regulatory one: on 2026-09-20 a re-applied bundle set 4,222 calls back to Unattended, and NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM COULD SAY WHAT THEY HAD BEEN. A client-written trail cannot answer that, because the write did not come through the client. 0103’s shape is what was restored, not 0048’s: a BULK load is ONE attributable event rather than a row per record, so the trail stays about what people did. The table also still holds everything it captured 2026-08 to 2026-09-05; that gap, 05-Sep to 21-Sep, is real and is not recoverable. | **OQ-09** | OQ · Audit trail is complete and tamper-resistant. Expected: Both actions are logged with actor and time; non-admin cannot read/modify the trail. |

FRS-104.3 Rule 2 shall be switchable by ffr.rule2_enabled, and its window and serial count held in app_settings separately from rule 1’s. FRS-104.4 The review shall show, for each rule, the count, the threshold and the earlier UCNs with date, days before, engineer and what they matched on. FRS-104.5 Answers already recorded shall not be re-based when a rule or its settings change. RATIONALE: URS-046 names the procedure’s rule, which is rule 1; rule 2 (0198, the user’s of 2026-09-15) sees the batch, component or design fault that rule 1 cannot, because every one of those calls is a first failure on its own machine. | **OQ-92** | OQ · The fleet-wide repeat-failure rule fires on distinct serials, says which rule fired, and does not re-base recorded answers. Training shall be recorded as sessions with the attendees, the trainer, the method, any assessment result and the attendance evidence, or as the person's own acknowledgement of having read the document; a failed assessment shall keep the training open. FRS-172.4 Every deletion shall be written to the audit trail with the name removed.
